author: mdnishath
body:
Wires the [`claude-in-mobile`](https://github.com/AlexGladkov/claude-in-mobile) MCP server into Claude Code so it can drive a real Android phone, an iOS simulator, Chrome, or a desktop app. This pairs with audit phases 3 and 5, which are stronger against a *running* app than against source alone.

## What's here

- **`mobile/setup-mobile.sh`** — checks Node >= 18, installs the all-in-one npm package, runs the toolchain doctor, reports which devices `adb` can see, and registers the server via `claude mcp add`. Falls back to printing the JSON snippet when the `claude` CLI isn't on `PATH`. Configurable through `SCOPE`, `PROFILE`, and `SERVER_NAME`.
- **`mobile/README.md`** — per-platform prerequisites, Android USB-debugging and wireless-pairing steps, iOS simulator setup, `MOBILE_PROFILE` tool counts, a standalone JSON-RPC verification probe, and troubleshooting.
- **`mobile/mcp.example.json`** — config snippet for clients configured by hand.
- **`README.md`** — new "Auditing a running app" section plus the updated repository layout.

## Important constraint, documented prominently

The server reaches the device over local USB (`adb`) or a local simulator (`xcrun`). A remote or cloud Claude Code session has no USB bus and cannot see the device, so the setup has to run on the machine the phone plugs into. This is called out at the top of `mobile/README.md`, in the main README section, and in the troubleshooting list.

## Verification

Checked against the real package rather than from the docs alone:

- `claude-in-mobile` and `mcp-devices` both resolve to **4.0.2** on npm; the all-in-one edition enables all five platforms out of the box (`platforms` reports `android, ios, web, desktop, aurora`), which is why the script prefers it.
- Installed it and ran `claude-in-mobile doctor` — the missing/ok toolchain lines in the README table are its actual output.
- Drove a JSON-RPC handshake straight at the binary: `initialize` returns `serverInfo` `claude-mobile` 4.0.2, and `tools/list` returns **14** tools under `MOBILE_PROFILE=core` and **27** under `full`. Both counts in the profile table are measured, not estimated.
- Ran `setup-mobile.sh` end to end (`bash -n` clean, then a live run with `SCOPE=local`). It completed and `claude mcp list` reported `mobile: claude-in-mobile - √ Connected`. The test registration was removed afterwards.

No device was attached in this environment, so the `adb devices` branch of the script printed its no-device guidance path rather than the device-listing path — that branch is unexercised.

author: kerlonr
body:
Trabalho feito **no Raspberry Pi 5 de produção** (Debian 13 Lite, sem desktop, tela de 800x480), preparando o robô para rodar sozinho. Cada mudança nasceu de um problema real encontrado lá, e os números foram medidos no próprio Pi.

## A face não achava a tela

Sem X nem Wayland, `DISPLAY` vazio fazia `face/app.py` cair no driver `dummy` e desenhar para lugar nenhum — justamente na máquina para a qual o projeto foi feito. Agora ele procura um conector ligado no DRM e usa KMSDRM, a tela do próprio kernel.

Duas armadilhas da imagem Lite que só aparecem no Pi, agora no `setup-raspberry-pi.sh`:

- a wheel do **pygame** no PyPI embute um SDL compilado **sem KMSDRM** — funciona em qualquer desktop e falha só no Pi. O pacote do Debian usa o SDL do sistema, que tem;
- faltava **`libGL.so.1`**, e essa foi a mais cara: o SDL não trata como erro. Registra "Could not initialize OpenGL / GLES library" só em log de depuração, cria os framebuffers, aceita todo `flip` — e não desenha nada. Serviço `active`, log dizendo "face iniciada", kernel jurando que o CRTC do HDMI aponta para o framebuffer da face, e o monitor preto. O que denuncia é a taxa de quadros: **2143 quadros/s** numa tela de 60 Hz é o SDL desenhando para lugar nenhum (com GL são 827).

## A IA de rede era ponto único de falha

Numa apresentação o robô fica na ponta de um Wi-Fi de faculdade, e quando ele cai a Atlas emudece. `llm/fallback.py` mantém um segundo Ollama — no próprio Pi, com um modelo pequeno — e troca sem que a conversa pare.

Quem vigia a rede é uma thread de fundo: descobrir a queda custa um tempo limite inteiro, e pagar isso a cada pergunta viraria segundos de silêncio antes de cada frase. Assim só a pergunta que estava no ar paga o preço. A escolha acontece antes do primeiro token, porque trocar de modelo depois faria a Atlas recomeçar a frase em voz alta.

Qual modelo cabe no Pi 5, medido:

| Modelo | Velocidade | Português |
|---|---|---|
| `gemma3:1b` | **12,7 tokens/s** | acentua certo |
| `llama3.2:1b` | 7,5 tokens/s | troca palavras, come acentos |
| `llama3.2:3b` | 4,9 tokens/s | o melhor dos três, e o mais lento |

## A primeira resposta custava 12 segundos, e não era o modelo

Num modelo em CPU, quase todo o tempo da primeira resposta é **ler a persona**: 9,9 s de prompt eval para 509 tokens, contra 0,9 s para gerar a resposta. Da segunda pergunta em diante o servidor reaproveita o prefixo e cai para 0,4 s — por isso o problema passava despercebido em teste. Só que a primeira pergunta é a de quem chegou perto do robô. `warm_up` passa a receber as mensagens que a conversa vai usar de verdade, e o custo é pago no arranque: **12 s → 1 s**.

## Desempenho e dívidas do `roboteye-keeper`

A face cai para **30 FPS em ARM** (dívida 1). Os movimentos desta face são todos medidos em décimos de segundo e a 30 não se distinguem dos de 60, mas o quadro é gasto contínuo — o que se economiza é metade de um núcleo, o dia inteiro. Medido em 800x480/low: 3,4 ms de mediana, 3,9 ms de p95. O serviço inteiro custa **17% de um núcleo e 130 MB**.

O `roboteye.service` não espera mais por um X11 que nunca chegaria (dívida 4) — era o que fazia reiniciar de 5 em 5 segundos para sempre. A heurística de ARM virou uma só, em `config.py::is_arm()` (dívida 1), e o `setup-raspberry-pi.sh` ganhou o `build-essential` que a imagem Lite não tem (dívida 2). Sobre a dívida 5: `vsync=1` é pedido, mas o KMSDRM do Pi aceita sem honrar (827 quadros/s com e sem, na mesma tela de 60 Hz) — o comentário no código diz isso, em vez de prometer o que não acontece.

## Diagnóstico

`doctor` mostra as duas IAs em linhas separadas: uma linha só escondia qual das duas tinha caído, e o robô responderia pelo modelo pequeno sem ninguém entender por que ficou menos esperto. Máquina de rede fora do ar é **aviso**, não falha — o robô ainda conversa.

Ele também parou de culpar a placa de som quando o culpado é o próprio robô: onde a saída ALSA é exclusiva, o serviço rodando impede o comando de abrir o áudio. E com `backend=null` não abre a placa nenhuma — o que fazia a suíte depender do hardware da máquina, contra o que o `roboteye-keeper` pede. Os testes agora passam **com o robô rodando**, o que antes falhava.

## Verificação

`ruff`, `mypy` e **565 testes** rodados no próprio Pi 5, além de `bench_face.py` dentro do orçamento. O robô sobe no boot em **6,9 s** e foi validado de ponta a ponta: face na tela, voz pelo alto-falante, conversa pela IA de rede em 1 s, e a troca para o modelo local testada cortando a rota até a outra máquina no meio de uma conversa.

author: jackspirou
body:
AON5 of the auth-and-onboarding plan. An operator could apply one provider
credential to the whole deployment and had no way to bound what any account
spent through it: `Tenant.Limits` existed and no enforcement path read it.

## The account plane

| Surface | Route | Guard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account plane (operator) | `/api/v1/admin/tenants[/{tenant_id}]` | `admin` |
| Account usage rollup | `/api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/usage/providers` | tenant access + `activity:read` or `admin` |

Two refusals carry the weight. The default account cannot be deleted — every
key without an explicit account resolves to it. An account that still holds a
gateway API key cannot be deleted either: that key would keep authenticating
with no account behind it and would fall back to the default credential policy
the operator just revoked.

## Deviation from the plan: both meters, not the stricter one

The plan said to resolve the effective limit as "the stricter of the tenant
limit and the key limit". That rule is unsound and this PR does not implement
it. An account limit and a key limit meter different populations: the account
meter counts every key the account holds. Taking the smaller value lets an
account with N keys spend N times its own cap, because each key stays inside
that value on its own meter and nothing totals them.

So a request satisfies every rule that applies to it. `internal/limits/rules.go`
owns the rule; each rule carries the scope that set it, so a 429 or a 402 names
the holder an operator has to talk to (`X-RateLimit-Scope`,
`X-Starport-Budget-Spend-Scope`, `X-Starport-Budget-Tokens-Scope`). The
`Tenant.Limits` doc comment that encoded the wrong semantics in AON1 is fixed.

Plan step 5 needed no work: `RequireAPIKey` already places the tenant record on
the request context, so neither enforcement path touches storage to learn the
account.

## Storage

`usage.Totals` took a key ID string where `""` meant "every key" — three
populations in one parameter, one of them spelled as the absence of another. It
now takes a comparable `usage.Scope` with one constructor per population, and a
scope naming no subject is `ErrInvalidScope` rather than a silent read of the
gateway total. Every record advances a key, a gateway, and an account counter.
`usage.Record` carries the account, deliberately optional so an existing record
stays readable and counts toward none.

## Breaking changes

- `/api/v1/keys/{key_id}/usage/providers` → `/api/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/usage/providers`.
- `usage.Repository.Totals` takes `usage.Scope`; `usage.AggregateAllKeys` is gone.
- `RequireKeyOwnership` is deleted — no route used it any more.

## Evidence

16 new tests, one rewritten. The fail-before case does not compile on `500dccb`
at eight call sites, because no counter population but the key's existed.

`scripts/verify-auth-onboarding.sh` reports `18 passed, 8 failed`, the AON5
target. AON-V17 is re-pointed from `Admin.ListTenants` to `Tenants.List`: the
account plane is its own controller, and the condition names a symbol so the
BYOK plane's `/tenants` prefix cannot turn it green by accident.

Full gate list, `go test ./...`, `-race` on the changed packages, `go vet`,
`make lint` (0 issues), `make build`, and the SDK smoke checks are clean.
Proof: `docs/proof/auth-and-onboarding/aon5.md`.

author: grahamcampbell
body: On PHP 8.6 putenv and getenv throw a ValueError when a name or value contains a null byte, and because the parser preserves null bytes and the repository name guard only rejects the empty string, such a byte reaches the putenv-backed adapter through a loaded file value or a direct set, get or clear call and crashes, uncaught, with safeLoad unable to suppress it. On earlier versions the same input is silently truncated at the null byte, which can quietly unset an unrelated variable. Guarding all three adapter methods against null bytes in the name, and the write against a null byte in the value, makes the operation simply fail, consistently across versions, matching the adapter's existing may-fail contract. This is stacked on #602 and is intended to land before v5.7.0 is tagged.

author: kekzl
body:
Both issues were filed against the same log line, and neither could be answered
from it. This PR makes the line answer them, then records what the two gates are
actually worth.

## The diagnosis named nothing

`spec-ngram: gates failed (temp=... top_k=... rep_pen=... 18 fields ...)` printed
the request and marked none of the fields as the cause, so "why is speculation
off" meant re-deriving `spec_verify_gates_ok_` by hand against a log line.

It reads `refused by 'sampling_not_greedy'` now, from the function that makes the
decision: `spec_verify_gate_refusal_` returns the gate's name or nullptr, and
`spec_verify_gates_ok_` is "is that null". Ten gates, ten names. No behaviour
change; the field dump stays, because a reader usually wants the neighbouring
values too.

## Both gates were measured, and both stay

Qwen3-14B-Q6_K, one RTX 5090, 400-token completions, same prompt, arms
alternated, 3 requests per arm after a warmup.

**#1538, the greedy restriction.** `verify_steps` is read from the server log per
request, so the control proves which arm actually speculated rather than assuming
it:

| arm | tok/s | verify steps in that request |
|---|---|---|
| `temperature: 0.7` (server default) | 157.79, 158.46 | 0 |
| `temperature: 0` (eligible) | 157.61, 157.87 | 6 |

Speculation ON is not faster. Why, from the same log: 18.6 % acceptance, 5.83
tokens emitted per verify, 51-68 ms per verify against a 6.3 ms decode step. A
verify costs eight to ten decode steps and returns under six tokens.

**#1539, the think-block gate.** Relaxed to fire only when a chunk could overshoot
the budget, rather than for the whole block. Two images, arms alternated:

| arm | tok/s | verify steps |
|---|---|---|
| gate as shipped | 162.43, 162.96 | 12 |
| gate relaxed | 157.92, 157.85 | 24 |

Twice the verify steps, 3.0 % less throughput. That code is in no commit: it was
written, tested (6 CPU tests on the new predicate), built, measured and dropped.

Relaxing that gate alone would also have been incoherent: the acceptance loop
breaks on `in_think_block` too, so a relaxed gate without a matching loop change
accepts one token per chunk, which is worse than refusing. Both were relaxed for
the measurement.

Recorded in `docs/DESIGN_DECISIONS.md` next to the existing speculation entry,
which already said the economics are per-model.

## A measurement that was wrong first

The first #1539 A/B read 157.67 / 157.67 / 157.93 / 157.81, four arms within
0.2 %, which looks like "no effect". It was one effect: port 8099 still held the
previous container, every `docker run -d` failed, and all four arms hit the same
stale server. The failure was invisible because the start was redirected to
/dev/null.

The harness now refuses to measure a container it did not start:
`docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}'` has to match the image asked for, and the
start is no longer silenced. The real numbers are the table above.

## Gates

```
== perf vs baseline ==
  pin: 2026-07-26T01:48:33Z (28 days old), model Qwen3-8B-Q8_0.gguf
  perf gate: median of 3 independent runs (spread 0.13%)
  decode  tg128 =  285.38 tok/s  (baseline  287.19, delta -0.63%)
  prefill pp512 = 12553.28 tok/s  (baseline 12406.87, delta 1.18%)
  GPU during bench: sm=2865MHz(med) mem=13801MHz(med) power=500W(max) n=13
PASS decode within 8% threshold
PASS prefill within 8% threshold
  prefill pp4096 = 15490.84 tok/s  (baseline 15324.70, delta 1.08%, FA2)
PASS long-ctx prefill (pp4096/FA2) within 8% threshold

== peak VRAM vs baseline ==
  own peak VRAM = 20718 MiB  (baseline 20716, delta 0.01%)
PASS peak VRAM within 10% of baseline

== graphs ON vs OFF decode gate ==
  graphs OFF tg256 =  186.49 tok/s
  graphs ON  tg256 =  454.48 tok/s   (2.44x, threshold 1.3x)
PASS graphs ON delivers ≥1.3x decode speedup

== smoke prompts (degeneration check) ==
PASS Qwen3-4B Q8_0 (dense) (distinct=11, tokens=11, max-run=1, max-3gram=1, contains 'Paris')

=== verify fast: OK === (started 00:36:07Z, ended 00:36:46Z)
```

Qwen3-8B-Q8_0 on one RTX 5090, median of 3 processes. `filesize_thresholds.toml`
re-pinned for engine_scheduler.cpp, 1995 -> 1997, for the two lines that name
the gate.

Not in here: speculative sampling for temperature > 0 (accept with min(1, p/q),
resample from the corrected distribution). That is the feature #1538 would need,
and the first table is what it would currently buy on this model.

author: cirwel
body:
## Summary
- `migrate-openai-gov-proxy.sh` did `bootout` then immediately `bootstrap` under the same LaunchAgent label. `bootout` returns before launchd finishes tearing the job out of the domain — `launchctl print` still reported `state = SIGTERMed` a full second later in live testing — so the immediate `bootstrap` raced the teardown and launchd answered `Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error`. The script correctly detected the missing listener and rolled back, so every real invocation of this migration silently no-op'd back to the dev-checkout config (this is why `cirwel update` kept reporting `openai-gov-proxy` BEHIND/failed instead of ever advancing it).
- Same root cause `deploy-orchestrator.sh` already documents ("the FIRST bootstrap often fails with an I/O error leaving the service DOWN") and works around with a blind `sleep 2` + retry. This fix instead polls (reusing the existing `deploy_lib_poll` helper) until the job is actually gone before bootstrapping, both on the primary reload path and the rollback-recovery path.

## Test plan
- [x] `bash -n scripts/ops/migrate-openai-gov-proxy.sh`
- [x] `scripts/ops/migrate-openai-gov-proxy.sh --dry-run` against the now-migrated live proxy — reports `OK — already runs from $DEPLOY`
- [x] `./scripts/dev/test-cache.sh --staged` — 13858 passed, 33 skipped, 83.44% coverage
- [x] Manually reproduced the race live (instrumented bootout/bootstrap), confirmed teardown completes in ~2s and the wait-then-bootstrap sequence succeeds; openai-gov-proxy is now running from `~/projects/unitares-host-adapter-deploy` and `cirwel status` reports it `CURRENT`

author: crank-git
body:
## Summary

- Adds `POST /api/policy/{id}/sections`, which parses the request body's `document`
  field through `internal/policy.Document` and returns every named section (per
  FR-model-2), plus a list of opaque top-level keys. A parse failure returns HTTP 400
  and the line and the column, per FR-model-4.
- Adds `POST /api/policy/{id}/sections/edit`, which applies one `add`, `replace`, or
  `remove` to a named section through `AddEntry`, `ReplaceEntry`, and `RemoveEntry`,
  then serializes the result with `Bytes`. Every request field validates before the
  route changes anything.
- Adds the Visual/Text `role="tab"` toggle to `internal/ui/static/policy.js`. Selecting
  Text switches the view and sends no request. Selecting Visual sends the staged text
  to `/sections`; a parse failure keeps the Visual control present but disabled and
  states the error inline (FR-vacl-2). Both editors share one staged string, so a
  toggle to Text after a visual edit shows every other line unchanged, and a toggle to
  Visual after a text edit re-parses and re-renders the current text (FR-vacl-3).

**Note on scope:** Epic 11 (#308) built typed read accessors (`Groups`, `ACLs`, `SSH`,
`AutoApprovers`) for four of the twelve sections FR-model-2 names, not all twelve. To
keep the sections route's response contract exactly as the plan documents (every
section the sibling issues #315-#319 depend on), this PR adds one exported method to
`internal/policy/document.go`, `RawSections`, and reads the eight remaining sections
(`hosts`, `tagOwners`, `ipsets`, `grants`, `nodeAttrs`, `postures`, `tests`,
`sshTests`) from the raw top-level key. `RawSections` reuses the existing
clone-then-minimize pattern that the unexported `sectionRaw` already used, so it adds
no new mutation risk to the byte-preservation guarantee.

This issue builds the toggle shell and the parse-on-toggle wiring alone, per its "Out
of scope" section. The visual editor draws a count per section (Groups, Hosts, Tag
owners, IP sets, Rules) and the list of opaque keys until #315 to #317 build the
matrix, the rule list, and the named-set editors.

## Test plan

- [x] TDD: `TestRawSections*` (internal/policy), `TestPolicySections*` and
      `TestPolicySectionsEdit*` (internal/api) were written failing, then made to pass.
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` (cross-compiled to `linux/arm64`, since the
      daemon package does not build on macOS — this is a pre-existing repo condition)
- [x] `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- [x] `go test ./internal/api/...` and `go test ./internal/policy/...` — cross-compiled
      and run on an Orin Linux test box (`brain`), full suite green (one unrelated,
      pre-existing failure in `headscale_test.go` when run as a standalone binary with
      no source tree present did not reproduce when run as part of the full suite; not
      touched by this change).
- [x] `node --test internal/ui/jstest/*.test.mjs`: 261 of 261 pass (87 in
      `policy.test.mjs`, up from 71), above `minimumConsoleJavaScriptTests` (226).
- [x] `bash scripts/check-hygiene.sh` passes.

author: grahamcampbell
body: The value parser rebuilt an immutable value object once per lexer token, copying the whole accumulated string and recomputing its length each time, which is quadratic in the length of a value composed of many small tokens, so a single call to the public parse method on an adversarial value takes seconds. This accumulates the characters and variable offsets directly and builds the value once, removing the repeated immutable value and prefix reconstruction and substantially reducing allocations and copying. Parsing a single entry whose 16MB double-quoted value contains an escaped dollar, which forces the chunked lexer path, drops from 12.4s to 75ms on PHP 8.4, and an unquoted value of 80,000 inline variable markers drops from 9.2s to 101ms, with measured scaling exponents of about 1.0 against 1.9 before; the same shapes measure linear on PHP 7.2, 7.4, 8.2 and 8.3, and output is byte-identical over a 211,158-input differential corpus. This is stacked on #603.

author: iandees
body:
Adds a spider for Cyca Parking (サイカパーキング), a Japanese bicycle/motorcycle parking operator (closes #9042).

Data source is the operator's own store-finder site, charinavi72.jp. Its sitemap lists ~411 detail pages, each of which embeds a rich JSON blob (via a `mapsinitialize(...)` JS call) containing id, name, address, lat/lon, phone, business hours, and bicycle/motorcycle capability flags for the parking lot plus its nearby neighbours; the spider parses out just the entry matching the current page's parking id. One item is yielded per parking, plus an additional motorcycle item for lots that also offer motorcycle parking (identified via the `charge_mc`/`contract_mc_*` fields), following the same one-item-per-type pattern used in `tobu_park_jp.py`.

A national toll-free ("0120") hotline is shared across roughly half of listed phone numbers, so it's nulled out as non-branch-specific rather than treated as each location's own number. Opening hours are only set for the common "24時間" (24-hour) case; other free-text hour formats are left blank rather than force-parsed.

Verified locally: 568 items (323 `amenity=bicycle_parking`, 245 `amenity=motorcycle_parking`), all with coordinates inside Japan's bounding box, addresses built from prefecture+city+street, and no leaked generic phone numbers.

author: ryancinsight
body:
Replaces #599, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch was deleted on merge of #597. Same content, rebased onto main as a single commit.

## What lands

`ivp_absorbing_2d`: the lossless 2-D reference case with power-law absorption switched on (`40 dB/(MHz^1.5 cm)`, `y = 1.5`) and **nothing else changed**, so the pair isolates the absorption model.

- kwavers matches the absorbing reference — **8.10e-3 relative L2, r = 0.999999924**
- the absorbing reference separates from the lossless one by **0.53** relative L2

The second assertion is the point. Agreement alone cannot distinguish a correct absorption model from an absent one: a solver ignoring `PowerLaw` would produce the lossless field, and at a realistic tissue coefficient that field would still sit inside the parity bound. Hence the deliberately extreme coefficient — at tissue values this path attenuates by under 1%, inside the comparison's noise; at 40 it attenuates by a third. Both codes receive the identical value.

The bound is `2e-2` rather than the lossless `1e-3`, because the residual is not the storage-precision floor: the two codes discretize the fractional-Laplacian operator and its Kramers-Kronig dispersion partner `η tan(πy/2)` differently, and that difference does not shrink with resolution.

## The defect this case exposed

It first measured `r = 0.836` — the kwavers absorbing field was **bit-identical to its lossless run** and **insensitive to `alpha_coeff` at any magnitude** (`40` and `4000` gave the same output to six digits).

`initialize_absorption_operators` preferred the medium's coefficient and fell back to the config's only when the medium reported exactly zero; `HomogeneousMedium::new` seeds water's value, which is never zero. The fix is a separate PR in this series (ADR 120), because the precedence is a design decision rather than a typo.

## Verification

```
cargo nextest run -p kwavers --test kwave_reference_parity   5 passed
scripts/lockfile.py --check   89 first-party git sources, resolves under --locked
```

The lockfile is regenerated by the repository's own tool from outside the stack overlay — the check that #597's series originally failed CI on.

## High-level PR Summary
This PR adds a new k-Wave reference test case (`ivp_absorbing_2d`) to validate the power-law absorption model in the kwavers pseudospectral solver. The test uses an extreme absorption coefficient (40 dB/(MHz^1.5 cm)) to ensure the absorbing field separates measurably from the lossless baseline, proving the absorption model actually runs rather than being silently absent. The implementation achieves r = 0.999999924 agreement with k-Wave while separating from the lossless field by 0.53 relative L2. This validation work exposed a configuration precedence issue (documented in `KW-ABSORPTION-CONFIG-PRECEDENCE`) where `PSTDConfig::absorption_mode`'s coefficient was unreachable when using `HomogeneousMedium`, requiring absorption to be set directly on the medium instead.

author: floriankraemer
body:
Tasks **F1-1 through F1-4**: `selection`, `transaction` and `line_ops` in `editor-core`. Pure Rust, no bridge, no C++, no `edit-ops` — those depend on this landing first.

## The types

| Type | What it owns |
|---|---|
| `Caret { anchor, head }` | One caret over **byte** offsets. `anchor == head` is a cursor, otherwise a selection, and the direction is kept so Shift+Arrow shrinks from the end the user grew from. |
| `SelectionSet` | One or more carets with a designated primary, permanently sorted and merged. Never empty. |
| `Transaction { edits: Vec<TextEdit> }` | One user-visible change, however many carets made it. Applied descending, all-or-nothing. |
| `map_carets(&SelectionSet, &Transaction)` | Where the carets land once their own edit has been applied. |
| `line_ops::{duplicate, move_up, move_down, delete, join}` | Multi-caret line operations, one transaction each. |

## The normalisation rule

On **every** mutation the set is sorted by position and any carets that overlap *or touch* are merged; two carets on one offset become one. It runs **before** an edit is computed, never after — carets left sitting on one offset produce two edits at that offset, which is the doubled character every multi-caret bug report turns out to be. A merged caret keeps the direction of the earliest caret in the merge.

## Decisions made explicit

- **Whole-word (Ctrl+D)** — the search is whole-word exactly when the primary selection is a whole word *in situ*, i.e. bounded by non-word characters in the text. Selecting `value` skips `values`; selecting the `alu` inside `value` matches substrings, which is the only reading under which a deliberate partial selection does anything at all. Stateless, so it survives the caret set being rebuilt at the seam.
- **Ragged column selection** — **clipped, not padded**. A line shorter than the requested column contributes a caret at its end; a line shorter than both contributes an empty caret there, and it is kept rather than dropped so typing into a column block still types on every line the user covered. Padding would mean writing spaces into lines that were only dragged across, and a selection must not change text before an edit is even asked for. Columns are visual: a tab counts as the distance to the next tab stop, and a column landing inside a tab snaps past it rather than splitting it.
- **The ceiling is 1024 carets**, stated in the module docs and enforced by `SelectionSet::from_carets`, `add_caret` and `column_block`. Over it, the operation is **refused** with `SelectionError::TooManyCarets` and the set is left exactly as it was. Truncating would hide the refusal somewhere the user only finds by counting.
- **Caret mapping** — a caret rides to the end of what was typed at it; a caret whose selection was replaced collapses after the replacement; a caret swallowed by another caret's deletion collapses onto that deletion's start, where normalisation merges it away instead of leaving it pointing into text that no longer exists.
- **Line-op edges** — first line up, last line down and last line join are no-ops rather than panics; the phantom line a trailing newline implies is a caret position, not something to swap with; deleting an unterminated last line takes the newline in front of it.

## Why every entry point takes `&str`

`Document`'s rope is populated on open and only updated by `save_tab`, which pulls the full text *out of* the Qt widget — it is one save behind at all times. A signature taking `&Document` would compute every caret operation against stale text. This mirrors `search::find_matches(text, …)` and `replacements(text, …)`, which are already stateless for exactly this reason.

Offsets are **bytes** internally (tree-sitter is byte-addressed and F1-5 onward needs that); the UTF-16 seam conversion stays in `editor_core::offsets`, which gains the line geometry (`line_starts`, `line_of`, `line_range`) the caret work needs so it is not reimplemented per module. No second converter.

## Application discipline

`Transaction::apply` validates every edit (bounds, char boundary, ordering) **before** writing anything, then applies last-first so earlier offsets stay valid. Same shape as `lsp_core::workspace_edit::apply_to_text` — the same discipline in two places should look the same to a reader.

## Tests

45 new tests in-file, all Qt-free, including the cases that actually matter: three carets one insert is one transaction and the carets land correctly; adjacent carets backspacing delete two different characters instead of one twice; two carets at one offset collapse; overlapping selections merge before the edit; a caret inside a deleted range is dropped; edits apply right-to-left; column selection over ragged lines, over a tab and across a 4-byte character; next-occurrence wraps and skips the caret it started from; line ops with three carets are one transaction; the first/last-line no-ops; multi-byte duplicate/delete/join land on char boundaries; and the ceiling refusing rather than truncating.

`cargo test --workspace` green; `cargo tree -p editor-core -e normal | grep -i qt` empty.

## One thing to know

`make lint`'s file-size gate is **red on `main` already**, independent of this branch: `bridge.rs` is 9388 lines against a 9346 baseline and `main_window.cpp` 4393 against 4263 — both baselines were measured while the branches that grew those files were still in flight. Clippy and rustfmt are clean. Re-ratcheting the two numbers is a one-line change but it raises a quality gate, so it is left for a deliberate decision rather than smuggled into this PR.

author: jmeyer1980
body:
Closes #77.

```
- You cast Lake-town Mariners
- You cast Long Lake Nuisance
- Gone Fishing triggers
```

`Gone Fishing` is the Adventure half of `Lake-town Mariners`. Nothing about it triggered.
That line is an **Island's mana ability**, wearing the name of the
`GameObjectType_Adventure` companion object whose instance id it inherited four messages
earlier:

```
L195  inst=269  type=Adventure  zone=27 (Stack)  grp=103417  Gone Fishing
L199  AbilityInstanceCreated  affector=218 (Island)  affected=[269]
```

Nothing ever re-describes 269, so the tracker keeps answering with the Adventure's name.

## Wider than the issue said, and measured

The issue framed this as an Adventure problem. Counting what the affected id of every
`AbilityInstanceCreated` in the archive already was:

| the id was… | count | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| never described | 31,250 | ordinary |
| already an Ability | 15,260 | ordinary |
| a Card | 35 | **reuse** |
| a Token | 7 | **reuse** |
| an Adventure | 6 | **reuse** |
| a RevealedCard | 1 | **reuse** |

The give-away in the output is the **missing possessive**. A named ability reads
`Long Lake Nuisance's ability triggers`, built from its `objectSourceGrpId`; a stale one
reads as a card's own bare name.

## The fix

An `AbilityInstanceCreated` must be pointing at an ability. When it is pointing at
something else, the name is refused and the existing placeholder check drops the line —
which is already what this code does for an ability it cannot name. An id with no object
behind it is untouched: that is the ordinary case and is already dropped by the same check.

Every one traced is a land's mana ability, and beats density does not narrate mana at all,
so dropping is both the honest answer and the one the reader wanted.

## Archive diff

767 matches rendered and diffed line by line against the shipped build:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| transcripts changed | **4** |
| lines removed | **6** |
| lines added | **0** |
| lines reworded | **0** |

`Gone Fishing` ×3, `Spew Flame`, `Seek the Heart`, `Ardenvale Fealty` — every
Adventure-named trigger line in the archive, and nothing else moved.

## Rejected

Naming the ability after its affector instead. `AbilityInstanceCreated` runs source → new
ability, so the affector really is the source and it would read `Island's ability
triggers`. But the same fallback would then apply to all 31,250 currently-unnameable
ability instances, narrating every mana ability in the archive. Far bigger than the defect.

## Not this, and not a defect

Four possessive-less trigger lines survive — `Final Vengeance triggers`, `Iron Man,
Futurist Paragon triggers`, `Dori, Bearer of Friends triggers`, `Fell triggers`. I traced
them expecting the same cause and it is not: no `AbilityInstanceCreated` reuse is involved.
The ability object carries its own name locId, so `NameOf` returns the bare card name
rather than composing `X's ability`. The ability really does belong to that card, so
nothing false is being said — it is a phrasing inconsistency, not a misattribution. One of
the four also sits directly under a `part of this turn is missing` marker, where the
ability's description was in the update Arena summarised away.

## Tests

One new test, written first and watched fail with `Expected: not some item equal to
"Lightning Bolt" / But was: < "Lightning Bolt" >`. 671 pass, 0 fail, Debug and Release.

author: actuallydan
body:
Custom emoji now render as inline images **while you type**. Picking `:partyparrot:` from the picker used to drop 70 characters of `<:partyparrot:d7da9055…>` into the composer; it now shows the parrot, and the message still puts the exact same token on the wire. Sent messages already rendered correctly (`Emoji/EmojiText`) — this was only ever an input problem. ## The approach, and why **A hand-rolled `contentEditable` over a plain-string model. No editor dependency.** The key decision is that the value stays **one plain string with integer offsets**, exactly as before. The DOM is a *projection* of that string (`ui/richInputModel.ts`), read back into it after every edit. So mentions, `:shortcode:` completion, drafts, the `@all` hint, the history hand-off and the send path all still operate on `(text, caret)` — none of them learned a document model, and the diff to `ChatInput` is mechanical rather than a rewrite. That is what makes the "smallest correct thing" a hand-rolled editor here rather than a framework. Lexical (~25–30 kB gzip) or Slate (~60 kB) would each have meant porting all of the above onto a foreign editor state for a document model with exactly one node type. Given the model stays a string, what remains is a projection, a serializer, and a bidirectional offset↔DOM-position mapping — and the mapping is not hand-rolled twice: `offsetOf` is implemented as `serialize(range.cloneContents()).length`, so it *cannot* drift from the serializer, because it is the serializer. **Bundle impact (measured, `vite build` before/after):** main chunk +7.00 kB raw / **+2.29 kB gzip**; CSS +0.70 kB raw / +0.10 kB gzip. No new dependency, no change to code-splitting — `emojiData.ts` stays behind its lazy chunk exactly as #874 requires. **The children are built imperatively, not by React.** React reconciliation of a `contentEditable`'s children destroys the caret and there is no way to opt out. The element renders empty and the component owns everything inside it. The DOM is rebuilt *only* when the value disagrees with what was last serialized out of it, so ordinary typing rebuilds nothing and IME composition and the caret survive; an external change (picker insert, `:joy:` substitution, draft switch, send-clear) does disagree and is rebuilt with the caret restored from a model offset. ## Serialization is the contract Byte-identical to what the textarea produced, because `parse_emoji_tokens` reads it: - a text node contributes its characters, verbatim; - an element contributes its `data-emoji-token`, and **only when that attribute parses as a token** — never its rendered contents, so a still-loading image, a resolved one and the `:shortcode:` fallback all serialize the same, and a forged attribute is read as ordinary markup; - the ghost contributes nothing; - a `
` in last position is an editing host's filler and contributes nothing; an inner one is a newline. No branch emits an element's markup, so `<`, `>` and `&` reach the wire only by having been typed. Paste is always `preventDefault`ed and reads **`text/plain` only** — the `text/html` flavour is never parsed, which is the cheapest sanitizer there is. Copy/cut are written too, serializing the selection with the same walker, so token → node → token round-trips through the clipboard as well as through the editor. `<:oops:>` stays literal characters throughout. ## The ghost moved inside the editable `ui/InlineGhost` is **deleted**. It was an absolutely-positioned invisible mirror of the textarea and worked only because it rendered identical text; an emoji image of a different width breaks the line-wrapping it depends on, which is exactly why the overlay approach is a dead end here. The completion is now a `contenteditable=false` span appended after the caret. That is not a workaround — the caller only ever offers a ghost with the caret at end-of-value (the deliberate fish / zsh-autosuggestions rule), so a trailing node lands precisely where the caret is with no measurement and no mirror at all. Both tracks keep their own testids (`mention-ghost`, `emoji-ghost`) and Tab still accepts. Nothing was dropped. ## Two real bugs the verification caught 1. **A second pick from the still-open picker landed *before* the first.** A textarea keeps `selectionStart` across a blur; a contentEditable does not, so the input remembers its last in-element selection — but `applySelection` was leaving that memory at the pre-insertion offset, because the `selectionchange` it fires is async and the picker click moved focus first. Caught by the existing `emoji.spec.ts` caret test. 2. **ArrowUp stopped handing off to the message log.** `handleKeyDown` was reading the caret from React state fed by the async `selectionchange`, so two arrow keys in quick succession judged the second against the first one's stale offset. Fixed by exposing `selection()` on the handle and reading the DOM synchronously — the exact semantics `selectionStart` had. Caught by `message-nav.spec.ts`. Both are the kind of thing that only shows up under real keystrokes, which is the argument for the verification below. ## Tested vs. reasoned about **Ran, green:** - `pnpm --filter frontend exec tsc` — clean. - `frontend/tests/` — 106 pass, including 15 new ones (`rich-input-model.test.ts`): round-trip over 15 shapes, the near-token, the forged-attribute case, the ghost, the `
` filler rule, atomic-delete boundaries, and the paste rules (including an assertion that `text/html` is *never read*). DOM-free, per this repo's unit-tier convention. - **Full Playwright suite: 239 passed.** The only 2 failures are `bookmarks.spec.ts` "the copied state is actually painted" — **confirmed pre-existing** by running that spec at the base commit (7ee85f43) and seeing it fail identically. Unrelated to the composer. - A temporary probe spec (written, run, deleted) exercised, all green: paste of arbitrary rich HTML (nothing injected, DOM stays escaped text); paste of a raw token → inline image; a near-token pasted alongside stays literal; Shift+Enter → `\n` in a clean text node, Enter sends; arrows step over an emoji in one press; select-all + Backspace removes it whole; **drafts round-trip across two channel switches with the emoji intact**; placeholder shows/hides; auto-grow measured at 30 → 97.5 → 135px, clamping at 9rem and scrolling past it; copy of a selection containing an emoji yields the token; a send puts the exact wire text through, rendering the emoji as an image and `<:oops:>` as text; **a pasted image becomes an attachment, leaves the text untouched, and returns focus to the composer**. - `vite build` before and after, for the bundle numbers above. **Reasoned about, not executed:** - **WebKit and Gecko.** Everything above ran in Chromium — that is what this repo's Playwright tier is. The shipping app is a Tauri webview (WebKit on macOS/Linux). Backspace/forward-delete beside an emoji are decided against the model precisely so engine differences there do not matter, and serialization tolerates whatever markup an engine produces; but arrow-stepping and drag-selection over the atom are still the engine's own behaviour, which is standard `contenteditable=false` handling and not verified on WebKit here. - **IME composition.** The design reason it should hold is stated above (typing never re-projects, because value and DOM already agree). I did not drive an IME. - **The five WebDriver scenarios** (`two-client*.js`, `emoji-picker.js`). `setValue` only works on form controls, so they now call a new `h.setComposerText`, which clicks in, types, and waits for `data-value` to catch up. Those run against the real Tauri app in CI and I could not run them locally. ## Other notes - `data-value` mirrors the serialized wire text onto the element, because a contentEditable has no `.value` for Playwright's `toHaveValue`. The composer assertions in `emoji.spec.ts`, `mentions.spec.js` and `message-nav.spec.ts` now read it. It is also just useful in devtools. - `r

author: leanderriefel
body:
Follow-up to #250. Two commits, in the order the problem was actually understood.

## 1. Reload only on a confirmed deployment change

#250 reloaded on *any* chunk load failure behind a 30s window. That was a heuristic with the wrong failure mode: a genuine failure — dropped network, a truly broken deployment — cost the user a full reload and their in-flight state, only to land on the same error screen.

The build now emits its id to `/assets/build-id.txt` and bakes the same value into the client bundle. A tab that hits a chunk failure asks what the deployment is currently serving and compares, and reloads only when the two actually differ. A genuine failure goes straight to the error screen with no reload.

The guard that matters: an unreadable answer counts as *unknown*, not stale. A missing asset falls through to the SPA shell, so a naive text comparison would read that HTML as a new deployment and reload on exactly the genuine failures this leaves alone. The check requires `ok` plus `text/plain`. That also makes the dev server, which emits no build id file, a no-op.

`sessionStorage` records the build id we last reloaded *for*, so each deployment earns at most one reload — no time window.

## 2. Serve superseded chunks from an R2 archive

The reload above is still a reload. This removes the failure instead of recovering from it.

Every release uploads `apps/web/dist/client/assets` to a `WebAssetArchive` R2 bucket, and the Worker serves from that archive when the live manifest misses. **A tab opened before a release keeps loading untouched — no error, no reload** — and picks up the new build on its next navigation. Hashed filenames are content addressed, so an archived object is always byte-for-byte the file that was asked for.

Wiring:

- `sst.cloudflare.Bucket("WebAssetArchive")` linked to the Web worker, giving a native R2 binding rather than an S3 client in the Worker bundle.
- A request middleware in `start.ts` intercepts `GET /assets/*`. It is only ever reached on a miss: assets still in the manifest never invoke the Worker. It sits before the site password gate because `/assets/` is already public.
- `pnpm run archive:web-assets` after `sst deploy`, reading the bucket name from the stack outputs rather than guessing at a name. It uploads with explicit content types — an archived chunk without one would reproduce the exact failure this prevents, so an unrecognised extension fails the deploy rather than being silently skipped.
- The archive is never pruned by a deploy, since older tabs are reading from it.

Every failure path falls through to current behaviour: a missing binding, a missing object, or an R2 error all defer to the request chain rather than failing the request.

## What this does not cover

Retention fixes **loading**, not **protocol**. An old client calling a server function whose shape has changed is a separate compatibility boundary, handled by expand/contract like any other. The build id check from the first commit stays as the backstop for that and for anything older than the retention window. The two compose: retention handles the common case invisibly, detection catches the rest.

## Verification

- Clean build with an injected build id: `/assets/build-id.txt` contains it and the same value is baked into the entry chunk.
- `cloudflare:workers` is externalized for the build (it is supplied by the Workers runtime); the client bundle contains **zero** references to it, and the archive module appears only in `dist/server`.
- `vp check --fix` clean across 634 files; `vp test` green (574 tests, 84 files); `check:bundles` passes for the Cloudflare handlers.
- 11 focused tests across the two mechanisms, including SPA-shell-as-unknown, R2 errors falling through, and the content type surviving into the response.

Not verified against a real deploy — the retention path only becomes observable on the *second* consecutive release, since the first one is what populates the archive. Worth watching the first two deploys after this merges.

body:
The tournament release.

Every tournament now runs on a day spine counted from its start date. Days hold their matches, rest days slot in between, shifts move whole days and push a notification to the followers unless the admin opts out, and the schedule generator lays the rounds onto free days. The live U18 adopts the model on first touch.

Tournaments carry a sport profile. Football keeps the full apparatus while board and pairs tournaments, الشطرنج والدامة والمارياس وأشباهها, show results only, with presets at creation and a settings dialog for existing ones.

Discipline is a real engine. A red card or accumulated yellows propose a suspension, an admin approves, dismisses or lifts from the الانضباط tab, match bans serve themselves down as results land, and a banned player drops out of every picker and wears موقوف on the rosters and the public page. The card rules per tournament are editable.

Results are recorded as events. Goals are added like cards, with جزاء and عكسي kinds, a مجهول scorer when nobody remembers, extra time, and per kick shootouts, and the score computes itself. Board matches keep the two number form.

Getting there is shorter. The admin home lists مباريات اليوم, tournament rows on the index open the workspace directly, the workspace lands on the matches, and one panel records a whole match. The two workspaces share one shell and one set of standings tables.

The public side lists teams one per row and the activity lists carry standing chips, a countdown before the start, a pulse while running, and a quiet انتهى after.

author: kwn00
body:
Makes the gap analysis run off mechanical inputs instead of prose judgment, and corrects two places where the skill documented capabilities the tools do not have.

The skill's stated value is the `Needs Answer` section. Before this PR only § 1 of the checklist had a mechanical input (`states_defined`); § 2–§ 9 had none, so whether a section got applied depended on re-reading the prose per screen. Long batches dropped whole sections silently.

## Changes

**Checklist selection is now a lookup (Step 3 → Step 4)**
- New `traits` field with a fixed vocabulary: `list`, `form`, `submit`, `money`, `permission`, `external`
- `references/gap-checklist.md` gains a section↔trait table; each section header names what selects it
- Step 4 selects sections from `states_defined` and `traits` rather than judging relevance. § 4 and § 5 apply to every screen; § 8 applies once per feature

**Component variants count as defined states**
- Variants moved out of `conditional`, which is now only for elements appearing or vanishing *within* a state
- A variant-drawn `error`/`empty`/`loading` maps onto the fixed vocabulary and goes in `states_defined`, with the original name kept in `states_other`. Previously it landed in `conditional` and Step 4 reported the state as missing — sending the user to ask a question the file already answered
- New `states_unconfirmed` for a state suspected from a component name but not verified on the screen. It is printed on neither the **States defined** nor the **States not defined** line; it routes to `Needs Answer` and Extraction notes, because both lines assert something a suspicion does not support

**Needs Answer deduplication**
- One question, one entry, with the screens listed together — 8 screens × 9 sections otherwise produces the same question 8 times
- Merge only questions with the same answer, so a screen-specific failure is not collapsed into a generic one
- Aim for ~7 🔴 per output file, with an explicit rule against demoting a real blocker to hit the number

**Prototype links matched to what the tools return**
- `reactions`/`transitionNodeID` live on the interactive node, so nothing Step 1 fetched contains them and `depth=2` does not reach them. Signal 3 never fired by accident
- Two retrieval routes documented: `flowStartingPoints` on the page node (cheap), then per-frame `reactions` on a few suspected frames
- Both are REST, so on the MCP-only route signal 3 is unavailable rather than expensive — stated, so no calls are spent hunting for it

**Step 1 page selection**
- Settle the page before either route, and ask when several pages are plausible candidates for one feature (`Mobile`/`Desktop`, `v1`/`v2`)
- Non-blocking fallback: with nobody available to answer the scope question, take the largest coherent group and record the choice in Extraction notes rather than halting

**Docs**
- `example-spec.md` now demonstrates the dedupe rule and an unconfirmed-variant question, and states that SKILL.md holds the canonical template
- § 3 narrowed to `traits: form`; the duplicate-submission questions consolidated into § 7, so a confirm-and-go screen no longer pulls in validation and keyboard-type questions

## Review notes

Commit 1 introduced a contradiction that commits 2–4 fix: "record an unconfirmed state in `states_other`" collided with "`states_other` collapses into the **States defined** line", which would have printed a guess as a fact. That is the mirror image of the false-blocker bug this PR set out to remove, and `states_unconfirmed` exists because of it.

Not included: splitting the ~80 lines of MCP/REST access detail into `references/`. The node-id hyphen rule and the branch-URL rule live in that block and are among the highest-value lines in the file; moving them behind a conditional read risks them going unread. Worth doing as a narrower split later.

author: langdy05
body:
Two commits. The PWA is the main one; the lesson-creation guide is a docs commit that was on this branch and hadn't been merged yet.

## Make REAN an installable PWA

Students can add REAN to the home screen and open it like a native app, and the shell loads on a flaky or dropped connection — the common case for much of the audience.

**Added**
- `public/manifest.webmanifest` — standalone display, teal theme, name + icons, so the browser offers "Add to Home Screen".
- `public/icons/` — 192, 512, maskable 512, apple-touch, favicon, generated to match the header's teal book glyph.
- `public/sw.js` — a deliberately minimal service worker: precaches the app shell, caches hashed build assets at runtime (stale-while-revalidate), network-first for navigations so the newest build wins when online.
- `index.html` — manifest link and iOS meta tags.

**The 405 bug cannot recur.** That regression came from a worker intercepting API calls, which is why the old code *unregistered* all workers on boot. This worker only ever handles **same-origin GET** requests. Every cross-origin call (Supabase, the Gemini edge function, Google Fonts) and every non-GET (submissions, points, AI) returns early and hits the network as if no worker existed. The unregister block is replaced by `services/registerServiceWorker.ts` (registers on load, secure-origin only, never throws).

**Verified in Chromium against the production build:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Manifest linked & valid | ✅ |
| Service worker reaches `active` | ✅ |
| Cross-origin POST reaches network **untouched** | ✅ (no interception — the 405 proof) |
| Page errors | 0 |
| App shell renders **after going offline** | ✅ |

## Add a guide for creating lessons

`docs/creating-lessons.md` — the authoring workflow for teachers: two-level structure, the one-module-one-task rule, every field with its real limit, LaTeX for formulas, the AI helpers, and a worked example. Linked from `docs/README.md`. (Was written earlier; it just never got merged.)

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run format:check` passes
- [x] `npm run lint` passes

- [x] `npm run build` succeeds; manifest, sw.js and all icons emitted to `dist`

- [ ] Installed app opens standalone (no browser bar) with the book icon

Remember this repo's live site follows the **`Production`** branch, not `main`. After this merges to `main`, `Production` needs updating too, or fix it permanently by pointing Cloudflare's Production branch at `main`.

author: mikeygabmiller
body:
The beacon counted page loads. It never said that somebody read the pricing section, pushed "See All Services", got to step 3 of the quote form and left at 86% down — which is the part worth knowing.

## What `site-stats.js` now records

- **Sections seen** — counted once half of one has been on screen
- **Buttons pushed** — labelled with the button's own visible text
- **Tap-to-call / tap-to-text** — called out by name, because on this site those are the most valuable things anyone does
- **Scroll depth and time on page** — sent when they leave
- **Quote form step reached**, and the booking itself, via `window.MDTrack`

All auto-instrumented — sections found by `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `id` or heading; buttons by their own text — so all thirty-odd pages are covered without editing one of them. Add `data-track="Some name"` to anything whose automatic label reads badly.

## Batched, not chatty

Events queue and go out together over `sendBeacon` as `text/plain` — no CORS preflight, and it survives the page closing mid-flight. Taps go out in about a second so a tap that navigates away isn't lost; everything else waits ~8s. Someone who taps six things costs one request, not six.

## It cannot break the page

The queue is capped, labels are trimmed, and every path is wrapped in try/catch. A detailing site that won't load because analytics broke is a catastrophe; missing analytics is a Tuesday.

The 1×1 GIF ping is unchanged, so the existing Grow → Website day counters read exactly as before.

## Privacy

The visitor id is a random string in that browser's localStorage. It identifies nobody until the customer fills out the quote or booking form and hands over their number — the form sends the same id with the lead, and that hand-off is the only moment an anonymous path gets a name on it. Clearing site data breaks the link, by design. No cookies, no third party.

## Where it shows up

mikeygabmiller/twillowdashbored#123 (merged) — Analytics → Journey replays each visitor's actions nested under the pages they happened on, and can hand the whole set to Gemini to find the patterns.

## Summary
- Adds a second job, `claude-review`, to `.github/workflows/sdd-sentinel.yml`
- Runs the `code-review` plugin (`anthropics/claude-code-action`) against the PR diff and posts findings as inline comments

sdd-agent-review already gates structure (specs, docs, unpinned deps, secrets) but has no semantic read of the diff. author: byjg
body:
Prepares this component for the **7.0** line (dependency level L1).

## Requirements

`"php": ">=8.3 <8.7"` — PHP 8.3, 8.4, 8.5 and 8.6.

The previous `<8.6` is *exclusive*, so it stopped at 8.5 and excluded PHP 8.6 entirely.

## Toolchain

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| PHPUnit | `^10.5\|^11.5` | `^12.5` |
| Psalm | `^5.9\|^6.13` in `require-dev` | `^6.16` in `tools/psalm/composer.json` |

PHPUnit 13 is deliberately **not** used. It requires PHP `>=8.4.1`, which would break the 8.3 floor, and it pulls `sebastian/diff ^9.0` — which the newest stable Psalm (6.16.1) does not accept. Because `minimum-stability: dev` is set, that combination does not fail; it silently resolves Psalm to an unreleased `6.x-dev` branch head. Pinning PHPUnit to `^12.5` keeps one stable PHPUnit and one stable Psalm across the whole matrix.

Resolved consistently as **PHPUnit 12.5.33 + Psalm 6.16.1 + sebastian/diff 7.0.0**.

## ByJG dependencies

Bumped to `^7.0`. While 7.0 is unreleased these resolve to `7.0.x-dev` from each component's `7.0` branch (`minimum-stability: dev` + `prefer-stable: true`), so the L0 branches must be pushed first — verified resolving on PHP 8.6.

## Psalm moved out of `require-dev`

Psalm enumerates the PHP versions it supports and no published release lists 8.6, so as a dev dependency it made `composer install` fail on the 8.6 build job before any test ran. It now lives in `tools/psalm/composer.json` and is installed only by the Psalm job (PHP 8.5). `composer psalm` bootstraps the tool, so local usage is unchanged.

## Continuous integration

- Build matrix now includes **PHP 8.6**.
- Psalm job moved to **PHP 8.5**. Psalm 6.16.1 declares `~8.1.31 || ~8.2.27 || ~8.3.16 || ~8.4.3 || ~8.5.0` and cannot be installed on 8.6 at all.

## Housekeeping

- `phpunit.xml.dist` → `phpunit.xml`
- 6.x changelogs carried onto the `7.0` branch
- `CHANGELOG-7.0.md` added/updated

## Verification

Tests run locally on **PHP 8.5.9** and **PHP 8.6.0beta1** — both green.

author: grahamcampbell
body: Nested-variable resolution folded across the variable offsets and re-sliced the entire value, prefix included, for every reference, which is costly for a value with many references. This preserves the exact right-to-left resolution order, including the cascade where a resolved inner reference forms an outer one, and rebuilds only the unresolved tail at each step, with markedly fewer string copies. Output is byte-identical whenever the parsed characters and every repository value incorporated during resolution are valid UTF-8, and on PHP 8.2 and earlier it is byte-identical on all input. For malformed bytes on later runtimes the old code re-sliced already-resolved text through mb_substr, which since PHP 8.3 replaces invalid bytes with the configured mbstring substitution character, so a value with several references could return already-substituted text; the new code preserves those bytes in the resolved tail on every runtime, which is what PHP 8.2 and earlier already produced. Resolving a value of 4,000 nested references to 64-byte substitutions drops from 849ms to 67ms on PHP 8.4 and from 2.1s to 135ms on PHP 7.2, with smaller gains on PHP 7.4 and 8.2, and resolution remains quadratic in the number of references, so this is a constant-factor improvement that could still be dropped without affecting the rest of the series. This is stacked on #604.

author: danfiedler-msft
body:
## Summary

This PR pins GitHub Actions to full-length commit SHAs for improved security and reproducibility and adds a 7 day cooldown to Dependabot configuration for GitHub Actions. This work is described in more detail at https://aka.ms/action-pinning.

## Why?

Pinning actions to commit SHAs prevents supply-chain attacks where a tag could be moved to point to malicious code. This is a recommended security best practice per the [GitHub Actions security hardening guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions).

This change mitigates the risk of tag retargeting to malicious code as seen in incidents like the [tj-actions/changed-files action compromise](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/harden-runner-detection-tj-actions-changed-files-action-is-compromised) or [codfish/semantic-release-action compromise](https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/supply-chain-compromise-codfish-semantic-release-action) and improves the integrity and reproducibility of the CI/CD pipeline.

## What changed?

**Action pinning:** Third-party action references in `.github/workflows/` that used mutable tag-based references (e.g., `actions/checkout@v4`) have been updated to full-length commit SHAs with a version comment (e.g., `actions/checkout@<sha> # v4`) using the [pinact](https://github.com/suzuki-shunsuke/pinact) tool. References that were already pinned to a SHA, or that used immutable release tags, were left unchanged.

**Dependabot configuration:** `.github/dependabot.yml` has been updated to ensure a `github-actions` package-ecosystem section is present with a `cooldown` configuration (`default-days: 7`). If the file did not exist, it was created. If a `github-actions` section already existed, only the `cooldown` block was added or its `default-days` value was increased to 7 if it was lower. The 7-day cooldown provides a window for the community to detect and report compromised releases before they are automatically proposed as updates, reducing exposure to supply-chain attacks via newly published malicious versions.

## Is this safe to merge?

Yes. The pinned SHAs correspond to the same commits that the existing tags pointed to. No behavioral changes in action execution are introduced. You can verify the pinned SHA value using the GitHub REST API (e.g., the commit hash for `actions/checkout@v7` can be found in the `sha` property in the JSON response for `GET https://api.github.com/repos/actions/checkout/commits/v7`).

## Additional Information

For more information, please see https://aka.ms/action-pinning

author: arcobaleno64
body:
## What broke

The Stop hook schema accepts only `"approve" | "block"` for `decision`. Letting a stop through means **omitting** the field. Three of the gate's four exits wrote `{"decision":"proceed"}`:

| exit | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| no completed write task | `{ decision: "proceed" }` | `{}` |
| review unavailable (fail-open) | `{ decision: "proceed", systemMessage }` | `{ systemMessage }` |
| clean verdict | `{ decision: "proceed" }` | `{}` |
| `needs-attention` | `{ decision: "block", reason }` | unchanged |

Claude Code rejected the whole payload with `Hook JSON output validation failed — (root): Invalid input` and acted on none of it — including the `systemMessage` the fail-open branch exists specifically to make visible. So on those three paths the gate has never delivered anything. The `block` path uses a legal value, was not reached in the observed failure, and is unverified either way.

Observed live at the end of a turn in this repo, on the 0.22.2 install cache.

## Why the tests did not catch it

Both stop-gate tests asserted `decision.decision === "proceed"` — read straight off the implementation. They pinned the value the hook happened to write, not the contract it has to satisfy, so they stayed green while the output was being thrown away downstream. They now assert that no `decision` key is present at all.

Any hook test in this repo that checks stdout without checking it against the published schema has the same blind spot.

## Verification

- `node --test tests/runtime.test.mjs` — 97 tests, 91 pass, 0 fail, 6 skipped.
- Mutation: restoring `decision: "proceed"` at the no-write-task exit turns `stop-gate proceeds without a warning when enabled but no write task completed` red. Restored.

## Note

The same schema rule was already discovered and fixed once, in `~/.claude/hooks/unreviewed-changes-stop-hook.mjs`, which carries a comment spelling it out. It did not reach the plugin. A comment above `emitDecision` now states it here too.

Takes effect only after a version bump — the running copy is the install cache.

author: grahamcampbell
body: Byte order marks are stripped when reading .env files but not when content is passed to the string parser, so the same bytes that load cleanly from a file throw an invalid-name error when handed to Dotenv::parse. Editors on Windows routinely prepend a UTF-8 byte order mark, and users increasingly fetch file contents themselves and parse the string. Stripping a leading UTF-8 byte order mark from string content makes the two entry points behave the same. This is stacked on #605.

author: wakeupmh
body:
Fecha o buraco que o PR #29 deixou explicitamente em aberto.

## O problema

Consultas que endereçam um registro pelo próprio `:id` faziam `WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2` — sem nenhuma dimensão de criança. Sob delegação esse `user_id` é o do **dono**, então um cuidador convidado para a criança A lia, alterava e apagava registros das outras crianças dele bastando saber o id: `GET /api/logs/:id`, `/api/documents/:id`, `/api/goals/:id`, `/api/medical/*/:id`, e os `PATCH`/`DELETE` correspondentes.

O PR #29 removeu o caminho prático de *descobrir* esses ids, mas "não dá para adivinhar o UUID" não é um controle.

## Onde a restrição passa a viver

Dentro dos construtores de SQL compartilhados (`scopedById`, `buildWhere`), alimentados por um escopo de requisição em `AsyncLocalStorage` que o middleware de delegação estabelece.

**A alternativa que descartei** foi passar um `DataScope` à mão por controllers → serviços → repositórios. Ela tem uma vantagem real — o compilador prova a cobertura — mas custa 20 repositórios de assinatura alterada, e significa que a próxima consulta escrita, daqui a um ano, por outra pessoa, vale por quem lembrou. Foi exatamente assim que isto vazou da primeira vez: a verificação existia num lugar e as consultas em outro.

**O custo dessa escolha, dito com todas as letras:** contexto implícito não é provado pelo compilador. Nada impede alguém de escrever uma consulta nova que o ignore. Por isso a correção vem com dois testes-guarda que rodam contra o schema vivo, no mesmo espírito do `accountErasureCoverage` que vocês já têm:

1. falha se **qualquer repositório** voltar a escrever `WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2` à mão;
2. falha se uma tabela com coluna `child_id` **ficar de fora** da lista de tabelas escopadas (e também se a lista declarar uma tabela que não tem a coluna).

O primeiro guarda já provou o próprio valor: pegou dois arquivos que a migração automática não alcançou (`PgAssessmentRepository` e as oito cópias da verificação de posse em `PgResponseRepository`).

## Verificação

O teste que importa roda contra Postgres real, com dono, duas crianças e registros de verdade:

```
✓ the owner can still read their own records
✓ a caregiver delegated to child A cannot read child B's log by id
✓ a caregiver delegated to child A cannot read child B's document by id
✓ a caregiver delegated to child A cannot DELETE child B's log by id
✓ delegation to the right child still works normally
```

Confirmei que **4 desses falham** sem a correção (incluindo o `DELETE`, que apagava mesmo).

Também há um caso cobrindo que o escopo sobrevive à cadeia de `await` — que é a premissa inteira do `AsyncLocalStorage`.

718/718 testes (12 novos), typecheck e build limpos. Sem migração.

## Escopo

44 predicados escritos à mão em 20 arquivos passaram a usar o helper. Tabelas sem `child_id` (`therapists`, `examiners`, `professionals`, `anamneses`) não são tocadas — acrescentar a coluna ali geraria SQL inválido, e elas são da conta, não da criança.

Com isto, `X-Delegate-Child-Id` pode enfim entrar no `allowedHeaders` do CORS — mas em PR separado, e só depois deste estar em produção.

author: lukia82-netizen
body:
💡 **What**: Refactored vehicle conflict snapshot collection in `src-tauri/src/main.rs`. Replaced flat snapshot iterations with `get_grouped_snaps`, which categorizes snapshots into fixed stack-allocated arrays by `lane_id` (`[Vec<ConflictSnap>; 4]`) and `path_id` (`[Vec<ConflictSnap>; 8]`) in a single $O(N)$ pass. Also eliminated unnecessary `cfg.idm` clones by borrowing references.

🎯 **Why**: In `idm_step`, `left_turn_step`, and `evaluate_conflict_point`, vehicles repeatedly scanned all other vehicles linearly across every lane and path to compute leader interactions, oncoming gaps, and conflict TTC. This led to redundant $O(N^2)$ iterations per tick.

📊 **Impact**: Reduces vehicle conflict lookup operations from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N)$ with direct $O(1)$ bucket indexing, resulting in an **~8.12x performance speedup** in snapshot processing during simulation steps.

🔬 **Measurement**: Verified via standalone logic benchmark (`validate_logic.rs`) comparing linear snapshot scan vs. grouped bucket scan over 20,000 simulation steps with 500 vehicles (10.63s linear vs 1.31s grouped).

author: joabertini
body:
The feat came from the hand-written catalog, which listed 27 backgrounds and knew the feat for 13. The index carries 161, of which 74 grant one. Everything outside those 13 granted nothing — including every 2024 background, all of which grant an origin feat.

The grant is now on the background row, and it is a **choice** rather than a list. 5etools records it as an array under `feats`, and every background in the data with more than one entry reads as an alternative: Ruined is "the Alert, Skilled, or Tough feat (your choice)". Reading that array as several grants would have handed Ruined all three.

Four backgrounds carry more than one entry and all four are worded "or", which is the whole evidence for that reading. A background that genuinely granted two feats would be misread; none exists in this data.

| | Example | What the builder does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one named feat | 2024 Farmer grants Tough | grants it, asks nothing |
| several named | Ruined: Alert, Skilled or Tough | asks, grants nothing until answered |
| open | Haunted One: Survivor or any Dark Gift | asks, with the whole feat list available |

An unanswered choice says so rather than picking the first option, and changing background clears the answer. A sub-choice the background already made travels in the label — the 2024 Acolyte grants Magic Initiate (Cleric), not a bare Magic Initiate.

author: danhandev
body:
## 무엇을 & 왜

`LoginService.login()`의 두 실패 경로가 모두 `ATH0101`을 쓰지만 `data`가 달랐습니다.

- 존재하지 않는 아이디 → `data: null`
- 존재하는 아이디 + 비밀번호 불일치 → `data: {errorCount, remainingAttempts}`

`data` 필드의 유무만으로 요청한 아이디가 실제 존재하는지 구분할 수 있어, REQ-AUTH-023("존재하지 않는 아이디와 잘못된 비밀번호 요청의 응답 본문이 동일하다")을 위반했습니다.

corebank-fe#94/PR#96 self review에서 발견되어 corebank-server#323으로 이슈가 열렸고, FE는 이 이슈가 닫히기 전까지 잔여 시도 횟수 화면 노출을 보류 중입니다.

## 변경 사항

- `LoginService.customerNotFound()`가 최초 실패처럼 보이는 위장값(`errorCount=1, remainingAttempts=4`, `LoginAttemptProcessor.process(1)` 재사용)을 채워 `LoginFailedException.invalidCredentials()`로 던지도록 변경. 더 이상 쓰이지 않는 `LoginFailedException.customerNotFound()` 팩토리는 제거.
- `docs/api_conventions.md`의 `ATH0101` 설명을 실제 동작(두 실패 모두 `data` 포함)에 맞게 수정.
- 단위(`LoginServiceTest`, `LoginFailedExceptionTest`)·컨트롤러(`LoginControllerTest`, `LoginExceptionHandlerTest`) 테스트를 새 동작에 맞게 갱신.
- `LoginApiIntegrationTest`에 존재하지 않는 아이디로 로그인 실패 시 실제 HTTP/DB 레벨에서 비밀번호 불일치 첫 실패와 동일한 응답(`errorCount=1, remainingAttempts=4`)을 받는지 검증하는 회귀 테스트 추가.

## 방향 결정 근거

이슈 본문에 제시된 두 방향(위장 데이터로 통일 vs `data` 필드 자체 제거) 중, FE#94/PR#96이 이미 `resolveRemainingAttempts` 매핑 로직을 구현해두고 이 이슈가 닫히면 화면에 재연결할 계획이라 위장 데이터로 통일하는 방향을 선택했습니다. 단일 요청 기준으로는 두 실패가 완전히 동일하며, 같은 존재하지 않는 아이디로 반복 요청 시 값이 고정된다는 잔존 한계는 있으나 이슈의 완료 조건(응답이 동일한 형태) 범위에서는 충분하다고 판단했습니다.

## 관련 이슈

Closes #323
FE 후속: corebank-fe#94 / corebank-fe#96 (이 PR 머지 후 `a01-login.tsx`에 `resolveRemainingAttempts` 재연결 가능)

## 셀프 체크

- [x] 도메인별 배치로 전체 테스트(account/transfer/signup·batch·adapter·terms/product·otp/auth·common/autotransfer·limit/customer·subscription·scheduledtransfer/Flyway) 통과
- [x] `docs/api_conventions.md` 갱신
