author: rogeriojorge
body:
Supersedes the strict `xfail` added to
`test_lasym_3d_stability_gradients_vs_frozen_path_fd` in #147: that test now
passes, and at a gate 100x tighter than the one it was failing.

## Root cause

The implicit function theorem gives the derivative of the equilibrium **at a
root of the residual**, and the host solver does not stop at one. `ftol`
gates `fsqr + fsqz + fsql`, the sum of SQUARES of the force, so a solve the
host reports converged returns with `|F| ~ sqrt(ftol)` — on every deck in the
gradient lane:

| deck | `ftol` | `\|F(P(x*), p)\|` at the host stop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `solovev` | 1e-14 | 3.696e-08 |
| `li383_low_res` | 1e-13 | 9.374e-08 |
| `up_down_asymmetric_tokamak` | 1e-12 | 1.295e-07 |
| `basic_non_stellsym_simsopt` | 1e-12 | 2.673e-07 |

Where `dF/dz` carries a small singular value that residual is a large
*displacement*: on `basic_non_stellsym_simsopt` the lasym m=1 direction has
`sigma = 1.473e-04`, so `|F| = 2.7e-07` sits `1.804e-03` from the root
(`|z*| = 1.65e+01`). Newton-polishing onto the root moves
`sum DMerc[2:-1]` by 9.4e-09 — 1.7x the whole `h = 1e-4` FD numerator.

Value, cotangent and linearization were all read off that point. The
frozen-path FD is the accurate side: its own Newton endpoints are roots, so
it measures `dm/dx` there as well.

## The fix

`_refined_state` Newton-refines the host state onto the root of the frozen
residual, in the host callback — the one place every lane reads the state
from — so all three move together. The knob is
`ImplicitConfig.refine_tol` (default 1e-10, `inf` disables), alongside the
`adjoint_tol` family and plumbed through `make_config` and `im.run`.

* The projector confines the correction to the evolved dofs, so the refined
  state solves exactly the equations the host solver iterates, only closer.
* A refinement that does not improve the residual — a stalled Krylov step, a
  non-finite iterate — leaves the host state untouched. The anchor is an
  accuracy gain, never a precondition for returning a gradient.
* The steps are inexact-Newton (forcing term 1e-6, three steps, 20 GCROT
  cycles each): the step only has to land `|F|` under `refine_tol`, and
  tightening it to `adjoint_tol` costs ~5x the Krylov work while moving the
  refined state by 4e-10.

Refining **only** the linearization is worse than not refining at all —
measured `-2.7799412542e-05` on the channel below, rel 5.7e-03 against the
FD, versus 4.2e-03 at the host state: the two errors partially cancel there.
That is why the returned state moves too.

The free-boundary implicit lane has its own host callback and its own
NESTOR-coupled residual; it is untouched.

## Before / after

`basic_non_stellsym_simsopt` (ns = 11, ftol = 1e-12), `h = 1e-4`:

| channel | AD before | AD after | frozen-path FD | rel before | rel after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DMerc / RBS(1,1) | -2.7839366520e-05 | -2.7957412179e-05 | -2.7957426980e-05 | 4.22e-03 | **5.29e-07** |
| DMerc / ZBC(1,1) | +1.4103345994e-04 | +1.4086931464e-04 | +1.4086950268e-04 | 1.16e-03 | **1.33e-06** |
| D_R / RBS(1,1) | +2.7307566346e-05 | +2.7425360516e-05 | +2.7425373749e-05 | 4.30e-03 | **4.83e-07** |
| D_R / ZBC(1,1) | -1.4181368428e-04 | -1.4165113528e-04 | -1.4165132549e-04 | 1.14e-03 | **1.34e-06** |

Two of the four channels were over the 2.0e-3 gate, not one. The symmetric
`RBC(0,1)` channel of the same deck showed the same-size gap (1.36e-03),
and the symmetric decks carry it too. Every channel of the shared helper,
before -> after:

| deck | channel | rel before | rel after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `solovev` | DMerc / RBC(0,1) | 9.21e-04 | 1.41e-06 |
| `solovev` | DMerc / ZBS(0,1) | 2.67e-05 | 3.19e-07 |
| `solovev` | DMerc / RBC(0,2) | 3.30e-05 | 9.58e-08 |
| `solovev` | DMerc / pres_scale | 2.45e-06 | 8.92e-07 |
| `solovev` | jdotb / RBC(0,1) | 3.34e-09 | 2.92e-08 |
| `solovev` | jdotb / pres_scale | 5.56e-06 | 1.59e-06 |
| `solovev` | D_R / RBC(0,1) | 9.21e-04 | 1.41e-06 |
| `solovev` | D_R / pres_scale | 2.45e-06 | 8.92e-07 |
| `li383_low_res` | DMerc / RBC(0,1) | 1.87e-04 | 1.73e-06 |
| `li383_low_res` | DMerc / ZBS(0,1) | 2.80e-04 | 4.62e-09 |
| `li383_low_res` | DMerc / curtor | 3.32e-05 | 7.65e-10 |
| `li383_low_res` | jdotb / RBC(0,1) | 1.95e-06 | 4.04e-07 |
| `li383_low_res` | jdotb / curtor | 2.70e-07 | 1.64e-10 |
| `li383_low_res` | D_R / RBC(0,1) | 1.86e-05 | 5.19e-07 |
| `li383_low_res` | D_R / curtor | 6.61e-04 | 1.41e-09 |

Worst channel anywhere after the change: 1.73e-06. The shared gate in
`_assert_stability_gradients` therefore goes from **2.0e-3 to 2.0e-5** (~10x
the worst measurement), which makes the lane a real guard on the anchor
rather than a formality — at 2e-3 the `solovev` DMerc channel was sitting a
factor of two under the gate.

## The `-h` warm-start anomaly, resolved

Reproduced exactly: `frozen_path_directional_fd` warm-started at the refined
root returned `-1.831234871447e-05` for DMerc/RBS(1,1) (previously reported
as `-1.8312348878e-05`).

The cause is the FD's own Newton **linear** solve. Those steps used
`_adjoint_solve`, plain restarted GMRES(30). On the `-h` branch from the
refined warm start the second step stagnated:

```
|F|=1.330e-04  it=3807  conv=True   lin_res=1.32e-15  |delta|=7.503e-04
|F|=2.211e-07  it=9000  conv=False  lin_res=2.19e-08  |delta|=2.297e-05
|F|=2.187e-08  it=9000  conv=False  lin_res=2.19e-08  |delta|=2.710e-09
|F|=2.187e-08  it=9000  conv=False  lin_res=2.19e-08  |delta|=1.639e-13   (x17)
```

9000 iterations for a relative residual of 1e-1, a null step, and Newton
frozen at `|F| = 2.187e-08` — `3.997e-04` from the root along the
`sigma = 1.5e-04` direction, which moves the `-h` metric by 1.93e-09 and the
FD by 35%. The `+h` branch converged from either warm start, hence the
1.15e-13 agreement there. This is the same truncated-cycle stagnation the
module's GCROT docstring already describes for the reverse pass.

`frozen_path_directional_fd` now takes its Newton steps with
`_adjoint_solve_gcrot`. The `-h` branch from the refined warm start then
converges to `|F| = 8.4e-15` in three steps, and both warm starts agree:

| warm start | GMRES | GCROT |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `P(x*)` | -2.795742698475e-05 | -2.795742698099e-05 |
| refined root | **-1.831234871447e-05** | -2.795742697237e-05 |

Both warm starts land on the same point whenever the linear solve converges
— the `+h` endpoints agree to 1.15e-13 in state and 3.7e-18 in the metric,
and the `-h` endpoints now agree to 1.7e-18 — so one root is all there is
here. The stall was also always detectable: `info["newton_res"]` reported
2.19e-08, and the lane's `assert residual < 1e-8` rejects it.

## User-visible numerical change

**The state returned by `solve_implicit` / `solve_implicit_status` /
`im.run` moves**, wherever the host solve stops above `refine_tol` — which,
per the table at the top, is every deck measured. It moves onto a better
root of the same equations: VMEC's own convergence measure at the returned
state drops by 5 to 10 orders of magnitude.

| deck | `\|F\|` host -> refined | `fsqr+fsqz+fsql` host -> refined |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `solovev` | 3.696e-08 -> 3.358e-14 | 1.633e-14 -> 5.269e-24 |
| `li383_low_res` | 9.374e-08 -> 9.719e-11 | 1.235e-13 -> 3.889e-19 |
| `up_down_asymmetric_tokamak` | 1.295e-07 -> 5.717e-13 | 1.605e-12 -> 2.538e-21 |
| `basic_non_stellsym_simsopt` | 2.673e-07 -> 2.975e-14 | 1.466e-12 -> 1.553e-24 |

Relative shifts in the derived scalars at the returned state:

| deck | `wb` | `aspect` | `iota_edge` | `sum DMerc[2:-1]` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `solovev` | 1.2e-13 | 2.9e-13 | 0 | 3.1e-05 |
| `li383_low_res` | 7.8e-09 | 1.9e-10 | 7.3e-07 | 1.3e-03 |
| `up_down_asymmetric_tokamak` | 2.1e-08 | 3.6e-08 | 0 | 1.9e-02 |
| `basic_non_stellsym_simsopt` | 4.8e-11 | 1.4e-09 | 2.1e-05 | 5.7e-04 |

The bulk integrals barely move; the solver-sensitive metrics this lane exists
for move by up to 1.9e-02, which is the size of the error being removed.

Gradients shipped in v0.6.0

author: apojomovsky
body:
Builds pic16f88x-hal for 16F887 through the epic-cc backend (epic_build.py --toolchain epic-cc).

Closes #71

- pic16f88x_gpio_epiccc.c: literal SFR addresses via if-else to avoid inttoptr var and switch lowering, with ANSEL handling for 88X (RE0..RE2, AN12/AN10 etc.), and memory barriers to avoid PHI of pointers.
- pic16f88x_usart_epiccc.c: avoids llvm.umin via volatile clamp and makes TX/RX ISRs not call the handle's function pointer under EPIC_AT.
- pic16f88x_timer0_epiccc.c: avoids const flash GEP for ps_ratio and makes ISR not call the overflow callback under EPIC_AT (blinky polls TMR0IF for the smoke).
- pic16_irq_epiccc.c / pic16_irq_dispatch_epiccc.c: make irq_table RAM for epic-cc and dispatch only Timer0/RB for the smoke, avoiding the full HAL's isel gaps (flash GEP, indirect calls).
- scripts/epic_build.py: map 88X gpio/usart/timer0/irq to epiccc, fix boren->bor mapping for 887, and keep the 887 smoke to the minimal slice (gpio+timer0+irq+wdt+isr/harness) while the remaining peripheral gaps are filed.
- example_blink.c: for __EPIC_CC__ poll TMR0IF and call on_t0_overflow directly, and make the handle static so its address is a global.

Companion compiler fix: apojomovsky/epic-cc#105 handles p16f887 ANSEL bank_of, isel trunc/indirect call/Gep gaps.

Smoke: `pic16f88x-hal` for 16F887 builds to HEX via `epic-cc --target 16F887` and blinky runs via polling (sim harness tick still pumps). Full peripheral matrix is out of scope per #71 and #70.

author: marcus-campos
body:
Seis frentes de trabalho, um PR. Tudo sai de `b828baa` e volta como uma branch só.

## O que entra

**`shape` — de onde vem o trabalho.** Um eixo novo, ortogonal a `mode`. `bus` é o parley de hoje. `pool` publica o que uma frente descobre como item no barramento em vez de mensagem de chat que evapora com o scrollback. `plan` lê um plano do `superpowers:writing-plans` e despacha as tarefas em ondas, calculando o paralelismo a partir dos caminhos que cada tarefa declara.

**Work pool.** Item fatiado por posse: quem já segura o arquivo recebe a oferta, o resto vai para o pool. A oferta compra primeira recusa, não obediência — `drop` não custa nada e devolve para quem o item realmente pertence. Oferta sem resposta e item de frente morta voltam sozinhos.

**Capacidade.** Quando há trabalho parado e ninguém livre, o parley recicla uma frente ociosa antes de criar qualquer coisa; só então gera uma nova, em worktree própria, no painel ou num terminal de verdade. Recém-nascida sem pool e sem item se aposenta e devolve a vaga. Teto configurável, e a pessoa tem veto.

**Recall das notas.** `--query` em `notes` e `results`, com um piso lexical BM25 que funciona sempre — sem download, sem modelo. Acima dele, um cérebro local opcional, desligado por padrão, que a pessoa liga e escolhe o modelo. Silêncio abaixo do piso é proposital: a nota menos ruim custa tokens e ensina o agente a desconfiar do canal.

**Voto humano.** `grant` e `deny` deixam de ser exclusivos de agentes.

**Site de documentação.** VitePress, publicado por GitHub Actions, com a referência de comandos **gerada** a partir do `--help` e um livro-razão que fixa o *texto* citado — então documentação não envelhece em silêncio.

## Como foi construído

Cada frente saiu de um plano escrito, foi implementada task a task com TDD, e passou por rodadas de revisão adversarial. As revisões não conferiram se os testes passam: elas **mutaram o código de produção** e checaram se os testes ficam vermelhos.

Isso importa porque o defeito dominante deste trabalho não foi código quebrado. Foi **teste que fica verde contra implementação sem lógica nenhuma** — dezenas de instâncias confirmadas. Três exemplos do que só apareceu por mutação:

- A capacidade inteira era **código morto**. `bearFront` escrevia `PARLEY_BORN` no ambiente do filho e nada lia. Os dois lados testados, o fio entre eles não. Apagar `retireFronts` inteiro deixava a suíte verde.
- O piso da busca vetorial **não filtrava nada**. `MIN_SIMILARITY = 0` contra modelos densos anisotrópicos, onde todo cosseno é positivo. `BRAIN OFF → []`, `BRAIN ON → [todas as notas]`.
- Uma onda podia ser dada como concluída **sem as revisões dela**. A regra que carrega o peso do `shape plan` não tinha teste até a última task.

Um frame `plan` malformado também matava o barramento de um repositório para sempre — o journal grava antes de aplicar, e o `restore()` reexecutava sem `try/catch`. Fechado nas duas pontas: fronteira que recusa em vez de inventar, e replay que pula e nomeia.

## Verificação

**741 testes, 0 falhas, 58 de 58 arquivos** — contagem conferida contra o esperado, porque `bun test` roda o subconjunto que casa e sai com código 0 em silêncio quando um caminho não casa. `typecheck` e `build` limpos, o site constrói, e os dois artefatos gerados — referência de comandos e livro-razão de citações — regeneram sem diff.

O único arquivo de teste que não roda é `tests/adapters/registry.test.ts`, pelo motivo no fim desta descrição.

## O que a integração encontrou

Merges limpos em quatro das seis. Os conflitos reais foram todos em cima de arquivos que todas tocam — `state/types.ts`, `state/machine.ts`, `daemon/server.ts`, `cli/main.ts` — e dois deles não eram aditivos:

- **Duas branches consertaram a mesma mentira do `HOOK_BUDGET_MS` de formas incompatíveis.** Uma manteve `30` e corrigiu os comentários para dizer "é a unidade, não o prazo; o `runHook` arma em ×40"; a outra trocou a constante para `1_200` e removeu o multiplicador. Pegar a constante de uma com o multiplicador da outra daria um prazo de hook de **48 segundos**. Resolvido para `1_200` sem multiplicador.
- **O `PROTOCOL.md` afirmava que humano não pode `grant`/`deny`** — verdade numa branch, e falso depois da que deu voto ao humano. Resolvido pelo que o código faz: no tri mesclado, `OBSERVER_ONLY` tem um único produtor, e é o `brain`.

E o merge tornou falsos dois parágrafos de documentação que eram verdadeiros na branch de origem: o `work-pool.md` dizia que o `publishWork` honra um `origin` vindo do frame (removido depois), e o `shapes.md` dizia que `shape plan` não faz nada, que não existe `parley plan` e que nada parseia `**Files:**`. Os dois foram reescritos.

**Divulgação sobre as citações.** O merge moveu linhas em quase todo arquivo compartilhado, então 85+ citações `src/…:NN` do site saíram do lugar. Reapontei-as a partir do texto que o livro-razão fixa — quatro verificadas à mão contra a construção que citam, o resto casado por bloco. Onde o código mudou de conteúdo e não só de posição, re-fixei o livro-razão com `--accept-changes`. **Isso é o desvio que a própria guarda documenta**: um re-fixamento por reflexo passa verde. As páginas de `docs/concepts/` merecem uma lida antes do merge — a guarda garante que a citação aponta para onde o texto está, não que a frase acima dela continua verdadeira.

## Aberto, e declarado

Nada disto é bug de execução; são lacunas de evidência ou de redação, todas medidas:

- **`summon` não gera frente e ainda bloqueia o caminho automático** por até um cooldown. Duas correções pequenas identificadas (parar de carimbar `lastBirthMs`, parar de responder `summoned: true`); a metade de desenho — dar ao `tick` um motivo de nascer que não seja pool velho — fica em aberto.
- **`git` bloqueia o event loop do daemon no nascimento** (124ms medidos num repositório de 800 arquivos, 0 ticks). Degrada corretamente contra o prazo real do hook (1200ms), mas o módulo promete um limite que essa função não tem.
- **Uma guarda de documentação dispara por uma frase escrita à mão**, e seis páginas publicadas descrevem o mesmo caso sem usar aquela frase.
- Números citados em comentários e relatórios que envelheceram junto com o código que descrevem.

## O que depende de você

1. **Settings → Pages → Source → "GitHub Actions"**, na mão. Nenhum workflow consegue mudar isso, e sem ele o site não publica.
2. **SHA-256 reais dos modelos** no registry do brain. O placeholder atual faz a verificação de integridade recusar qualquer download — que é o comportamento certo, e é o que segura a feature até você preencher.
3. **`tests/adapters/registry.test.ts`** chama `refreshAllAdapters()` contra o registry real da máquina em vez de um diretório temporário, e reescreve o `SKILL.md` de todo repositório registrado. Todo agente desta sessão foi instruído a não rodar aquele arquivo. O conserto precisa pousar em algum lugar, e escolher onde é sua decisão.

author: jomkz
body:
Stage C of the pre-audit DRY consolidation epic. Three contracts that were each written out dozens
of times get one home apiece; the file shrinks by ~640 lines net with no behaviour change. Verified
with the full debug suite (4917 tests, 0 failures) — test_server_config's 142 cases and
test_userconfig_enums' round-trip suite are the acceptance gates here — plus -Wshadow -fsyntax-only
on each changed TU, tools/docs_drift.py all, tools/lint_test_names.py and reuse lint.

Operator-facing strings are the sensitive surface in this one, so they were treated as output to be
preserved rather than code to be tidied. Every migrated warning keeps its "<section>.<key> out of
range" prefix and its "unknown <key> '<value>', defaulting to <default>" wording, including the
parenthetical glosses that carry real meaning — "using default 0 (disabled)" and "using default 0
(auto)" answer a different question from "using default 0", so the helper takes an optional note
rather than dropping them. The bracket spacing and the printed default now come from the live bound
and the live default instead of a hand-copied literal, which is the drift this removes: the bound
was in the code and the message repeated it as a string.

The UserConfig half is worth its own note. Nineteen enums each carried a switch naming their values
and a strcmp chain parsing them back — two halves that had to be edited together forever, where a
value added to one and forgotten in the other silently round-trips to the default. To a player that
reads as "the game keeps resetting my setting", with nothing in the log. One table per enum, read by
both directions, makes that structural rather than only tested for. It is a plain table plus two
function templates, deliberately not an X-macro: there is no macro precedent anywhere in engine/,
game/ or server/, and the tables stay file-local.

- ServerCommands.cpp: 34 sim-callback print sites adopt printAdmin, which is widened to
  std::string_view so the std::string sites need no .c_str(). The two shared-fflush blocks (the peers
  loop and spawn's five prints) convert too — printAdmin only flushes more eagerly, so the bytes and
  the shell ring are unchanged — and their now-orphan trailing fflush goes. pause/resume are NOT
  touched: they run on the dispatch thread and return their message as the dispatch result, so
  converting them would double-print.
- server_config.cpp: new clampInt (templated on the destination integer type, built on fl::tomlInt)
  and a [sec.sub] overload of each, beside clampDouble which is templated the same way so the
  float-typed keys can adopt it. 54 hand-spelled integer sites and 15 double sites migrate; the four
  interchangeable spellings they were written in (braced and unbraced `< lo || > hi`, the inverted
  `>= lo && <= hi`, and the int64_t{...} bound form) collapse to one call each.
- left alone deliberately: motd_display_s's clamp-with-warn policy (a different contract, pinned by
  its own test), world.time_scale's exclusive `must be > 0` rule, and overrun_low_watermark's bound
  against another live setting rather than a constant.
- tools/docs_drift.py: the config-keys check reads keys off `tbl["sec"]["key"]` subscripts, so the
  ~70 keys that just moved behind a helper would have vanished from the code side. Its clampDouble
  special case now covers clampInt and the three-level form, and config-keys still reports 142 vs 142.
- UserConfig.cpp: per-enum constexpr name tables plus enumName / parseEnum. The four graphics
  settings that inferred "the value was unknown" by comparing the parse result against the default,
  and log_level which did the same, now warn from inside the parse. parseLogLevel keeps its public
  signature and stays silent — an unknown --log-level on the command line is not a user-config
  problem. The MSAA-to-TAA migration becomes legacy alias rows placed after the canonical ones, so
  they parse but are never written back, which is exactly the silent migration it was.

Closes #1266

author: warp-agent-staging[bot]
body:
## Summary
Second of three stacked PRs splitting #15446 into separable layers. This layer adds the CLI `--team` flag: an `warp <object> create --team [UID]` invocation can now name which team owns the new object, needed once a user is on more than one team.

## Stack
1. #15485 — the module split (base: `master`).
2. **This PR** — the CLI `--team` flag (base: layer 1).
3. #15446 (retargeted onto this branch) — the BYO team-scope lookups.

## Changes
- `ObjectScope::team` becomes `Option<Option<String>>`: absent (no `--team`), bare `--team` (use your sole team), or `--team <UID>` (use that team, verified to be one you belong to). New `ObjectScope::is_team()`/`requested_team_uid()` helpers.
- `UserWorkspaces::sole_team`/`sole_team_uid` now return `Result<_, SoleTeamError>` instead of `Option`, since "you're on several teams" is a real, reportable case for a CLI caller rather than a silent `None`.
- `team_workspace_settings.rs` gains `TeamScopeForCli`/`CliTeamError` and `UserWorkspaces::cli_team_uid`/`team_scope_for_cli`, which resolve the requested (or sole) team, checking membership so a mistyped UID fails loudly.
- `app/src/ai/agent_sdk/common.rs`'s `resolve_owner` is rewritten around `ObjectScope` and the new team resolution, with clearer per-case error messages.
- Call sites in `agent_sdk/{runner,schedule,secret,environment,ambient}.rs` and `ai_document_model.rs` are updated for the new signatures.

Out of scope for this layer: anything that reads team-scoped BYO policy (`is_model_allowed_for_scope`, `validate_agent_mode_base_model_id_for_scope`, and their CLI call sites) — those getters don't exist yet at this point in the stack, so they land in layer 3 along with their callers.

## Verification
- `./script/format` — clean.
- `cargo clippy -p warp --all-targets --tests -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo clippy -p warp_cli --all-targets --tests -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo check -p warp_tui --lib --tests` — clean (confirms the `sole_team`/`sole_team_uid` signature change doesn't leak into the TUI front-end).
- `cargo nextest run -p warp user_workspaces agent_sdk ai_document_model` — 613/613 passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p warp_cli` — 231/231 passed, including new `schedule_create_accepts_team_scope_with_uid` covering `--team <UID>`.

author: dem-extra1
body:
Closes #1382

### Summary of changes

1. **Trailing reserve positioning in `General.reserve_directives`**:
   - Updated `General.reserve_directives(reserve_units, active_units, all_units, trail_distance)` to position held reserve units at `RESERVE_TRAIL_DISTANCE` (140.0 wu, well within `RELIEF_CALL_RANGE` 220.0 wu) trailing behind the active committed line's centroid along the army's advance axis.
   - Preserves each reserve unit's lateral offset relative to the line along the perpendicular axis so reserves don't collapse onto a single coordinate.
   - Retains fallback to holding at current unit position if there are no active units or no advance axis.
   - Returned `active_units` from `General.decide_army()` and threaded `active_units` and `all_units` through `Battle._run_enemy_ai()`.

2. **Unit & integration test coverage**:
   - Added unit tests in `test/unit/test_general.gd` verifying `reserve_directives` trailing offset calculations, lateral offset preservation, and fallback behavior.
   - Updated `test/unit/test_battle_ai_general.gd` assertions to check positional trailing reserve directives under `cautious` vs all-in forward attack under `aggressive`.

### Local Verification
- `tools/check.sh validate chars comments units patch_coverage test`: All 199 test scripts, 2,814 unit tests, and 57,639 assertions passed cleanly.

<!-- sparta-demo -->
### 🎬 Gameplay demo

Under cautious doctrine, General.reserve_directives holds reserve units trailing 140 wu behind the advancing active line rather than pinned at spawn. As the active line advances toward the enemy, the reserves follow behind in reserve formation and promptly join the fight when the line engages.

![demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Lacaedemon/sparta/demo-media/pr-1383-875f287.gif)

🔊 The GIF above plays once and is silent — [watch with sound, pause and scrub (MP4)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Lacaedemon/sparta/demo-media/pr-1383-875f287.mp4).

🔬 Per-tick state transcript posted as a [PR comment](https://github.com/Lacaedemon/sparta/pull/1383) — search the conversation for "state transcript".

<sub>Recorded from `demos/inputs/reserve-trailing-advance.json` at `875f287`. Updated automatically on each push.</sub>
<!-- /sparta-demo -->

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes army-level AI positioning for held reserves, which can alter engagement timing and relief availability. Deterministic HOLD_LINE math with tests and a spawn-position fallback keep the risk moderate.
> 
> **Overview**
> Held-back reserves now **trail the committed line** instead of sitting at spawn. `General.reserve_directives` places each reserve 140 wu behind the active centroid along the advance axis (inside `RELIEF_CALL_RANGE`), keeping each unit’s lateral offset so the reserve line does not collapse to one point.
> 
> `decide_army` now returns `active_units`, and `_run_enemy_ai` passes that plus `all_units` into the directive helper. If there is no living active line or no advance axis, reserves still hold at their current position.
> 
> Docs, the doctrine demo, and unit/integration tests cover trailing offset, lateral spread, and cautious vs aggressive order signatures.

author: nemo
body:
## Summary

Adds `electron/` — a wrapper around the existing built site, purely so a control UI can live on one screen while the show fullscreens on another. Chrome refuses to let one window trigger fullscreen on another (cross-window `requestFullscreen` throws — confirmed empirically), so a single-tab app can never do "control here, show there." This is a **new way to run the show**; it changes nothing about how scenes get built, previewed, or verified — the plain web app (Netlify, `tools/verify.sh`, `docs/PREVIEW.md`) is untouched.

Resolves the architecture laid out on wayfinder map [#27](https://github.com/lwcassid/source-scenes/issues/27) (tickets #28–#37).

- Two windows, one process, told apart by `?role=show`/`?role=control` (`window.ELECTRON_ROLE`, `part1_head.html`). The show window owns AudioContext, Web MIDI in/out, and rendering exclusively; the control window reuses the exact same UI unchanged and relays through `electron/main.js`'s IPC contract (`docs/adr/0003`).
- Gate-and-relay at the top of shared functions (`AE.ensure()`, `connectMidi()`, `MOut.testBurst()`) means every existing UI trigger — CONNECT, TEST, SHOW CHECK's fix buttons — works from either window for free, no per-call-site patching.
- SHOW CHECK's SOUND/HANDS/CALIBRATION rows now mirror the show window's real state over the same relay instead of reading local state that's permanently inert in the control window by design.
- Window close now explicitly `destroy()`s the sibling before quitting, so closing either window reliably takes the whole app down.
- `document.fullscreenElement` never gets set by Electron's native `setFullScreen()` — was silently breaking SHOWTIME's auto-advance and the fullscreen show layout. Show role now forces `.fs` / hides panels unconditionally instead of depending on a DOM event that never fires.
- Chromium's autoplay policy held `AudioContext.resume()` suspended forever in the show window (no visible chrome to click, by design) — lifted via the same `--autoplay-policy` flag the test harnesses already use, since this is a closed kiosk app, not a general webpage.
- `MOut.port` staleness fixed on MIDI device disconnect/reconnect.

**Not yet wired** (documented in `CLAUDE.md`/`docs/SHOW-KIT.md`): LEARN (hand-sensor CC mapping) and calibration sweeps can't run from the control window — no live raw-value feed relayed back yet. Do them directly in the show window; SHOW CHECK says so instead of offering a dead button.

`docs/adr/0001`–`0006` record the architecture decisions.

Also includes an unrelated small fix: `tools/shot.mjs`/`shotcam.mjs`/`shotevt.mjs` wrote screenshots to a hardcoded `/home/user/source-scenes/...` path — now relative to the repo root so the harnesses work on any machine.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash tools/build.sh` — index.html rebuilds clean
- [x] `bash tools/verify.sh --quick` — PASSED; read `scratchshots/verify_wall.png` and `verify_drawer.png`, plain web app unaffected

body:
# Relates to

Seven of the ten failures in the `pr-deterministic` scenario lane on `develop`. Sibling of #25932 (scenario action scoping) and #26757 (fixture isolation) — all three are the lane becoming trustworthy again.

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest `origin/develop` with zero conflicts.
- [ ] `bun install` and `bun run verify` were run after sync — `bun install` yes; `bun run verify` not run (repository-wide lane); the targeted gates below were run on the exact head.
- [x] A reviewer can confirm the change works without reading the code, from the evidence below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Rebased onto `origin/develop` (`21cbe704aba`); zero conflicts.
- [ ] `bun run verify` — see Known gaps.

# Risks

**Low, and deliberately confined to the legacy lane.** The new branch is reached only when `modelFixtureMode === "legacy-fallback"`; scenarios that declare a model manifest (`mode: "fixtures"`) or run model-free bypass this resolver entirely and stay fail-closed. Strict-mode enforcement is untouched — a test pins that a plugin built without the fallback resolver still rejects the call and still fails `assertFixturesConsumed()`.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

The lane showed **32 passed / 10 failed**, and nine failures shared a signature: `deterministic model calls were unexpected: [{"modelType":"TEXT_SMALL", …}]`. They are not one cause — they are **7 + 1 + 1**.

The seven are `EvaluatorService`'s merged post-turn evaluation call: `generateEvaluationOutput` → `runtime.useModel(TEXT_SMALL, { messages, responseSchema, … })` in `packages/core/src/services/evaluator.ts`. It runs every active evaluator in one call after **every** turn, on the same runtime the scenario drives. It is runtime-wide background work that nothing in those scenarios asserts on, but it reaches the strict registry and fails the whole scenario at `assertConsumed()`.

**The call is legitimate and the scenarios were the ones missing a declaration.** The decisive evidence: two already-*passing* scenarios declare a fixture for this exact call — `deterministic-workflow-actions-routes.scenario.ts` (`input: { includes: "# Task: Post-turn evaluation" }`) and `deterministic-active-view-agent-surface.scenario.ts`. Scenarios that migrated to explicit manifests declare it; the seven that never declared one run in `legacy-fallback` and depend on `resolveScenarioDeterministicModelCall`, which only knew about scheduled-dispatch prompts.

The fix teaches that fallback resolver to answer the post-turn evaluator call with `"{}"` — the "nothing to record" empty shape the evaluator prompt itself prescribes, which `processPreparedEntries` skips section by section without error. It matches on **two** signals (the `# Task: Post-turn evaluation` header `renderSharedContext` emits, plus the `## Active Evaluators` section `renderPrompt` appends), so ordinary conversation text quoting the header alone is never answered, and it is checked before the dispatch branches because the evaluator prompt embeds the turn's provider context.

Incidental notes for the record: `promptLength: 0` in the diagnostic is not a defect — the evaluator passes `messages`, not `prompt`. And the evaluator prompt reaches roughly 1.1 MB, which follows from the deliberate "preserve complete model context" policy; left alone.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (test harness; non-breaking).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation; the new predicate and the branch each carry the reasoning in-code.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`isPostTurnEvaluationPrompt` and the single branch that consumes it in `resolveScenarioDeterministicModelCall`, then the four tests in `runtime-factory.test.ts`.

## Detailed testing steps

- **Lane before: 32 passed / 10 failed. Lane after: 39 passed / 3 failed.** All seven evaluator failures green, zero regressions. `pgrep -f "cli.ts run test/scenarios"` verified clean before *and* after every measurement.
- `bunx vitest run src/runtime-factory.test.ts` → 22 pass (4 new). Mutation: disabling the branch → the two behavioural tests fail (`expected null to be '{}'`, `promise rejected … instead of resolving`); restored → 22/22.
- Independently re-verified after rebase onto current develop: `deterministic-media-actions` and `deterministic-agent-skills-actions` each 1 passed / 0 failed.
- Biome clean on both touched files. `typecheck`: 119 errors byte-identical before and after apart from one line-number shift on a pre-existing `TS2307` (all pre-existing unbuilt-sibling module resolution). `test:unit` 538 passed / 1 failed — `corpus-assertion-guard.test.ts`, reproduced on pristine files. `test:mocks` 21/21.

author: dangeratio
body: A pass over every feature, driving the app rather than only re-reading it. Three real bugs, two nits, one file, `+35 -7`. ## 1. Cook mode showed the wrong quantities The worst of the three, because it is wrong in the one view you are holding a pan for. `drawCook()` read `state.servings` directly, and nothing reset that when the recipe under it changed. Open a recipe, scale it, then go to `#cook/` and the second recipe is cooked at the first one's servings. ``` Oats (serves 1) scaled to 2, then #cook/demo_chili (serves 6): before: 2/3 tbsp oil, 2/3 onions, 1 1/3 cloves garlic <- 6 scaled by 2/6 after: 2 tbsp oil, 2 onions, 4 cloves garlic ``` Both readers now go through `servingsFor()`, which resets the scale when the recipe changes and leaves a deliberate scale alone. Verified the other direction too: scaling chili to 8 and then cooking it still reads `2 2/3 tbsp oil`. ## 2. The full-screen grid on phones leaked, and could look like a freeze `openGridFull()` appended an overlay without removing an existing one, and `closeGridFull()` took only the first node. So three taps left three overlays and one close left two. Worse: nothing took the overlay down on navigation. Open the grid, then use the back gesture, and the overlay sits over the next page with `body` still `overflow: hidden`. On a phone there is no Escape key, so the only way out is reloading. **The app looks dead.** ``` before: 3 taps -> 3 overlays; navigate away -> overlay stays, overflow: hidden after: 3 taps -> 1 overlay; navigate away -> 0 overlays, overflow: visible, page usable ``` Opening replaces, closing removes them all, and `route()` takes it down the way it already did for cook mode. The scroll lock is shared with cook mode, so it is only released when cook mode is not the one holding it - checked that cook mode still locks and unlocks correctly. ## 3. "Paste in" from the editor silently discarded unsaved edits A paste always lands in a *new* recipe, so using the button from inside the editor threw away whatever was unsaved there. The saved recipe was never at risk, but every other path that loses work asks first and this one did not. It now asks, and declining leaves your edits and the modal alone. ## Nits - "Start a 8 minutes timer" -> "Start a timer for 8 minutes". The amount comes from the step text, so no article rule fixes it; rewording around it does. - A `delId` ternary whose two branches were identical. ## Regression pass After the fixes, from a cleared browser: all routes render, no console errors, the coffee-cake grid geometry is cell-for-cell unchanged (rowspans and colspans included), list view and scaling work, the shopping list still merges 16 items across two recipes, paste-parsing is unchanged, and re-importing an export still adds zero duplicates. ## Checked and deliberately left alone - **Cycles in the step tree** (two steps each claiming the other) are still broken safely and render, rather than hanging. - **Empty recipes, ingredients-only, and steps-only** all render sensibly in both views. - **Deleting a recipe** correctly removes it from the planner and the shopping list. - **Import merge** still keeps the newer side; an old backup cannot clobber an edit. - **`photo` goes into an inline `style` attribute.** I probed it with a crafted URL: not exploitable, because the parens are stripped and CSS then drops the invalid declaration, and `esc()` handles quotes. Cleaner as an ``, but it is not a bug and I left it. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: quantm-zeus
body:
## Summary

Third control-plane defect found by the real generation-1 activation (after #38 reset, #39 first-tick drain):

The pre-fix supervisor start latched a fatal pause on the retired gen-0 identity (expected — see #39). The supported operator recovery `--clear-fatal` removed only the `pausedFatal` flag and **left the fatal-paused entry tracked**. That zombie row:

- occupies the package's selection slot forever (`selectAndLaunch` skips candidates with a non-done tracked row),
- cannot be recovered (`--recover-fatal` refuses cross-generation recovery — correct by design), and
- cannot be spliced (terminal-row reconciliation deliberately ignores paused rows).

Net effect: a permanent selection deadlock with no supported exit short of manual state surgery — which is forbidden.

## Change

`--clear-fatal` now drops every fatal-paused entry along with the flag (recorded as `fatal_pause_entries_dropped`). The pre-existing orphan refusal still runs FIRST, so clearing can never orphan a RUNNING package without a live track; stranded reconciliation rebuilds whatever tracking is warranted against current truth on the next tick.

## Evidence

- Hermetic: clear drops the gen-0 zombie under a PENDING gen-1 milestone (flag null, `activeRuns` empty, drop event recorded); RUNNING-without-track still refuses with exit 1 and mutates nothing.
- Full `pnpm verify` green at 76cf529: spec:verify 13 checks, 257 tests.

author: josejmizrahi
body:
## Qué cambia

El `odoo-update` del build anterior (PR #176) reventó al cargar el registro:

```
KeyError: 'Field activity_type_id referenced in related field definition
sgi.process.activity_type_id does not exist.'
```

**Causa:** `sgi.process` ya tenía un one2many llamado `activity_ids` (las actividades del procedimiento vivo) y `mail.activity.mixin` — heredado en el PR #176 para el aviso de eslabón atorado — define **su propio** `activity_ids` (mail.activity) con campos related como `activity_type_id`. Nuestro campo pisaba al del mixin, sus related quedaban colgando, el registro no cargaba y **el build de producción se quedó en la versión anterior** (por eso el error de `activity_schedule` seguía apareciendo).

### Arreglo
- El one2many del procedimiento se renombra a **`procedure_activity_ids`** en todos sus usos: definición y cómputos (`activity_count`, `_compute_measure_stats`, formatos referenciados), diagnóstico, carga desde `sgi_format_map`, reporte F-P-G01-02, la vista de la pestaña Procedimiento y las pruebas.
- Al ser one2many **no hay columna en BD**: el rename no necesita migración de datos.
- `next_activity_ids`/`prev_activity_ids` viven en `sgi.process.activity` (sin mixin) — sin colisión, no se tocan.

### Versión
`__manifest__.py`: 19.0.23.0.0 → **19.0.23.1.0**. Este es el build que por fin debe cargar completo (mixin + chatter + cron blindado del PR #176 incluidos).

## Validación
- `py_compile` sobre todos los `.py` ✔
- `flake8` con las reglas del repo ✔
- Parse de todos los XML ✔
- `tools/check_addons.py --base-ref origin/main`: 0 errores, 0 advertencias ✔

author: firefoxic
body:
`block-closing-brace-space-before` under every option a multi-line block can reach, and `block-closing-brace-newline-before` under `never-multi-line`, write the whitespace standing between the last node of a block and its closing brace, and neither asked what that whitespace stands behind. An inline comment is closed by a line break and by nothing else, so where the last node of the block leaves one open, the break in that whitespace is the comment's close, and writing over it takes the brace into the comment's text:

```scss
a {
	color: pink // c
}
```

came back from `--fix` under `never` as

```scss
a {
	color: pink // c}
```

a block with no close at all, which the next run reports as `Unclosed block`. Under `always` the same happens with a space in front of the brace, and a comment standing on a line of its own goes the same way. These are the ten rows `converge` has carried since it was written, and the last ten it carries: **the oracle is empty as of this branch**, no rule of its corpus leaving a file its own syntax cannot read any more.

`postcss-less` writes the same output and reads its own brace back out of the comment, so the round trip is stable there and only the text looked wrong. The spec left open whether Less agrees with its PostCSS parser about that brace, and it does not: `less.render` on that output fails with `Parse: Unrecognised input`, while the file the fix was given renders fine. The file is as unreadable under Less as under Sass, so the guard belongs to both syntaxes rather than to one.

## The fix

Both rules ask `writesIntoInlineComment` about the last node of the block and decline the fix where the answer is yes. Neither asks about the node alone, though. The whitespace a fix writes over is the room the write goes into, and that is the question the name was written for, but these two fixes write into the block's own final raw rather than into anything of the node's, so the whitespace the node ends with survives them — and a break standing there closes the comment as surely as one the fix leaves in the raw.

So both rules spell out the run that will stand between the node and the brace once the fix has run. The name already takes such a run, from #248, which landed hours before this branch and hands it the semicolon a declaration's own `never-multi-line` fix writes behind; it scanned that run along with the node's text while still reading the whitespace at the end as room, which is right wherever the run is spelled and wrong wherever it is empty. The run is read as a run throughout now — none of it is room, and neither is the whitespace the node ends with — and #248's caller answers exactly as it did, a semicolon being no whitespace for the scan to trim away. Of the run itself, `block-closing-brace-space-before` leaves everything in front of the whitespace ending that raw, a stray semicolon among it, and `block-closing-brace-newline-before` under `never-multi-line` leaves nothing of the raw at all. A comment closed by a break of the last node's own trailing whitespace is therefore still fixed, and so is one closed by a break standing in front of a stray semicolon; only where no break survives anywhere in that run is the statement left alone and the warning left standing.

The `always` options of `block-closing-brace-newline-before` never ask. The break they write is what closes such a comment anyway, and under `postcss-less`, where a block whose brace a comment has already swallowed still parses, they put it right.

An exhaustive sweep of the two rules — 280 inputs over 18 block bodies and 16 spellings of the block's final raw, under every option and both custom syntaxes — makes 1692 fixes with **no output that fails to reparse**, cures 431 that did on the base, and puts every Less output whose input compiled through `less.render`.

## What the review turned up

- **The reading the spec pointed at would have fixed nothing.** It named the one #208 gave the `declaration-block-semicolon-*` rules — the last node of a block sought *past* its trailing comments. Under `postcss-scss` the node that reading skips is exactly the comment that swallows the brace, so what these two rules ask about is `statement.last`, comments included.
- **`block-closing-brace-empty-line-before` writes into the same raw and never reaches this form**, which the spec asked to be settled either way. `removeEmptyLinesAfter` writes a run of empty lines back as its first break, and `addEmptyLineAfter` doubles a break rather than taking one away, so a break stands in front of the brace whichever of its two options ran — measured over nine shapes under both options and three syntaxes, against the `addEmptyLineAfter` this branch rebased onto rather than the one the spec was written against.
- **`twins` gains twenty-five rows, and every one is [#284](https://github.com/stylelint-stylistic/stylelint-stylistic/issues/284), filed by this review.** `endsWithInlineComment` reads no form feed as closing an inline comment, which is right for Less and wrong for Sass, so a file spelling its breaks that way now has a fix declined that nothing is at risk from. Five rows of that shape have stood since #211, and every further caller of the shared name adds its own — thirty rows over six pairs of a rule and an option today. The repair is a third verdict on the probe `readsInlineComments` already runs.
- **A family of declines comes in that no oracle sees, and it is [#306](https://github.com/stylelint-stylistic/stylelint-stylistic/issues/306), also filed by this review.** Under `postcss-less`, `@extend .b // c;` standing last in a block keeps its double slash in `params`, since Less opens no comment there, and the scan reads one anyway: five pairs of a rule and an option refuse a fix `less.render` renders exactly as it renders the file they were given. A Less at-variable, `@x: 1 // c;`, wears the same shape and has to keep being declined, since moving the brace onto its line makes Less read it as a property rather than as a variable declaration — so the repair has to tell the two apart. Of the 541 declines this branch introduces, those seven rows are the only ones that decline a sound fix on a sound input.
- **[#292](https://github.com/stylelint-stylistic/stylelint-stylistic/issues/292) is older than either guard and has nothing to do with comments.** Where the last node of a block is an at-rule carrying neither a block nor a semicolon, PostCSS files the whitespace in front of the brace into that at-rule's `raws.between`, so all three `block-closing-brace-*-before` rules report a run they never write. Their `always` options put their space or their break in the raw beside it and grow the file on every run — by one character each, and by two for `block-closing-brace-empty-line-before` — with the warning standing after each. It reproduces in plain CSS, and `converge` misses it only because no fixture of its corpus ends a block that way. This branch neither causes it nor cures it.
- **[#307](https://github.com/stylelint-stylistic/stylelint-stylistic/issues/307) is tooling.** `bind-prose.js` walks `node_modules` and `tmp` in full before filtering them out, so one unreadable entry under either fails `make verify` with a path the repository does not carry.
- **[#309](https://github.com/stylelint-stylistic/stylelint-stylistic/issues/309) came out of checking that census, and is a corruption rather than a decline.** `declaration-block-trailing-semicolon` under `never` takes away the semicolon that closes an `@extend`, which Less will not part with: `a {\n\t@extend .b;\n}` compiles and `a {\n\t@extend .b\n}` is refused with `@extend rule is missing block or ending semi-colon`. No comment is involved, `converge` cannot see it — `postcss-less` reads the output back happily, the parser not being the compiler — and it is the shape #231 wore under that syntax, a semicolon in place of a brace.

author: schmug
body:
Closes #144.

All 75 published episodes carry the same date-only title, so the public show's back
catalogue is 75 interchangeable date stamps — conspicuous now that #139 gives new
episodes topical ones. This lands the code and the reviewed copy. **Nothing has been
published yet**: no R2 write and no Pages deploy hook has fired. The canary and the
batch are a separate, confirmed step.

## What ships

`skills/daily-podcast/retitle.py` — a maintenance CLI (no run calls it) that rewrites
`title` on entries already in the R2 `manifest.json`, plus `backfill_topics.json`, the
reviewed topic phrases for all 75 published slugs.

```bash
python3 skills/daily-podcast/retitle.py                        # review every title
python3 skills/daily-podcast/retitle.py --only <slug> --apply  # canary: one episode
python3 skills/daily-podcast/retitle.py --apply                # the rest
```

## Why this is guid-neutral, and how far that reaches

Only one of the two Spotify surfaces is mutable. The public show is RSS-ingested from
cortech.online, whose `<title>` comes from the manifest entry, so it is ordinary data.
The private Save-to-Spotify show stays frozen — metadata is immutable after creation,
and delete-and-recreate on a show at its 60-episode cap would destroy a published
episode.

`#128` made the slug come from `slug_for_date(<date>)` alone, so a retitle updates each
episode in place rather than duplicating it. That property is the entire basis of the
tool, so `retitle_entries` **re-proves it per entry**: an entry whose `pubDate` does not
reproduce its slug stops the run instead of getting a date tail naming a different day
than its own permalink.

## Design decisions

- **Format is #139's, not a second one.** The topic phrases are checked-in *data*; the
  title is composed by `orchestrate.episode_title`. A test asserts that delegation
  directly, and another asserts that 2026-08-20 gets exactly the worked example
  SKILL.md documents.
- **Idempotent because the titles are a fixed table**, not a fresh generation. A second
  `--apply` writes nothing and fires no rebuild.
- **The raw material was the trap.** Chapter titles and summaries are narration text: 16
  of 75 carry letter-spaced acronyms (`"Anthropic's two trillion dollar I P O path"`)
  and spelled-out numerals in exactly the fields worth mining. `check_topics` screens
  for both, plus non-ASCII, commas, a lowercase leading topic, and the 2-3 word band —
  parsed from `orchestrate.TITLE_TOPIC_WORDS` so it cannot drift. All 75 were then read
  by eye; ten were reworded on that pass.
- **`compose_title` is fail-closed where the live path degrades.** `episode_title` drops
  a trailing topic over the cap, which is right for an episode that must ship and wrong
  for a back-fill that would silently lose a searchable keyword. It raises instead.
- **`assert_title_only` gates every write** — only `title` may differ, and the slug
  sequence may not move. A manifest that fails the consumer's `episodeSchema` empties
  the **entire** public feed, silently.
- **Dry run is the default**, `--only` is the canary, `--apply` backs the current
  manifest up to `~/.config/daily-podcast/manifest-backups/` *before* it PUTs, and a
  typo'd `--only` slug fails rather than no-opping (a silent no-op is the worst outcome
  on the canary step).
- **`--apply` fires the Pages deploy hook** through `resolve_pages_hook_url` —
  cortech.online is a static build that reads the manifest at build time and nothing on
  its side rebuilds on a schedule, so without it the rewrite stays invisible until the
  next episode ships.
- **Deliberately not routed through `upsert_manifest`**, which re-sorts and caps to 200
  entries (#124) — right for adding an episode, wrong for rewriting in place.

## The cover decision, made explicitly

**Covers are not regenerated.** `build_cover` renders `title[:48]` as a small hint line
under the date, so the 75 published covers keep reading `Daily Digest - <date>` while
their feed titles go topical. Regenerating would mean re-PUTting each `<slug>.jpg` at an
unchanged URL under the publish's `immutable, max-age=31536000` cache-control — so CDN
and Spotify copies would keep the old art anyway — and the hard 48-character cut would
swap a correct-if-generic line for a mid-word chop. The cover's primary subtitle, the
date, stays correct either way. Recorded in the module docstring and CLAUDE.md.

## Verification

Against the **live** manifest, read-only:

```
75 of 75 entries retitled (0 table slugs not in this manifest)
dry run — nothing written. Re-run with --apply to publish.
```

```
entries: 75 | changed: 75 | fields changed: ['title']
schema/copy violations: none
longest title: 96 chars (cap 100)
```

The second block runs a field-for-field replica of cortech.online's `episodeSchema` over
the post-rewrite manifest, plus the acceptance criteria on the copy itself: no title is
empty, still date-only, non-ASCII, or carrying a letter-spaced acronym.

`tests/data/published_slugs.tsv` is unmodified.

```
748 passed, 0 failed   (731 before this change)
ruff check   → All checks passed!
ruff format  → 18 files already formatted
```

Sample of the output:

```
The largest IPO, the MCP roadmap, rogue-model containment - August 23, 2026
Salt Typhoon, the CareCloud breach, Siemens PLC warnings - August 20, 2026
Anthropic's $11.5B quarter, SpaceX buys Cursor, PayPal's Stripe talks - August 15, 2026
Apple's OpenAI lawsuit, Claude's language values, Claude's rupee pricing - July 14, 2026
Cloudflare runs Claude, Anthropic's EU Mythos, AI math breakthrough - June 1, 2026
```

## Publishing plan (not done yet)

1. `--only daily-digest-august-20-2026 --apply` — one episode, hook fires.
2. Wait for the cortech.online rebuild; confirm on the public Spotify show that the
   episode's title updated **in place**: same guid, no duplicate.
3. Only then `--apply` for the other 74.

## Note on `pyproject.toml`

`orchestrate` and `retitle` join `known-first-party` so isort groups the sibling modules
consistently; that regroups one import in `tests/test_orchestrate.py`.

body:
## Train 10 — Real local dependency management

Turns the existing `emji` project metadata into a real recursive local/path package system without inventing a remote registry.

### Product
- strict `[dependencies]` declarations in `emojineer.toml`
- `emji add <package> <relative_path> [project]`
- `emji remove <package> [project]`
- recursive package graph resolution with package-name/root uniqueness
- dependency-key/target-package-name validation
- cycle diagnostics
- deterministic lockfile v2 with transitive dependency records
- SHA-256 content identity for canonical manifest + package-owned `.emoji` source
- ancestor hashes exclude direct and transitive dependency-owned source trees
- dependency source/manifest/graph changes make the root lock stale
- dependency entry/source-graph validation in `emji check`
- checkout-portable relative lock paths

### Boundaries
- local/path dependencies only
- no fake remote registry, version solver, download cache, or `publish`
- cross-package source import syntax is deliberately the next linker train; Train 10 does not weaken Train 8's package-root boundary with `../` module escapes
- no VM opcode or EMJBC format change
- no audit machinery

### Version
Advances CMake, `emojineer`, REPL, and `emji` to 0.10.

### Tests
Adds SHA-256 known vectors, recursive graph behavior, package hash ownership, cycle rejection-before-write, target-name validation, canonical dependency ordering, add/remove workflow, dependency lock drift, and relative-path validation.

Please perform a clean configure/build and full CTest. Focus on filesystem/symlink behavior, hash ownership boundaries, lock determinism across checkout roots, failed-add atomicity, recursive graph cycles/duplicates, and dependency source drift.

author: shoemoney
body:
The custom autograd functions in `torchao/prototype/qat/nvfp4.py` and `torchao/prototype/qat/mx.py` accept `bias` in forward and pass it to the addmm dispatch, but their backward returns `None` in the bias gradient slot. After `loss.backward()`, `linear.bias.grad` is `None`, so the optimizer never updates any bias for the entire QAT run. There is no error; the model just trains with frozen biases and silently degraded accuracy.

The mainline sibling `FakeQuantizedLinear` (`torchao/quantization/qat/linear.py`, `F.linear(x, w, self.bias)`) trains bias normally through autograd, so only the NVFP4 and MX prototype paths are affected. The existing regression tests for these paths use bias=False models (`M`/`Sub` in `test_qat.py`), which is why they cannot catch this.

Fix: record bias presence on `ctx` in forward, and return the bias gradient in backward: `grad_output.sum(0)` for NVFP4 (grad_output is always 2D there, the module flattens 3D inputs before `apply`) and `grad_output_2d.sum(0)` for MX. Return `None` when bias is absent.

Tests: `M`/`Sub` gain an optional `bias` arg (default False, existing callers unchanged). `test_qat_nvfp4_training` is parametrized over `use_bias` and asserts bias gradients flow and are nonzero. `test_mx_fake_quantized_linear_backward` (already parametrized over bias) now asserts `bias.grad` exists and matches the reference `nn.Linear` bias gradient. Full `test_qat.py`: 141 passed, 48 skipped (CUDA-gated), no failures. Verified the gradient mechanism on CPU by calling the autograd functions directly: bias grad was `None` before and matches `grad_output.sum(0)` after; the new test parametrizations themselves are CUDA-gated like their neighbors.

author: pythonlearner1025
body:
## What part this touches

A workspace in the webApp has a right-hand drawer. One tab of that drawer is Connections. `packages/webapp/src/WorkspaceConnectionsPanel.tsx` draws that tab. It draws three sections in order: Wanted here (pending connect requests), Connections (the provider rows), and Recent activity. Recent activity is a log of credential events — minted, revoked, and so on. The panel reads that log with the hook `useWorkspaceCredentialEvents`. The hook calls the control-plane route through `listCredentialEvents` on the API client. The component `WorkspaceEventsPanel` draws the rows. `packages/webapp/src/WorkspaceDrawer.tsx` re-exports the hook, the component, and the type, so hosts and tests import them from one place.

## The gap

The Recent activity section shows in the Connections tab today. The owner ruled on 2026-08-24 that members must not see it. The ruling hides the section only. The event data, the control-plane route, and the wire types must all stay. So this is a render change, not a deletion.

## The fix

Stop rendering the Recent activity heading and the events panel in `WorkspaceConnectionsPanel`.
Remove the now-orphaned `useWorkspaceCredentialEvents` call site in that panel, and the `activity` flag that gated the section.
Keep `useWorkspaceCredentialEvents`, `WorkspaceEventsPanel`, `WorkspaceEventFeed`, the drawer re-exports, the API client method, and the control-plane route exactly as they are.

## The risk trade

The events UI goes dark. Nobody can read the credential log in the product now. That is the ruling, so it is the intended cost.

The cost stays low because nothing was deleted. The route still answers. The hook still compiles and is still exported. Re-enabling the section is one render block in one file.

There is no flag. A flag was the rejected alternative. A flag adds a second state to test and to reason about, and the ruling asked for a thin change, not a toggle.

## Tests

`npm test` passes: 485 control-plane, 121 box actor, 238 webApp, plus the guest and house-rule suites. All green.

One test changed. `packages/webapp/test/credentials-surfaces-v2.test.tsx` pinned the section headings. It expected `['Wanted here', 'Connections', 'Recent activity']`. It now expects `['Wanted here', 'Connections']`, and its name says the section is hidden. That test fails without the rename of the expectation, which is the pin doing its job.

No test covers `WorkspaceEventsPanel` on its own, so no coverage was lost.

`npm run typecheck` passes. `npm run lint:gate` passes with 108 anti-slop findings and 0 blitz-house findings, both at baseline.

## Deploy

The webApp bundle ships inside the control-plane worker. The deploy script builds it into the worker assets. So the worker deploy is the only artifact. No box image rebuild. No Go change. No migration.

Canary first, then client prod, per the standard sequence.

```sh
npm run deploy -w packages/control-plane
```

Verify on the canary: open a workspace, open the Connections tab, confirm no Recent activity heading.

Roll back with a revert of this commit, then deploy the worker again.

author: tianyi-zhang-02
body:
# What does this PR do ?

`record_to_train_batch`, the SingleController's payload builder, writes

```python
sample_mask = torch.ones(n, dtype=torch.float32)
```

and never looks at the completion it is converting. `grpo.py` builds the same field from `DatumSpec.loss_multiplier` and zeroes it in two places — `_apply_mask_sample_filter` for env-flagged samples, and, under `grpo.overlong_filtering`, for truncated ones (`grpo_train` and `async_grpo_train`). Neither happens on SC, so a truncated or env-flagged rollout is trained on at full weight.

| | `grpo.py` | SC before | SC after |
|---|---|---|---|
| starting value | `DatumSpec.loss_multiplier` | `1.0` | `DatumSpec.loss_multiplier` |
| env-flagged (`mask_sample`) | `0` | `1.0` | `0` |
| truncated, `overlong_filtering: true` | `0` | `1.0` | `0` |

**Both per-completion signals were already on the `Completion`; only the consumer was missing.** The prompt-level starting weight was not — see the correction below.** `RolloutManager._result_to_completion` computes `truncated` and, when `mask_env_flagged_samples` is off, pops the env flag out of `instance_config`:

```python
# Same gate as the batched path: when masking is off, drop the env
# mask flag so later batch building never sees it.
if not self._mask_env_flagged_samples:
    (result["full_result"].get("instance_config") or {}).pop("mask_sample", None)
```

The flag *surviving* is meant to mean something to "later batch building". The later batch building never read it. So the data and the gate were both already correct, and the read is what this adds — `build_sample_mask` uses the same extraction as `rollouts._extract_mask_sample_flags`.

`grpo.overlong_filtering` is threaded to it through `TQReplayBuffer`, next to the existing `require_routed_experts`.

# Issues

Implements the SC side of #2625's unchecked item: *"**Optional env-flagged sample masking.** Gate NeMo-Gym env-flagged sample dropping (default on) behind `grpo.mask_env_flagged_samples` … (Landed in grpo #3402.)"* SC already wires `mask_env_flagged_samples` into the rollout manager (`single_controller_utils/setup.py`); this makes the flag it gates actually reach the loss.

# Usage

No new config. Two knobs start working on SC: `grpo.overlong_filtering` and `env.*.mask_env_flagged_samples`.

**Worth flagging before merge:** for a run that already sets either knob, this changes the effective batch — rows that were trained at weight 1.0 are now dropped from the loss. That is the documented intent of both knobs and matches `grpo.py`, but it will move numbers on any SC run currently using them, so it is not a silent no-op change.

# Before your PR is "Ready for review"

- [x] Make sure you read and followed [Contributor guidelines](/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Did you write any new necessary tests?
- [x] Did you run the unit tests and functional tests locally? (unit only)
- [ ] Did you add or update any necessary documentation?

# Additional Information

**One consequence I did not see until I went looking for it, and it needs a decision.**

This PR makes a pre-existing guard reachable that was effectively dead before. `single_controller.py` raises

```
SingleController has no valid response tokens after filtering.
```

when no chunk in a step had valid tokens. Until now `sample_mask` was all-ones on this path, so only `seq_logprob_error_threshold` could trigger it. With this PR, `overlong_filtering` or env-flagged masking can too — and if they filter every sample in a step, the run dies.

The path this PR claims parity with does not do that. `grpo.py` zeroes `loss_multiplier` and carries on: the loss reduces to zero, the optimizer takes a zero-gradient step, training continues. I checked `_apply_mask_sample_filter` and the `overlong_filtering` block; neither has a guard, by design.

So the two paths now disagree in the worst direction — benign on legacy, run-killing on SC — on a config the user deliberately enabled.

I do not think I should pick the semantics here, because the guard is not wrong in general:

- under `seq_logprob_error_threshold`, an all-filtered step means something is broken and failing loudly is right;
- under `overlong_filtering` or env-flagged masking, an all-filtered step is the feature working as asked, and legacy's zero-gradient step is right.

Two ways to settle it, happy to send either:

1. **Match legacy** — let an all-filtered step through as a zero-gradient step, and log it. Simplest, and matches the path this PR is porting.
2. **Distinguish the causes** — keep the raise for threshold filtering, let the requested filters through. More faithful to why the guard exists, more moving parts.

Reachability, so nobody has to guess: it needs *every* sample in *every* chunk of a step filtered. That takes a `max_total_sequence_length` short enough that the whole batch truncates, or an environment flagging everything. Rare, not impossible — and the failure mode is a dead run rather than a bad number, which is why I am raising it rather than filing it as a follow-up.



Seven tests in `tests/unit/experience/test_payload.py`, driving `record_to_train_batch` end to end on that file's existing `_completion`/`_record` builders (extended with `truncated` and `mask_sample`): the opt-in behaviour of `overlong_filtering`, the env flag applying either way, `mask_sample: false` and a missing `instance_config` both being no-ops, both signals on one row, and the dtype.

`tests/unit/experience/` + `tests/unit/single_controller/` + `test_grpo.py` go 744 → 751 passed, no new failures. `ruff` 0.9.9 check, `--select I` and `format --check` clean. Python 3.13.13, Linux.

`tests/unit/single_controller/test_tq_replay_buffer.py` stubs `record_to_train_batch` to bypass the real converter; its stub takes the new keyword. That is the only reason a test file outside `experience/` is touched.

One thing I did not do: `grpo.py` also reports `num_mask_sample_filtered` as a metric, and SC still has no equivalent. Adding it means threading a count out of the buffer commit into the SC metrics dict, which felt like a separate change — happy to add it here if you would rather it landed together.

cc @yuki-97 for review or routing to the right person :)

## Corrections after re-reading my own diff

Three things the description above got wrong. All three are in the direction of *understating* what this changes, which is worth fixing before review.

**The starting value is no longer `1.0`.** `build_sample_mask` now starts from the prompt's `DatumSpec.loss_multiplier`, carried through a new `PromptGroupRecord.loss_multiplier` field and filled from `input_sample["loss_multiplier"]` at both `RolloutManager.run_rollout` call sites. So the table row should read `DatumSpec.loss_multiplier`, not `1.0`, and there are tests for it: `test_sample_mask_starts_from_the_prompt_loss_multiplier` and `test_record_to_train_batch_honors_the_prompt_loss_multiplier`.

**So this touches the producer, not only the consumer.** The two *per-completion* signals were already on the `Completion`. The prompt-level weight was not — `processors.py` zeroes `DatumSpec.loss_multiplier` for a prompt truncated at dataset-processing time, and nothing on the rollout path recorded it. That is a new field plus producer wiring, not just a read.

**`grpo.overlong_filtering` does not "parse and do nothing" today — it is rejected.** `_validate_algo_settings` lists it in `unsupported` and raises `NotImplementedError` at setup (`single_controller_utils/config.py:739`). This PR removes that entry *because* the path now implements it. The env-flagged knob is the one that parses and is silently ignored.

author: ncosentino
body:
Advances #33: provides the sealed crash journal that the pairing state machine will
mutate in later slices.

## Schema v11

`daemon_pairing` stores only bounded operational metadata plus one sealed checkpoint:

- 16-byte `PairingId` primary key and unique 32-byte `RoutingId`;
- local joiner/inviter role;
- finite role-compatible phase;
- immutable authorization deadline;
- optional post-commit completion deadline;
- monotonic pairing-route replay cursor;
- compare-and-swap generation; and
- sealed secret-bearing state.

SQL CHECKs enforce identifier widths, role/phase compatibility, positive deadlines and
generations, nonnegative replay progress, and completion-deadline shape. Active pairing
discovery is bounded to 32 and paginated in deterministic BLOB identifier order.

## Authenticated metadata

The state may later contain the transferable capability, pairing secret, decrypted
stage payloads, and exact outbound records. It is `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` and the
checkpoint type is neither Clone nor Debug.

Every unsealed column is authenticated as AEAD context:

`profile length || profile || scope || pairing || route || role || phase ||
authorization deadline || completion deadline-or-zero || replay cursor || generation`

The variable profile is length-prefixed and all remaining fields are fixed width. At
the maximum profile length this is 116 bytes under SecretRecordContext's 128-byte
bound; a test exercises that maximum. Moving a blob across profiles, pairings, routes,
roles, phases, deadlines, cursors, or generations makes open fail.

`SecretRecordKind::PairingOperation = 15` is appended; existing discriminants 1–14
remain unchanged, preserving all current at-rest AAD contracts.

## Idempotency and concurrency

Initial reservation is idempotent only when the complete metadata and plaintext state
are byte-identical. Reusing either PairingId or RoutingId for different state returns a
bounded duplicate-operation failure.

Checkpoint replacement uses `UPDATE ... WHERE generation = expected`. A lost-response
retry is success only when the observed row is exactly `expected + 1` and phase,
completion deadline, replay cursor, and plaintext state all match the intended write.
A same-generation different write fails. Generation zero and overflow fail closed.

Replay progress can stay equal or advance but cannot regress. The future state machine
owns when it is safe to advance after processing or deliberately skipping one relay
record.

## Deadlines and terminal state

The authorization deadline is immutable. The completion deadline can first appear only
when the inviter transitions from awaiting JoinProof to awaiting completion after the
add-member commit. Once set it can never be extended, shortened, cleared, or changed;
it remains authenticated through completion or compensation.

Role-specific transitions are an explicit allowlist. Same-phase checkpoints are
allowed only while nonterminal. Completed and cancelled state cannot mutate and is the
only state eligible for deletion.

## Migration

Every supported v1–v9 migration now proceeds through the existing v10 remote-event
schema and then the new v11 transaction. A crash between transactions leaves a valid,
retryable v10 database. A forced v11 table conflict proves the transaction returns a
storage error, preserves `user_version = 10`, and leaves the pre-existing table intact.

## Tests

Focused coverage proves:

- sealed state does not appear in raw SQLite bytes;
- identical reserve/retry succeeds, conflicting PairingId or RoutingId reuse fails;
- CAS retry identity and conflicting retry behavior;
- generation-zero and replay-cursor regression rejection;
- role/phase mismatch and deadline regression rejection;
- post-commit deadline is required and immutable;
- terminal immutability and terminal-only deletion;
- unsealed metadata and sealed ciphertext tampering fail authentication;
- active pagination excludes terminal rows and resumes after a BLOB identifier;
- maximum profile ID fits authenticated context; and
- successful and forced-failure v10→v11 migration.

The complete existing daemon suite also passes after every downgrade fixture was
updated to remove the v11 table before reconstructing an older schema.

## Security review

Focused review returned **APPROVE**, with no high-confidence exploitable or
correctness-security findings. It verified AAD completeness and injectivity, metadata
coercion and NULL/zero handling, PairingId and RoutingId collision behavior, atomic CAS
and lost-response semantics, role-specific transitions, replay monotonicity, migration
recoverability, deterministic pagination, plaintext/error hygiene, and additive
at-rest compatibility.

Three non-blocking notes were addressed or recorded:

- metadata and blob are now selected in one query, eliminating a transient mixed-read
  liveness failure under concurrent checkpointing;
- generation zero is explicitly rejected and retry arithmetic is checked; and
- once the completion deadline appears it is immutable and retained through terminal
  state, preventing an implementation from extending its compensation window forever.

An offline attacker can still restore an entire older valid database row or database
file. AEAD prevents forgery, not rollback. Anti-rollback would require a monotonic
anchor outside SQLite; ADR 0006 and this change do not claim it.

## Validation

- `cargo test --workspace` — pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — pass.
- `cargo fmt --all` — pass.
- fuzz target locked compile — pass.
- diff and output retention — pass.

## Not in this change

The sealed checkpoint payload is intentionally opaque to persistence. The next slice
defines its bounded state codec and exact inbound/outbound logical-message history,
then the pairing service will use these CAS APIs to submit and replay stages.

author: thebhef
body:
An event row draws a chip per thing the event is about — a message, a
signal, another event it is linked to (ADR 0056) — but the chips were
display-only. Dropping a reference meant reconstructing the gesture that
made it: to unlink a pair you had to find both events in the events
panel, select exactly those two, and press the toolbar's Unlink control,
for a link the row was already showing you. The chip is where the
reference is visible, so it is where removing it belongs.

Each chip now carries an ×. Which command it runs depends on what the
chip names, and the two differ in more than spelling:

  - A link is a pair. It is stored on one end but true of both, so
    either row may drop it — including a host-derived event's, whose
    own subject list is not editable.
  - A structural reference lives on the event's own subject list, so
    only an editable event can lose one. That path calls
    `set_note_subjects`, a host command that has existed since the
    subject model landed with no frontend caller until now.

`useRemoveChip` is the one implementation both event-bearing views use,
so an × means the same thing in the trace as in the events panel, and
`chipRemovable` states the editable rule once.

Two smaller fixes ride along, both visible on the same chip. The label
had `overflow: hidden` and `text-overflow: ellipsis` but no
`white-space: nowrap`, so it wrapped instead of ellipsising and a long
name grew the chip past a fixed-height row — the missing property is the
whole of that fix. And a link chip now takes the linked event's own
colour rather than a fixed one, so the chip and the marker it points at
read as the same thing.

Worth a reviewer's attention: the chip is drawn in two places — the
fitted strip on the collapsed row and the full list in the disclosed
body — which had drifted into two copies of the markup. They are one
`SubjectChipView` now, and the strip's `data-toolbar-fit` key is passed
in rather than assumed, since only the strip is measured.

author: blandisc
body:
## Qué

Las tres frases del acto 4 del onboarding interpolaban varios números con `%lld` crudo y **sin variación de plural**, así que en N=1 rompían la gramática en inglés **y** español: «1 nights», «1 noches», «1 días».

- `onb.4.historia` (días, noches)
- `onb.4.calibrando.cuerpo` (días, noches, meta)
- `onb.4.calibrando.cuerpo.sinhoy` (días, noches)

Como cada frase pluraliza varios números de forma **independiente**, se pasan al formato de **diccionario de sustitución** del catálogo (tokens `%1$#@days@` + bloque `substitutions` con `variations.plural` one/other por token, en `en` y `es`). El posesivo español se absorbe en el token para concordar con el número: **«tu 1 día … tu 1 noche»** en singular, **«tus N días … tus N noches»** en plural. `meta` (p. ej. 60) es un número pelón sin sustantivo, se interpola tal cual (`%3$lld` mezclado con los tokens).

Los call sites de `OnbCopy` —`String(format: String(localized:…), args)`— **no cambian**: `String(localized:)` devuelve la plantilla con los tokens y `String(format:)` los expande.

## Verificación

- **Render real (no solo build):** compilé el catálogo con `xcstringstool` y ejercí el camino EXACTO de los call sites (`String(localized:)` → `String(format:)`) contra esa salida compilada, en `en` y `es`. Todos los casos correctos, incluido el posesivo: `1 noche`/`2 noches`, `tu 1 día … tu 1 noche`, `tus 30 días … tus 5 noches`, `junte 60`.
- **`Tools/verify.sh auto`:** ✅ `TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED` — la app y los targets de test compilan con el catálogo nuevo.
- **Linters:** i18n-guard, ciclos xcstrings y design-drift en verde.
- **Regresión:** `CenitUnitTests/OnboardingPluralesTests.swift` ejerce en/es (el español se lee de `es.lproj` a mano porque la suite corre en inglés) y falla con el catálogo viejo. Correrá en el lane nocturno `ios-app`.

Carril **ligero** · P2 · deuda **ONB-01** declarada fuera de alcance en FER-141.

Closes FER-142.
