author: thebhef
body:
A note's label is truncated everywhere it is drawn. The plot marker caps
it at fifty characters; the trace row ellipsises it at whatever width the
panel has. Neither surface offered the rest, and the disclosed body — the
one place with room — showed only the tag and the description. A note
whose text ran long was unreadable in the application that stored it.

The body now leads with a `label` row carrying the whole thing. It is the
one body value allowed to wrap, and it claims as many rows of the row
space as it needs (sixty characters a row, capped at four), so the row
heights, the scroll extent and the keyboard cursor still agree on how
tall an open event is — the invariant `contentCountOf` exists to keep.

Two consequences a reviewer should weigh:

  - **A read-only event with a long label now opens.** `eventDiscloses`
    previously said no unless the event carried a tag, a description or
    a subject. A bus-error event has none of those and exactly the kind
    of generated label that overruns, so its text had nowhere to be
    read at all. It discloses when its label needs more than one row;
    a short one still does not.
  - **The wrapped label is one field, not N.** The continuation rows
    exist only to carry the ids `aria-activedescendant` names them by;
    the label element spans their height and the spacers are inert. So
    arrowing down walks the label's rows without the text fragmenting
    into separate fields, and no cursor position names an id that has
    no element.

The row is editable in place like the tag and the description, which
makes the body a second way to rename an event beside the ✎ button and
double-clicking the row label. That follows the surrounding pattern
rather than inventing a read-only variant of `EventBodyField`.

author: timchristensen89-boop
body:
Second fix batch from the review — the outsider-reachable paths. Adds two deps (`express-rate-limit`, `helmet`); `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes, so the container build is unaffected.

## C5 · Rate limiting — there was none, anywhere
Login, PIN checks and gift-card routes were open to unbounded brute force. Added `express-rate-limit` with **venue-safe** windows — sized to kill an automated sweep without ever tripping a whole venue behind one NAT IP in normal service:

| paths | window |
|---|---|
| password login + reset request | 30 / 15 min |
| device PIN login + manager approval | 120 / 5 min |
| gift-card public routes + promo quote | 100 / 5 min |
| reserve public routes | 60 / 10 min |

Mounted below the webhook and cron routes, so neither is ever throttled.

## C5 · `trust proxy` + `helmet`
The app never set `trust proxy`, so behind Caddy every request's IP was the proxy and the per-IP throttles (new and existing) couldn't tell clients apart — set to one hop. Added `helmet` with **CSP and the cross-origin isolation headers off on purpose**: this is a JSON API whose browser clients are on other origins (CORS handles them), and helmet's CORP/COEP defaults would block those reads. HSTS, no-sniff, frame-deny and referrer policy stay on.

## H11 · Staff invite tokens
`GET /api/staff/invites` had no `requireManager` (its siblings all do) and returned raw rows including the **token** — the credential that sets a password on a new hire's account. Now manager-only, and the token is dropped from the list payload (nothing in the UI read it).

## M7 · Gift-card codes in logs
The failure-context logger and the redeem success line both wrote the full code — the bearer secret — to stdout. Both now log only `***<last 4>`.

## C4 (partial) · Print-poll status write
The `SetResponse` branch marked a print job done/failed by id with **no station scoping**, so an anonymous caller could mark any station's jobs. Scoped to the polling station. The deeper print-auth rethink (a per-station secret) needs a coordinated print-bridge change and is left for that — flagged.

## Verification
- `@alma/api` suite: 662 pass, 0 fail. Typecheck clean. helmet + express-rate-limit resolve and construct as middleware. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes.

author: thebhef
body:
Three of a plot panel's readouts belong to the *column* rather than to
any one axis: the x-axis time label and the A/B cursor delta at the
bottom, the event marker labels at the top. Each was anchored
positionally — `idx === 0`, `idx === renderedAxes.length - 1` — and a
collapsed area is a heading row with no canvas and no uPlot behind it.
So collapsing the bottom area took the time label and the delta chip
with it, and collapsing the top area took the marker labels. Three
reports, one cause.

`bottomDrawingAxis` and `topDrawingAxis` answer the question the props
were really asking: the lowest, and highest, axis that still has a
canvas. When the whole stack is collapsed the answer is unobservable,
and the panel deliberately holds the flag still rather than moving it —
`isLast` is a uPlot-rebuild input, and letting it flip on a canvas-less
axis buys a rebuild that paints nothing. That is not a micro-optimisation
bolted on afterwards: the first cut of this change failed the
resample-budget test in `PlotPanel.dom.test.tsx`, which is what surfaced
it.

The A/B cursors also stop repeating their timestamps down the stack.
Their *lines* still cross every area — that is what lines a reading in
one area up with a reading in another — but one x is one time however
many areas it crosses, so the chip is drawn once, beside the x-axis
label and the delta it belongs with.

ADR 0026 is amended in the same change, because it recorded the opposite
rule. Cursor labels were moved to "every axis" precisely because adding
a plot area used to hide them; that fix addressed the symptom, and
"bottom *drawing* axis" addresses the cause, so the old failure cannot
return. The four new panel tests are written to go red against the
positional version — each reproduces a reported symptom directly.

author: pedronxp
body:
## Objetivo

Separar o módulo de comunicações da operação do WhatsApp, tornar o bot realmente multi-organização e oferecer ao Console TCS e ao portal municipal uma leitura confiável da saúde do serviço e de cada organização.

O fluxo foi pensado principalmente para comunicados da Defesa Civil destinados à população, bairros, grupos e comunidades do WhatsApp.

## Problema resolvido

Antes, `/app/comunicacoes` e `/app/whatsapp` apresentavam praticamente a mesma operação. Além disso, o painel podia mostrar um número como vinculado mesmo quando a conexão real já havia caído, e o status global do Docker não permitia descobrir qual organização precisava de suporte.

Este PR separa responsabilidades, adiciona heartbeat real e impede que sessões, canais ou entregas de uma organização sejam misturados com outra.

## Principais alterações

### Rotas e experiência

- `/app/comunicacoes`: criação, publicação, agendamento e histórico dos comunicados.
- `/app/whatsapp`: visão de suporte das organizações habilitadas no módulo.
- `/app/whatsapp/:orgId`: operação dos números de uma organização.
- `/app/whatsapp/:orgId/comunidades`: gestão dedicada das comunidades e grupos.
- `/portal/municipal/whatsapp`: operação municipal com acesso controlado pelo módulo e pelas permissões do usuário.
- Indicadores do bot adicionados ao Console TCS e ao painel municipal.
- Organizações sem o módulo aparecem como `Módulo não habilitado`, sem serem classificadas incorretamente como offline.

### Monitoramento por organização

- Heartbeat do worker a cada 20 segundos.
- Heartbeat independente para cada sessão WhatsApp.
- Estados consolidados: `online`, `operação parcial`, `reconectando`, `aguardando QR`, `pausado`, `fora do ar`, `Docker fora do ar`, `não configurado` e `banido`.
- Contagem `números online / números configurados` por organização.
- Registro do último heartbeat, da última transição e do último erro da sessão.
- Transições relevantes geram eventos para a caixa de mensagens do Console e da organização, sem criar uma notificação a cada heartbeat.

### Segurança e isolamento

- Cada sessão, canal, comunicado e entrega é validado contra a organização correta.
- Triggers de banco bloqueiam entregas cruzadas entre organizações.
- Endpoints de QR, verificação e controle exigem JWT válido e permissão no módulo.
- `/healthz` continua público, mas devolve apenas `{ "ok": true }`.
- Estado de autenticação do WhatsApp é criptografado no Supabase.
- Heartbeats e erros operacionais ficam em tabelas do schema `private`.
- QR Code não é mais impresso nos logs do Render; ele aparece somente no painel autorizado.
- A chave `service_role` permanece exclusivamente no bot hospedado.

### Caixa de mensagens e ajuda

- Caixa de mensagens unificada entre Console TCS, organização e conta individual.
- Eventos dinâmicos para alterações de comunicação e do bot.
- Tutoriais contextuais com opção de não exibir novamente.
- Tutorial redesenhado para não bloquear a tela inteira durante o atendimento.

### Melhorias complementares do painel

- Ajustes de densidade, filtros e hierarquia visual em comunicados, assinaturas, formulários, clientes e equipe municipal.
- Gestão individual de membro da equipe em rota própria.
- Correções de navegação, títulos e permissões de owner.

## Banco de dados

Migrações incluídas:

- `20260824013135_unified_inbox_whatsapp_access_tutorials.sql`
- `20260824024000_whatsapp_session_operations.sql`
- `20260824035557_bot_runtime_monitoring.sql`
- `20260824093000_bot_organization_isolation.sql`
- `20260824094500_bot_http_authorization.sql`

As migrações do WhatsApp já foram aplicadas e verificadas no projeto Supabase atual. As tabelas novas usam RLS, grants explícitos e funções com acesso restrito.

## Infraestrutura

- Blueprint `render.yaml` adicionado.
- Bot publicado como Docker no plano gratuito do Render.
- Health check: `https://tcs-whatsapp-bot-cataguases.onrender.com/healthz`.
- Serviço mantido acordado por verificação externa do cron-job.org a cada 5 minutos.
- O serviço do Render está com `autoDeploy` desligado e apontando atualmente para `codex/whatsapp-defesa-civil`.

## Validação executada

- [x] Build completo do dashboard.
- [x] 62 arquivos de teste do dashboard aprovados.
- [x] 352 testes do dashboard aprovados.
- [x] 3 testes de isolamento do bot aprovados.
- [x] Validação de sintaxe do worker Node.js.
- [x] Migração aplicada no Supabase.
- [x] Leitura do estado consolidado por organização validada.
- [x] Geração e roteamento de evento para a caixa de mensagens validados em transação com rollback.
- [x] Deploy do bot no Render concluído.
- [x] `/healthz` respondendo HTTP 200 com `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- [x] Heartbeat real do worker e das sessões confirmado em produção.
- [x] Dashboard local respondendo em `http://127.0.0.1:5173`.

## Estado atual do piloto

- Docker do bot: **online**.
- Organização piloto: **Prefeitura de Cataguases**.
- Estado atual: **Aguardando QR**.
- Números online: **0 de 2**.

Esse estado é esperado até que um responsável leia um novo QR pelo painel da organização.

## Atenção antes/depois do merge

- [ ] Revisar a ordem e o conteúdo das cinco migrações listadas acima.
- [ ] Confirmar que `VITE_BOT_WHATSAPP_URL` no Netlify aponta para o serviço do Render.
- [ ] Liberar ou renovar os créditos da conta Netlify. O deploy desta branch foi recusado com `Skipped due to account credit usage exceeded`; não houve falha de build do código.
- [ ] Após liberar o Netlify, publicar o dashboard e validar `/app/whatsapp`, `/app/whatsapp/:orgId` e `/portal/municipal/whatsapp`.
- [ ] Depois do merge, alterar a branch do serviço Render para `main` ou disparar manualmente um deploy do commit de merge.
- [ ] Ler o QR de pelo menos um número oficial de Cataguases e confirmar que o estado muda para `Online`.
- [ ] Confirmar que uma organização sem o módulo aparece como `Módulo não habilitado`.
- [ ] Confirmar que membros sem permissão no módulo continuam sem acesso à operação do WhatsApp.

## Risco e rollback

- O bot mantém mensagens pendentes na fila quando o Docker ou a sessão fica offline.
- Heartbeats não alteram comunicados nem entregas; apenas atualizam estado operacional privado.
- O painel continua acessível durante indisponibilidade do bot.
- Para rollback de aplicação, voltar o dashboard e o worker ao commit anterior. Não remover tabelas de runtime enquanto houver worker reportando heartbeat; elas podem permanecer sem impacto caso o código seja revertido.

## Resultado esperado após o merge

O time TCS consegue abrir `/app/whatsapp`, identificar exatamente qual organização está online, parcial, pausada ou fora do ar e entrar na operação correta. No portal municipal, cada organização enxerga apenas seus próprios números, comunidades, estados e mensagens.

author: matthewjhunter
body:
A live client reads the structured channel, not the text channel, and everything memstore sent there was either unprotected or empty.

The text channel has carried a nonce fence for a year. The structured channel shipped stored content raw, so a client that prefers it saw no delimiters at all. Typed structs cannot carry the boundary -- `FactResult` declares `id` first and a live client delivered the fields alphabetized, so containment expressed as field order breaks on one re-serializing hop. The read tools now return `fence.Envelope{framing, nonce, payload}`, with the marshalled result sealed between `<untrusted-NONCE>` tags inside a single string value. Citable fact ids ride in the framing, outside the fence: sealing the whole result would put every id inside the untrusted region, and ids are the one thing the instructions tell the model to act on. Cost, stated plainly: `tools/list` advertises an envelope rather than the fact shape, and callers recover the struct with `Envelope.Unseal`.

The failure paths then needed the same treatment. Every failure return handed its message to the text channel alone and left the structured channel an all-empty struct, so a structured-only client got `{"framing":"","nonce":"","payload":""}` for "query is required", for an empty store, and for a seal failure alike. `fence.Notice` puts the neutralized message in the framing and mints no fence -- a boundary around nothing advertises an untrusted region that does not exist.

That exposed a second bug on top of it: `IsError=true` makes Claude Code render the text block and drop `StructuredContent`, so the framing added for exactly this case went out on the wire and vanished. A missing argument is not memstore failing at something it was asked to do, so validation returns in both the read and write tools now report `Status: "invalid_input"` with `IsError` unset. Genuine failures keep the flag, covered by `TestStoreFailuresKeepIsError`.

Docs: the session instructions describe an envelope whose payload arrives sealed, but said nothing about results carrying no stored content -- the natural reading of an empty payload is "returned nothing", wrong in exactly the case where the framing is the error message. Also states that the citation duty outlives the turn the fact was retrieved in and covers paraphrase, both after live misses.

Not converted: naming a fact or link that does not exist. It arrives as an ordinary store error with no sentinel, so the handler cannot tell it from a query that failed. Needs a `memstore.ErrNotFound` first.

Verified against the restarted server: blank-query search returns a framed envelope, contentless store returns `invalid_input` on the typed channel with no error flag, full suite green.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: thebhef
body:
An event label is free text and the plot drew it as a single chip, so a
long one ran across the area and over its neighbours' markers.
`wrapMarkerLabel` lays it out as at most two lines, ellipsising when it
does not fit. The budget is fifty characters rather than a fraction of
the plot: a third of a 4K plot is still a paragraph, and a chip should
be the same size whatever monitor it lands on. It is still clamped to
the plot width, so a narrow area wraps at the area instead.

Two smaller corrections to how a highlight reads:

  - Unlit markers were faded to 0.28, which was dim enough to lose
    them. 0.6 keeps what the highlight is *not* about legible, which is
    the point of fading rather than hiding.
  - Lit markers now draw last (`litLast`). Draw order was list order,
    so the event a reader had selected could be buried under a quiet
    neighbour's label chip — fading the neighbours and then painting
    one of them over the lit marker says two opposite things at once.
    Stable within each group, and a no-op at rest.

Reviewers should look at the canvas-level tests rather than the helper
tests. `wrapMarkerLabel` and `litLast` are pure and easy to pin, but the
question that matters is whether the layout reaches the plot — the draw
hook reads its inputs through a ref, so a change can be correct and
still never repaint. The new `PlotPanel.dom.test.tsx` cases drive the
recording context: they assert the wrapped lines, the ellipsis inside
the budget, that a selection triggers a redraw at all, and that the lit
label is the last one painted.

body:
## Lo medido, y lo que no

`CausaEncontrada.referencia` es un JWT: su carga va **firmada, no cifrada**, así que se lee. Su
`exp - iat` da **1.800 segundos exactos** (24 de agosto de 2026). Queda en
`SEGUNDOS_DECLARADOS_POR_LA_REFERENCIA`, con la fecha y con cuál token fue, y la prosa se deriva
de ahí.

Dos cosas que **no** se aplanaron, aunque aplanarlas se siente limpieza:

| | por qué no |
|---|---|
| `documento_referencia` | es OTRO token y no se midió. Derivarlo de la constante habría hecho la documentación más falsa |
| "caduca a los 30 minutos" | afirma lo que hace la plataforma. Medido está lo que el token DICE: entre las dos cosas hay una petición que nadie hizo. Ahora dice "declara durar" |

Y un test decía que la carga de esos JWT "va cifrada". Va firmada, y de leerla salió justamente
la duración que este PR mide.

## Guardia

Barre la prosa **y el código**, porque la copia que el modelo lee está en la descripción de un
campo. Visto en rojo dos veces: con `docs/verificacion.md` diciendo "caduca a los 30", y con la
salvedad de `documento_referencia` borrada.

author: shroominic
body:
## Summary

Partial implementation of #41. This branch is stacked on #68 and uses `feature/issue-36-source-aware-spine` as its base.

- Adds a Settings-only, compact local diary for meal, activity, and sleep entries.
- Persists typed manual events through the existing source-aware `HealthRepository`.
- Lets a person change the recorded event start date and time.
- Keeps the default glucose-reader view unchanged.
- Adds a typed `FastJournalRecentRiseProvider` seam for an optional one-time, newest-only observational link.

## Deliberate partial boundary

This does **not** close #41.

- Production defaults to **no rise cue**. It contains no glucose threshold, fixed time window, or trend detector. A future reviewed deterministic analytics policy (#37 / follow-up) must supply a qualified candidate.
- No Apple Health or Health Connect import/export work.
- No AI, photo capture, food database, templates, duplicate, edit/delete, final combined chart, or causal/medical conclusion.
- No fallback to an older rise; a supplied candidate can be linked only once.

## Privacy and safety

- New diary records stay in the existing local repository; this PR adds no network client, model call, or health-platform import.
- The UI and data model use non-causal wording only: a link records timing/proximity, not cause, treatment, or dosing advice.
- The diary is optional and is reachable from Settings so the glucose reader remains uncluttered.

## Risk / rollback (R2)

This adds persisted `sleep` event records and optional rise references to the local event JSON. An older app build cannot decode a newly saved `sleep` event. Do not downgrade an install after it has diary entries. If rollback is necessary, use a forward-compatible recovery build; any data removal needs an explicit user backup/consent decision. No SQLite schema migration is included.

## Validation

- `make format-check lint`
- `make test`
- Normal pre-commit hook
- Normal pre-push `make check` (including Android/web/iOS/macOS builds plus iOS and macOS native tests)

author: thebhef
body:
Linking two events, and dropping a link, were the only pointing gestures
in the event surface that Mod+Z could not reverse. A mis-clicked pair, or
an × pressed on the wrong chip, had no way back short of redoing the
gesture by hand.

Event links become a third undo stack beside the dockview layout and the
element registry, interleaved with them by the order log that already
exists, so one chord still reverses the most recent change whichever
stack it lives on.

**Steps, not snapshots.** The other two stacks snapshot what they cover,
because a view has a great deal of state and no natural inverse. A link
has exactly one inverse and three fields. Snapshotting the notes list
instead would hold strictly more state, be strictly more to put back, and
would quietly drag every other note edit into undo's reach on the way —
the boundary below would then be enforced by nothing but care.

The subtlety worth reviewing is `linkStoredOn`. The host stores a link on
one end though both ends read it, and an unlink is about to erase the
evidence of which end that was. So a step records the storing side, read
before the write, and a restore puts the reference back on that event
rather than on whichever end the caller happened to name first —
otherwise undoing an unlink would silently move the chip to the other
row. `useEventLinkUndo.dom.test.tsx` pins exactly that case.

ADR 0050 listed "notes / markers" as never undoable and closes by saying
the allowlist should not be broadened lightly, so it is amended here
rather than left contradicting the code. Its safety argument was never
about notes — it is about not surprising an operator into transmitting —
and nothing in the rationale resists this. The new line is drawn on the
ADR's own asymmetry test: undoing a link costs the link and one chord to
restore it, while undoing an "add note" or a rename destroys prose the
user wrote and cannot re-derive. So links are in, note content is out,
and Mod+Z still cannot delete something you typed.

author: jcnm
body:
## Le défaut, visible à l'écran

`FeedPostCard:1422` rendait la ligne de statistiques d'un commentaire par :

```swift
Text(String(localized: "feed.post.comment.replies_count",
            defaultValue: "\(comment.replies) réponses", bundle: .main))
```

La clé est **plate**. Pour un commentaire à 1 réponse, l'écran affichait
« **1 réponses** » en français, « **1 replies** » en anglais. **Pas à
VoiceOver — à l'écran, en toutes locales, à tout le monde**. Ce n'est pas un
défaut d'accessibilité, c'est une **faute de français visible en production**.

## La cause : un doc-comment périmé

La source unique existait déjà : `PostStatAccessibility` + trois clés
`feed.post.stat.{likes,comments,reposts}`, chacune une `variations.plural`
complète — 2 formes latines, **6 formes arabes**. Elle n'était appelée que par
les **DEUX cellules UIKit** (`TextPostCell`, `MediaPostCell`). Les **CINQ
surfaces SwiftUI** du fil ont recopié la règle par **QUATRE clés plates
différentes**, sans jamais la trouver — parce que le doc-comment de 2025
disait :

> Proper multi-language plurals would require a `.xcstrings` plural variant.

Les variantes existaient sur ce type même. La phrase — vraie à sa rédaction,
fausse depuis — faisait lire le helper comme un pis-aller UIKit.

## Inventaire

| Site | Rendu (fr, n = 1) avant | Clé plate |
|---|---|---|
| `FeedPostCard:1422` | « **1 réponses** » — **VISIBLE** | `feed.post.comment.replies_count` |
| `FeedPostCard:1088` | « Aimer, 1 j'aime » | `a11y.feed.post.like.value` |
| `ReelFeedCard:598` | « Aimer, 1 j'aime » | `a11y.feed.post.like.value` |
| `FeedCommentsSheet:2381` | « Répondre, **1 réponses** » | `a11y.comment.replies.count` |
| `FeedCommentsSheet:2402` | « **Voir 1 réponses** » | `a11y.comment.show_replies` |

## Correctif

- `PostStatAccessibility.repliesLabel(_:)` (**4e** nom compté) + clé
  `feed.post.stat.replies` plurielle (7 locales, 6 formes arabes).
- Les 5 sites passent par le helper (sauf `show_replies` qui reste une clé
  propre — c'est une **phrase** — mais convertie sur place flat → plural).
- Les **3 clés plates** devenues orphelines sont retirées du catalogue :
  `test_everyAppCatalogIdentifierKeyIsReferencedInCode` en aurait refusé toute
  survivance (leçon 239i).
- Doc-comment de `PostStatAccessibility` réécrit — il cite les 4 clés retirées
  avec des **backticks** (` `…` `) pour que la garde ne l'attrape pas.

## Ce qui NE bouge PAS (leçon 238i — découper par NIVEAU DE DOUTE)

Les compteurs de type **label + valeur nue** (`PostDetailView:1642/1772/2264`
+ `FeedCommentsSheet:2354`) NE sont **pas** rebranchés sur
`PostStatAccessibility.*Label(_:)` : « J'aime » (label) + « 5 j'aime » (value)
donnerait « **J'aime, 5 j'aime** » — VoiceOver lit le nom compté deux fois. Ils
demandent un autre fix (`count.formatted(locale:)`, idiome `ReachMetricLabel.spokenCount`),
suite 241i.

## Garde

`EngagementCountConsolidationGuardTests` — deux versants :

- **Interdiction** — les 3 IDs plats supprimés (`"…"`) ne peuvent réapparaître
  nulle part dans les 6 racines scannées.
- **Consolidation** — 5 hôtes SwiftUI + 2 UIKit citent `PostStatAccessibility.`.

Auto-garde façon 238i (balayage ≥ 400 fichiers, dépouilleur laisse les
littéraux et mange les commentaires).

## Vérification

| Contrôle déterministe | Résultat |
|---|---|
| 3 clés plates bannies dans les 6 racines (hors tests) | **0 occurrence** |
| 5 hôtes SwiftUI + 2 UIKit citent `PostStatAccessibility.` | **7/7** |
| `feed.post.stat.replies` référencée en source | **oui** |
| Catalogue JSON valide, structure préservée | **oui** |
| Total clés catalogue | 3312 → **3310** (−3, +1) |
| Diff catalogue | +284 / −162 lignes (localisé, pas un reformat global) |
| Tests neufs | **4** dans `PostStatAccessibilityTests` + **4** dans la garde |

CI iOS Tests reste le gate réel (aucune toolchain Swift sous Linux) — opt-in
` — run test` dans le sujet du commit (leçon 238i).

## Changement visuel assumé

« 1 réponses » → « 1 réponse » (fr) · « 1 replies » → « 1 reply » (en). **C'est
une régression graphique corrigée**, pas un choix stylistique.

## Périmètre

- 5 fichiers prod + 1 catalogue + 1 helper étendu
- 1 suite étendue (+4 tests) + 1 garde neuve (+4 tests)
- 3 fichiers docs (plan, analyse, tracking)
- 0 logique métier · 0 réseau · pbxproj non touché (xcodegen en CI)

author: venetanji
body:
## What

`@media (max-height: 460px)`'s `.ico { width: 13px; height: 13px; }` in `app/src/styles/app.css` had no scope. It was written for the menu's short-viewport pass, but it matched **every** `<svg class="ico">` in the app — and ten of the thirteen rows in `sim/uifit/devices.ts` are 460px or shorter in landscape, so it applied to every phone in the matrix, on every screen.

Reported but deliberately deferred by the Contract HUD branch's `30a1c12`, which pinned `.pl-tier b .ico` locally and left the global rule for a pass of its own. This is that pass.

## Why it wins the cascade

`.ico` carries no size of its own — the base rule sets `flex`/`display` only, and each glyph's box comes from the `width`/`height` **attributes** `icons.ts` writes per call site. An SVG presentation attribute loses to *any* author rule at *any* specificity, so a bare `.ico` beat all of them. Only call sites already covered by a more specific selector were spared.

Effect at <=460px viewport height:

| requested | rendered | where |
|---|---|---|
| 22px | 13px | side rail: fullscreen, pause, rotate x2, cancel |
| 20px | 13px | Bond Breaker, Demolition |
| 18px | 13px | every back button |
| 17px | 13px | Autoloader |
| 16px | 13px | currency chips, salvage rows |
| 15px | 13px | mod glyphs |
| 10-12px | **13px** | inline currency glyphs in prose — these *grew* |

## Why scoped, not deleted

The menu genuinely relies on it. How to Play, Leaderboard and Settings carry no `.btn--menu` class, so `.menu__actions .btn--menu .ico` never reached them — their 13px came from this rule alone, as did the status chips (16px) and the Unlock Unlimited CTA (12px). The action rail fits with 2px to spare, so growing any of them was not free. `.menu .ico` preserves all of it.

## Verification

Measured with Playwright across 36 of the harness's 37 screens, comparing every `svg.ico`'s `width` attribute against `getComputedStyle`:

| viewport | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 792x360 (short) | 227 / 240 mis-sized | 77 |
| 1024x768 (tall) | 35 | 35 |

The remaining 77 are the 65 inside `.menu` — byte-identical to before — plus the 12 held by the two deliberate `max-height: 520px` refit rules. The tall row not moving in either direction is what isolates the media query as the sole cause. **150 glyphs restored to their requested size.**

- `npm run test:uifit`: **0 violations across 481 combos**, before and after
- `npm run typecheck` (both configs) and `npx tsx sim/systems.ts`: clean
- Ellipsis truncations **61 -> 57** — the refit buy button narrowed once its arrow returned to 10px, so four previously-cut labels now fit

WebKit (non-gating, `continue-on-error: true`): **0 new violations**. It also reports 60 baselined `inkline` entries no longer reproducing, but the *unmodified* file reports the identical 60/18/0 — pre-existing local engine drift against the CI-recorded baseline, not this change. `baseline.webkit.json` untouched.

## Not in scope

- `.btn`/`.btn--lg` in the same block are unscoped too, but unlike `.ico` they have a coherent global "compact on short viewports" reading, and the sheet already overrides them deliberately (`.modal .btn`, `.modal--refit .refit-card__buy`).
- Separately reported: `.btn--menu .ico` is a *descendant* selector, so it also inflates the 10px currency glyphs inside `.btn__sub` to 20px on tall viewports (measured `10->20` on iPad mini). Unrelated to and unchanged by this fix.

author: zhiyuan-zhang0206
body:
## Persistent shell idle reminders (task #1491)

When an agent's persistent shell sits idle at its prompt, its owner is
reminded — and asked, never killed. Backoff sequence per the user ruling:
5m / 30m / 1h / 2h / 4h / 8h / 16h, then a 24h cadence; any activity resets
the sequence; an owner reply containing `保留` marks the covered sessions
standing-exempt until they end.

### File tree

```
shared/
└── pty_sessions/host.py               (M)  ★ new `is_idle` op: tty foreground
                                            process group == shell group ⇒
                                            prompt available; + last-output
                                            monotonic clock as idle anchor
services/
├── idle_shell_reminder/               (A)  ★ new gateway-only daemon
│   ├── daemon.py                      (A)  60s tick; polls local live PTY
│   │                                      sessions via the existing
│   │                                      session_request protocol; sends
│   │                                      one merged chat inbound per owner
│   │                                      (source=system); never closes a
│   │                                      session
│   ├── engine.py                      (A)  pure backoff/merge/reset/exempt
│   │                                      state machine (fake-clock tested)
│   └── state.py                       (A)  atomic versioned JSON persistence
│                                          ($AVA_HOME/run/idle_shell_reminder.json)
├── healthchecks/
│   └── idle_shell_reminder.py         (A)  identity-verified watchdog keepalive
ops/spec.py                            (M)  roster entry + gate (gateway-only)
shared/config/{daemon,services}.py     (M)  AVA_IDLE_SHELL_REMINDER_ENABLED /
                                            pidfile / health port settings
shared/env_registry.py                 (M)  health-port service registration
shared/port_block.py                   (M)  offset 20 / legacy port 8115
services/*.ava.okf.md, conventions/runbook.md,
services/healthchecks/check-roster.ava.okf.md  (M/A)  roster + OKF docs
tests/
├── services/test_idle_shell_reminder.py  (A)  every threshold exactly,
│                                            24h cap, resets, merge, exempt,
│                                            terminated skip, state round-trip
└── shared/test_pty_sessions_cli.py       (M)  unit (mocked pgrp) + real-shell
                                               prompt → foreground job → idle
docs/history/2026-08-24/persistent-shell-idle-reminders.md  (A)
```

### Data flow

Watchdog keepalive → daemon tick (60s) → `live_sessions()` record scan →
`is_idle` over each session's own unix socket → engine decides due sessions
per owner (backoff per session, merged per owner) → `insert_inbound_message`
(chat, source=system) + Redis wake → owner agent replies in its dialog →
daemon scans the owner's checkpoint for an AI reply containing `保留` after
the reminder's `ava_inbound_id` anchor → covered sessions become
standing-exempt.

Idle truth: foreground pgrp == shell pgrp (a foreground job is busy, a
background job does not block the prompt). `idle_since` = last output byte
(monotonic, converted to epoch at observation); a changed value starts a new
idle period, i.e. activity resets.

### Not tested / boundaries

- Exemption matching is anchored on the checkpoint's `ava_inbound_id`
  (the message contract in `agent/messages.py`); after a compaction the
  anchor may be gone and reminders simply continue.
- The daemon polls only sessions on its own machine (gateway host); sessions
  on other machines' PTY backends are out of scope by design (spec).
- The merged reminder exempts every session covered by that reminder when the
  owner replies `保留`; a per-session selective keep is not supported.
- Real end-to-end daemon run (tick loop against a live cluster DB) is not
  exercised in CI; covered by unit/fake-clock tests + the existing
  heartbeat-daemon pattern.
- Local verification: full non-e2e suite green except one pre-existing
  host-specific failure (`test_stale_manifest_rules_covers_legacy_family`
  assumes adb is absent; it exists on this machine).

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agents refreshing a custom HTML dashboard widget could choose the plugin-only dashboard writer, conclude that the existing widget was not replaceable, and end the run without updating the dashboard.

The same stable widget name could also be overwritten across incompatible content owners at the shared board-write boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Board snapshots now retain and expose the canonical content owner for each widget, including the original registered source kind. Same-name writes must preserve that owner, plugin kind, and registered source kind; changing ownership requires removing the widget first.

Dashboard guidance identifies plugin-only writes and directs other content through its owning authoring capability. The HTML authoring surface explicitly describes same-name pinned refreshes. Existing rows are upgraded from their persisted content and descriptor shape without a SQLite schema or protocol version bump.

## User Impact

Custom HTML widgets can be refreshed in place by stable name across later runs in the same session. An accidental plugin write can no longer destroy an HTML, registered-source, or MCP widget.

## Evidence

Isolated live Gateway + real Control UI proof:

1. Created a custom HTML widget named `daily-proof`; the dashboard rendered revision 1.
2. Attempted a same-name `session:progress` plugin replacement. Gateway returned `INVALID_REQUEST`, and revision 1 remained visibly intact.
3. Refreshed the same HTML owner under the same name. The dashboard rendered revision 2 in place.
4. Final `board.get`: board revision 2, widget revision 2, `contentKind: html`, `contentOwner: html`.

Focused verification:

- 103 ownership/protocol/tool/Gateway tests passed across four Vitest shards.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <changed paths>` passed, including native checks and app tests.
- `pnpm build` passed.
- Fresh Codex autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings.

Production growth establishes a previously missing persisted ownership boundary and bounded legacy-row upgrade. Tests cover HTML, trusted plugin, registered-source, and MCP owners plus the same-session HTML refresh sequence.

Provenance: the ambiguous plugin-only dashboard authoring surface predates this PR; available shallow checkout history does not establish its original introducing change. Custom HTML authoring remains separately owned by `show_widget`.

author: lmc-karma
body:
## Summary

- Add process-local native Space identities and exact per-display session activation.
- Dynamically resolve the three SkyLight observation symbols approved in #32, validate the complete topology, and retain inferred matching as the fallback.
- Float multi-Space windows, suppress ambient writes and dividers on native fullscreen Spaces, and preserve the two-sample Space-change stabilization gate.
- Add a debounced Core Graphics display callback while retaining the AppKit notification fallback.

## Behavior

Before this change, BetterTile inferred the active desktop from visible-window overlap. Similar memberships could select the wrong runtime Bento tree, and the app could not identify sticky or native fullscreen Space topology.

After this change, a valid native observation selects the exact display and Space session. Missing symbols, malformed topology, and unknown memberships preserve the existing public-API behavior. Sessions remain process-local and are removed only after a valid topology confirms that a Space disappeared.

## Security and compatibility

This implements the read-only SkyLight capability approved in #32. All private symbols resolve at runtime and have no launch-link dependency. The existing disablePrivateAPIs default disables this capability. Logs contain only availability and one-time fallback reasons; they do not contain window titles, identifiers, or raw topology. The change adds no permission, telemetry, network behavior, persisted Space data, Space mutation, or external dependency. ColorSync is a public system framework used only to map display IDs to display UUIDs.

## Validation

- swift test: 374 passed
- Debug Swift package build: passed
- Release Swift package build: passed
- Debug unsigned BetterTile app build: passed
- Release unsigned BetterTile app build: passed
- Manual macOS 26 Space, sticky-window, fullscreen, and display hardware matrix: not run in this non-interactive environment

Related to #32.

## 목적

결론 문장 **"같은 프롬프트(주제)를 넣었을 때 수동/반자동/자동 중 무엇이 가장 효과적이었다"** 를 내기 위한 분류 체계. 기존 auto·hybrid 2모드에 `manual`(수동)을 더해 3분류로 확정하고, 어느 모드의 발행인지 **증빙이 발행 행 자체에 남게** 한다.

## 3분류 정의 (`sns/publish/modes.py` 정본)

| 모드 | 정의 | 발행 주체 |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` (자동) | AI 생성 → 품질 게이트 → 기계 발행 | 발행 러너 |
| `hybrid` (반자동) | AI 초안 → 사람 검수·수정·승인(needs_review 관문) → 기계 발행 | 발행 러너 |
| `manual` (수동) | 사람이 **같은 주제**를 배정받아 직접 작성·앱에서 직접 발행 → `external_post_id`만 등록 | 사람 |

## 변경

- **002 마이그레이션**: `channel.mode`에 `manual` 추가 · `publication.mode` 발행 시점 스냅샷(채널 mode가 바뀌어도 증빙 보존, 비교 리포트 단일 출처) · `(channel_id, external_post_id)` 부분 유니크(수동 이중 등록 물리 차단)
- **사이클 러너**: manual 대상은 AI 초안·발행 대기 생성 없이 같은 주제 배정 notice만 남김(주제는 사이클당 1건 공유 유지) — `manual_assigned` outcome 신설
- **발행 러너**: 기계 발행 선택을 `auto·hybrid`로 한정(manual·off 미선택) + `publish_attempted` 이벤트에 mode 기록
- **`sns/publish/manual.py` 신설**: 수동 발행+ID 등록 경계 — manual 채널 검증(기계 채널 등록=실험군 오염 → 거부), (채널, external_post_id) 멱등, 등록 후엔 지표 수집이 기계 발행 건과 동일 경로
- **01-실험설계.md v4**: 실험군 표에 IG-M/YT-M 추가, FR-E1/E4 갱신, FR-E5 신설

## 검증

`ruff check` · `ruff format --check` · `mypy sns` · `pytest` **289 passed, 0 skipped** (PostgreSQL 기동 상태 — 002 적용·유니크 인덱스·manual 등록 멱등·러너 미선택 통합 테스트 포함)

author: feffef
body:
🤖 [Claude Sonnet 5](https://claude.ai/code/session_01WdpMeEFpVL77frTHvwUJDM)

**Human-only to merge (ADR-0004) — this is the escalation PR for a scheduled `/audit-docs` sweep.** Its sibling, #1031, carries that sweep's three Live-tier fixes and self-merges on green; these two touch ADR text, so they ride here instead.

Both findings were CONFIRMED by an independent fact-checker reading the ADR text directly.

## Why these are in-place edits

Under ADR-0018's factual-correction-vs-decision-reversal rule, both are **pure factual corrections** — a missing cross-reference in prose describing a decision. Neither ADR's decision is being changed, narrowed, or reversed; each Decision line is simply unreadable in isolation because the amendment that qualifies it sits above with no pointer down. No amendment banner is therefore added, and no Decision text is rewritten. Per that same section, the category never changes the merge gate — hence this human-reviewed PR.

## Finding 1 — ADR-0003

`docs/adr/0003-agent-operating-model-and-governance.md:184` states flatly:

> **Merge is always gated. No self-merge.**

Five amendments above it (`digest`, `audit-docs`, `audit-skills`, `blog-post`, `prune-trial`) each grant the **same authoring session** authority to merge its own PR on a green gate, naming no distinct reviewer — self-merge by plain reading. `prune-trial`'s amendment even uses the literal word "self-merged". Only the `frictions-to-fixes` amendment reconciles the base rule, and it does so via a mechanism the other five don't share ("the merging session is never the author of the diff it merges; it is a distinct reviewer").

The two live docs then describe this in opposite terms: `CLAUDE.md:66-67` calls the tiers an *exception* to no-self-merge, while ADR-0003's own amendments frame them as *not really* self-merge because the gate decides. `CONTEXT.md` has no `### Self-merge` glossary term to settle it — the word appears only inline inside `### Trusted` and `### Human-only`.

Added a parenthetical pointing the Decision line at those amendments, phrased to hold both truths: the gate decides, *and* the merging session is the authoring one.

**A reviewer may prefer a different resolution** — notably adding a `### Self-merge` term to `CONTEXT.md` that defines it precisely (e.g. "the same session that authored the diff executing the merge, regardless of whether the trigger is judgement or an objective gate"), which would make the five tiers unambiguous exceptions and let CLAUDE.md's framing stand as the correct one. That's a governance call, not an audit call, so this PR takes the minimal option.

## Finding 2 — ADR-0004

`docs/adr/0004-objective-safety-gate.md:168-169` (Decision):

> **Low-risk (auto-mergeable when green):** content only, or a single Tenant's layer/manifest.

Directly contradicted by its own 2026-07-19 amendment at lines 94-109:

> **An ordinary work PR — even one that is content-only or touches a single Tenant's layer/manifest — is always human-merged**

The amendment does self-acknowledge the tension and points at `docs/agents/pr-workflow.md` as authoritative, but the Decision text itself was never given a forward-pointer — so a reader who stops at the Decision (which is what CLAUDE.md's Ground-rules summaries draw from) gets the wrong answer. This is the failure mode ADR-0018's never-rewrite-Decision-in-place convention structurally invites, and a pointer is its intended remedy.

## Gate

`pnpm gate:scoped` green locally on this branch.

body:
Closes #350

## Summary

Restructure `idd-lint` into explicit, independently testable phases while preserving its CLI output and exit behavior: issue checks now use ordered table dispatch, GitHub statistics use three focused collectors, report rendering delegates to section helpers, and numeric thresholds have descriptive names.

## Approach

Option 2 — Balanced behavior-preserving decomposition: extract the requested seams without changing public entry-point signatures or data shapes, add focused structural regressions, and run differential output checks plus the complete shell suite.

## Decision Record

- **Root cause:** `lint_issue`, `collect_github_stats`, and `render_stats` each combined orchestration with unrelated check, collection, or formatting details; important boundary values were embedded as literals, making those flows harder to review and change without drift.
- **Options considered:** Option 1 — rename constants only; Option 2 — balanced behavior-preserving decomposition with focused regressions; Option 3 — split `idd-lint` into multiple modules and redesign its data model.
- **Options rejected:** Option 1 — leaves the check, collector, and renderer structure debt unresolved; Option 3 — expands scope and compatibility risk beyond the requested in-module refactor.
- **Selected option:** Option 2 — balanced behavior-preserving decomposition with focused regressions.
- **Residual risk:** future tests may intentionally evolve output formatting; the new differential evidence proves parity for this change but does not freeze every possible runtime environment.

Analyzed at: `main @ e0aace2` (2026-08-24)

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `scripts/idd-lint.py` | Add ordered issue-check dispatch, three GitHub collectors, report section renderers, and named thresholds. |
| `tests/test-idd-lint-structure-350.sh` | Add 13 focused checks for dispatch order, collector boundaries, renderer delegation, output ownership, and named literals. |
| `.github/workflows/dist-check.yml` | Run the new regression in pull-request CI. |

## Test Results

- Unit tests: 13 focused structure checks passed
- Integration tests: 72 tracked shell test files passed
- E2e tests: skipped — no applicable UI/runtime flow
- Build: passed (`bash scripts/build.sh --out /tmp/idd-350-build-final --quiet` and `python3 -m compileall -q scripts src/shared/scripts`)
- QA cycles: 2

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status | Evidence |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| `lint_issue` dispatches via a table of per-check functions; stats collection split into three collector functions; render helpers replace hand-built f-string rows | pass | `scripts/idd-lint.py`; `tests/test-idd-lint-structure-350.sh` verifies all three seams and their orchestration. |
| No bare magic thresholds remain | pass | Source scan finds `40`, `50`, `60`, `72`, `80`, `200`, and `500` only in named constant declarations; truncation derives the former `57` value from `COMMIT_LABEL_MAX_LENGTH`. |
| Test command of record passes at >= 61/61 with identical lint output on the repo itself | pass | All 72 tracked `tests/*.sh` files pass; `python3 scripts/idd-lint.py repo --base origin/main` exits 0; old/new stdout, stderr, and exit status match byte-for-byte on repo, stats, issue, branch, and commit fixtures. |

body:
estate-integrity has been red on this for a while (issue #300): `AGENT-PLAYBOOK.md` had 2 versions across the estate and `.agents/rules/00-agent-playbook.md` had 3. Both are declared byte-identical in all seven repos, and the guard checks it hourly.

club-arena was the odd one out on both — and it was the one that was AHEAD, not behind. Its copies carry the full VERIFICATION PASS (Parts A-E), including the interrogation items this estate keeps needing:

- PART C.5 HOSTILE STATE & CACHE — stale localStorage, six-month-old bookmarks, mid-flight drops
- PART C.6 USER INTENT VERIFICATION — prove the actual reported bug is gone
- RULE 7 — fix your own build, do not wait for a human
- RULE 8 — the Zero-Assumption Doctrine

The other six repos had a thinner pointer-summary with none of it. This syncs all six to the club-arena version so the rules are the same everywhere.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: I hit this myself. I spent a full session working from the root playbook, which in this repo does not contain RULE 8, and so never ran a hostile-state analysis on anything I shipped until Dan pointed me at the other file. An agent cannot follow a rule it was never shown.

Docs only. No code, no workflows, no behaviour.

author: thegreenjedi
body:
## Problem
Canonical model pages currently render every `no` capability under **Verified absent**. That accidentally includes inverse Finder helper fields such as `no_camera` and `no_display`.

For a display-equipped model, `display=yes` correctly forces the helper `no_display=no`; the page then renders the label **No Display** under **Verified absent**, producing a user-visible contradiction such as `Display: Yes` alongside `Verified absent: No Display`.

This is visible on multiple live catalog pages, including Snap SPECS, RayNeo X3 Pro, Brilliant Labs Frame, and several display-only products.

## Change
- explicitly mark `no_camera` and `no_display` as inverse helper capabilities for page presentation
- exclude those helper fields from the user-facing **Verified absent** list
- preserve the underlying Finder capability matrix and inverse logic unchanged

## Evidence / semantics
This does **not** change canonical product evidence, Finder matching, guide inclusion, provenance, or unknown handling. Actual capability fields such as `camera=no` or `display=no` still render as verified absences when supported by evidence. Unknown remains unknown.

## Validation
- branch diff is limited to `scripts/build_model_pages.py` (2 additions, 1 deletion)
- Finder helper semantics remain untouched in `build_finder_capabilities.py`
- generated-page build remains covered by the existing strict Pages workflow

No merge requested; this is a review proposal.

author: yangwei-x
body:
## What

A full-size overlay page for organizing bookmarks — opened from the bookmark sidebar's ⚙ button, **View ▸ 书签管理…**, or the command palette. The sidebar stays the quick-connect surface; this page is where bookmarks get maintained in bulk.

Design doc: `docs/plans/bookmark-manager-design.md` (lives in the shared docs tree, outside this repo).

- **Three columns** — group tree (all / recent / ungrouped + the derived folders, sharing the sidebar's collapse state), a sortable table exposing protocol, target, auth, group and last-used (password auth flagged in the warning colour), and `BookmarkEditor` reused through a new `embedded` mode.
- **Selection** — checkbox, ⌘/Ctrl-click, Shift range, header select-all. The batch bar moves, exports, duplicates or deletes the selection; rows can be dragged onto a group to move them; right-clicking a row acts on it (or on the whole selection if it is part of one).
- **Groups are first-class** — create an empty group, rename, add a subgroup, dissolve it (children move up one level), or delete it with its bookmarks.
- **Transfer** — export all or a selection as AuraTerm JSON (credentials opt-in, behind a confirmation), and import with the format sniffed from the file (AuraTerm / PuTTY `.reg` / OpenSSH config) into a chosen group.
- **Keyboard** — `/` or ⌘/Ctrl+F focuses search, ↑↓ walk the list, Enter connects, Esc clears the search then closes.

## Why the new backend commands

`delete_connections`, `move_connections`, `rename_group`, `duplicate_connection` and `export_bookmarks` do batch work in a single pass. Looping `save_connection` from the frontend rewrites the whole metadata file *and* the credential store per bookmark, and in master-password mode every write uses a fresh salt, so it derives a new Argon2id key (16 MB, t=3) each time — 50 rows meant 50 derivations.

`move_connections` and `rename_group` touch metadata only and never open the credential store, so they keep working while the master password is locked.

## Bug fixes carried along

- Bookmark save failures went through `window.alert`, which is a silent no-op in the macOS WebView (see `CLAUDE.md`) — users saw nothing when a save failed. Now `alertDialog`.
- Deleting from the sidebar's context menu had no confirmation.
- Saving a bookmark while credentials are locked used to overwrite the encrypted entry with the stripped copy the frontend holds, erasing the stored password/key. It is now refused with a "unlock first" dialog.

## Verification

- `npm run build` (vue-tsc + vite) — clean
- `npx vitest run` — 14 files, **114 tests** passing, including a mounted-component suite for the page (list order, group scoping, batch delete, drag-to-move, group rename with the explicit group list, empty-group creation, row context menu, export, locked-save refusal)
- `cargo test` — **151 tests** passing, incl. new coverage for the group-rename path rewriting and an export → import round trip

Not yet exercised in a real window (`npm run tauri dev`): drag-and-drop, the native confirm dialogs, and the file download.

author: ardiannurcahya
body:
## 📋 Overview

Audit and refactor the repository into a clean, reusable, and secure K3s multi-node VPS provisioning project.

### 🚀 Key Improvements

1. **Repository Structure**:
   - Relocated operational scripts from `examples/` to `scripts/`.
   - Renamed `install-k3s-single.*` to `install-k3s-cluster.*` to clarify single control-plane multi-worker architecture.
   - Organized configuration templates and reference schemas into `config/`.
   - Maintained focused, modular documentation in `docs/`.

2. **Configuration & Schema**:
   - Defined canonical inventory format in `config/nodes.example.json`.
   - Added JSON Schema validation in `config/inventory.schema.json`.
   - Supported configurable SSH user, SSH port, SSH key, and network interface (`network.interface`).
   - Documented explicit IPv4-only cluster transport support.

3. **Networking & WireGuard Integration**:
   - Integrated automatic `--flannel-iface`, `--node-ip`, `--node-external-ip`, and `--tls-san` argument generation when `network.interface` (e.g. `wg0`) is configured.
   - Added safety warnings for unencrypted VXLAN over public IPs.

4. **Bash & PowerShell Parity**:
   - Full validation parity across Linux Bash and Windows PowerShell implementations.
   - Pinned K3s version enforcement (`^vX.Y.Z+k3sN`).
   - Strict host key checking (`StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`).
   - Zero secret leak token retrieval & clearing.
   - 5-minute health check verification loop.

5. **Safety & Quality**:
   - Added `--dry-run` / `-DryRun` plan mode across operational scripts.
   - Added GitHub Actions CI workflow (ShellCheck, PSScriptAnalyzer, JSON Schema test, and Gitleaks).
   - Added local validation test suite (`tests/test_validation.sh` and `tests/test_schema.py`).
   - Added MIT LICENSE.

author: lfrmonteiro99
body:
## Resumo

fix/689: App Library não cai no ecrã do Android quando o blob de apps recentes está corrompido (normaliza @iostoandroid/recent_apps na leitura)

## Causa raiz

O issue diz "App Library frame shows Android system home screen instead of iOS App Library" e o corpo está vazio ("## What is wrong" sem texto). O sintoma descrito — cair no ecrã inicial do Android em vez da App Library — é, neste projecto, sempre o mesmo mecanismo: a `AppLibraryContent` é montada **inline como última página do pager da home** (`src/screens/LauncherHomeScreen.tsx:1753`), por isso qualquer throw no seu render derruba o launcher inteiro e o Android volta ao launcher do sistema. Os fixes issue 688 (categoryOverrides) e #699 (`app.name` ausente) fecharam duas dessas fontes; ficou aberta uma terceira, no mesmo padrão exacto e com a mesma consequência.

A fonte que faltava é o blob persistido de apps recentes, `@iostoandroid/recent_apps`:

- `src/store/AppsStore.tsx:279-296` (antes do fix) aceitava o blob **desde que fosse um array**, e fazia `setRecentApps(parsed as RecentApp[])` — um `as` que valida zero coisas em runtime. As **entradas** nunca eram verificadas.
- A `AppLibraryContent` consome essas entradas directamente no render: `src/screens/AppLibraryScreen.tsx:648-651` faz `[...recentApps].sort((a, b) => b.launchedAt - a.launchedAt).map(r => visibleApps.find(a => a.packageName === r.packageName))`, e `AppLibraryScreen.tsx:666-670` repete-o para as Suggestions.
- Uma entrada `null` no blob (ou qualquer não-objecto) faz `b.launchedAt` rebentar com `TypeError: Cannot read property 'launchedAt' of null` **durante o render**. O throw sobe pela árvore, derruba o `AppsProvider`/launcher, e o utilizador vê o ecrã inicial do Android — sem nenhuma pista de que a causa está no AsyncStorage.
- Como o blob é **persistido**, o crash é determinístico e repete-se em cada arranque até a app ser limpa. É exactamente a assinatura de #688/#699: "a App Library mostra o ecrã do Android".

Correcção onde a #688 já pôs a defesa do irmão (normalizar na leitura), não com um `?.` no consumidor.

## O que mudou

**`src/store/AppsStore.tsx`**
- Nova função exportada `normalizeRecentApps(raw: unknown): RecentApp[]`: devolve `[]` para tudo o que não é array e, para arrays, aceita apenas entradas que sejam objectos (não-array) com `packageName` string não-vazia e `launchedAt` numérico finito. Duplicados por `packageName` colapsam na primeira ocorrência (como `addToRecents` faz), e o resultado é truncado em `MAX_RECENTS` (8), a mesma fronteira que a escrita já respeita.
- O carregamento do blob (`useEffect` dos recentes) passa a chamar `normalizeRecentApps(parsed)` em vez de `parsed as RecentApp[]`, e reescreve o blob saneado quando descartou entradas — para que o arranque seguinte não volte a herdar o lixo.
- O ramo de migração do formato legado (`string[]`) passa a filtrar entradas que sejam de facto strings não-vazias antes de mapear. Um array misto (legado parcialmente reescrito) produzia `{ packageName: undefined }`, que alimentava o mesmo crash pelo outro caminho.

**`src/store/__tests__/AppsStore.normalizeRecentApps.test.ts`** (novo) — unidade da função exportada.

**`src/screens/__tests__/AppLibraryContent.malformedRecents.test.tsx`** (novo) — integração: monta a `AppLibraryContent` real com o blob corrompido no AsyncStorage mockado.

## Porque assim

- **Sanear na leitura, não no consumidor.** É o padrão já estabelecido neste repositório para blobs não confiáveis do AsyncStorage: `normalizeCategoryOverrides` (#688), `normalizeFocusPageVisibility` (#618), `clampWallpaperIndex` (#674) — todos em `SettingsStore.tsx:406-440`. Um `?? 0` ou `?.` nos comparadores da App Library taparia o crash mas deixaria entradas inválidas a circular por `MultitaskScreen` e `QuickSwitchHomeBar`, que também leem `recentApps`.
- **Descartar, não reparar.** Uma entrada sem `packageName` utilizável não é informação recuperável; inventar um `launchedAt` daria ordenação arbitrária nas strips. Descartada, a strip cai no fallback alfabético que já existe.
- **Reescrever o blob saneado**: alternativa descartada era só filtrar em memória. Persistir corta o lixo de vez, e é uma escrita só no arranque em que houve corrupção.
- **`MAX_RECENTS` na normalização**: a escrita já trunca em 8; um blob escrito por outra versão podia trazer 200 entradas e as strips passariam a resolver 200 `find()` por render. Repor a fronteira na leitura mantém o invariante nos dois sentidos.
- Alternativa descartada: pôr a normalização em `src/utils/`. Ficou junto ao `RecentApp` e ao `MAX_RECENTS` que ela usa, no único ficheiro que lê o blob.

## Critérios de aceitação

- [x] **Um blob de recentes com uma entrada `null` não derruba a App Library**: teste de integração monta `AppLibraryContent` com `[null, {...}]` e o header "Categories" renderiza. Antes falhava com "Unable to find node on an unmounted component" (a árvore tinha morrido).
- [x] **Nem string, objecto sem `launchedAt`, `launchedAt` não numérico, `packageName` não string, nem entrada aninhada em array**: 6 variantes cobertas por `it.each`.
- [x] **O inverso do fix: entradas válidas continuam a alimentar "Recently Added"** — teste confirma que com `[{com.spotify, 100}, {com.facebook, 50}]` o header "Recently Added" aparece e "Spotify" ocorre mais de uma vez (strip + categoria). Sem isto, um `normalizeRecentApps` que devolvesse sempre `[]` passaria todos os outros testes.
- [x] **Válidas misturadas com lixo: as válidas sobrevivem** — `[null, {com.spotify,100}, 'lixo']` continua a produzir a strip com Spotify.
- [x] **`launchedAt: 0` e negativo são aceites** (relógio do sistema atrasado é estado legítimo, não corrupção) — verificado na unidade.
- [x] **A fronteira `MAX_RECENTS` (8) é respeitada** — 20 entradas válidas com lixo intercalado devolvem exactamente 8, a começar na primeira.
- [x] **O que NÃO devia mudar:** nenhum ficheiro fora de `src/store/AppsStore.tsx` foi tocado em produção. `AppLibraryScreen.tsx`, `LauncherHomeScreen.tsx`, `MultitaskScreen.tsx` e `QuickSwitchHomeBar.tsx` ficaram intactos; a forma de `RecentApp` e a assinatura de `recentApps` no contexto não mudaram, por isso os consumidores não precisaram de alteração. Confirmado por `git status --porcelain`, que lista só o `AppsStore.tsx` modificado e os dois testes novos.
- [x] **Sem regressão na suite:** 25 falhas antes e depois, as mesmas 6 suites da LINHA DE BASE.
- [x] **Nenhum `any` novo, nenhum `as` a calar o compilador**: `normalizeRecentApps` recebe `unknown` e estreita por verificações de runtime; `npx tsc --noEmit` limpo.

## Testes

**Passo vermelho** — `git stash push -- src/store/AppsStore.tsx` (tira só o fix, deixa os testes), output real do jest:

```
● AppLibraryContent — blob de recentes corrompido não derruba a App Library (#689) › renderiza a grelha com uma entrada null no blob de recentes

    Unable to find node on an unmounted component.
      49 |     const utils = render(<AppLibraryContent />);
      50 |     await waitFor(() => expect(utils.getByText('Categories')).toBeTruthy());
    > 51 |     expect(utils.getAllByText('Facebook').length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
         |                  ^
      52 |   });

● AppLibraryContent — blob de recentes corrompido não derruba a App Library (#689) › entradas válidas misturadas com lixo: as válidas sobrevivem à filtragem

      74 |     mockStorage([null, { packageName: 'com.spotify', launchedAt: 100 }, 'lixo']);
      75 |     const utils = render(<AppLibraryContent />);
    > 76 |     await waitFor(() => expect(utils.getByText('Recently Added')).toBeTruthy());

      77 |     await waitFor(() => expect(utils.getAllByText('Spotify').length).toBeGreaterThan(1));

Test Suites: 1 failed, 1 total
Tests:       2 failed, 7 passed, 9 total
```

author: lwshanbd
body:
最后摆好板子、对照原图改格子那一屏（「擦掉 / 补上」）两处体验问题。

## 图纸原来是盖上来的，现在挪到旁边

「对照图纸」原来是把格子那一层整个换成图纸、原地盖住 —— 换过去看不见自己改的格子，换回来看不见图纸，用户得来回按十几次，靠脑子记住上一眼看到的是什么。要比的两样东西必须同时在眼里。

现在按一下画布左右对半分：左边图纸原图、右边能擦能补的格子。两边共用同一个 `transform`（两栏宽高一致 ⇒ 同一格落在两边同一个位置），所以同一块地方、同一个放大倍数、同一批格线，横着扫一眼就是同一行；放大、拖动哪一边两边一起动。

图纸那一栏 **只能挪图不能画**（`gestureCatcher(paints:)`）—— 比对时手指多半落在图纸那边，那一下要是也在画，改掉的是自己正照着看的东西。

按钮文案 `对照图纸 ⇄ 收起图纸`，收起来格子仍占满整屏。没有图纸时按钮照旧不出现。

## 板底从近乎纯白改成中灰

空格子露出来的是板底，原来用 `Surface.elevated`（近乎纯白）—— 白色豆子铺在白板底上就是一片白，用户分不出哪几格是空的、哪几格是白豆子，而这一屏问的正是「这儿到底有没有豆子」。

改成固定一档中灰（`PartCellBrushView.boardColor`，深浅色模式同一个值：板底是「桌上那块板」，不该跟着界面变亮变暗，否则同一张图两种模式下擦出来不一样多）。格线跟着从提亮的白线改成压暗的深线 —— 白线在灰板底上还行，但两颗挨着的白豆子中间那条缝就没了。

## 验证

模拟器（iPhone 17 Pro Max）走了一遍：单图纸模式 → 量格子 → 底色 → 核对颜色 → 改格子。拼豆板那屏点零件进的是同一个组件。

- 分栏后两边行列对齐，放大 / 缩小同步；
- 用接近纯白的 A2 在灰板底上补了一行，一眼看得出来（颗数 36 → 48）；
- 在图纸那一栏划手指颗数不变，确认不会误画；
- 「收起图纸」回到整屏，平移量重新夹过、内容没跑出框；
- 深色、浅色两种模式都看过。

Two cleanups from the post-merge review of the netmap series: retrack the one piece of work whose pointers went stale, and stop explaining code through work-tracking codes.

## Commit 1 — split the spelling flip into NM6

The canonical-spelling flip (`validator`/`endpoint` to `bp`/`en` in argv and persisted workspaces) was scoped out of NM3 when `netmap.Is` made both spellings safe to compare, but the rescope never reached the places that referenced it: LegacySpelling's comment promised to die with NM3, topology.NodeRole pointed at NM3, and the worklist's N0 row deferred to a stage already marked complete. A work item whose every pointer names a closed stage is on its way to being forgotten.

- netmap-design §4: new NM6 row carrying the deferred flip with its gate — canonical values emitted, LegacySpelling deleted, old workspaces stay readable via NormalizeRole, live re-verification since argv changes. The stage-order line loses its stale trailing text, and NM2b is checked off where its substance landed (`netmap.Layout` in NM5), with the bin/material/run destination layout explicitly out of that stage's scope.
- worklist: N0 tracks NM6 by name; the NM3 and NM5 completion notes say what was split out and where it lives.

## Commit 2 — comments describe the code, not the process that built it

Comments across the tree explained themselves through work-tracking codes (K0, T7.11, NM3, A0) that mean nothing without the worklist open beside the code. Every such comment for finished work now states the fact in plain terms: a gate names the contract it pins, a moved package names the retirement that moved it, a constant names the failure that made it necessary. 49 files, comment lines only.

What stays: references into the contract documents (feature-spec ids like F11/F16-O5, design findings like S2, requirement numbers) — those documents are the permanent record — and one pointer to the pending spelling migration (NM6), which is not finished work.

author: chronick
body:
Implements **vault-khu7l** — rytm-bridge: stale-daemon detection at client.start.

Label: `routine:fable-executor`

## Acceptance

- [x] **RustDaemonClient.start detects an existing analog-rytm-agent-daemon process and warns/refuses before spawning a second** — `start()` now runs `guardAgainstExistingDaemon()` before `spawn()`. Detection lists the host process table (injectable `listProcesses` option; default `ps -eo pid=,ppid=,args=`), matches on the daemon binary basename only (never the `cargo run` wrapper), and excludes daemons that are descendants of the current process (ppid walk), so the client's own children and deliberately-dual-daemon scripts are never flagged. A hardware-adapter start **refuses** with `RytmDaemonRpcError` `daemon_already_running` naming the PIDs and the `kill` command; a mock start only **warns**, keeping the test suite's parallel mock daemons working. A failing/absent `ps` degrades to a warning — detection is advisory and never blocks a start.
- [x] **Helper scripts get a clean stop() path so process.exit() cannot orphan the cargo child** — the client arms a synchronous `process.on("exit")` hook while a child is alive that SIGKILLs it, and disarms it on child close and in `close()`. Implemented inside the client, so every helper script gets the guard with no bin-script edits. (`close()`'s existing SIGTERM-2s/SIGKILL-7s escalation is unchanged, moved verbatim into a private `terminate()`.)
- [x] **Unit tests with a mocked process listing** — 5 new tests in `test/rust-daemon-client.test.ts` using an injected process listing and a stdio stub daemon (no cargo, no hardware): hardware refusal (error code, PID in message, nothing spawned), mock-adapter warn-and-start, no-foreign-daemon start (cargo wrapper + own-descendant exclusion), real `ps`-output parsing/matching, and exit-hook arm/disarm symmetry.

## Verification

Run by the reviewing lead in-session on this branch:

body:
💡 What: Extracted the static default scene dictionary into its own dedicated function `_default_scene_dict` and refactored `_parse_scene_payload` to utilize it instead of calling `json.loads(_default_scene_payload())`.
🎯 Why: In `plugin.py`, `_default_scene_payload()` was building a static dictionary and immediately calling `json.dumps()` on it to return a string. However, `_parse_scene_payload()` needed a dictionary and was thus forced to call `json.loads(_default_scene_payload())`. This process of constantly stringifying and re-parsing a static structure is extremely slow and redundant. By extracting the dictionary directly, we bypass the serialization overhead entirely.
📊 Impact: The execution time of resolving the fallback payload data dropped from ~7.17s to ~0.84s for 100,000 iterations (approx an 8.5x improvement). This reduces blocking operations when dealing with default configurations and empty scene initialization.
🔬 Measurement: Run a python profile comparing `json.loads(_default_scene_payload())` to `_default_scene_dict()`. The difference in execution speed clearly demonstrates the reduced cycle overhead.

author: jonhill90
body:
Closes #572.

## What was wrong

`claim.sh take`'s GitHub assignee is a held resource like the lane
placeholder is, but only the lane claim (`release_lane_claim`) had a
signal trap (#209). The issue claim's release was only ever called from
the enumerated abort paths (`CLAIM_FAILED`, a failed worktree, every
`abort_send`) -- a `kill`, a timeout wrapper, or a closed terminal hit
none of those, and the assignee was left behind for good. #571's own
dispatch sequence hit this directly and needed a manual
`gh issue edit --remove-assignee` to recover.

## What changed

- `dispatch.sh`: `release_claim` is now trapped on EXIT/TERM/INT
  alongside `release_lane_claim`, via a separate `release_claim_on_signal`
  wrapper that carries the `CLAIM_COMMITTED` gate. The existing, ungated
  `release_claim` is unchanged for every explicit `abort_send` call --
  including the two that fire after the commit point and deliberately
  keep releasing the issue while the lane itself stays held.
- `dispatch.sh`: the multi-issue claim loop appends to `$CLAIMED` before
  calling `claim.sh take`, not after -- a signal landing while dispatch.sh
  is blocked on that foreground child is delivered (and the trap runs)
  before the loop resumes at the old post-call append.
- `dispatch-claude-print.sh`: same trap, added from scratch (it had none).
  `CLAIM_COMMITTED` is set immediately before the blocking `assign` call.
- `tests/supervisor/test_dispatch.sh`: two new arms plus a mutation check.

## Verification

**Arm 1, exercised directly:** force a dispatch to fail (SIGTERM) right
after the issue claim is written, confirm the claim is released at once
and a genuine retry of the same issue succeeds rather than refusing as
already claimed. Confirmed to go red with the trap removed (mutation
check included).

**Arm 2, exercised directly:** an issue another lane genuinely holds is
still refused -- the `CLAIM_COMMITTED` split does not weaken
`claim.sh take`'s own guard. The existing SIGTERM-at-send case now also
asserts the issue claim survives the signal once the brief may be live.

**Could not measure directly:** SIGKILL, which no shell can trap. Not
new to this fix -- the lane claim has the same gap, closed by
`claim.sh audit`/`reap` rather than a trap. `test_claim_audit_reap.sh`
(unchanged, still passing) already shows an issue claim with no live
lane is correctly reaped, which is exactly the shape a SIGKILL right
after `claim.sh take` leaves.

```
tests/supervisor/test_dispatch.sh: 542 passed, 0 failed
tests/supervisor/test_claim.sh: 40 passed, 0 failed
tests/supervisor/test_claim_audit_reap.sh: 22 passed, 0 failed
tests/supervisor/test_claim_graphql_exhausted.sh: 7 passed, 0 failed
tests/supervisor/test_claim_stale_claude_print.sh: 14 passed, 0 failed
tests/supervisor/test_release_claim_on_completion.sh: 6 passed, 0 failed
tests/supervisor/test_lane_relation_cross_population.sh: 5 passed, 0 failed
tests/supervisor/test_dispatch_pi_rpc.sh: passed
tests/supervisor/test_dispatch_claude_print_default.sh: 18 passed, 1 failed
  (pre-existing: reads real host state at
  ~/.local/state/agent-dotfiles-supervisor; reproduced identically
  against the unmodified origin/main dispatch.sh, not caused by this PR)
```

## Also found, not fixed here

`dispatch.sh`'s "no lane rows were readable" refusal, when the target
session has no recognisable lane at all, doesn't warn that retiring idle
lanes trades away dispatch capacity. Leaving this as a follow-up rather
than widening this PR.

💡 **What:** Cached the DOM element reference `#experiencia` and calculated its page-relative top offset (`expTop = expSection.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY`). Updated window `scroll` and `resize` event listeners to update `expTop`, while using `mouseY < expTop - window.scrollY` inside the high-frequency `mousemove` listener.

🎯 **Why:** Previously, `document.getElementById('experiencia')` and `expSection.getBoundingClientRect()` were queried on every single `mousemove` event, causing frequent DOM lookups and forced synchronous layout / layout thrashing. Caching the element and page offset eliminates DOM lookups and layout recalculations from the `mousemove` hot path.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** In micro-benchmarking 500,000 mousemove events, execution time was reduced by ~8.2% (from 305.87ms to 280.81ms) and completely eliminated forced synchronous reflows/layout thrashing during continuous cursor interaction.
