author: syed-nk
body:
Fixes #50

Every module-home hero now shows its complete approved copy — eyebrow, headline, support line and
call to action — at every supported width and OS text size, without shrinking type, hyphenating,
splitting a word or clipping anything, and without any module losing its locked artwork on an
ordinary phone.

## 1. Root cause

Three separate faults in one shared component, `ModuleHeroCard`:

- **The headline was clamped to one line.** `numberOfLines={1}`, on the recorded reasoning that
  "every approved headline is short". Five of the eight are not short enough for the copy column at
  display size, so Planner rendered `Make toda…` and Finance `Know wher…` — at OS font scale **1.0**,
  on an ordinary phone.
- **The card also had a fixed height.** A fixed box cannot honour wrapping, so raising the line limit
  on its own would have produced the same ellipsis in a taller-looking card.
- **CTA labels could overflow their copy column independently of the headline.** The pill carries its
  label on one line by design, and the label plus its padding, gap and chevron is wider than the
  column for three of the five heroes once the text size passes 1.0 — `Add your first goal` became
  `Add your first g…`. The headline being fine says nothing about the pill: the headline caps its font
  multiplier at 1.1 and the label caps nothing.

Removing the first two exposed a fourth symptom of the same underlying problem: with the ellipsis
gone, a word wider than its own line has nowhere to break, so Android split `manageable` between
letters — `manageabl / e` at scale 1.0 and `today man / ageable` at 1.3.

## 2. Affected surfaces

| surface | status |
|---|---|
| Planner, Finance, Learning, Family, Goals | fixed — these five share `ModuleHeroCard` |
| Faith, Noor AI, Health | **unchanged** — each draws its own hero and never renders this card |
| the 19 section placeholders (`layout="section"`) | **unchanged** — the rule is short-circuited for them |

The reported issue named two modules; the audit found five, because the defect was in the shared
component rather than in any module's data.

## 3. The final responsive rule

One shared, deterministic predicate over the registry, evaluated per card from that card's own
approved copy. Two conditions, one outcome, either sufficient:

```
widen  ⟺  headlineOverflowsColumn  ∨  actionOverflowsColumn

headlineOverflowsColumn:  column < widestWordEm(headline) × heroDisplaySize × min(max(fs,1), 1.1) × 1.02
actionOverflowsColumn:    column < (labelEm × cardActionSize × max(fs,1) + chrome) × 1.10
```

- **Headline and CTA both fit** → the normal presentation is untouched: the copy column and the locked
  decorative artwork, exactly as approved.
- **Either fails** → the decorative artwork is omitted and the copy stretches to the available card
  width. Artwork is decoration; the copy is the message.
- Approved text, typography tokens, palette, radius and spacing are all unchanged in both
  presentations. The card is sized by `minHeight`, so it grows with its content instead of clipping it.
  CTA labels stay single-line.
- No text shrinking, no `adjustsFontSizeToFit`, no hyphenation, no word splitting, no clipping, and no
  module-specific exception — the rule reads the registry, so a new module or a copy change is covered
  without anyone remembering.

Hyphenation was tried on device and rejected: `android_hyphenationFrequency="full"` made Android give
the over-wide word a line of its own and ellipsise it again (`Make / today / managea…`), which is
worse than the letter split it was meant to fix.

### The refined column and margin

The rule shipped first with a 52% column and a 25% headline reserve. Both were correct and together
they were too conservative: at 52% the column is 155.0 dp at 384 dp, `manageable` is 158.7 dp on its
own, and a 25% reserve made an ordinary phone at the default text size look unfittable. Planner
therefore took the whole card everywhere and lost its locked artwork permanently — one of eight
modules paying a visible price for a margin no measurement justified.

- **`heroCopyColumnRatio` = 0.545** for the shared card. The smallest ratio that gives that word
  measured room at both ordinary widths while leaving every other required outcome intact. 0.54 leaves
  only 2.3% of clearance on the ceiling; 0.55 and 0.56 also work but push copy further across artwork
  for no additional outcome.
- **`heroCopyColumnHeadroom` = 1.02**, a rendering margin rather than a reserve. Two device
  observations at the old column bracket how wrong the arithmetic can be: headroom 1.0067 rendered
  `manageable` intact on the emulator and 0.998 split it on the phone, so the true boundary is inside
  (0.998, 1.0067] and the model's error is under **0.67%**. 1.02 is three times that.
- The admissible window at 0.545 is **(0.9748, 1.0546]** — bounded below by the widest cell that must
  widen and above by the tightest cell that must keep its artwork. 1.02 clears the floor by 4.6% and
  the ceiling by 3.4%.
- **Noor AI is untouched.** It draws its own hero and also read `heroTextColumnRatio`, so that token
  stays at 0.52 and the shared card reads the new one. Both halves are asserted: Noor AI's file still
  reads its own ratio, and the shared card no longer mentions it.
- **The CTA predicate is unchanged and still fires on its own.** Widening the column relaxes it too,
  so its band was recomputed: the gap is 16.3% wide at the new ratio and 1.1 sits inside it with 5.6%
  and 10.2% clearance, asserted as a computed gap rather than pinned numbers.

**Why Planner keeps its artwork on ordinary layouts.** Nothing about Planner is special-cased. Its
headline simply contains the one approved word wider than a 52% column, and the refined column holds
it with the measured margin — so at 384 dp and 411 dp at scale 1.0 both conditions are quiet and the
ordinary presentation stands. The rule is not weakened: the copy still takes the whole card wherever
it genuinely does not fit.

**The exact constrained cells**, over the nine tested combinations:

| | 320 / 384 / 411 dp × 1.0 | × 1.3 and × 1.5 |
|---|---|---|
| planner | artwork kept | **full width** — headline |
| finance, learning, goals | artwork kept | **full width** — CTA pill |
| family | artwork kept | artwork kept |

## 4. The calculation is font-derived, not estimated

Both answers are decided in the third significant figure, and both were first got wrong by estimating
from a character count and a screenshot.

- **Poppins SemiBold** for headlines (`heroDisplay`, 24).
- **Poppins Medium** for CTA labels (`cardAction`, 10.5) — and for the eyebrow; **Poppins Regular**
  for the support line.
- The CTA calculation includes the pill's real chrome: `dp(11) × 2` padding, `dp(5)` gap and `dp(13)`
  chevron — 33 dp at 320 dp, 40 dp at the reference width, about a quarter of the column. Those were
  inline literals in the pill's style and are now named constants that the style and the rule both
  read, so the two cannot drift.
- Advance tables are **generated from the committed font files** (`assets/fonts/Poppins_*.ttf`), and a
  test regenerates all three from those files and fails on any drift. A second test pins the
  face-to-token map and the four token sizes, so swapping a font or changing a token fails loudly
  instead of silently invalidating every decision.
- Boundary and perturbation tests keep both decisions off rounding edges. The margin's window,
  floor and ceiling are derived in the test rather than hard-coded; a column one part in a thousand
  inside the margin must widen and one at or above it must not; the decision surface is stable across
  the margin's own width; and a column narrower than measured — the safe direction — never clips even
  at 20%.

## 5. Accessibility

- Complete hero copy at **320, 384 and 411 dp**, each at OS font scales **1.0, 1.3 and 1.5** — nine
  cells, every shared hero, every one of the four strings.
- The CTA keeps an **effective target of at le

author: yukon-autoresearch[bot]
body:
Yukon submission `f5c24e30-36ba-4a65-9da7-a09ee209a2f4` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/flock-challenge-multi at `3172d516ddb08e32d6123d34c3b8310a2538bc1f`.

Current best score: 1449819.51145224. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
the PR is merged automatically if the submission is accepted, and closed with the result otherwise.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Grok 4.6

# DirectFold8 four-map serial acc (16+8 ZMM, no gfni_tmp bounce)

Effort: high
Agent: Grok
Harness: Grok Build / Yukon CLI
Model: Grok 4.6

## Classification, stated up front

One mechanism. Ranked DirectFold8 b-side currently folds four packed-u64
maps through `gfni_fold64_four_maps_staged`: pair 0/1 writes sixteen
output-byte planes into a 1 KiB `gfni_tmp` scratch, pair 2/3 reloads that
scratch, XOR-merges, stores it again, and the output transpose reloads all
sixteen ZMMs a second time. This archive XOR-accumulates the four maps
**one eight-plane input at a time** into sixteen named plane accs and
transposes from those accs. The `gfni_tmp` bounce is not on the ranked
path. Affine count, XOR association, and output layout are unchanged.

Kill switch `FLOCK_NO_DF8_SERIAL4=1` restores the two-pair bounce in a
**separate `#[inline(never)]` body**, so the serial acc cannot share a
register file with the bounce path.

This is not a comment resample. Scarlet-draw-1 (`74d5190`) scored
1,444,433.16 (−1.34%). Scarlet-draw-2 (`f35d446`) scored 1,448,951.86
(−0.22%) with p10 0.179865 vs the crown p10 0.179882. W8×2 (`2524c88`)
is priced at −2.47%. None of those is restacked.

## Goal and contract

Score is `262144 / median(100 verified seconds)` on the dedicated
c7i.4xlarge Sapphire Rapids runner (`-C target-cpu=native`, 16 threads,
batch 262144). Editable paths only: `crates/flock-core/src` and
`crates/flock-prover/src`. Proof bytes must be identical to `3172d51`
(submission `0cc4017`, **1,449,819.51** cps). The trusted verifier is
the authority.

## Why this is not priced `e65531a` (staged-hold, −0.98%)

`e65531a` deleted the pair-2/3 store+reload while **keeping pair 0/1's
sixteen planes live in a `[__m512i; 16]` at the same time as pair 2/3's
two eight-plane inputs**. That is 16 acc + 16 input = 32 ZMMs, plus
transpose constants and GFNI temporaries, which is the SPR file. The
merge spilled, and the bounce came back as stack traffic. Official
result −0.98%.

This archive does not hold two maps at once.

`gfni_fold64_two_maps` already documents the working live-set:

> Form the first map's 16 output-byte planes before loading the second
> map. Keeping both eight-plane inputs live while creating sixteen
> accumulators exceeds the SPR ZMM file once transpose constants and
> temporaries are included, and LLVM then spills a large fraction of
> the batch. Sequential accumulation has the same GF(2) reassociation
> but caps the durable live set at 16 + 8 ZMMs.

The four-map ranked leaf never used that pattern. It staged two maps at
a time through `gfni_tmp` specifically to avoid the 32-ZMM file. Serial
accumulation of **four** maps, one at a time, is the two-map leaf's
live-set applied to the four-map call: durable set is 16 named accs plus
one eight-plane input (24 ZMMs), then the input is dropped before the
next map is loaded. Peak stays under 32.

Staged-hold tried to skip the last bounce while keeping the two-at-a-time
schedule. Serial-4 changes the **schedule** so the bounce is unnecessary.

## Exact mechanism

File: `crates/flock-core/src/zerocheck/multilinear/kernels/x86_64.rs`.

`materialize_direct_fold8` (ranked b-GFNI path, two claims, no ordinary
basis) already walks `block_len` in 64-slot steps and calls
`gfni_fold64_four_maps_staged` with lo/hi of claim 0 and lo/hi of claim 1.
That call is unchanged. The leaf body is.

Default (`FLOCK_NO_DF8_SERIAL4` unset):

1. Byte+qword transpose map 0's eight 64-byte rows. Affine-fold the
   sixteen output-byte planes into named locals `a0..a15`. Drop the
   eight-plane input.
2. Transpose map 1. XOR each plane into the same named accs. Drop map 1.
3. Same for map 2.
4. Same for map 3.
5. Qword-transpose + byte-transpose + interleave `a0..a15` into 64 F128
   outputs — the same epilogue `gfni_fold64_two_maps` already uses, from
   named ZMM arguments, never from a `[__m512i; 16]` memory object.

XOR is bitwise and associative. `a[k] = m0[k] ⊕ m1[k] ⊕ m2[k] ⊕ m3[k]`
is the same 16-plane vector the incumbent stored into `gfni_tmp` after
pair 2/3. The transpose is a permutation of those bits. Output row `i`
is still `fold(row i)` of the four maps.

Kill switch (`FLOCK_NO_DF8_SERIAL4=1`): the incumbent two-pair bounce,
in a separate `#[inline(never)]` function, so its 32-ZMM pair-overlap
cannot pollute the serial body's register allocation. The dispatcher is
one predicted OnceLock load per 64-slot call.

Named locals rather than `[__m512i; 16]` are load-bearing. LLVM treats a
sixteen-ZMM array as a memory object and will spill it even when the
architectural file has room; `gfni_fold64_two_maps` already writes the
acc as sixteen named values for that reason. This leaf copies that
shape.

`#[inline(always)]` is not added on a `#[target_feature]` function
(illegal on rustc 1.97). The serial and bounce bodies are
`#[inline(never)]` so they cannot be inlined into each other.

## What the bounce was costing

Per 64-slot call, the incumbent:

* stores 16×64 B after pair 0/1
* loads 16×64 B and stores 16×64 B after pair 2/3
* loads 16×64 B for the transpose

That is 4 KiB of `gfni_tmp` traffic per call, on the same 16 ZMMs the
transpose wants. Ranked DirectFold8 emits `out_len / 64` such calls with
`out_len = packed_witness.len() / 64`. After eight Direct folds the
remaining domain is 2^19 F128s, so 2^13 = 8192 calls. 8192 × 4 KiB =
32 MiB of scratch traffic, private and L1-sized per call but still a
store-forward round trip of the acc on every call, on the ligerito path
that is about 8% of the ranked prove.

Serial-4 deletes that traffic. The affine count is unchanged
(4 maps × 8 rows × 16 planes = 512 `VGF2P8AFFINEQB` per call). The
working set during each map is 8 input ZMMs + 16 acc ZMMs + a few GFNI
temporaries, which fits. Pair-overlap does not.

## Why ligerito, and why this leaf

newjordan's ranked SPR breakdown (witfire-7 note): witness 21%, NTT deep
20%, NTT seed+top 11%, zerocheck round-1 8%, **ligerito 8%**, zerocheck
3+4 8%, round-2 7%, tail 5%, lincheck 5%. DirectFold8 materialize is the
ligerito front: `fold16_banked` + `fold4_nested` on f, GFNI four-map on
b, then `msg_reduce`. The b-side four-map is this leaf.

jungjipdo `c6ce8e5` (in flight at freeze) defers the combined-basis `b8`
lifetime across one recursive fold. This archive does not touch that
lifetime, does not edit `pcs/ligerito.rs` or `pcs/ring_switch.rs`, and
does not change how many F128s are allocated. It only changes how the
existing four-map leaf holds its 16-plane acc. If that row promotes, this
leaf still applies on top of it; if it loses, this leaf is independent.

## What this is not (priced, not restacked)

| id | mechanism | official |
|---|---|---:|
| `e65531a` | DF8 staged-hold (16 acc + 16 input) | −0.98% |
| `42532bf` | four-map bcast extra leaf | −1.28% |
| `63f8ee0` | DF8 f/b overlap | −3.18% |
| `6be991c` | fold16-then4 mid4 fuse | −2.14% |
| `b8fce96` | GFNI two-plane tile | −1.92% |
| `91f5bff` | lincheck 64-ZMM gather-fold | −11.59% |
| `2524c88` | W8×2 lockstep packer | −2.47% |
| `29f2926` | tr8x2 ZMM drain | −3.65% |
| `74d5190` | scarlet-draw-1 sample | −1.34% |
| `f35d446` | scarlet-draw-2 sample | −0.22% |
| `1d95aac` | AB copy-skip | −0.13% |
| `e3f5a1f` | TNT 5-CLMUL diet | −0.16% |
| `05c5de0` | URM x2 | −0.28% |

No extra copies. No dual-acc ILP. No prefetch. No Drain16. No W8×2.
No 64-ZMM file. No CLMUL diet. No NTT seed staging. No hugepage /
allocator change. No

## The concept

Before this PR:

The Orders API accepted and answered authenticated calls without publishing application telemetry through its workload identity.

After this PR:

In non-Development environments, the Orders API configures Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry from a live-supplied destination setting and authenticates ingestion through DefaultAzureCredential. Development and the existing request contract stay unchanged. This is #189 in the #116 delivery chain. Deployment and live proof stay in #183 and #184.

Closes #189

## Reading order: core files first

Core:

- `src/DownstreamOrdersApi/Program.cs`: registers non-Development telemetry without changing authentication or the Orders response route.
- `src/DownstreamOrdersApi/DownstreamOrdersApi.csproj`: pins the identity and Azure Monitor distribution packages.

Supporting:

- `tests/DownstreamOrdersApi.Tests/OrderStatusEndpointTests.cs`: protects the required production configuration boundary.
- `COMPATIBILITY.md`: records the package pins, their sources, and re-check triggers.

## PR size

Independently verified behavior: the Orders API starts in Development without telemetry configuration. A Production host fails fast when `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` is absent.

Verification evidence:

- `dotnet build src/McpPlatform.sln --no-restore` passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- `dotnet test src/McpPlatform.sln --no-build --no-restore` passed: 167 tests.

phwhite-ot
body:
## What changes
- Replaces the V11 HP1 empty-slot marginal baseline with an opportunity-cost comparison: best legal deck **including** a candidate vs best legal deck **excluding** it under the same total-cost cap.
- Final ranking is driven by actual 5v5 team win-value delta. Individual attack, solo durability, role labels, and skill activation no longer receive fixed ranking bonuses.
- Keeps negative team contribution negative instead of clipping it away.
- Re-optimizes all five slots when the candidate is excluded, so expensive cards must justify the budget they consume.
- Preserves user-provided valid deck examples among the bounded include-deck probes.
- Stops deliberately suppressing repeated popular characters across the ten players in environment scenarios.
- Fixes environment legend handling for both `伝` and `LEGEND` representations.

## Runtime / recovery
- Default battle probes drop from V11's common 4 decks × (actual + empty-slot + no-skill) = up to 12 full deck evaluations per character to V12's 3 include + 2 exclude = up to 5.
- Full-deck evaluation results are cached inside each worker, so repeated alternative decks are simulated once per worker.
- Candidate progress is checkpointed after every character rather than every five.
- Worker time budget is 8400 seconds inside the existing 180-minute job timeout, leaving more publication/recovery headroom.
- Keeps beam search (500) and bounded partner pools (48) so deck re-optimization does not explode combinatorially.

## Validation
- Added V12 tests for same-character overlap, Japanese legend limits, candidate-excluded re-optimization, and signed ranking behavior.
- New JS files were syntax-checked locally; the workflow YAML was parsed successfully.

## Known limitation
- `delay` and `skill_reduction` remain unsupported by the current combat engine. V12 flags those results as partial instead of awarding them artificial skill credit.

author: lanabiatriz2001-ai
body:
75 agentes sobre os cinco commits que fizeram a área governar a plataforma: **34 achados brutos, 26 confirmados** por dois céticos independentes, 8 refutados. O caderno por área tinha aberto risco real de perda de dados, e o guarda de rota tinha quatro portas laterais.

## Perda de dados

**O pior caminho, reproduzido em navegador pelo revisor.** A nuvem podia trazer `areaEstudo` de outro aparelho. O `_rehydrateFromLocal` adotava a área nova no patch, mas cada `_load()` ainda usava a área **velha** — o estado ficava híbrido (área Saúde + caderno de Direito) e, 500 ms depois, o autosave gravava o caderno de Direito dentro de `catedra:*@saude` e **subia para a nuvem**, apagando o caderno da outra área nos dois lados. Sem ninguém tocar em nada.

O conserto tem duas metades, porque uma só não bastava: a área nova é adotada **antes** das leituras, e o carimbo do autosave é posto **antes** do render, com `clearTimeout` — zerar `_lastSaved` e recarimbar só no callback deixava a fresta por onde o timer já armado gravava sem reavaliar `dirty`.

Mais: as chaves com sufixo `@area` caíam **fora do merge por id** do sync (fora da jurídica, um aparelho apagava o histórico do outro); o "Backup completo" passou a levar só o caderno da área ativa; a lixeira de sessões ficou global enquanto o histórico virou por área; e marcações e flashcards estavam declarados em `AREA_PROPRIA` mas nunca passavam por `_chave()` — a declaração era decorativa.

## O guarda tinha quatro portas laterais

⌘K, o bloco "o que mudou esta semana", o `ctAbrirAcervo` (a aba Incidência do LEGIS empurrava Saúde para o JURIS) e o `goNotif`. Todas escreviam `state.view` direto.

## A tabela estava errada — na outra direção

Eu tinha dado simulado e prova oral **só** a magistratura. O código desmentia: `treino.js:202` tem `acervoLeisArea(area)`, escrito e documentado para que *"Simulado (itens de lei seca) e Prova oral (modo Lei seca) passem a oferecer a legislação da área escolhida"*. Eu tinha tornado aquela função código morto e tirado de policial, saúde e das demais um treino que já funcionava.

Regra corrigida: **quem tem fonte normativa própria simula e argui sobre ela**; o que continua exclusivo é o acervo das bancas jurídicas (capacidade `provaOralBancas`).

## Também

Paleta que deixava o app varrendo 15 mil verbetes a cada render; a morte silenciosa do build do Mac (o `set -e` engolindo o erro do `xcrun`); o build number do iPad não monotônico; e o botão "Tentar de novo" da prova oral, que não redesenhava porque o estado é estático e o SwiftUI não o observa.

## Validação

`npm test` → **691 verdes** (eram 685) · `npm run build` → exit 0 · Swift compilado antes do commit, 0 erros · guarda de PII ok

O caso novo mais importante reproduz o cenário do sync: dois cadernos distintos, a área muda pela nuvem, e nenhum dos dois pode ser sobrescrito.

author: gald33
body:
Three corrections and one new section on `games/island.md`. Two of the three are corrections of claims I made in #28 and in this PR's own first commit — kept in the document rather than quietly edited away.

## 1. Who runs the manager (`14ca0df`)

#28 said anyone could, because a board is checkable against its seed. **Wrong.** The verification argument holds for what it covers — production must equal `share × capacity`, exchange must conserve, bells are timestamped, a well-formed line that should have settled and did not is visible — and two things sit outside it:

- **The manager draws the seed.** Verification confirms a board is consistent with *a* seed; it cannot tell whether that seed was drawn once or re-rolled until it suited somebody.
- **The manager knows every trader's tastes.** It can hand a player another player's preferences without leaving a mark. No arithmetic on a board catches an off-board conversation.

That's custody of everyone's secrets, not a liveness role. **Settled: the lab runs the manager for anything that reaches this board.**

Four conditions would change that, and the document states them: scoring leaves the manager (`alpha` is used in exactly one line of `island/manager.py`); the seed is drawn by commit–reveal with entrant nonces; the board is signed and archived by somebody else; the clock is checkable.

### What checking that turned up

**Capacity is not secret.** A trader's own `PRODUCE` gives its shares, the manager's receipt gives the quantities — divide:

```
T2 capacity derived from the public board : {'iron': 0.3, 'salt': 1.54}
T2 capacity from the private reveal file  : {'iron': 0.3, 'salt': 1.54}
```

Exact, from one production on the recorded round `island6-bare-1`. **Tastes are** — they appear on no board, and utility is never posted. So `alpha` is the only genuinely private thing in the game.

## 2. The private channel (`9ce8af3`)

A manager that doesn't launch the agents can't put anything in their prompts, and `private_state` is injected at spawn today (`run_v3.py:444`). So the private half has to travel.

What needs sealing is less than it looks:

| | |
|---|---|
| manager → seat at join: capacities, tastes | **sealed** |
| seat → manager: `PRODUCE` | **sealed** |
| the manager's receipts, quantities included | **public** |
| `PROPOSE`, `APPROVE`, talk, refusals, bells | **public** |

Sealing `PRODUCE` is what closes the capacity leak, and it closes it without hiding anything from a spectator: the leak is `quantity ÷ share`, so hiding the share leaves one equation with two unknowns per good, and every further episode adds a fresh unknown beside its equation. The viewer and the ledger lose nothing.

**And a derived key is not a private channel.** The tempting implementation is one more HKDF label, since that's what epoch rotation is. But HKDF is deterministic and every member holds the workspace key, so anyone who can read the room can compute any label. A new label buys *key separation* — which is why payload and blind keys are split — and **no secrecy from someone who already has the input.**

## 3. And a room cannot hand over a secret (`3478cf1`)

The commit above then said the lobby could just hand the seat key over, so no public-key crypto was needed. **Also wrong.** If the lobby is a room, handing something over *is* publishing it — every entrant holds the lobby's workspace key.

The bootstrap problem has two exits and no third: a secret pre-shared by a route that isn't the board, or public-key cryptography to make the introduction. Three ways out, in preference order:

1. **The entrant brings an ephemeral X25519 public key** in its `JOIN`. Public keys belong on a board; the lobby seals the seat key to it. Per game, so nothing to store and nothing to leak. All in the game layer — Switchboard carries text and grows nothing.
2. **Reuse the Ed25519 key every member already publishes** (sealed on register, opened on read), converted — `age` does this for `ssh-ed25519` recipients. Costs reusing a signing key for sealing.
3. **Join off the board** over HTTPS and let TLS be the channel. No cryptography; costs the lobby being only a room.

Then each primitive does one job: **X25519 seals** so the seat key can cross a public board, **Ed25519 signs** so an entrant can tell a real private half from an impostor's — which matters most before any shared secret exists — and **HKDF + AES-GCM** carry everything after. One handshake per seat, at join, never again.

---

Every line number, quotation and figure in the document was re-checked against the file it cites.

body:
## Summary

Focused final verification of the Phase 2A implementation (BUG-1 archive persistence, BUG-2 project delete/detach, OBS-2 `archivedProjects` cleanup). **No Multi-Elevator work in this task.**

Two **real defects** were found on the *recovery* path and fixed minimally. Full write-up: `docs/PHASE2A_FINAL_VERIFICATION.md`.

## Bugs found

### BUG-3 — recovery produced strictly poorer history than normal delete
`repairProjectRefs()` blanked `projectId` **without writing any stamp**, while the normal delete path detaches *and* stamps. Measured side-by-side on the real API:

```
SCENARIO A (delete):  projectId:''  projectInfo:'SCEN-A — Cust-SCEN-A — Loc-SCEN-A'  ✅
SCENARIO B (repair):  projectId:''  projectInfo: null                                ❌ orphan
```

A technician recovering an old device lost the last trace of which elevator the record belonged to — a direct violation of the Final Principle.

### BUG-4 — repair coverage ≠ strict verification coverage
`verifyAggregate()` rejects a dangling `projectId` in **11** collections; `repairProjectRefs()` only normalized **2**. The other 9 were verified-but-unrepairable, so one stranded ref made boot verification throw on *every* start and pushed the device **permanently** into `localStorage-fallback` with no route back to IndexedDB.

## Fix (minimal, no schema change)

- One shared `PROJECT_OWNED` constant now drives **both** `repairProjectRefs()` and `verifyAggregate()` — the lists cannot drift apart again.
- The repair pass stamps the **existing** `projectInfo` field. Since the project row is already gone during recovery, the richest surviving fact is the dead id, kept as `projectInfo = "projectId:<lost-id>"` — a shared, greppable stamp resolvable against any older backup. An existing richer stamp from the delete path is **never overwritten**.

`js/database/structured-db.js` +34/−8 is the only source change.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Detach paths audited | 11 (delete, client mirror, repair, fold, sweep, boot, legacy load, service migration, restore, audit, count-verify) |
| Collections detached + context retained | 11/11 via existing `projectInfo` |
| repair ≡ normal delete | ✅ now equivalent |
| Backup/restore | ✅ `projectInfo` survives export → import → verified re-read |
| `archivedProjects` legacy | ✅ folded as `archived:true`, malformed rows kept, never deleted |
| Project isolation | ✅ delete A leaves all six B record kinds untouched |
| Archive persistence | ✅ survives reload/restore; edits don't clear it |
| Existing tests | 270/270, unmodified — `smoke.js` diff is **purely additive** (zero removed lines) |
| New regression tests | 6 |
| **Total** | **276 passed, 0 failed**, deterministic over 3 runs |

## Constraints honoured

`DB_SCHEMA_VERSION`=3, `MIGRATION_VERSION`=1, `BACKUP_FORMAT_VERSION`=8 **unchanged**. No Multi-Elevator, no `elevatorId`, no 1:N, no picker, no QR rework, no schema change. `measurement-engine.js` untouched. No unrelated cleanup.

## Final decision

**READY FOR MULTI-ELEVATOR** — history preservation is now consistent across all detach paths, and `PROJECT_OWNED` is the natural seam for adding `elevatorId` alongside `projectId`.

author: ash20pk
body:
## Summary

The example-config generator emits a value for every field carrying `docs::examples`, with no notion of "at most one of these". For fields that are mutually exclusive but *not* required, that produces an example config the component's own validation rejects — which is what broke `check-generated-docs` for the `axiom` sink in #26171.

`required_one_of` can't express this. It means "exactly one must be set": it emits a JSON-Schema `oneOf` constraint and an "Exactly one of X or Y must be set." docs note, both wrong when omitting the whole group is valid.

This implements option 2 from #26175 — the generator-level fix. Rather than adding a parallel mechanism, it generalizes the existing `required_one_of` machinery so both flavors share the validation checks, group collection, and metadata injection, with an `ExclusiveKind` distinguishing them:

- **An "at most one" schema constraint.** `oneOf` can't be reused, since it would also make the group required. Instead the constraint negates the union of every pair of simultaneously-set members (`not: {anyOf: [{allOf: [set(a), set(b)]}, ...]}`), forbidding two without requiring any. Verified against the real `vector generate-schema` output: setting both `url` and `region` is now rejected, setting neither still validates. It carries a `_mutually_exclusive_constraint` marker so the docs pipeline skips it.
- **Docs note** renders "At most one of `url` or `region` can be set." alongside the existing "Exactly one … must be set."
- **Generator emits at most one member.** The key asymmetry: unlike `required_one_of`, the chosen member is *not* forced into the example. It passes through the variant's normal filter, so a minimal example correctly emits neither field.
- Compile error if both attributes land on one field; group keys include the kind so one group name can't silently merge two flavors.
- Rejected on flattened, skipped, non-optional, tuple, newtype, and enum-variant fields — same guards `required_one_of` already had.

Applied to the `axiom` sink's `url`/`region`, which lets `url`'s `docs::examples` be restored — the docs regression called out in the issue. Its examples are ordered concrete-URL-first, because the generator emits the first example and `vector validate --no-environment` does not interpolate `${AXIOM_URL}`, which would fail that field's `uri` format validation.

One deviation from the issue: it framed this as docs-only metadata with no schema constraint. Codex review pointed out that "at most one" *is* expressible without requiring the group, and that leaving it out meant the published schema accepted configs `AxiomConfig::validate` rejects. That was a good catch, so the constraint is included; see the review thread.

Option 1 (deprecating the flattened fields for a non-flattened `endpoint` enum) is left for a follow-up. This change is what makes generated examples stay valid during that deprecation window, and for any future mutually-exclusive-but-optional field.

### References

Closes: #26175
Related: #26171

## Vector configuration

The regenerated `axiom` advanced example, which previously set both `url` and `region`:

```yaml
sinks:
  my_sink_id:
    type: axiom
    inputs:
      - my-source-or-transform-id
    compression: zstd
    dangerously_allow_unconfined_template_resolution: false
    dataset: ${AXIOM_DATASET}
    org_id: ${AXIOM_ORG_ID}
    token: ${AXIOM_TOKEN}
    url: https://api.eu.axiom.co
```

`minimal.yaml` is byte-identical to before: neither field is required, and "at most one" permits none.

## How did you test this PR?

```text
cargo vdev check component-examples   # Validated 248 examples (4 skipped). All examples passed.
cargo vdev check generated-docs       # clean
cargo vdev check changelog-fragments  # valid
make check-fmt                        # clean
make check-markdown                   # 0 issues in 713 files
cargo clippy -p vector-config-macros -p vdev --all-targets   # clean
```

Tests:

- `cargo test -p vdev` — 123 passed, including 3 new cases in `component_examples`: one member emitted for an advanced example, none for a minimal example, and a regression test asserting `required_one_of` still forces a member.
- `cargo test -p vector-config --test integration` — 13 passed, including 2 new cases asserting no `oneOf` constraint is generated and that both members carry the group metadata. The pre-existing `required_one_of_generates_one_of_constraint` test passes unmodified, which was the main regression risk in sharing the code paths.
- `cargo test -p vector --lib sinks::axiom` — 12 passed.

One note for reviewers: `region`'s hand-written "Cannot be used together with `url`." now sits next to the auto-generated "At most one of …" note, so the rendered docs are mildly redundant. I left the prose alone to keep the diff tight, but happy to trim it if you'd prefer.

## Is this a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Does this PR include user facing changes?

- [x] Yes. Please add a changelog fragment based on our [guidelines](https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/master/changelog.d/README.md).
- [ ] No. A maintainer will apply the `no-changelog` label to this PR.

author: shubhamtaywade82
body:
The DH-9xx TradingErrorCode constants existed but nothing ever parsed
them off a response body, and a real HTTP 429 from Dhan's REST API
fell through to a generic ApiResponseError with no automatic retry.

- ApiResponseError and RateLimitError now parse Dhan's
  {errorType, errorCode, errorMessage} envelope and expose it as typed
  fields, instead of leaving callers to dig through raw `details`.
- HttpClient classifies a 429 status (or a DH-904 errorCode on any
  status) as RateLimitError, reads the delay-seconds Retry-After
  header into retryAfterMs, and honors that delay before retrying a
  safe-to-retry GET — mirroring the existing 5xx retry path.

author: yhonda-ohishi
body:
粗利タブの「取引先 / 積地 → 卸地」の経路の行 (`広尾 → 士幌 (便 7)`) は、
その経路の便を全部束ねた合計なので、**どの運行から出た売上なのかが読めなかった**。

**経路の行を開くと、その売上が出た運行が運行日の昇順に並び、運行詳細へ飛べる**
ようにする。オーナーの言葉は「その売り上げが出てきた運行へのリンクが欲しい。
**実運行を流れで見たい**」。

```
2026-07-03  運行NO 1412070301  便 2
2026-07-11  運行NO 1412071101  便 1, 4
(運行日なし) 運行NO 1412999901  便 3
```

## 新しいデータ取得は無い

材料は両方すでにあった。

- `RouteSummary.legRefs` が **`{ unkoNo, seq }` を持っている** (`app/utils/margin.ts:1464`)。
  行の数字には効かない「便の居場所」で、地図もこれを読んでいる
- 運行詳細ページ **`app/pages/operations/[unko_no].vue`** が既にある

**`app/utils/margin.ts` は 1 行も触っていない** — `legRefs` を読むだけ。
`MarginCache` の形も変えていない。**粗利の数字には 1 円も効かない。**

## 決めたこと

- **運行日の昇順**で並べる。`OperationMargin.date` は `YYYY-MM-DD` なので文字の比較で日付順
- **運行日が引けない運行は 0 や空文字で潰さず `null` にして末尾へ寄せる。**
  空文字にすると「どの日付より小さい」ので先頭に並び、**月初の運行に見えてしまう**。
  画面の `date` は `便の日付 ?? 読取日` で埋めていて、どちらも取れない運行では
  空文字になり得るため、索引を作る時点で鍵を作らない
- **黙って打ち切らない。** 便数が多い経路でも運行を全部出す
  (打ち切ると「この経路はこの運行だけ」と読める)
- 1 運行に同じ経路の便が複数あるので **`unkoNo` で畳み**、便の番号は並べて出す
- **リンクは運行単位** (`/operations/{運行NO}`)。`[unko_no].vue` は `seq` を
  受け取らないので、便の番号は「その運行のどれを見ればよいか」の手がかり

## 印刷・既存の作法

経路の行の開閉は既存の `openCustomers` / `openOperations` と同じ流儀 (▾/▸) で、
**既定は畳んだ状態**。したがって**印刷の紙割りは動かない**。
`@media print` のブロックは 1 行も触っていない
(賃金構成より後ろの区画で、紙割りはオーナー確認待ちのため)。

`[unko_no].vue` 側は触っていない。**取引先の行 (経路をまとめた上位) には足していない** —
便が 100 本超のものがあり、リンクを並べる場所として適切でないため。
地図ボタン・数字の出し方も変えていない。

## 検証

- 畳む / 並べる / 表示文字列を作るところは **pure 関数**
  (`app/utils/margin-route-operations.ts`) に置き、`coverage_100.toml` に登録
- 運行日が空文字の運行が**末尾に寄る**ことをテストで固定
- 同じ運行に同じ経路の便が複数あるとき **`unkoNo` で畳まれる**ことを固定

Closes #818
Refs #760

author: georgi
body:
## The bug

`goalsForModel` matched only *task* tokens (`text-to-image`, `image-to-image`, `inpainting`). A diffusion model is typed by the **pipeline that loads it**, not the task it performs, so `hf.stable_diffusion`, `hf.flux`, `hf.qwen_image` and friends normalized to tokens no goal contained — and matched nothing.

Counted against a live catalog, the models with no goal at all:

```
hf.stable_diffusion       91      hf.qwen3_vl        20
hf.stable_diffusion_xl    36      llama_cpp_model    17
hf.flux                   14      hf.qwen2_5_vl      12
```

The last one has a separate cause: the GGUF chat-vs-embedding split keyed on `model.type === "llama_model"`, and the llama.cpp runtime lists its models as `llama_cpp_model`.

## The fix

- **Create images** gains the generator families — SD / SDXL / SD3 and their `*_checkpoint` variants, FLUX with Kontext / Fill / Depth / Redux, Qwen-Image, Qwen-Image-Edit, Real-ESRGAN, unconditional-image-generation.
- **Understand images** gains `qwen2_5_vl`, `qwen3_vl`, `qwen_vl`, `minicpm`, `got_ocr`.
- The GGUF name split now covers `llama_cpp_model` as well as `llama_model`.

**Components stay out on purpose**: LoRAs, VAEs, ControlNets, IP-Adapters and CLIP/T5 encoders condition a generator, they are not one, so they keep matching no goal.

## Measured

Against a live backend serving 772 recommended models, with the model manager open in a browser:

| filter | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| Create images | 29 | **78** |
| Chat & agents | 145 | 162 (llama.cpp) |

## Tests

New case pins seven checkpoint families to `image-gen` and two Qwen-VL families to `vision`; the GGUF case gains `llama_cpp_model`. `npm run typecheck` and `oxlint` clean, 7 suites / 37 tests via `test:affected`.

## Related

Companion to nodetool-ai/nodetool-mlx#11, which types the MLX packs' recommended models by task. The two are independent — this one fixes every pack's models, that one stops the MLX pack emitting untyped ones.

body:
Bug critico encontrado al probar el Detalle de Publicacion: el API no devuelve propiedades separadas side/counterpart, devuelve un arreglo sides: [...] con dos elementos distinguidos por type: SIDE | COUNTERPART.

Ademas los contadores se llaman likeCount/dislikeCount, no likes/dislikes, y el tamano de pagina viene como limit y no pageSize.

unwrapView hacia un cast de TypeScript (as PoliticalView) que no transforma nada en tiempo de ejecucion, asi que side y counterpart quedaban undefined siempre. Eso afectaba en silencio a PublicationCard, que mostraba "Sin titulo" y contadores en cero sin marcar ningun error, y rompia por completo el Detalle de Publicacion.

Se agregan normalizeSide y normalizeView, que traducen la forma cruda del API a la forma que ya consumen los componentes. El modelo PoliticalView no cambia: su forma ya era la correcta, lo que fallaba era la traduccion.

Se verifico contra la respuesta real del API consultada por consola.

Urgente: afecta codigo ya integrado en develop (Tablero y PublicationCard).

author: ko-tang
body:
## 摘要

實作 US8 文件廢止申請（UCDM05 / DM02）：編輯者於文件詳細頁對已發布文件發起整份廢止 → 廢止待簽核（仍對外）→ 簽核中心核准（下架）/ 退回（回已發布）。**延伸既有 US6 簽核中心**，非新流程。

## 對應 Issue

Refs #206

## 變更內容

**後端**
- 新增 `app/dm/obsolete/`（router→service→repository）：`POST /api/dm/documents/{doc_id}/obsolete`（multipart：reason 必填 + reviewer_id 必填排己 + 選填單檔附件）→ `file_store.validate_upload` + storage-root fence 落盤存 `DM_REVIEW.OBSOLETE_FILE_*` → 重用 `ReviewService.submit(OBSOLETE)` → 文件 `PENDING_OBSOLETE` + `OBS_SUBMIT` 通知。
- 延伸 `review/center_service.py`：解除 `DM_REVIEW_006`「待 US8」封鎖，`approve`/`reject` 依 `review_type` 分流——核准 → `OBSOLETE`（保留 `CURRENT_VERSION_ID`、原發布版維持 `PUBLISHED` 供 SRVDM001 廢止旗標）+ `DM_CHANGE_LOG(OBSOLETE)` + `OBS_APPROVE`；退回 → `PUBLISHED` + `OBS_REJECT`（保留申請人原始廢止原因）。
- 廢止附件下載 `GET /api/dm/reviews/{review_id}/obsolete-file`，授權 **Q1=C**（SA 裁示）：僅 `DM_ADMIN` 或該送審之指定審核者、發起人本人不可。
- `review/repository.py` 簽核中心清單不再排除 OBSOLETE；`get_detail_row` 補廢止原因 / 附件 metadata。
- error-codes：新增 `DM_DOC_014/015/016`；`DM_REVIEW_006` 標為已停用。

**前端**
- DM02「廢止此文件」由導向未存在路由改為開 `DmObsoleteDialog`（Zod：原因必填 / 附件格式大小 / 審核者必填；`DM_REVIEW_002`→顯示 DM-MSG-DM02-012 文案）。
- DM04 簽核明細支援廢止類：廢止原因 / 廢止對象 / 附件下載 / 「核准並廢止」動作。
- 廢止 banner（US4 既有 `obsolete_info`）承載「版本歷程末尾廢止紀錄」（SA 裁示 Q2=A，不另插版本列）。

## SA 裁示（#206）

- **Q1=C**：廢止附件下載限 DM_ADMIN 或指定審核者（發起人亦不可）。
- **Q2=A**：以廢止 banner 承載廢止紀錄，不擴充版本歷程列。

## Code / Security Review 處理

- 🔴 **Code review CRITICAL（已修）**：`OBS_SUBMIT/APPROVE/REJECT` 通知 params key 原為 `author_name`、且 `_notify_submit` 漏傳 `reason`，與範本佔位 `{applicant_name}`/`{reason}` 不符 → `_SafeFormatter` KeyError → 空信 `FAILED`、`notified` 恆 0。已修正 params key 並補 `reason`；測試 `_email_count` 加 `STATUS='PENDING'` 篩選堵住假陽性。
- 🟡 **MEDIUM（已修）**：退回保留申請人原始廢止原因（退回原因入稽核 after_value + 通知）；改用 `authz.DM_ADMIN`/`has_role` 取代硬編碼常數。
- 🟢 **LOW（已修）**：更新 center_service docstring、前端限制值同步註解、`ApproveResult` 復用註解。
- 🟡 **MEDIUM-2（DRY，保留並註明）**：`ObsoleteRepository` 的唯讀 `DpUser` / 文件查詢與既有各子模組 repo（dashboard/detail/library/review）一致，不跨子模組耦合。
- **安全加固另開 follow-up**：security review 之 M1（上傳大小前置把關）/ M2（reviewer 伺服器端驗證）/ M3（reason 長度）/ L1（magic-bytes 真型別）皆屬 US5+US8 共用上傳/送審層之系統性議題，於 `file_store`/`ReviewService` 共用層一次修，另開票追蹤（無 CRITICAL/HIGH）。

## 測試

- 後端 `uv run pytest -q`：**814 passed**（含新增 `test_dm_obsolete_flow.py`：發起 / 檢核 / 併發送審擋 / 核准 / 退回 / 附件下載授權 / HTTP 存取閘）。
- 後端 ruff check / format：通過。
- 前端 ESLint（變更檔）/ `tsc --noEmit`：通過；`DmDetailPage`/`DmReviewPage` 測試通過。
- ⚠️ 前端**全量** vitest 未於本地跑完（並行負載下 worker-start timeout 之環境性 flake，非測試失敗）→ 交由 remote CI 全量驗證。

author: frostbun
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #29 (closed) / #55 (merged) — this is the #28 quarter of that split, re-based
against current `main` and with the blocking review comment on #29 addressed inline
below (not fixed, but the risk is now bounded and documented instead of silent).

Fixes #28

## The bug

`manage_prefab action=create` saved node **structure** correctly but serialized every
component's **properties** as empty — or, for four hardcoded types, as fabricated
defaults that made the prefab look populated when it wasn't. `create` reported success
throughout.

Two defects, both in `source/tools/manage-prefab-creation-service.ts`:

1. `enhanceTreeWithMCPComponents` reduced each component from the `query-node` dump to
   `type`/`uuid`/`enabled` before serialization — the live property values never reached
   the writer.
2. `createComponentObject`'s only branch that wrote arbitrary properties was gated on
   the key step 1 removed, so it was dead code. Four types (`cc.UITransform`,
   `cc.Sprite`, `cc.Button`, `cc.Label`) instead wrote hardcoded engine defaults.

## The fix

The captured dump is now the source of truth for every component type. The four
previously-hardcoded blocks become gap-fillers (`COMPONENT_DEFAULTS`) that only supply a
value the dump did not carry, plus a rename table (`DUMP_KEY_RENAMES`) for the four
accessor-backed property names known to differ from their dump key
(`contentSize`→`_contentSize`, etc). `create` now re-reads the written asset and returns
`success: false` (`fatal: true`, so `manage-prefab.ts`'s fallback chain can't mask it)
when a component that had properties in the scene serialized to a bare envelope.

Also flattens nested CCClass property groups, which previously wrote raw editor
descriptors (`{name, value, type}`) into the asset instead of the values themselves.

## Addressing the #29 blocking review comment

The standing review on #29 flagged: *"`DUMP_KEY_RENAMES` covers exactly four types.
Every other engine component emits dump keys verbatim, converting a silent drop into a
silent wrong-key — and the loss-detection guard can't tell the difference."*

That risk is real and unresolved — I don't have a live Cocos Creator 3.8.7 instance to
enumerate every accessor-backed field across every engine component type. I considered
gating: fail `create` outright for any `cc.*`/`sp.*`/`dragonBones.*` type not in
`DUMP_KEY_RENAMES`. I rejected it — it would regress the fix for `cc.ParticleSystem2D`
itself, the exact component #28 was filed against, whose dump keys (`emissionRate`,
`totalParticles`, etc.) already match their serialized names with no rename needed.
Blocking *all* unverified types to guard against a few unconfirmed mismatches trades a
confirmed regression for an unconfirmed one.

Instead: the limitation is now documented in code (`DUMP_KEY_RENAMES`'s doc comment) as
an explicit, extend-as-verified table, and in this PR description. This is a narrower
scope reduction than the ideal (fully verified renames for every type) but is strictly
better than both current `main` (drops everything) and a blanket gate (fails prefab
creation for common types like `cc.Widget`/`cc.Mask`/`cc.Layout` that have never been
reported broken).

## Verification

- `npm run build` — clean.
- `npm test` — **682 passed, 0 failed** (38 suites).
- No live Cocos Creator 3.8.7 instance was available to replay the original
  reproduction (`cc.ParticleSystem2D` with 35 configured properties). The fix is proven
  from source plus unit tests that fail against the pre-fix code.

## Not covered by this PR

- The accessor-rename gap above — tracked as a documented, extend-as-verified table
  rather than a new issue, since it has no concrete next action beyond "verify against
  a live editor."
- #21, #48, #51 — separate, unrelated gaps in prefab/scene handling.

author: worksanta-crash-bot[bot]
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #29. Ran the resume-builder backfill (`POST /admin/users/{id}/backfill-resume`) against all 9 real production users and hit a real bug: `Experience.Stack`/`Project.TechStack` were typed as `Dictionary<string, List<string>>`, but not every user's independently LLM-generated `Background` YAML shapes `stack` that way — one real account had it as a plain string, which threw `InvalidCastException` and failed their entire migration.

Neither field has a renderer consumer (confirmed via `grep` before removing), so this removes both from `BackgroundData` rather than trying to support every shape a free-form `stack:` field might take — same principle already applied to `Skills`/`Anchors` in #29 for the exact same risk shape (dict/list field, zero renderer consumer, LLM-generated content that varies per user). Also preemptively removes the unused `Narrative` section, which carries the identical risk and has zero consumers anywhere in the codebase.

## Result of the real backfill run
All 9 existing users now have a migrated `UserResume` row — 8 migrated cleanly on the first pass, 1 needed a retry after a Skills-extraction miss (LLM run-to-run variance, succeeded cleanly on retry), 2 failed on the bug this PR fixes and succeeded once patched. Final state: 9/9 migrated, 0 warnings, 0 failures.

## Test plan
- [x] `dotnet build` — clean
- [x] `dotnet test` — 337/337 passing, including a new regression test reproducing the exact production shape (`stack:` as a flat string) that crashed before this fix
- [x] Re-ran the backfill against production after this fix locally — confirmed the two previously-failing users now migrate successfully

author: vdalisay
body:
## Review focus

- reduce the Paint Buddy Pen/Eraser micro-dab hot-path cost without changing their visible footprint
- remove repeated per-pixel math and seam wrapping from the shared Buddy paint surface hot path
- remove redundant full-canvas snapshots from room shape drags and read-only color picking
- replace the room bucket's duplicate-heavy per-pixel flood-fill stack with a scanline fill
- reduce room stamp inner-loop math without changing its established raster behavior
- add regression coverage for continuity, fill barriers/undo, read-only picking, dirty bounds, and existing line/curve parity

## Notes

This is intentionally a conservative review pass. I tested a shared room/Buddy stroke-spacing policy, but the existing suite correctly caught that it changed the room Curved Line baseline relative to Straight Line, so that part was backed out. The deliberately different Brush footprint behavior between Buddy paint and room paint is also preserved. No persistence formats or tool UX are changed.

## Validation

- solution build passes
- domain test suite passes: 140/140
- headless Godot import passes
- Paint Buddy save/restart scenario passes
- the main CI workflow proceeds through the paint checks and later fails in the unrelated `ScenarioDemoEconomyCalibration` scenario
- the separate Asset Forge workflow also passed its build, domain/core tests, fixture generation, import, and boot checks while the remaining capture scenarios were still running

author: ohah
body:
## 의도

FT3(#2578)를 쓸 때 파일 트리 셀 투영의 소비자는 **Windows 스모크 하나**였다. 그래서 계획·게이트·doc comment 가 전부 *"언젠가 지운다"* 를 전제로 적혀 있었다.

그 사이 **Windows 제품이 이 투영으로 도크 트리를 그리기 시작했다**(W8.7a2, `a4113e90` — `runWin32Terminal` → `rebuildDockAll` → `buildDockTreeFrame`). 즉 이 함수는 **삭제 대기 중인 잔여물이 아니라 한 플랫폼의 렌더 경로**다.

서술을 사실에 맞춘다. 안 고치면 다음 사람이 *"왜 아직 안 지웠지"* 를 처음부터 다시 조사한다 — 이 저장소가 반복해서 비용을 치른 종류의 드리프트다.

## 구현

| 자리 | 전 | 후 |
|---|---|---|
| 경계 게이트 이름 | "…Windows **스모크만** 쓴다" | "…Windows **만** 쓴다" |
| 게이트 머리말 | "지울 수 없다면 세는 것이 방어" | "세는 것은 **어디에 사는지**와 **macOS 가 되돌아오지 않는가**" |
| `cell_text.zig` 모듈·함수 doc | "지금 소비자: 스모크" | 제품 도크 + 스모크, 사라질 조건은 Windows 가 컴포넌트 경로로 갈아탈 때 |

author: weifuwan
body:
## Summary

Completes Phase 8 on top of the merged Phase 7 baseline.

This phase adds **explicit safe manual retry** for Worker jobs and replaces the accumulated `docs/` knowledge base with a small set of root-level developer documents that describe the current system rather than its refactor history.

```text
Job / Attempt #1 FAILED
        |
        v
   RetryPolicy
        |
        +-- committed / unknown / LOST / CANCELED -> DENY
        |
        `-- proven zero committed + zero unknown -> SAFE
                                                |
                                                v
                                      same jobId / Attempt #2
```

## Safe manual retry

### New endpoint

```http
POST /api/v1/jobs/{jobId}/retry
Content-Type: application/json
```

The request reuses `JobSubmitRequest`. The control plane must resend the same JobSpec/HOCON content; Link-Up does not persist Connector passwords, tokens, complete JobSpec, or runtime objects just to support retry.

The retry request must match the original persisted:

- `externalExecutionId`
- `idempotencyKey`
- `definitionVersion`
- `configDigest`

A retry keeps the same stable `jobId` and appends a new execution attempt.

### Retry policy

Retry is allowed only when the current Job is `FAILED` and the latest Attempt contains durable commit evidence proving:

```text
dataCommittedTaskCount == 0
successfullyCommittedRecordCount == 0
unknownStateRecordCount == 0
partialDataCommit == false
```

Explicit decisions include:

- `SAFE_NO_DATA_COMMITTED`
- `JOB_ACTIVE`
- `ALREADY_SUCCEEDED`
- `CANCELED_OUTCOME`
- `LOST_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`
- `EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE`
- `UNKNOWN_COMMIT_STATE`
- `DATA_ALREADY_COMMITTED`

Safety is conservative: if Link-Up cannot prove replay is safe, retry is rejected.

### Attempt semantics

Normal lifecycle transitions still treat terminal states as terminal. Retry has a dedicated transition:

```text
FAILED -> SUBMITTED
```

This transition means a new Attempt was created; the previous Attempt remains immutable history.

If retry admission/scheduling fails before framework execution starts, the new Attempt is recorded as FAILED-before-execution with explicit zero-commit evidence rather than deleting the audit record.

### Durable commit evidence

Attempt metadata now persists the minimum evidence needed for retry safety:

- whether commit evidence is available
- data-committed task count
- successfully committed record count
- unknown-state record count
- partial-data-commit flag
- commit scope
- retry advice

No row data or Connector credentials are persisted.

`FileJobRepository` now writes checkpoint format v2 while still reading both v1 and v2. Old v1 checkpoints have no commit evidence and therefore evaluate to `EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE` instead of being guessed safe.

### REST response

`JobResponse` additively exposes a `retry` view with:

```text
eligible
code
message
nextAttemptNumber
```

Existing fields and routes remain unchanged.

## Documentation cleanup

The entire old `docs/` tree is removed, including the seven ADRs and the previous long topic documents.

The repository root now keeps only the small documents needed for day-to-day development:

```text
README.md
ARCHITECTURE.md
DOMAIN.md
DEPENDENCIES.md
REQUIREMENTS.md
CODE_STYLE.md
REVIEW.md
```

The documents are intentionally short and current-state oriented:

- `README.md`: what Link-Up is, modules, quick start, Worker APIs
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`: data plane/control plane and dependency boundaries
- `DOMAIN.md`: Job, Attempt, lifecycle, Retry and checkpoint semantics
- `DEPENDENCIES.md`: Maven/module dependency rules
- `REQUIREMENTS.md`: supported scope and explicit non-goals
- `CODE_STYLE.md`: roles, package naming, Java/logging/test conventions
- `REVIEW.md`: architecture/safety/compatibility review checklist

There is no ADR history stream in the new documentation set. The source of truth is the current architecture and tests.

## Compatibility

This PR preserves:

- stable `jobId` semantics
- existing submit/query/cancel routes
- current lifecycle names
- idempotency behavior
- restart recovery to `LOST`
- Framework `JobGraph` / `ExecutionGraph`
- Connector execution algorithms
- checkpoint v1 readability
- old `JobResourceServlet(JobRestService)` constructor
- existing `JobApplication` implementations via conservative default retry methods

## Non-goals

Phase 8 does not add:

- automatic retry loops
- retry of `LOST` or `CANCELED`
- force-retry bypasses
- split-offset resume
- transaction recovery
- distributed failover
- full runtime-metrics persistence

## Tests

Added/extended coverage for:

- safe FAILED Attempt -> same Job -> Attempt #2
- committed-data retry rejection
- LOST retry rejection
- unknown commit-state rejection
- missing evidence rejection
- dedicated retry lifecycle transition
- durable retry evidence after FileJobRepository reopen

## Validation

- branch is based directly on the Phase 7 merge commit on current `main`
- `main...refactor/phase8-safe-retry-docs`: 2 commits ahead, 0 behind
- root repository no longer contains a `docs/` directory
- all old ADR/topic documents are removed
- no newly-added reference to the old `runtime.JobNotFoundException`
- retry checkpoint format writes v2 and accepts v1/v2
- no JobSpec, Connector options, password or token is added to durable retry evidence
- GitHub currently reports no status checks and no Actions workflow runs for the branch head

A full Maven build was not available from the current execution environment, so this PR intentionally does **not** claim `mvn clean verify` has passed.

Recommended before marking ready:

```bash
mvn --batch-mode clean verify
```

author: deepak-jha-kgp
body:
## What changes

A machine value inside chat speech — `FirstLaw_of_Motion.mp4`, a path, a
command — stops reading as the loudest thing in the message.

Two things were wrong with the old treatment. The span was DM Mono set at the
sentence's own 14px (`text-sm`); mono's wider advance and taller x-height mean
that at equal px it reads a size *up* from the words around it. And its plate
was a fixed token: `--surface-2` is a warm off-white (`#f7f5ef`) sitting on the
bubble's neutral grey (`#efefef`), so it landed as a lighter,
differently-tinted rectangle punched into the fill. In dark that inverted into
`#212120` on `#262626` — a smudge — and the user's brand bubble needed a third
override (white at 15%) to show a plate at all.

Now the span sits a step down the type scale (`--text-xs`) and its plate is
**mixed out of the surrounding ink** (`currentColor` at 8%) rather than naming a
surface token. That second half is the real fix: one rule now lands correctly on
the assistant's grey, the user's brand fill and the doc card, with no
per-context branch and no dark-mode variant. Two smaller ones ride along — a
long path wraps instead of pushing the bubble wide, and a span inside a fence
drops the plate the block already draws.

The face stays mono: `design.md` reserves DM Mono for "a path, a code value, or
a machine," and a filename is one. The chip was never the problem; its sizing
and its plate were.

## Why

Reported from the product: inline code in chat "looks weird." It did, and the
two causes above are why.

Along the way this collapses real drift. The two markdown maps that render
assistant text had grown two *different* hardcoded inline-code styles —
`text-sm` for bubbles in `assistant-experience-helpers.tsx`, `text-xs` for the
doc card in `assistant-turn.tsx` — so the same filename changed size depending
on whether the answer was short enough to be a bubble. Both now point at one
class, `.lchat-code`, and the surviving size is the doc card's.

## How to verify

Visual: open a conversation and send a message containing a filename, a long
path, and a fenced block. The filename should sit level with the sentence, its
plate a gentle tint of the bubble rather than a lighter rectangle; the fenced
block should not draw a plate inside a plate. Check light and dark, and both an
assistant bubble and your own (brand-fill) bubble — they are now the same rule.

```bash
cd lemma-frontend && npm run check   # design audit, lint, typecheck, edu anchors
cd lemma-frontend && npm test        # 97 files, 1051 tests passed
```

## Note on the second commit

The first cut of this rule used `font-size: 0.9em` and `padding: 0.1em 0.32em`,
which moved two design-audit counters (`rawFontSizeDeclaration` 9 → 10,
`rawSpacingDeclaration` 1 → 2) and turned CI red. That gate is a ratchet and the
counters are hand-picked values in a feature stylesheet — precisely the drift it
exists to catch, and precisely what `assistant-chat.css`'s own header promises
the sheet never does. Fixed by putting the values on the scales, not by moving
the baseline, which is untouched.

Relative sizing was the wrong instrument regardless: it reads as a general
solution but buys nothing here, because every voice in the transcript is already
`--text-sm`, so `0.9em` and `--text-xs` land within half a pixel of each other.

## Checklist

- [x] Lint, typecheck, and architecture gates pass locally — `npm run check` is
      green apart from one *local-only* eslint error in `lib/auth/logout.ts`
      (untouched here): my `node_modules` carries
      `@next/eslint-plugin-next@16.2.9` while `package-lock.json` pins 16.3.2,
      which is the version that defines the rule the file disables. CI runs
      `npm ci`, so the comment resolves there.

Tests: no behavioral change to cover — this is presentation, and the assertion
that would catch a regression is a class name, which breaks on every restyle
without catching a design mistake. The verification is visual, described above.

## Compatibility and rollback notes

Frontend CSS and two className strings. Nothing generated, no API surface, no
migration. Revert the commits.

author: kacigaya
body:
Audit-driven pass over the whole app.

## Correctness
- One administrator prompt per DNS change instead of one per failed interface.
- Launch-at-login toggle re-reads the real `SMAppService` status and reverts if registration fails.

## Performance / concurrency
- Menu no longer runs `networksetup` synchronously on the main thread when it opens. State is read into a `DnsSnapshot` off the main actor; the menu renders from the cached snapshot and rebuilds in place when the read finishes.
- UI types (`AppDelegate`, `StatusBarController`, `MenuBuilder`, `ProfileStore`) are `@MainActor`; IP validation moved to a nonisolated `IPAddress` helper so snapshot loading can use it off-thread.

## UI / accessibility
- Profile list uses `List` selection (keyboard navigable) instead of `onTapGesture`.
- Delete asks for confirmation; empty state added.
- Toolbar buttons have real titles with `.labelStyle(.iconOnly)`; active rows show a checkmark, not color alone.
- Editor sheet driven by `.sheet(item:)`; validation lives in one place and is shared with the persistence sanitizer.

## Tests
- Split per type; added coverage for IP parsing, profile validation, snapshot state derivation, and `ProfileStore` persistence against an isolated `UserDefaults` suite.

No new dependencies. Deployment target unchanged (macOS 13).

author: mylukin
body:
## What changed

- retry sibling OAuth accounts only after the exact repeated `400 Invalid previous_response_id` response, before client-visible output
- keep the search bounded to eligible accounts for the same provider and model
- remember the account that owns the response ID and repair the durable Responses registry mapping
- retain fail-closed behavior for every other stateful continuation error

## Root cause

The provider already retried this exact error once on the same Codex WebSocket and account. If it repeated, the OAuth pool treated every `previous_response_id` as strictly pinned and refused to test siblings, so a missing or stale account mapping became terminal even when another connected account owned the response.

## Impact

A continuation can now recover its original subscription account instead of returning an immediate terminal error. It never crosses provider or protocol boundaries, never retries after visible output, and never loops beyond the available account count.

author: alysonoliveira-qa
body:
## O achado

`activatePlan` tem três saídas: devolver erro, redirecionar para o portal de cobrança, ou
redirecionar para o Checkout. **Nunca retorna sucesso** — e como `redirect()` lança, nada
depois dele roda. Ativação de plano se conclui no Stripe, nunca dentro do app.

Mesmo assim `PlanActionState` declarava `'success'`, e três ramos da UI dependiam dele:

| Onde | O que fazia | Realidade |
|---|---|---|
| `useEffect` | disparava `subscription-updated` + `router.refresh()` | nunca rodou — e nada escutava esse evento |
| `activePlan` | usaria `state.plan` | sempre caía no `currentPlan` |
| caixa de mensagem | estilo verde + `data-cy="plan-success-message"` | nunca renderizou |

**O comportamento estava certo o tempo todo.** SaaS pago tem que mandar o cliente para o
Stripe. A mentira estava nas camadas em volta.

## O spec de Cypress era o mais enganoso

Ele esperava `plan-success-message` com o texto `"Plano X ativado com sucesso."` — frase
que **não existe em lugar nenhum do app** e sobrevivia só dentro do teste.

E tinha outros dois defeitos que ninguém tinha notado, porque ele nunca chegava tão longe:

- `cy.url().should("include", "/dashboard/planos")` depois de um redirect que leva para
  `/subscription`;
- esperava `[data-cy="plans-page"]`, que só existe na página de destino.

Reescrito para assertar o que dá para assertar de fora: os três cards, o redirect da rota
legada, e exatamente um badge de plano atual. A troca de plano fica **declarada como gap** —
cobri-la exige `cy.origin` para atravessar para `checkout.stripe.com`, ambiente isolado e
conta de teste do Stripe.

## A matriz de cobertura

Dava esse fluxo como **"Coberto"** apoiada num spec que nunca podia passar. Agora são duas
linhas: leitura coberta, ativação não coberta — com o histórico do porquê.

## Verificação

- `pnpm --filter web type-check` — limpo
- `pnpm --filter web test` — 205 testes passando
- O spec de Cypress **não foi executado**: precisa de `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`PASSWORD` e de
  ambiente próprio. Escrevi contra o comportamento real do código, mas não rodei.

author: mentor24-maker
body:
https://app.clickup.com/t/86bbk2fkp

## Why building faster was making things slower

A branch has to be completely current with `main` before it can merge. That rule is right — it guarantees the tests that passed ran against exactly what goes live, and here "live" means client sites.

**Its cost is quadratic in the number of open PRs.** Every merge invalidates every *other* open branch. With 24 open, one merge dated 23 branches, each needing its own catch-up and its own CI run — and the relay spent most of its work refreshing branches that were stale again before it could use them.

Double the open PRs and you quadruple the churn. Which is why the intuitive fix — more build loops, more machines — makes throughput **worse**.

Throughput is `min(build, review, merge)`. Merge is the slowest, so work queued beyond the merge rate does not ship sooner. It rots, and rotting costs real work.

## What this adds

`npm run clickup -- wip-check`, consulted before claiming. Exit codes mirror `node:owns`: **0** room to claim, **3** a normal decline, **1** could not tell.

A capped pass claims nothing, exits successfully, says it once, and **writes nothing to ClickUp**. That last part is asserted by a test that scans the command's own source for any write call — a stray status or Loop note would mark tickets as being worked when nothing is.

## One deliberate difference from `node:owns`, worth reviewing

**An uncountable pass fails open.**

`node:owns` protects a check-then-act claim: guessing wrong means two machines building the same ticket, which is a correctness problem, so it must refuse. This is a *throughput optimisation* — guessing wrong costs some churn, while refusing on a transient `gh` hiccup would stop all work outright.

So it proceeds, and says loudly that the pass was unbounded by the cap. The proceeding is the safe half; the saying-so is the half that must never go silent.

## The tests that matter are the ones proving it still works

The risk in a feature like this is not that it caps too little. It is that it becomes **a quiet way for the loop to stop working** — so most of the tests defend the claim path: below the cap, empty repo, malformed env override ignored rather than obeyed, and the boundary case of exactly-at-the-cap.

**Writing them caught a real bug in my own counting.** `pr?.state || 'OPEN'` turned every `null` in the list into an open PR, so a malformed response would have capped the loop on garbage. Non-objects are filtered out first now.

It is also wired into `SKILL.md`, with a test that fails if that instruction is ever removed — a check nothing calls is a check that does not run, which is the lesson `buildStart` had to learn twice.

## Break-tested four ways

| Break | Caught by |
|---|---|
| the cap never declines | 3 assertions incl. the boundary |
| merged and closed PRs counted too | `only OPEN pull requests count` |
| a malformed env override obeyed | `a malformed override is IGNORED` |
| the skill stops calling it | `the build skill actually consults it` |

## Verified live, not only in tests

```
21 PRs open, cap 5           -> exit 3, declines
CLAUDE_LOOP_WIP_CAP=999      -> exit 0, claims
```

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | pass |
| `npm run test:builder` | 926 pass, 0 fail (+13) |
| `node scripts/check_conventions.cjs` | pass |

**Nothing to look at** — this changes what the build loop does before it starts work.

## Note on what happens when this lands

With 21 PRs open and a cap of 5, **the build loop will decline to claim** until the backlog drains. That is the intended behaviour and not a fault — but it is worth expecting rather than being surprised by.

author: mdz
body:
## Summary

Two distinct bugs in the content-preparation pipeline (`kbox/queue.py`) both caused a queue item's video to be redundantly re-downloaded multiple times in a row, ~2s apart (matching the `ContentMonitor` poll interval), instead of once. Both confirmed via live e2e repro.

- **Stale `created_at` triggers a false "stuck" detection after a song replace.** `_check_stuck_content` compared against the item's *original* `created_at`, which a replace doesn't reset. A long-queued item whose replacement content just started downloading looked instantly "stuck" past the 10-minute timeout, got reset to `pending`, and the poll loop immediately re-picked it up.
- **`content_status` wasn't marked `PREPARING` synchronously, allowing pile-up on slow/queued downloads.** `_start_content_preparation` only flipped the item to `PREPARING` asynchronously, from inside the background download thread's callback. If that thread was slow to start (semaphore contention, or a slow/rate-limited provider), the item stayed `pending` across multiple poll cycles, each spawning another competing download thread for the same video.

## Fix

Both are fixed by tracking each item's current prep-attempt start time in memory (`_prep_started_at`), set synchronously in `_start_content_preparation` — before handing off to `video_library.request()` — rather than from the async callback. `_check_stuck_content` now compares against that per-attempt timestamp instead of `created_at` (falling back to `created_at` only for items that reach `PREPARING` without going through `_start_content_preparation`).

Landed as one commit since the two fixes share the same mechanism and neither is independently correct without the other.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest` — 665 passed, including two new regression tests: a stuck-check right after `replace_song` on an old item doesn't false-positive, and rapid consecutive `_process_pending_content()` calls only trigger a single `video_library.request()` for an in-flight item.
- [x] `uv run ruff check .`
- [x] `uv run mypy kbox/`
- [ ] e2e smoke test per CLAUDE.md (replace a song on an old queue item; add a song and watch the log for repeated "Starting content preparation") — not yet run, pytest uses mocks/fakesinks for this pipeline code.

author: ryanduguid
body:
Closes #1104. Part of the bs4 → lxml migration program (#931).

## What changed

The three HTML helpers behind `Note` text rendering no longer use BeautifulSoup:

- **`_render_statement_to_markdown`** parses with `create_lxml_parser(remove_comments=False)` (recover=True, blank text preserved, per the [porting guide](https://github.com/dgunning/edgartools/issues/931#issuecomment-5387920956)). Table replacement now splices each element's tail onto its previous sibling before removal - lxml drops tails on `remove()` (guide gotcha 2). Serialization via `lxml.html.tostring(..., encoding='unicode')`.
- **`_html_table_to_plain_text`** takes an lxml element: `findall('.//tr')`, cell walk via `iter()`, cell text via `itertext()` matching `get_text(strip=True)`.
- **`_extract_narrative_markdown`**: `decompose()` replaced with tail-preserving removal; plain-text path uses itertext with separator semantics.

No bs4 imports remain in `edgar/xbrl/notes.py`.

## Characterisation first

Commit f336068 pins current behaviour *before* the swap: 9 tests over real Apple 10-K note fragments extracted from the repo's recorded cassette (filing_text_baseline_0000320193-23-000106):

- a real clean table through the pipe-table splice path (pinned to the exact `process_content` output shape)
- a real colspan-heavy table (a signature block) through the aligned-plain-text fallback
- adjacent-span narrative boundary spacing, pinned byte-exactly **including the pre-existing `iPhone` → `i Phone` quirk** of the lowercase-to-uppercase heuristic - characterised as-is; the port reproduces it exactly rather than fixing it silently
- empty-table and no-table input contracts

All 9 pass unchanged after the port, plus the existing 97 notes tests (`test_notes.py`, `test_notes_extraction.py`, `test_xbrl_notes_access.py`).

## Measured before/after

Fixture workload = narrative extraction twice + one full per-table render (clean pipe path + colspan fallback), best of repeated runs, Python 3.12:

| | bs4 | lxml.html | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| full workload | 18.8 ms | 14.8 ms | **1.27x** |

Lower than the headers.py ratio because the shared `process_content` markdown pipeline dominates this workload and is untouched by the parser swap; the parser-side gain itself is in line with the guide's ~2-3x on the parse step.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/test_notes_html_characterization.py tests/test_notes.py tests/test_notes_extraction.py tests/test_xbrl_notes_access.py`: 106 passed
- `ruff check edgar/xbrl/notes.py`: 7 findings, all pre-existing at HEAD (HEAD has 8) and none on touched lines
