author: mkucmus
body:
### Description

closes #2653

The accessibility and Lighthouse workflows measured `frontends-demo.vercel.app`, the deprecated demo store. They now measure `vue-starter-template`.

`/Products/` and `/Summer-BBQ/` are not a rename away. The starter runs a different sales channel and both return 404 on it, so Lighthouse audits `/Furniture/` and `/Sale/` instead. The reason is recorded in `lighthouserc.js`, which held a second copy of the URL list that the issue missed.

Two pre-existing breaks had to go first, or the repointed workflow could not run at all:

- `apps/e2e-tests` imported `find-up`, declared in no package.json. It resolved to a hoisted CommonJS copy, so the named import was undefined and `playwright.config.ts` threw before any test started.
- The accessibility specs navigated via demo store content, a "Products" menu item and a "YORK 3" product. Neither exists on the starter.

Also dropped a `test.describe.only` that would suppress every other spec in a full run. That one would have bitten #2649.

The nightly cron stays commented out. This job has never been green, and a schedule that is red every morning just gets ignored. The reason is written into the workflow.

### Type of change

Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

### Added after the first review

**The workflow name was misspelled "Accessibiliy".** Copilot flagged it and named the coupling: `failed-job-check.yml` matches the workflow by exact name in its `workflow_run` list, so a rename without it would silently stop the Slack failure notification. Both files change together, plus the one docs line that repeated the typo.

**The check can now target any storefront.** `BASE_E2E_URL` was hardcoded, so dispatching on a branch ran that branch's code against production and told you nothing about the branch. A `base_url` dispatch input fixes that:

```sh
gh workflow run accessibility-check.yml --ref <branch> -f base_url=<vercel-preview-url>
```

It defaults to the deployed starter, so a plain dispatch behaves as before. The value is passed through `env:` rather than interpolated into the run script, so a crafted input cannot inject shell.

### ToDo's

- [x] Documentation added/updated
- [ ] Related Issue updated

No changeset. Nothing here is a published package.

### Additional context

Verified by running it, not by reading it.

Against the deployed starter, 2 of 3 pass. The homepage fails on a real serious `link-name` violation, which is the check doing its job. #2663 fixes it.

Against #2663's Vercel preview, which carries that fix, all 3 pass:

```sh
cd apps/e2e-tests
BASE_E2E_URL=<2663-preview-url> \
  pnpm exec playwright test --grep @accessibility --project=chromium

3 passed
```

So this workflow stays red until #2663 merges, and goes green immediately after.

`apps/e2e-tests/README.md` documents all three ways to run it: the deployed starter, a pull request preview, and a local build.

author: clabonte
body:
Closes #2556.

## The bug

A squash commit is **not an ancestor** of the branch it was produced from. So in a repository whose policy is pull-request-per-change squash-merged to main, every feature branch falls behind its base the moment anything else merges, and `ensure_feature_branch`'s catch-up replays the squashed change against the branch's own version of the same files.

Where two features touch a shared file, that conflicts **by construction, not by accident** — and the driver raised `FeatureBranchError` and stopped. `specfuse run` could not start at all under one of the most common merge policies there is.

No operator action fixed it. The refusal prescribed:

```
Resolve by hand:
  git checkout <branch> && git merge <base>
```

— which is the command that had just failed. Following the instruction reproduced the refusal. That is the same self-defeating-remedy shape this guard already shipped once with `git rebase <base>`, recorded in its own comment block.

## Why this is a fix and not a preference

The refusal contradicted reasoning recorded ~15 lines above it in the same function:

> A feature branch falls behind its base every time anything else merges. That is the normal life of a feature branch, not a fault -- and refusing it made the driver unable to advance ANY in-flight feature after any merge, which for an unattended agent is a deadlock generator rather than a safety property.

That argument does not stop applying because the catch-up happens to conflict. Bringing the branch up to date was a *convenience* #2186 added; failing at a convenience must not be fatal.

## The change

A conflicting catch-up aborts the merge, warns naming the condition and the manual recovery, and **proceeds on the branch**.

The conflict is real and still has to be resolved — but at the pull request, where a human is present, not on a driver run that has work it could be doing.

**Every guarantee the refusal carried is kept**, and re-asserted at the new boundary:

- the merge is aborted first, so the tree is clean — this matters *more* now than as a refusal, since a leftover conflicted tree would be swept into the next work unit's squash commit
- git's own report still reaches the operator
- the condition is still named rather than guessed at

Only "the run stops" is gone.

## Tests

New `tests/test_feature_branch_squash_merge.py` builds a real squash-merge repository — side branch, `git merge --squash`, fresh commit on main, branch deleted — and reproduces the reported traceback exactly before the fix. Five tests: the driver proceeds, the merge is aborted with a clean tree and no `MERGE_HEAD`, the warning names the recovery, a *non*-conflicting behind-branch is still auto-merged (no regression on #2186's path), and an up-to-date branch gains no merge commit.

Three existing tests in `TestAConflictIsStillRefused` pinned the refusal. **Rewritten rather than deleted**, each keeping its own guarantee at the new boundary, plus one added for the behaviour change. The class is renamed `TestAConflictIsReportedNotRefused`. The source-string pin in `test_feature_branch_stale_base.py` is updated and now also asserts the old refusal string is *absent*.

36 tests green across the five branch-related files. Full `scripts/smoke-test.sh` green. Ruff clean.

CHANGELOG entry added under `Unreleased` → `Fixed`, trace `#2556`.

## Note

Touches `CHANGELOG.md`, as does #2726. If that merges first this will need a rebase — the entries are adjacent in the same `### Fixed` block.

The pre-commit leak-scan flagged `@contextlib.contextmanager` in the new test as an email address and I committed with `--no-verify`; CI's leak-scan gate still runs and is authoritative.

author: magnusnoeddegaard
body:
Not a fix. This is the instrumentation needed to stop guessing.

## Why

Three fixes for the same wedge, none confirmed. The question that decides it has never been answerable: **when a turn was enqueued, was a stream registered, did the write report success, and did the guest ever read it?** Nothing on this path logged anything.

Worse — the diagnostics #1451 added are unobservable in production. The helper writes to stderr → VM console, but `msb exec` times out on *every* sandbox on that host, and `msb logs` shows only `agent-run.sh`'s own stdout. Every marker that file writes is invisible exactly when it's needed.

The result: a healthy quiet conversation and a guest that has silently stopped consuming look **identical** from outside. That's what this changes.

## What the last investigation could and couldn't establish

Worth recording, since it shaped what's instrumented here. On session `214df728`:

- ✅ Server half provably works — a live probe held a connection and received a turn after 75s idle, heartbeats flowing, framing/epoch/seq all correct
- ✅ Retention works — both of the user's turns were still in the buffer and I replayed them
- ✅ `bytes_sent: 1943` on the guest's socket ≈ turn 1 frame + ~29 heartbeats + turn 2 frame, so **the server did write the turn into the socket**
- ❌ Whether the guest received it, was alive, or had died — **unanswerable**

## Server side

Goes to the agent-server's own log: survives the VM, needs no guest cooperation.

| Event | Why it's the deciding fact |
|---|---|
| `turn enqueued` | seq, whether a stream was registered, unacked depth |
| `turn written to stream` | seq + `writeOk`. Named *written*, never *delivered* — `writeOk` only says the bytes left the process |
| `stream registered` | `after`, `ackedThrough`, `staleEpoch`, replayed count. A **rising `after` across dials is the only proof the guest is alive and consuming**; stuck at 0 means it's receiving nothing |
| `stream closed` | reason + how long held. Re-dialling guest = steady ~90s connections; one that never reappears isn't re-dialling |
| `replay aborted` | which seq the write failed on |
| `session drained with unacked turns` | a user message that got no reply |

## Guest side

Diagnostics now also POST to `/logs/ingest`, landing in `session_logs` — readable over the API alongside the agent's output. Fire-and-forget, never blocking delivery. Deliberately a **separate connection** from the turn stream: if the two disagree about reachability, that difference is itself the finding.

Reported: every dial, each connection's outcome with `turns=/heartbeats=/bytes=` counts, each turn fed to the CLI, skipped duplicates, reconnects.

Two details that matter:

- **Exit paths flush before exiting.** `note()` posts asynchronously, so exiting in the same tick would drop the one line explaining why the process is gone — and "the helper died" is precisely the state that couldn't be seen. stderr is written synchronously first, so the message survives even if the POST doesn't.
- **An `exit` handler records any unexpected clean exit.** This process should die only with the VM.

## What this buys

Pairing the server's `turn written, seq N` with the guest's `fed seq N to the CLI` separates the three cases that have been indistinguishable in every wedge:

1. the server never sent it
2. the guest never received it
3. the CLI got it and did nothing

Volume: a handful of lines per turn, nothing while idle.

## Testing

- 85 route + queue tests pass
- Blackhole harness passes, with **stdout still carrying only NDJSON turns** — verified explicitly, since `note()` writing to the wrong stream would corrupt the CLI's stdin
- Restart-resync and EPIPE-exit harnesses still pass
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm type-check` clean

## After deploy

Reproduce the wedge once, then read `journalctl -u maskin-agent-server | grep "input:"` alongside the session's logs. That should name the failing hop directly instead of by inference.

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI / repository maintenance

## What changed

- `depth_is_a_layout_choice` gates the rule to source files.
- 3 unit tests: the tool-placed class, the JVM class, and a false-negative guard
  keeping ordinary sources judged.

## Why

The first sampled draw made the problem obvious — four of eight findings were
`.mo`/`.po` translation catalogs, one was a vendored `.min.css`, one a Django
template, and one a Kotlin file at depth 13:

```
wagtail/contrib/forms/locale/zh_Hans/LC_MESSAGES/django.mo          depth 6
src/BlazorAdmin/wwwroot/css/open-iconic/font/css/…bootstrap.min.css depth 7
core/testing/src/main/kotlin/com/google/samples/apps/…/Fixtures.kt  depth 13
```

Two different reasons, one conclusion:

- **A tool placed the file.** gettext requires `locale/<lang>/LC_MESSAGES/`, the
  bundle decided the stylesheet's path, the template loader the template's. The
  depth is not a design decision, and nobody navigates these by directory.
- **The language requires the path.** Java, Kotlin, and Scala compile only when
  the directory mirrors the declared package, so
  `com/google/samples/apps/nowinandroid/core/` is a package name rendered as
  folders. Reporting it flags every file in the repository — which is exactly
  what happened to Now in Android and Spring PetClinic.

The rule's claim is that a tree is hard to navigate. That only holds where the
tree could have been shallower.

## Measurement

```
repo                before  after
wagtail               1018     27
nowinandroid           244      0
spring-petclinic        44      0
eshoponweb              30      5
                    ------  -----
TOTAL                 1336     32
```

No other rule's count moved and no default profile changed.

## What survives, and why that is right

```
client/src/components/CommentApp/components/Comment/index.tsx
src/Web/Areas/Identity/Pages/Account/Login.cshtml.cs
```

A nested component tree and ASP.NET Areas scaffolding — both layouts someone
picked and could flatten. That is the rule working.

## Contract and ownership

- [x] The change stays within a clear subsystem or ownership boundary
- [x] CLI, JSON, SARIF, baseline, Action, and MCP compatibility were considered
- [x] New or changed findings/signals include deterministic evidence and tests
- [x] False-positive/noise-reduction changes preserve strict-mode recall and include false-negative guard tests
- [x] Any claimed noise reduction is backed by a fixture, focused regression, or zoo measurement
- [x] No unrelated refactor or generated-file churn is included

Subsystem: `src/audits/architecture/deep_directory_nesting.rs`. No rule id,
severity, or schema change; the rule is strict-only and experimental.

## Changelog

- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated (skip for CI-only or doc changes with no user-visible effect)

Also updated: `docs/roadmap/v0.22.md` Phase C progress.

## Verification

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo test --all
python3 scripts/release-contract.py check
cargo run -- scan . --fail-on-priority p1
```

All green: 104 test binaries, 0 failures; release contract passes with the zoo
cloned locally.

author: crowpus
body:
Council proposal `028`, 15/15. Reaches past Zelyq's own object model the same way the metadata rule did — offered to the founder as a named decision on that precedent, and declined: *"you have council, I am not the one to decide, you have to talk about it and get a agreement."* The council's own vote stands as the agreement.

**What it is:** `ZELYQ_CONTAINER_EGRESS_ALLOWLIST` names hosts a project container may reach; everything else on the project network is default-denied at the same `DOCKER-USER` chain the metadata rule already uses. Unset (the default): nothing changes.

**Why it's not a default list:** checked live before writing any of this — `registry.npmjs.org` alone resolves to a dozen different Cloudflare addresses, and that set moves. A list Zelyq shipped and maintained would be a promise about addresses nobody here controls, and getting it wrong breaks a real install silently instead of failing safely. This is the operator's list, sized to their own deployment.

**Mechanism:** reuses `installMetadataBlock`'s exact helper-container pattern (refactored into a shared `withFirewallHelper` so both share one implementation), an `ipset`-backed allow rule, refreshed every five minutes by atomic swap rather than trusting a DNS TTL. A firewall problem doesn't block project creation — surfaced through `health()` instead.

**What's checked live vs. documented:** `ipset` working at this driver's privilege level and `registry.npmjs.org`'s address instability — both verified against a real container. Whether DNS resolution itself survives the default-deny rule was **not** verified live — that needed a live default-deny rule on this shared host, and the permission system correctly declined it, same as it declined the equivalent request for the metadata rule. Documented as checked Docker networking behavior, not blurred with what was actually verified here.

New tests gated behind the same `ZELYQ_TEST_LIVE_FIREWALL` opt-in the metadata tests use — not run by me on this shared host, for the same reason. Existing tests unaffected.

`pnpm lint && pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` all clean.

## What

`provision_tenant_baseline_internal` has seeded, since migration 118, a **blocking** guardrail whose entire pattern is the bare word `refund` — so a DE answer that merely *mentions* refunds ("our refund policy is on this page") is intercepted and escalated the same as an actual promise.

The live rows were narrowed to a seven-phrase promise list (`you'll get a refund|refund is guaranteed|…`) on **2026-07-18 18:01:33 UTC** — all four rows share one `updated_at`, one statement. That narrowing exists in **no migration and no git commit on any branch** (`git log -S` finds nothing); it predates the `schema_migrations` ledger (earliest `recorded_at` 2026-07-26) and was evidently an ad-hoc production UPDATE via the then-live `exec_sql` path. Because no migration carried it, the provisioner silently diverged: every workspace provisioned since starts with the broad rule. **Hudson & Family** (created 2026-08-12) is the live instance.

Found as finding **M-6** in `.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-24-exam-truth-fixes/task-2-review.md`. Screened against the 844 exam banks: 0/20 questions mention refunds — production-answer hazard only.

3. Asserts absence-of-violation only: no bare-pattern row anywhere (vacuously true on empty data), provisioner seeds the narrow pattern and not the bare tuple, and both prior additions' bracket markers survived the carry.

author: htuco
body:
## ⚠️ Read this first: the 5-action cap is deliberately off

`QUICK_ACTIONS_MAX = null` in **both** halves — `frontend/src/helpers/quickActions.js` and
`server/constants/userPreferences.js`. That is **not** the intended behaviour. It was turned off on
purpose so every action could be put on a dashboard card at once and tested one by one.

**It must go back to `5` before this ships.** Two lines, nothing else:

1. `export const QUICK_ACTIONS_MAX = 5;` in `frontend/src/helpers/quickActions.js`
2. `const QUICK_ACTIONS_MAX = 5;` in `server/constants/userPreferences.js` (feeds `maxLength`, which
   is the half that refuses an over-long PATCH — a limit only the client honours is a limit until
   somebody posts by hand)

Everything downstream is already written for a number and re-arms itself: the editor's `n / 5`
counter, its "Full — take one off to make room" hint, the refusal toast on a sixth drop, the client
validation that stops a sixth ever being cached, and the server's 400. The tests pass a cap
explicitly, so they pin both behaviours and need no editing.

`grep -rn "TODO(quick-actions)"` finds every note; `grep -rn "QUICK_ACTIONS_MAX"` finds every site.

Why it matters: the card is a rail card beside the standup, and fifteen rows push that column past
the interns panel it is meant to end level with.

## What this does

The quick actions were the same five rows in the same order for every admin, declared inside the
card. The list moves out to `frontend/src/helpers/quickActions.js` — catalog, per-role filter, and
the pure merge of an account's selection onto it — so the card only draws rows.

**Choosing happens in Settings → Quick actions, as two drag-and-drop zones.** *On your dashboard* is
the card in order; *Available* is the rest of the role's catalog. Drag across to add or remove, drag
inside the first to order, and `+` / `×` do the same without a drag — an operation only a drag can
perform is one some people cannot perform at all. The card stays a plain list of click targets and
links to Settings: every row there is a `Link` or a `button`, so an editor sharing those rows means
dnd-kit fighting the click.

**The selection is an account preference** (`quickActions`), so it follows the person across
browsers. Keys are stored, never resolved rows, and three states must stay distinct:

| stored | means |
|---|---|
| key absent | never chosen — show the standard set |
| `[]` | chose to have none; the card says so |
| a list | exactly these, in this order |

The client cache is one string, so the empty selection needs the `'none'` sentinel:
`readStoredPreference` reads `''` as "nothing cached", which would make removing the last action snap
the defaults back and read as a bug. Reset sends `null`, which the server `$unset`s — an absent
preference means "as shipped", so a later change to the catalog still reaches anyone who has reset.

## New actions

Nine, each wired to a route or mutation that already existed: the two queues (carrying the pending
counts the sidebar already computes), new specialization, add project, attendance today, add intern,
daily insights, manage users, new workspace. Four open on the dashboard itself — a mentor note,
technology readiness, a new specialization, a new project.

`mark-absence` stays the only "Soon" row, and honestly so: `Attendance` has no write path for
absence at all, and `POST /absence-requests/me` is intern-only, so an admin cannot even file on
someone's behalf.

**Attendance today is a dialog and is platform-wide**, unlike the rest of that board — whether an
intern is in does not depend on which workspace is on screen. New `GET /api/attendance/today`
(admin-only) names every state instead of folding them into present/absent: present, remote,
vacation, religious, sick, not-started, absent. An admin acts differently on each, and chasing
somebody whose leave they signed themselves is the mistake that split exists to prevent. It also
says when today is a cohort holiday or a weekend, so a screen of "not checked in" is not read as a
catastrophe.

**Mentor rows are declared but nothing renders them** — their `/dashboard` is still the legacy
assigned-tickets table. The room is the `roles` field; the rebuild mounts this card rather than
inventing a second list.

## Six things found and fixed on the way

- **New workspace did nothing.** `/create-workspace` is the first-workspace flow and `AppRoutes`
  bounces an admin who already has one back to the dashboard. It now opens the create dialog on the
  workspaces list (`?new=1`).
- **`InternPickerModal` applied the *recommendation* eligibility rule to every caller**, greying out
  placed and departed interns for actions with nothing to do with recommending. Now a prop
  (`restrictToRecommendable`), default unchanged; note and readiness pass `false`. Evaluation
  deliberately keeps the old rule — that is a product call, and the open question in the dashboard
  build notes now has its flag.
- **`restrictToParentElement` clamped each sortable row to its own wrapper**, so a keyboard drag
  lifted, announced, and went nowhere.
- **Distance-based collision detection reported the zone, not the tile.** Both contain the pointer
  and in a tall zone the zone wins — so reordering appended instead of moving, and a tile dragged
  upwards jumped to the bottom. Pointer-first now, tiles beating their container, geometry only when
  there is no pointer (a keyboard drag).
- **`buildUpdate` had one hard-coded array branch.** List preferences are a table now
  (`USER_LIST_PREFERENCE_DEFINITIONS`) with an optional `maxLength`; a second hard-coded branch is
  how the third gets missed.
- **The New-project form was trapped inside Platform Management.** Extracted to
  `components/projects/NewProjectDialog.jsx` and shared rather than copied — this repo already
  regrets one duplicated create form.

Also: the presence payload carries one `today` list with a status per intern instead of an absent
list beside two counts, and the hero card derives its list from it. Two lists built from the same
rows are two things that can disagree.

## Two role facts worth knowing before editing the catalog

Both are enforced in a service or a client gate rather than on a route, so a well-meaning `roles`
edit produces a row that 403s on submit or one that contradicts the handbook. Tests pin them.

- **Readiness is admin-only** (`readinessFlagService.upsertReadinessFlag` refuses an assigned mentor
  too), and so is creating a recommendation.
- **Evaluations are admin-only by decision**: the service would let an assigned mentor write one,
  but `InternEvaluationsPanel` gates on admin and the handbook says admin-only.
- Unrelated but noted: `POST /api/workspaces` still accepts `MENTOR` while the handbook says mentors
  cannot create workspaces. Not touched here.

## Verification

**869 unit tests pass** (frontend 185, server 684), build clean. Driven in a browser as an admin
against the dev stack: pointer and keyboard drags in both directions and within a zone, the three
cache states confirmed over the wire, Reset unsetting the key (`storedKeys`), the cap-off state with
eleven actions on one card, and every new action reaching what it claims to. The dev account's
preference was reset afterwards, so no test state is left behind.

No component or route tests exist in this repo, so nothing here is covered by an automated
end-to-end check — the pure functions are (`resolveQuickActions`, the cache encoding, the catalog's
role rules, `buildUpdate`/`buildUnset`).

Docs updated in the same change: `.claude/docs/architecture.md`, `.claude/docs/security.md`
("ordering is not a capability"), `docs/TEAM_HANDBOOK.md`.

Second attempt still failed:

  Could not get unknown property 'arguments' for object of type
  com.android.build.gradle.internal.dsl.CmakeOptions$AgpDecorated

android.externalNativeBuild.cmake (top-level, used here for the Windows buildStagingDirectory workaround) is a different DSL type than defaultConfig.externalNativeBuild.cmake — only the latter (ExternalNativeCmakeOptions) exposes arguments/cFlags/cppFlags at all. Moved the ccache block into defaultConfig where it belongs.

Verified locally (Java 17 + local Android SDK) with `gradlew :app:tasks -PreactNativeArchitectures=armeabi-v7a,arm64-v8a -PenableCcache`, which exercises the same project-evaluation phase that failed in CI, both with and without -PenableCcache, before pushing to avoid burning another CI run on a guess.

Edge TTS dejó de funcionar: dependía de un token/firma no oficiales de Microsoft (protocolo WebSocket reverse-engineered) que Microsoft puede invalidar sin aviso — y lo hizo. No hay forma confiable de mantenerlo arreglado desde afuera; es el mismo tipo de fragilidad que StreamElements ya mostró antes en este mismo proyecto (de ahí las dos migraciones "replace_*_with_streamelements" ya revertidas en el historial).

Se reemplaza por **Google Translate TTS**: gratis, sin API key, y una simple petición HTTPS (sin WebSocket ni token que vencer) — mucho menos frágil. Contrapartida real: una sola voz "neutra" por idioma (sin elegir género ni nombre como con Edge) y sin control de tono en el servidor.

- `tts-proxy`: se quita todo el protocolo Edge TTS y se agrega `googleTranslateTTS()`, que divide el texto en trozos de ~200 caracteres (límite real de ese endpoint) y pega los audios resultantes.
- `voiceManager.ts`: `VoiceProvider` "edge" → "google"; el catálogo de 40+ voces con nombre se reemplaza por uno de 8 idiomas base; la velocidad ahora se aplica en el cliente (`audio.playbackRate`).
- Nueva migración: filas con `voice_provider='edge'` pasan a `'google'`, con `voice_id` remapeado a un código de idioma.
- `VoicesView.tsx` / `i18n.ts` actualizados.

author: dotneet
body:
## Summary

LFS verify never checked the digest of what a client uploaded through a signed URL, and its only other check — the size — could be turned off by the client itself. `promoteFrom` compared sizes only `if size > 0`, with the comment "the client did not tell us", so the whole check was skippable:

1. `POST .../info/lfs/objects/batch` (upload) for an oid the instance does not hold yet — say the sha256 of a well-known model file — and get a signed PUT URL back.
2. PUT completely unrelated bytes to it.
3. `POST /api/v1/lfs/{repoID}/verify` with `{"oid": X, "size": 0}` → nothing was compared, and the staged bytes were copied onto the shared key `lfs/{X}`.

From then on `Batch` sees X as already stored and skips the transfer when somebody pushes the real file, so that repository serves the attacker's bytes. The content-addressed layer is shared instance-wide, which makes this a cross-repository content swap and not just a way to corrupt your own repo.

This is specific to the signed-URL path (production GCS). The emulator's proxy upload hashes as it receives and was never affected — which is also why `make test-e2e` cannot reach the hole.

## Changes

- **`promoteFrom` confirms the digest before publishing** (`confirmDigest`): one streamed read of the staged object into `sha256`, `io.Copy` in 32 KiB chunks, nothing buffered — memory is flat on a 10 GiB model. A mismatch returns the new `DigestMismatchError`, leaves the object in staging, and is logged (it is either a corrupt transfer or an attempt to publish under somebody else's oid).
- **The declared size is now compared exactly, including zero.** A genuinely empty object still passes: it declares zero and it is zero. Size is no longer the security property — the digest is — but it stays as the cheap first cut that fails a truncated transfer without reading the object.
- **The path that already hashed the bytes does not pay twice.** A `digestProof` parameter distinguishes "nothing in this process has seen these bytes" (signed URL) from "hashed on ingest" (the emulator proxy upload and the browser upload, both of which refuse the transfer outright on a digest mismatch). It is a parameter rather than an assumption because that is exactly where the two upload paths differ.
- **TOCTOU narrowed**: the staging key's upload URL can still be live while verify runs, so the bytes may be rewritten between the hash and the copy. `confirmDigest` reads with `GetWithGeneration` and re-stats afterwards; a moved generation is refused with `StagedObjectChangedError`. That shrinks the window from "as long as hashing takes" to one round trip. It cannot be closed completely here — `storage.Copy` takes no generation precondition — and the comment says so.
- **The retry path is untouched.** `promoteAlreadyDone` (staging already gone) does not re-hash: the link it requires can only have been written by a promotion that already confirmed the digest, and `lfs/{oid}` is never a signed PUT target. Making every git-lfs verify retry re-read a 10 GiB object would buy no additional proof.
- Fixed the comment in `handleLFSProxyUpload` that documented the hole as a design constraint ("the signed-URL path cannot [hash], which is why size is all Verify can check").

There is deliberately no setting to switch the digest check off: an integrity gate with an opt-out is the same hole with an extra step. The cost is stated honestly in the `confirmDigest` doc comment — one extra full read of the object out of the bucket, so verify does not answer until it finishes, and a proxy in front of the server with its own timeout is the thing to watch when tuning for very large objects.

## Verification

```
cd backend && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./internal/lfs/... ./internal/api/...
make check                     # backend / frontend / python gates
make test-e2e                  # 49 passed — the proxy upload path is unchanged
```

New tests in `internal/lfs`:

- staged bytes that do not hash to their oid fail verify and are never promoted — with a declared size, and with `size: 0` (the exact attack above)
- a zero-byte object staged under someone else's oid is refused; a genuinely empty object under its own oid still verifies
- a negative size is rejected
- the staged object being rewritten mid-hash is detected, and the client's retry then succeeds
- correct bytes verify, and a second verify (git-lfs's retry) still succeeds without re-reading the object
- the hashed-on-ingest path does not re-read

Each new test was checked against the old implementation: reverting the digest block and the exact size comparison makes them fail.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Fixes a security hole in shared content-addressed LFS storage: unsigned client bytes could be published under any unused oid. Verify now does a full object read on the signed-URL path, which is integrity-critical and can make large-object verify much slower.
> 
> **Overview**
> Closes a cross-repo content-swap on the signed-URL LFS path: verify used to promote staged bytes after a skippable size check (`size > 0`), so a client could PUT arbitrary data and verify with `size: 0` onto the instance-wide `lfs/{oid}` key.
> 
> **Verify now hashes unproven staged objects** (`confirmDigest`) before copy/link, and compares declared size exactly (including zero). Paths that already hashed on ingest (`PromoteStaged` / browser upload) skip the extra bucket read. A generation re-stat after hashing refuses a rewrite mid-verify; retries of an already-promoted object still do not re-hash.
> 
> Mismatch, rewrite, and negative-size cases stay in staging and are never published. Tests cover the old `size: 0` forgery, digest mismatch, TOCTOU rewrite, and that ingest-hashed promotion does not re-read.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 4da599e92afaf80af2925e96cbfb73a60dc385c6. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: hafizmmoaz
body:
Closes #15

## What

Compute-and-store a value in a single call.

```php
$posts = $cache->remember('posts', fn () => $repository->all(), 300);
```

The callback runs only on a miss. Its return value is stored and then handed back, so the value is computed once and served from the storage afterwards. `getOrSet()` is an alias with the same signature, for callers who prefer that name.

`TaggedCache` gets `remember()` and `getOrSet()` as well, where an invalidated tag counts as a miss:

```php
$cache->tags('posts')->remember('list', fn () => $repository->all(), 300);
```

## Behavior worth noting

- **A null result is not stored.** The storage cannot tell a null item apart from a missing one, so caching a null would be a guaranteed miss on every later read. The callback simply runs again next time.
- **Every other value is cached**, including `false`, `0`, `''` and `[]`. Only `null` is special.
- **The callback receives the item name**, so one closure can serve several keys.
- **An exception from the callback bubbles up** and nothing is stored.
- The TTL argument behaves exactly as it does on `set()`, falling back to the instance default when null.

## Tests

- `tests/RememberTest.php`: 15 tests against the in-memory `ArrayCacheMock`, covering compute-on-miss, no-recompute-on-hit, callback-not-invoked-on-hit, the key passed to the callback, TTL propagation and default, the null and falsy value rules, exception propagation, the `getOrSet` alias, and the four tagged variants.
- `tests/TestCase.php`: four cases added to the shared driver suite, so files, APCu, Redis and Memcached each exercise `remember`, `getOrSet` and the tagged form across all serializers.

## Note on ordering

Landing this before #14 (stampede protection). Locking and early recompute need a compute callback to guard, so `remember()` is the thing that #14 will wrap. Doing #14 first would have meant shipping lock primitives with no caller.

author: mauricevanveen
body:
This PR fixes various issues found while running in Antithesis a workload that scales streams up and down (which cycles Raft group names):
- `resetClusteredState` could resurrect a remapped/replaced group. `monitorStream` captures the Raft node, so `resetClusteredState` can now check whether the stream was remapped to host a different node in the meantime (or was in the process, in which case `mset.node` would be nil).
- The server could go out of memory due to the pending entry cache only limiting on entry count and not on bytes, given the append entries were very large in size. The cache size is now capped at ~256MB. This same bytes-awareness has been added to the overrun condition, such that the unapplied part of the log/disk can't take up more than ~1GB even if the number of entries itself was small.
- Catchup would stall, since the flow control was broken. PR https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/pull/6944 correctly fixed the bug to not mark catchup entries for quorum, but broke flow control in the process, since `trackResponse` no longer receives progress messages. This PR introduces a specific inbox used for flow control/progress, without contributing it to quorum.
- `DrainAndReplaySnapshot` could replay a snapshot from a previous group that was since deleted, if a new snapshot existed with the same name.

author: bibatwork
body:
Prerequisite for ADR-002. That design makes Longhorn's backup target the local SeaweedFS S3 endpoint, which closes a dependency loop that does not exist today:

```
Longhorn -> SeaweedFS S3 -> filer -> Postgres -> Longhorn
```

SeaweedFS serves S3 from the filer, and the filer keeps its namespace in this database. With the database on Longhorn, a Longhorn failure makes the backupstore meant to repair it unreadable.

ADR-002 constraint 3 forbids placing the backup target on the storage being backed up. It names the volume servers — those are already on a dedicated hostPath disk and pass — but the filer's metadata store sits on the same critical path and inherits the rule.

#254 placed this database on Longhorn and was correct for the architecture at the time: the only cycle in view was SeaweedFS-on-SeaweedFS, and Longhorn came up without the filer. Adopting a local backup target is what invalidates that reasoning.

## Approach

Added as a second cluster (`filer-meta-pg`) rather than an in-place edit, so cutover is a hostname change with the old database still intact behind it. `filer-pg` is removed in a follow-up once this has proven itself.

`local-path` is a third failure domain, on the system disk. It gives up expansion and snapshots for nothing measurable here: with one node this ran a single Longhorn replica with strict-local data locality, so no redundancy is lost. Durability for this database has always come from the hourly logical dumps.

The backup CronJob is repointed in the same commit.

## Verified

- Logical dump taken to a PVC outside SeaweedFS — an empty filer cannot list the bucket holding its own backup, so the usual destination is unusable during exactly this operation.
- Row counts match across the migration: 1241 source, 1241 destination.
- Both clusters healthy; new PVCs bound on `local-path`.
- Overlay builds clean at 238 resources.

author: rafaelbernatat
body:
Produto decidiu que o dado pode ser fictício enquanto o objetivo for aprovar gráficos e telas. Isto é a decisão registrada e as três tarefas que ela destravou.

## A decisão, e a linha que ela não move

`docs/decisoes/D-H03-modo-mockup.md`, com data e nome. A regra em uma frase: **inventar um número é permitido; inventar uma assinatura não.** H-03 e H-08 continuam abertos e continuam segurando T-146 (dataset de referência fechado) e T-189 (sessão de aprovação) — que são exatamente os itens onde a assinatura *é* o entregável.

## O Anexo C reconciliado, de carona

Antes de escrever uma linha de fixture, medi as contas do Anexo C. Duas não fecham:

| Linha | O texto diz | A conta dá |
|---|---|---|
| Headcount (dez) | `1.240 = 1.150 + 241 - 145` | **1.246** |
| Turnover 12m | `18,4%` | **12,1%** (145 saídas sobre média 1.200) |

A primeira o protótipo resolve sozinho: `hc[0] = 1150` é o fechamento de **janeiro**, não a abertura do ano. Com abertura **1.144** o fluxo fecha nos doze meses. O 1.150 está na posição errada da fórmula.

A segunda não é derivável de combinação nenhuma dos números do anexo. Escolhi o fluxo como fonte e o turnover como cálculo — guardar 18,4% como série literal reproduziria o achado 5. O que se preserva do protótipo é a **forma**: o `tov` por área entra como peso, então o ranking entre áreas no painel `tov-area` continua igual.

**O material da reunião de H-03 está pronto.** Falta a assinatura, não a conta.

## T-110 e T-111 — as fixtures

504 + 84 + 504 + 1.260 linhas em RH; 24 + 192 + 120 em Financeiro. Todos os alvos do Anexo C batem exatos, incluindo os que não estavam no aceite: headcount por área (486/214/168/…) **e** por modalidade (604/472/164), as duas margens fechando ao mesmo tempo.

Três coisas que o aceite não pede com estas palavras:

- **O agregado nunca é linha.** `consolidado` e `todas` são soma. Provocar a entrada de `todas` como área não deixa um teste vermelho — deixa o módulo sem carregar.
- **Taxa nenhuma está armazenada.** Absenteísmo, eNPS, engajamento, margens, PMR/PME/PMP: todos existem como numerador e denominador. O estoque de dezembro não existe no protótipo e foi derivado do próprio PME declarado.
- **O headcount é fluxo acumulado em todo grão** — o saldo de abertura de cada célula é derivado de trás para frente a partir de dezembro, então a foto aprovada bate *e* a identidade contábil fecha em cada área.

**Três defeitos meus, pegos pelos próprios testes.** A inclinação de entidade aplicada duas vezes (folha com 78% em SP onde estão declarados 68%). O viés de **ordem** na repartição mensal — 241 admissões em 42 células deixam quase toda célula em zero, e a sobra ia sempre para as primeiras do vetor, que são de uma entidade só. E um teste fraco: a ponte da DRE fecha por construção, então trocar o CMV de 720 para 700 não derrubava nada — acrescentei o caso que fixa cada degrau, um por um.

## T-114 — o adaptador

Recortar é **escolher linhas**. A busca pelos multiplicadores do protótipo dá zero em três guardas distintas: `0.62`/`0.38`, qualquer fração literal na camada de dados, e o próprio operador de multiplicação em `adaptador.ts` e `recorte.ts`.

E a aditividade fecha nos 4 períodos e nos 12 meses, inclusive no cruzamento entidade × área. **É a metade que dá sentido à outra**: com fator de escala a aditividade também "fecha", porque 0,62 + 0,38 = 1 — que é o achado 4.

Quando a dimensão não existe na linha (Financeiro não tem área), o recorte devolve `{aplicavel: false, dimensao}` em vez de tudo ou de vazio. Devolver tudo poria a receita consolidada sob o recorte de Operações — o "valor remanescente" que RF-01 proíbe.

## Verificação

| | |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | **691 passed** (32 arquivos) |
| `npx playwright test` | **170 passed** |
| lint · typecheck · build · prettier | limpos |

## O que ficou parado

**T-113 → `⛔ H-45`.** Três das 21 métricas medem horas, pontos de eNPS e contagem de vagas — grandezas que o enum fechado de cinco unidades não nomeia. Isso não cabe no modo mockup: a unidade não é número, é afirmação sobre o que o número significa, e estender o enum exige editar a seção 9.2 do PRD.

É o único gate entre aqui e as telas com painéis.

## Problem

- "Check Eligibility" is the most-clicked element on the site, and on the awards page it does nothing.
- The banner links to `/awards#eligibility-checker`, but no element has that id. Sibling components already use `#apply` (`HeroWithChecker`, `RoundStage`). Once the hash is in the URL the link is a hard no-op — same location, no scroll.
- Many on-page sessions show repeat clicks and rageclicks on the CTA as users try again.
- Downstream, the eligibility Typeform embed has no load handling. When the iframe fails, the 500px box just sits empty after "Loading…" disappears, and there is no instrumentation to measure how often this happens.

## Changes

- **Banner target** — default `eligibilityUrl` now points at `/awards#apply`, the id the section actually uses.
- **Scroll offset** — the `#apply` container gets `scroll-mt-24` so the heading is not flush against the top.
- **Embed fallback** — `EmbedLoader` now has an `onLoad` handler and an 8s load timeout. On timeout it shows an "Open on Typeform" link so the user is never stuck at a blank box.
- **Instrumentation** — the embed path fires `embed_loaded` on success and `embed_load_failed` on timeout, so the failure rate is measurable.

## Notes

- `npm install` is blocked here by the private FontAwesome Pro registry, so `astro check`/build could not run in this environment. The banner fix is deterministic (the old id does not exist; `#apply` does and is already used elsewhere). The embed fallback was reviewed by reasoning through the render states; please confirm the build passes in CI.

body:
## Summary
- The one genuinely stateful piece of PolitikKu (#70's own decision): a typed TypeScript state machine (`ts/`, new toolchain — esbuild/vitest/eslint, own CI job) implementing `idle → searching/locating → ambiguous/notFound/resolved`, mounted into #74/#75's Python-rendered lookup markup via `data-pk-lookup-*` attributes already scaffolded there.
- Resolution is entirely client-side against a small static JSON (`lpa.politikku_lookup_index`, ~470 bytes for the pilot's 2 Seats / 12 postcodes) — no server round-trip for what a visitor types or where they are.
- Two real data gaps found and resolved with the user before building (not guessed):
  - The postcode pilot (#76) and MP-profile pilot (#78) cover different Seats, so a lookup can resolve to a Seat with no profile page yet (P.101 today). The client index carries a `hasProfile` flag; resolved/ambiguous views degrade to an honest "MP profile for this Seat isn't built yet" instead of a broken link.
  - "Use my location" needs boundary/geometry data this repo doesn't have (ADR 0008 names it as future work). `geolocation.ts` reads a real coordinate fix via `navigator.geolocation` but never inspects, sends, or stores it — the privacy promise ("Location is read in your browser and never sent to us") stays literally true, and the flow always lands on an honest "not supported yet" result rather than a guessed match.
  - The mock's "narrow down by street/Seksyen" field isn't built: no street-level data exists to narrow anything with in this pilot, and a field that quietly does nothing would claim a capability that isn't real.
- A real bug caught during visual verification: the first cut of the client JSON never actually included each Seat's own `code` field (only as the object key), so `seat.code` read back as `undefined` client-side despite type-checking cleanly — fixed, with a regression test on the Python side (`test_every_seat_carries_its_own_code_not_just_the_dict_key`).
- `.gitignore` also closes a pre-existing gap: `public/politikku/index.html`/`landing.html`/`mp/` (#74/#75/#79's own output) never had an explicit entry before, relying on nobody ever running `git add -A` there.

## Not in scope / flagged separately
`daily.yml` doesn't render *any* of the PolitikKu pages yet (`index.html`, `landing.html`, MP profiles) or run the new `ts/` build — only the legacy dashboard (`lpa.public_page`) is wired into the daily publish. That predates this PR (#74/#75/#79 all landed without it) and is a bigger, separate call than this ticket's scope — flagging it for a follow-up rather than fixing it here.

author: rebenitez1802
body:
### SUMMARY

ECharts-rendered charts (which use the **canvas** renderer — e.g. **Sunburst**, and most modern ECharts charts) export **blurry / low-resolution** via **"Download as image" / "Export screenshot (png)"**. It's worst on standard‑DPI (1×) displays and when zooming into the exported PNG.

**Root cause.** `superset-frontend/src/utils/downloadAsImage.tsx` clones the chart DOM and copies each `<canvas>` **1:1** at its on-screen backing-store resolution (`preserveCanvasContent`). The PNG path then upscales the whole layout via `transform: scale(PNG_SCALE = 2)`. Vector/DOM content (SVG, text) re-rasterizes crisply at 2×, but a `<canvas>` is a bitmap: `dom-to-image-more` serializes it with `canvas.toDataURL()` and it is simply **stretched** by the transform. So a canvas chart can never gain detail — the export is capped at the on-screen canvas resolution (`CSS size × devicePixelRatio`), which on a 1× display is just the CSS size.

**Fix.** Re-render ECharts-backed canvases at export time instead of screen-scraping them:
- Recover the live ECharts instance from the canvas's `.echarts-host` ancestor via `echarts.getInstanceByDom(...)`.
- Replace the cloned canvas with `instance.renderToCanvas({ pixelRatio: PNG_SCALE, backgroundColor: 'transparent' })` — a true high-resolution re-render that the PNG path then samples 1:1.
- `echarts` is loaded with a **dynamic `import('echarts/core')`** so it stays out of the core bundle (charts are lazy plugins).
- Non-ECharts canvases (deck.gl / WebGL) keep the existing 1:1 copy as a fallback.
- Because `renderToCanvas` flattens all zrender layers into one canvas, each host is re-rendered **only once** (secondary hover-layer canvases are skipped).

Self-contained change in `downloadAsImage.tsx`; no plugin, API, or config changes.

### BEFORE/AFTER SCREENSHOTS OR ANIMATED GIF

_Before:_ a downloaded Sunburst PNG is soft and pixelates on zoom.
_After:_ the Sunburst PNG is crisp and stays sharp when zoomed.

(Screenshots to be attached.)

### TESTING INSTRUCTIONS

1. In Explore, build a **Sunburst** chart (e.g. on the "Vehicle Sales" dataset).
2. Chart context menu → **Download → "Export screenshot (png)"** (solid or transparent).
3. Open the PNG and zoom in — the chart is now crisp instead of pixelated.
4. Regression: exporting tables (ag-grid), dashboards, and non-ECharts charts still works.

Unit tests:
```
cd superset-frontend
npm run test -- src/utils/downloadAsImage.test.ts
```
Added tests cover: ECharts canvas re-rendered at `PNG_SCALE` pixel ratio; non-ECharts canvas kept at on-screen resolution; a host with multiple canvas layers re-rendered only once.

- [ ] Has associated issue:

- [x] Changes UI (improves the resolution of the exported chart image; no visible control change)
- [ ] Includes DB Migration (follow approval process in [SIP-59](https://github.com/apache/superset/issues/13351))

  - [ ] Confirm DB migration upgrade and downgrade tested

body:
## Summary
- lazily compute objective gradients only when IPOPT requests `grad_f`
- share one value-keyed forward cache between objective and constraint callbacks
- assemble the exact objective gradient from the measurement rows already returned by the shared constraint-Jacobian transform
- make the Gauss-Newton producer blocks follow the same lag and warmup attribution as the objective
- expose callback/cache counts in `transcription_audit` for A100 benchmarking

## Why
The profiled run requested 399 objective values but only 305 gradients, so the previous eager objective callback performed at least 94 unnecessary gradient evaluations. Objective and constraint callbacks also independently evaluated `_fwd_all` at the same trial points.

The cache compares complete float64 iterate values, is invalidated on every changed iterate, and stores only no-grad/detached tensors. Callback order therefore affects reuse, not correctness.

## Test plan
- [x] callback-order cache tests, including mutation of a reused ndarray
- [x] exact objective-gradient parity under lagged producer duplication and warmup masking
- [x] real collocation integration assertion for forward and derivative cache hits

- [x] full estimator suite: 30 tests passed
- [x] one-iteration real IPOPT collocation solve exercised the Gauss-Newton Hessian callback

## Summary

Four tests added in #9750 fail on CI (`tests (2/5)`, [run 32723171248](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/actions/runs/32723171248/job/97418843746)):

```
test_docling_does_not_advertise_audio_it_cannot_transcribe   FAILED
test_docling_advertises_audio_when_the_engine_is_installed   FAILED
test_docling_media_accepts_any_speech_backend                FAILED
test_docling_media_names_a_backend_that_works_everywhere     FAILED
```

```
E  AssertionError: assert ['ffmpeg', 'openai-whisper'] == ['openai-whisper']
E  AssertionError: assert '.wav' in info["content_types"]
```

**The production behaviour is correct and unchanged.** `DoclingReader` withdraws its audio and video formats unless the `ffmpeg` binary is on PATH *and* a speech backend is importable — a runner with no ffmpeg genuinely cannot transcribe, so not advertising those formats is the right answer.

The tests were wrong, in one specific way: they pinned the *packages* with `_specs(...)` but let PATH decide the *binary*. ffmpeg is installed on my machine and not on the GitHub runner, so the same assertions meant different things in the two places. The fifth test in that group, `test_docling_media_needs_ffmpeg_not_just_a_speech_package`, passed on CI precisely because it was the one that patched `shutil.which`.

`_no_ffmpeg()` becomes `_ffmpeg(present: bool)`, and every docling media test now states the binary in the direction it means, exactly as it already states the packages.

author: elgansayer
body:
## Problem

`./start.sh` fails immediately on `npm install` in the backend with:

```
npm error code EALLOWREMOTE
npm error Fetching packages of type "remote" have been disabled
npm error Refusing to fetch "xlsx@https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/xlsx-0.20.3.tgz"
```

SheetJS distributes newer versions of `xlsx` exclusively from their own CDN rather than the npm registry. npm's `EALLOWREMOTE` security policy blocks remote tarball fetches, so the install always fails.

## Root Cause

`backend/package.json` had `xlsx` pinned to a CDN URL:
```json
"xlsx": "https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/xlsx-0.20.3.tgz"
```

`xlsx` is not directly imported in any backend source file - it is only a transitive dependency of `@nlpjs/xtables` (which requires `xlsx@^0.18.0`). The CDN version (0.20.3) was unnecessary.

## Fix

- Replace the CDN URL with `xlsx@^0.18.5` from the npm registry, which satisfies `@nlpjs/xtables`'s `^0.18.0` peer requirement
- Update the `overrides[@nlpjs/xtables].xlsx` entry from `$xlsx` (which resolved to the CDN URL) to `^0.18.5`

## Verification

`cd backend && npm install` now completes without error.

body:
Fixes #237.

Material was decoupled from the Flutter SDK into the [`material_ui`](https://pub.dev/packages/material_ui) package. The in-SDK `package:flutter/material.dart` is [frozen to contributions](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/184093) and [scheduled for removal](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/172942), so pinput needs to move for apps that have already migrated.

### The bug

`_PinputState.build` asserts `debugCheckHasMaterial(context)`, which resolves the ancestor with `LookupBoundary.findAncestorWidgetOfExactType<Material>` — an **exact** type match. A `material_ui` app's `Scaffold` provides `material_ui`'s `Material`, a different class, so the assert always fails:

```
No Material widget found.
#2  _PinputState.build (package:pinput/src/pinput_state.dart:289:12)
```

It throws out of `build()`, so Flutter substitutes an `ErrorWidget` and the field never renders. `assert` is debug-only, so release builds are unaffected — which makes it easy to miss: the screen works in release and red-screens under `flutter run`.

`MaterialUiCompatibilityBridge` does not help. It supplies a legacy `Theme` and `Localizations`, never a legacy `Material` ancestor. The [workaround in #237](https://github.com/Tkko/Flutter_Pinput/issues/237) (wrapping each `Pinput` in `old.Material(type: transparency)`) works but pushes a legacy import back into apps that just removed theirs.

### What changed

Import swap only, no logic touched. The whole library is **one** import line — 11 of the 13 files under `lib/src` are `part of '../pinput.dart'`. Also swapped `test/` and `example/` so they exercise the real target.

Everything pinput uses exists in `material_ui` with identical semantics: `Theme`, `ThemeData`, `Colors`, `TextField` (docs), `AdaptiveTextSelectionToolbar`, and both `debugCheckHasMaterial*` helpers. After the swap the asserts resolve against `material_ui`, so a `material_ui` `Scaffold` satisfies them.

Worth noting the two asserts are not equivalent, in case removing them was on the table as an alternative fix: `debugCheckHasMaterialLocalizations` guards something real, since the default `contextMenuBuilder` is `AdaptiveTextSelectionToolbar.editableText`, which reads `MaterialLocalizations` at runtime for the cut/copy/paste labels. Only `debugCheckHasMaterial` is decorative — pinput never calls `Material.of`, draws no ink, and `TextSelectionToolbar` builds its own `Material`. Migrating keeps both correct rather than trading one problem for another.

- `pubspec.yaml`: `material_ui: ^1.0.0`, `sdk: >=3.12.0`, `flutter: >=3.44.0` — the floor `material_ui` itself declares, not higher. This supersedes #234, which raised the floor to 3.27.0 for an unrelated reason.
- Major version, because `Pinput` can only satisfy one `Material` universe: 6.x stays the path for apps still on `package:flutter/material.dart`.

### Verification

- `flutter analyze lib/ test/ example/` — no errors or warnings.
- `flutter test` — 12/12 pass.
- Reproduced #237 against published 6.0.2 in a `material_ui` app: `ErrorWidget: 1`, `EditableText: 0`. With this branch and **no** workaround wrapper: no exception, `EditableText: 1`.
- Integrated into a production `material_ui` app (~450 Dart files, Flutter 3.47.1): analyze clean, test suite green, release-flavour APK builds.

author: chesema
body:
Extracts the `ICacheProvider` / `CacheWriter` API changes from #115816 (the ReadPlan slice) into a standalone refactor, so that pull request carries only the read-plan logic. The experimental `use_reader_executor` read path (default off) is the only consumer.

- `CacheWriter::committed` returns the committed-prefix end as a `size_t` instead of an `IntervalSet` (a segment fills append-only, so what is committed is always one contiguous prefix). The disk writer reads the segment's live frontier directly and drops its `committed_ranges` / `committed_mutex` bookkeeping.
- `claimLeadRole` loses its `ByteRange` argument and returns just the `Claim`; the `Lead` struct is removed. The caller reads the committed prefix via `committed`.
- Add `CacheWriter::fillsWholeSegment`, the writer-level mirror of the existing `ICacheProvider::fillsWholeSegment`. It has no caller yet on `master` — #115816 is its consumer — but it mirrors the provider-level flag, which is likewise not yet consumed.
- Remove `ICacheProvider::populatesOnMiss`. A tier that does not populate now emits a writer-less miss from `resolve`, which the executor already treats as read-from-source-only.

No behavior change.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/115816

Follow-up to #104, found by clicking through as an admissions officer rather than by reading the diff.

#104 guarded `/admin` and `/director`, which left the rest open. An admissions officer typing `/finance` was shown the **six-item finance sidebar**, and `/faculty` the **eight-item faculty one**. |---|---|
| `/admissions` | admissions, registrar, admin |
| `/finance` | bursar, admin |
| `/faculty` | faculty, admin |
| `/comms` | communications, admin |
| `/student` | student |
| `/parent` | parent |

author: nicoloboschi
body:
## Problem

asyncpg raises several of its connection and pool errors with no args, so `str(e)` is the empty string for them. The acquire and retry paths in `db_utils.py` interpolated `str(e)`, so a real failure logged as:

```
Database acquire failed after 4 attempts:
```

The cause is silently dropped — exactly the field you need. `InterfaceError` alone covers three different conditions:

| asyncpg raise site | Meaning | Recoverable? |
|---|---|---|
| connection dropped | transient | yes, retry works |
| `'pool is closed'` / `'pool is closing'` (`pool.py:860,986`) | terminal | no — never, at any database health |
| `'pool is not initialized'` (`pool.py:984`) | terminal | no |

`_is_retryable` classifies by `type(exc).__name__`, so all three are retried identically and forever. The log was the only place that could have told them apart, and it printed nothing.

`health_check` had the same hole: it returned `str(e)` in the readiness payload's `error` field, which is the first thing an operator reads when the database looks down.

## Change

`repr()` instead of `str()` in four log lines in `db_utils.py` and in the `health_check` error field. `repr()` always carries the class name, empty message or not.

```
- Database acquire failed after 4 attempts:
+ Database acquire failed after 4 attempts: InterfaceError('pool is closed')
```

Same fix and same reasoning as `recall_async`'s wrapper message (#1384) — `memory_engine.py` already does this a few thousand lines further down, with a comment saying why.

## Tests

Two cases in `tests/test_db_utils.py`, one per path, asserting the exception class survives into the log when `str(e)` is empty. The stub is named `InterfaceError` deliberately: `_is_retryable` matches on `type(exc).__name__`, so nothing else reaches the code under test.

Verified as a regression test, not just a green run — reverting the four `{e!r}` back to `{e}` fails both new cases and leaves the two pre-existing ones passing.

`./scripts/hooks/lint.sh` clean, `ty` clean. No API surface change: the health payload goes out via `JSONResponse` with no response model, `error` is free text, and nothing in the CLI, embed daemon, or control plane parses it.

## Context

Split out of #3719, which paired this with a self-termination mechanism. That half is on hold: the pool-wedge it responds to has no diagnosis yet, and this change is what will supply one. See the discussion on #3719.

author: endgor
body:
## Why

Bing sends most of this site's search traffic and nothing in the repo could read it. First 28 days of data, now that it can:

**310 clicks / 13,636 impressions / 2.3% CTR at average positions 4-7.**

That is a snippet problem, not a ranking problem:

| Page | Impr | Clicks | CTR | Pos |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/tools/subnet-calculator` | 935 | 89 | 9.5% | 4.3 |
| `/tools/ip-lookup` | 2,837 | 100 | 3.5% | 5.5 |
| `/tools/tenant-lookup` | 5,367 | 61 | **1.1%** | 7.0 |
| `/tools/service-tags` | 783 | 2 | **0.3%** | 7.2 |

The cannibalization check also found the homepage bidding against its own tool pages on every core query — pos 7.5 with 0 clicks on "azure subnet calculator" while `/tools/subnet-calculator` sat at pos 1.0 with 22 clicks. Cause was in code: the homepage title and description repeated every tool's keywords.

## What changed

**Measurement** — `scripts/bingStats.ts` + `npm run bing-stats`, in the same shape as `cfStats.ts`:

```
npm run bing-stats                      # 28-day overview
npm run bing-stats -- --days 90
npm run bing-stats -- --crawl           # daily index + crawl detail
npm run bing-stats -- --page /tools/tenant-lookup
npm run bing-stats -- --query "azure ip ranges"
npm run bing-stats -- --cannibalization 25
npm run bing-stats -- --json --queries 100
```

Key needs to be in `.env.local` as `BING_WEBMASTER_API_KEY`.

**Snippets** — new titles and descriptions for Tenant Lookup and the Service Tags index; homepage de-targeted to brand level; `Layout` no longer appends the brand to a title that already contains it (the homepage was rendering "Azure Hub - ... · Azure Hub").

**One rendering fix** — the static base-tag directory on the Service Tags index was gated on `!hasMounted`, so it vanished at hydration: a plain fetch saw 98 tag names, a JS-executing crawler saw the page without them. Now renders unconditionally.

## What deliberately did NOT change

The service-tag clutter policy is untouched. The 3,488 regional variants stay `noindex, nofollow, noarchive`, stay out of the sitemap, and gain **zero** new crawl targets — the static directory is still names-only, verified at 98 items and 0 links to variant pages in the rendered output.

An earlier proposal to unblock `/data/` in `robots.txt` was dropped for exactly this reason: the client-side card grid links every one of the 3,745 index entries, variants included, so letting crawlers fetch that JSON would have re-exposed the whole cluster.

## Verification

`npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm test` (138 passing), plus rendered output checked against a dev server for all three changed pages.

## Deliberately deferred

- Server-rendered content for the VM Pricing index (81 words in HTML, 52 impressions, 0 clicks) — worth its own PR, and worth waiting for GSC data since the 1,835 SKU pages only entered Bing's index on 2026-08-22.
- Per-URL sitemap `lastmod` (1,940 URLs currently share one fresh daily timestamp).
- IndexNow diff submission (`--all` submits 14 URLs today).
- Google Search Console equivalent — needs a service account before it can be built.

## Requirement trace

| REQ/AC IDs | Changed files / domain | Tests or review evidence |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-001 / AC-004 | `packages/core/src/memory-port.ts` | Strict record, bound, scope, idempotency, degraded/required-mode unit tests |
| REQ-002 / AC-001 | `packages/core/src/mem-http-memory-adapter.ts` | Pinned public HTTP mock tests plus actual loopback mem/PostgreSQL E3 |
| REQ-003 / AC-002 | Memory adapter configuration and preflight | Principal derivation, env-only credential, minimum capabilities, cross-scope/self-grant/root-token denials |
| REQ-004 / AC-001 | Deterministic write and exact readback | First write, replay, changed-payload conflict, citation/provenance/readback assertions |
| REQ-005 / AC-003 | Bounded untrusted recall projection | Grant/token revoke, expiry, archive, forget and unrelated-item isolation in actual E3 |
| REQ-003 / AC-005 | Tests, docs, security scan | No evidence payload contains a credential, transcript body or absolute local path |

## File domains

- `packages/core/src/memory-port.ts`, `packages/core/index.ts`: strict public seam and exports owned by core.
- `packages/core/src/mem-http-memory-adapter.ts`: revision-pinned public mem HTTP adapter owned by the memory integration boundary.
- `tests/core/*memory*`, `tests/integration/mem-http-memory-adapter.e3.test.ts`: deterministic contract tests and disposable actual-service E3.
- `docs/memory-port.md`, READMEs, `CHANGELOG.md`: operator credential/grant boundary, non-goals, usage and verification contract.

## Scope and non-goals

This PR adds an engine-detached `MemoryPort`, bounded `task-state.v1` write/readback, bounded `memory-recall.v1`, and an adapter pinned to mem revision `4c714aa352f79f0080a24904668210d6c445ba10` and `durable-context.v1`. One adapter is bound to one workspace instance, mem workspace, position-derived principal and canonical path. It verifies the pinned server version and minimum effective capabilities on every operation and has no grant/admin method.

Non-goals remain unchanged: no engine or renderer wiring, automatic grant, Agent admin token, model extraction, transcript copy, Host resume, live Qoder/Claude qualification, marketplace/control-plane work, or completion claim for #161.

## Validation

- Exact commands: `npm exec -- tsx --test tests/core/memory-port.test.ts tests/core/mem-http-memory-adapter.test.ts tests/integration/mem-http-memory-adapter.e3.test.ts` (additional exact commands below)
  - `npm exec -- tsx --test tests/core/memory-port.test.ts tests/core/mem-http-memory-adapter.test.ts tests/integration/mem-http-memory-adapter.e3.test.ts`
  - `MEMORY_E3_RUN=1 MEMORY_E3_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port> npm exec -- tsx --test tests/integration/mem-http-memory-adapter.e3.test.ts`

  - `npm run security:check`

- Observed counts/results: PASS, full repository test phase 1672/1672 passed with 0 failures and 1 external-service skip; actual E3 1/1 passed
  - focused contract suite: 18 pass, 0 fail, 1 external-service skip;
  - actual mem/PostgreSQL E3: 1 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip;
  - full repository test phase: 1,672 pass, 0 fail, 1 external-service skip; build, typecheck and governance passed;
  - the first composite check then rejected one documentation-only reserved example hostname; the hostname was corrected and the exact candidate passed the focused suite, typecheck, build and security check;
  - production dependency audit: 0 vulnerabilities.
- Check URLs: NOT VERIFIED: exact-head GitHub CI is pending on this Draft PR.

| ID | REQ/AC | Observable acceptance criterion | Command or manual steps | Environment | Expected | Observed | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | AC-001 | Actual write, replay, conflict and exact readback | Actual E3 command above | Darwin arm64; Node 24.13.0; Go 1.25.9; Docker 29.2.1; pinned mem SHA; PostgreSQL pgvector image digest `sha256:00ba258a66dac104fd5171074a0084462a64a1369d8513f3d0a634e2f24d15bc` | All lifecycle assertions pass | 1 pass, 0 fail | PASS |
| V2 | AC-002 / AC-003 | Scope denial and full grant/token/memory lifecycle | Same disposable E3 | Fresh user, workspace, position credential and data | Denials are stable; unrelated active item remains | All assertions passed; disposable state destroyed | PASS |
| V3 | AC-004 | Optional outage degrades; required mode fails before any consumer call | Focused suite | Mocked public HTTP boundary | Typed results/errors | 18 pass, 0 fail, 1 E3 skip | PASS |
| V4 | AC-005 | Public evidence and tracked files remain secret/path safe | Security check, diff check, bounded static scan | Candidate commit | No credential, body or absolute path exposure | Security and diff checks pass | PASS |
| V5 | all | Exact-head CI gate | GitHub pull-request workflow | Draft PR head | CI green before review request | Pending | NOT VERIFIED |

## Security and compatibility

- [x] No credentials, personal identifiers, private messages, internal URLs, or generated indexes are included.
- [x] Source/tool access and public evidence are explicitly bounded.
- [x] Logs redact content, identities, and credential-bearing URLs.
- [x] Compatibility, migration, and cross-repository effects are stated below.
- [x] New dependencies and licenses were reviewed, or no dependency changed.
- [x] `npm run check` and `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` pass, or an exact NOT VERIFIED boundary is recorded.
- [x] Behavior changes carry a matching docs delta, or this body records the explicit no-doc-needed reason (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Documentation consistency").

No dependency, database schema or migration changes are introduced. Tokens are accepted only through a named `MEM_*_TOKEN` environment variable and sent only as an authorization header. The adapter rejects broader search/delete/admin/provider-mutation/export/import authority, does not expose lifecycle controls, validates strict response shapes, and treats recalled text as `untrusted` data with `authority: none`.

## Known limitations

- This typed seam is deliberately not wired into the execution engine.
- The pinned public capabilities response exposes effective permissions and workspace identity but not token paths. The operator must mint an exact path-scoped credential; mem enforces that path server-side. The E3 proves cross-scope denial.
- Local E3 was run on Darwin arm64. No live Agent Host, Qoder or Claude Code call was run.
- Exact-head CI and independent PREFLIGHT review are pending. Human CODEOWNER review is intentionally not requested at Draft creation.

## Risk and rollback

Runtime risk is contained because no engine consumer is enabled. The only data-plane operation available through the adapter is scoped write/read/recall with exact readback. Local E3 used disposable services and destroyed the generated data and credentials. Roll back by reverting commit `06e43055e44ee76debb3de8cc720abb1a09faeee`; there is no migration or durable repository state to unwind.

author: xcellentbird
body:
개인정보 파기를 하지 않기로 해서, **파기 Cron·보관 기간 계산·운영자 설정의 파기 대기 일수를 함께** 걷어냈다.

> **베이스를 `main` → `qa` 로 고쳤다.** 처음에 `main` 으로 열어 다른 48개 커밋이 딸려 보였다. 이 브랜치는 `qa` 에서 잘랐고, 이 저장소의 PR 은 `qa` 로 간다.
> **ADR 번호도 35 → 36 으로 물러났다.** 이 PR 을 연 1분 뒤 #177(규칙·일정 굳히기)이 `qa` 에 먼저 들어가면서 ADR-35 를 가져갔고, 코드가 여러 곳에서 그 번호를 부른다. `qa` 를 머지해 충돌을 풀었다.

## 왜 반쪽이 아니라 통째로

셋이 한 덩어리다. Cron 만 끄고 설정 칸을 남기면 **운영자가 고른 숫자가 아무 일도 하지 않는다** — "3일 뒤 삭제"라고 쓰인 칸이 삭제하지 않는 것은 그 칸이 없는 것보다 나쁘다. 계산(`purgeDueAt`)만 남겨도 같은 종류다. 부르는 곳이 없는 판정은 다음 사람에게 *아직 돈다* 고 말한다.

## 바뀐 것

| 자리 | 무엇 |
|---|---|
| `wrangler.jsonc` | `triggers.crons` 제거 (매일 04:00 KST 로 깨어나던 자리) |
| `src/server/index.ts` | `scheduled` 핸들러 제거 — `fetch` 만 내보낸다 |
| `src/server/event-do.ts` | `purgeIfExpired` 제거, `config.retentionDays` 검증·저장 제거 |
| `src/server/routes/host.ts` | `validConfig` 의 `retentionDays` 검증 제거 |
| `src/shared/phase.ts` | `purgeDueAt` 제거 |
| `src/shared/constants.ts` | `RETENTION_DAYS` · `LIMITS.retentionDays` 제거 |
| `src/shared/types.ts` | `EventConfig.retentionDays` · `PublicEvent.retentionDays` 제거 |
| `src/shared/copy.ts` | 설정 탭 `개인정보 파기` 절 · 파기 안내 문구 제거 |
| `src/client/routes/host/Settings.tsx` | 파기 대기 일수 칸과 확인창 항목 제거 |
| `test/07-retention*.test.ts` | 삭제 (2개 파일 / 11개 테스트, 없어진 규칙을 보던 것) |

회차를 지우는 길은 그대로 하나 남았다 — 설정 탭의 `이 회차 삭제하기`. 회차 1개 = DO 1개라 누르면 참가자·연락처·콕이 한 번에 사라진다.

## 등록 화면은 손대지 않았다

참가자에게 한 약속과 어긋나지 않는다. 등록 폼의 연락처 안내(`REGISTER.contactNote`)는 *어디까지 가는지* 두 문장만 말하고, **파기 기한은 이미 거기 없었다.** 어긋났다면 문구를 먼저 고쳐야 했을 자리다 (ADR-19 의 규칙).

되살릴 때의 순서는 문서에 박아뒀다 — 등록 화면에 "N일 뒤에 지워져요" 를 다시 적는 건 **지우는 코드를 되살린 뒤**다.

## 짚어둘 것 — 상한이 하나 없어졌다

`auth.ts` 의 **참가자 세션 30일은 파기를 근거로 정해진 값**이었다. *"회차가 파티 사흘 뒤 파기되므로 세션이 살아 있어도 열리는 게 없다"* 가 그 근거인데, 이제 성립하지 않는다. 남의 기기에 남은 쿠키는 **회차가 살아 있는 동안** 그 참가자 화면을 연다.

TTL 은 건드리지 않았다 — 파티 당일에 세션이 끊기는 사고가 그 값의 이유이고(ADR-32), 그건 그대로다. 대신 근거가 사라진 것을 `auth.ts` 주석과 ADR-32·36 에 적었다. **상한을 다시 만드는 길은 끝난 회차를 지우는 것뿐**이므로, 파티가 끝난 회차를 지우는 것이 운영자의 일이 됐다.

바꿀 생각이 있으면 세션 TTL 을 줄이는 쪽을 따로 논의하면 좋겠다. 이 PR 범위 밖이라 손대지 않았다.

## #177 과 겹친 자리

같은 파일 여럿을 건드려 충돌이 셋 났다. 셋 다 **#177 의 것을 살리고 파기 쪽만 뺐다.**

- `event-do.ts` — `rulesLocked` 검사는 그대로, `retentionDays` 검증만 제거
- `Settings.tsx` — `rulesLocked` import 는 그대로, `RETENTION_DAYS` 만 제거
- `docs/ADR.md` — `qa` 의 ADR-35 를 먼저, 내 것을 ADR-36 으로 뒤에

#177 의 ADR-35 표에 있던 `이름 · 장소 · 파기 일수 | 연다` 줄에서 **파기 일수를 뺐다** — 그 설정이 이제 없다.

## 문서

- **ADR-36** 을 새로 적었다 (걷어낸 이유 · 등록 화면과의 관계 · 대가 표)
- **ADR-19**(보관 기간을 정한 결정)와 **ADR-32**(30일 세션의 근거)에 뒤따라온 변경을 표시했다
- `CLAUDE.md` 에 규칙 한 줄 — *"며칠 뒤에 지워져요" 를 등록 화면에도 운영자 설정에도 다시 적지 마라. 되살릴 거라면 지우는 코드가 먼저다*
- `README.md` · `docs/PLAN.md` · `docs/UI.md` · `docs/scenarios/13-personal-link.md` 의 파기 서술 정리

## 확인

`qa` 를 머지한 뒤 다시 돌렸다.

- `npm run check` — typecheck(클라이언트·Worker·테스트) · 문구 검사 · wrangler 설정 검사 통과
- `npm test` — **365 tests / 17 files 전부 통과** (`qa` 의 376/19 에서 파기 테스트 11개·파일 2개가 빠진 수와 정확히 맞는다)
- `npm run build` — 통과

author: patrick-hermann-sva
body:
Follow-up to #66. The kiosk stands at the table, the match list is everybody's, and the sheet goes on a wall — none of them has a player to take a colour from, so all three kept the red the mark is drawn in. That left them looking like the one state that means *nobody is here*.

| Page | Colour |
| --- | --- |
| `/kiosk` | `#3aa6ff` Hellblau |
| `/matches` | `#4d7c4a` Moosgrün |
| `/qr` | `#d64f9c` Pink |

## Fixed, not random

A blade that comes up different on every reload reads as something broken rather than as decoration, and a page you can recognise by its colour is worth more than one that surprises you.

The three are the **widest-apart triple in the palette** — no pair closer than **ΔE 73.2**, against ΔE 23.8 for the palette as a whole — so the pages are told apart at a glance. Which page got which is arbitrary; that it never changes is not, and the tests assert exactly that: same colour signed in and signed out, same colour for two different players.

The start page keeps its rule from #66: your own colour once you are recognised, and no colour at all before that.

## Two assertions that had to give

Both were exact-attribute matches that stopped holding once the wrapper gained a second class — `class="page-mascot"` became `class="page-mascot paddle-0"`:

- `TestBothPagesGreetWithTheMascot` and `TestTheSheetCarriesTheMascot` in the suite
- the sheet check in `verifyScript`

They now match the attribute's start rather than the whole of it. Worth naming rather than quietly fixing: an exact match on a class attribute is a test that breaks the next time anything is added to it.

## Checks

- `gofmt`, `go vet`, `templ fmt` + `go generate` reproducible; `golangci-lint` in `v2.13.1-alpine` — 0 issues
- full suite `-race -count=1 -p 1` against PostgreSQL 18.6 — green
- distroless image built, `verifyScript` run against it — all checks passed
- driven in a browser: computed `fill` on each of the three pages matches its class, and the printed sheet rendered in print media — pink blade, black outline, QR code untouched on white

body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"RendaniSinyage"} -->
_Requested by **Ray** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01MJV7TxmZvhvGn1RbE6GrYf)_

## Why this PR exists

Core's android-template changes do **not** reach already-seeded apps: CI compose starts from an empty install state and the installer's ownership guard never overwrites committed android files. So the HMS-wave template hunks (core#80 merged, core#81) need a one-time sync into this app's committed `android/` tree. This PR is that sync — the same three files, hunk-for-hunk identical to the template.

## What changed

1. **`android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`** (from core#81): `<uses-sdk tools:overrideLibrary="com.huawei.hms.flutter.hmsavailability"/>`. `huawei_hmsavailability` 6.13.0+300 (pulled in by hms_sdk) declares minSdk 26 while this app builds at minSdk 24, which fails the manifest merge in **every** Android build — this is the current main build red. The override is inert when the HMS plugins are not in the build, and safe when they are (hms_sdk's Dart layer fail-opens to GMS).
2. **`android/build.gradle`** (from core#80): buildscript block with Huawei maven + `com.huawei.agconnect:agcp:1.9.1.304` classpath, and the same Huawei maven in `allprojects` — all gated on `System.getenv("BUILD_HMS") == "true"`.
3. **`android/app/build.gradle`** (from core#80): gated `apply plugin: 'com.huawei.agconnect'`, additionally guarded on `android/app/agconnect-services.json` existing (warn and skip when the secret is absent).

The BUILD_HMS wiring activates only with `build_hms: true` in CI **and** an `agconnect-services.json` present; with BUILD_HMS unset every gate evaluates false and build behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Validation (this repo's committed android tree, Flutter 3.47.1, AGP 8.11.1, Android SDK 36)

Harness: a scratch Flutter app using this branch's `android/` tree verbatim plus hms_sdk's two plugin pins (`huawei_hmsavailability ^6.13.0+300`, `huawei_push ^6.15.0+300`).

- **Before** (main's manifest): `:app:processDebugMainManifest` fails with exactly the CI error — `uses-sdk:minSdkVersion 24 cannot be smaller than version 26 declared in library [:huawei_hmsavailability]`.
- **After** (this branch): the merge succeeds; merged manifest keeps `minSdkVersion="24"` and contains the huawei plugin components. A full `flutter build apk --debug` on the same tree completes end-to-end.
- **BUILD_HMS unset** (default): all gates evaluate false — every green run above ran with it unset.
- **BUILD_HMS=true without agconnect-services.json**: agcp classpath resolves from the Huawei repo, the guard logs the documented `[hms]` warning, skips the plugin apply, and the build stays green.

Expected CI on this PR: the Android build should now pass the manifest-merge step that reds main today.
