body: ## Overview Adds a **Roof only** filter to the Pipeline tab (`/pipeline`) allowing users to view pipeline metrics filtered to roof-only jobs. ## Changes ### UI - Added **Roof Only** toggle button next to record type selector - Button shows active state with checkmark when enabled - Filter state displayed in page subtitle when active - Monthly Close Rate card title shows "(Roof)" suffix when filter active - Monthly Close Rate tooltip explains roof-scoped calculation ### API Changes #### `/api/pipeline` - Added `roofOnly` query parameter (accepts `1` or `true`) - Filters jobs by `cf_string_24 = '🏠 Y'` when enabled - Applied to all pipeline queries: - Current stages summary - Current statuses breakdown - Record type rollups - Timing analysis (status/stage transitions) - Status conversions - Forecast buckets - Top jobs list - Returns `roofOnlyFilter` boolean in response #### `/api/sales` - Extended to support `roofOnly` query parameter - Applied to job filters and invoice filters - Monthly Close Rate card on pipeline page now respects this filter - Returns `roofOnly` in filters response ### Monthly Close Rate Card Integration - Query key includes `roofOnly` for proper cache invalidation - Fetches `/api/sales?period=month&roofOnly=1` when roof filter is on - Fetches `/api/sales?period=month` when roof filter is off - Card title: "Monthly Close Rate" → "Monthly Close Rate (Roof)" when filtered - Job counts: "25/100" → "25/100 roof" when filtered - Tooltip updated to explain roof-scoped calculation ## Technical Details ### Field Mapping (EXACT values - emoji/spacing matters) - **Roof Install**: `cf_string_24 = '🏠 Y'` ← this PR - **Siding Install**: `cf_string_25 = '🧱 Y'` - **Gutter Install**: `cf_string_26 = '💧Y'` (no space) - **Window Install**: `cf_string_27 = '🪟 Y'` ### Filter Predicate ```sql -- Roof-only filter (exact match) j.cf_string_24 = '🏠 Y' ``` ### Data Quality Notes - Null values treated as unset (excluded from roof-only filter) - ~24% of active jobs have null Roof Install field - One known mis-tag exists (siding job marked as roof) - not special-cased - Filter uses exact match only; no fuzzy matching or record_type fallback ### Filter Logic - **Default**: All trades shown (current behavior unchanged) - **When enabled**: Only jobs with exact match `cf_string_24 = '🏠 Y'` included - Filter works independently of record type filter - Both filters can be active simultaneously - Null values explicitly excluded (not treated as "No") ## Behavior - Pipeline page: Roof Only button toggles filter state - Pipeline metrics: All stage counts, timing, conversions filtered to roof-only - Sales API: Respects same filter when `roofOnly` parameter passed - Monthly Close Rate: Filtered to roof jobs when Roof Only is on - Close rate calculation: When roof-only is on, both pipeline and sales metrics filtered consistently ## Testing - [x] Branch rebased onto latest main (includes PR #8 Monthly Close Rate card) - [x] Build passes with no errors - [ ] Pipeline loads with default (all trades) view - [ ] Roof Only button toggles filter state - [ ] Filtered metrics reflect only roof jobs (cf_string_24 = '🏠 Y') - [ ] Monthly Close Rate card shows "(Roof)" when filtered - [ ] Monthly Close Rate fetches with roofOnly parameter when filter on - [ ] Record type filter still works with roof filter - [ ] API returns correct `roofOnlyFilter` value - [ ] Null Roof Install values excluded from roof-only view ## Notes - Close rate definition unchanged (won jobs / total jobs in period) - No revenue fabrication; all metrics derived from filtered job set - Timing/conversion queries respect roof filter for consistency - Monthly Close Rate card now fully integrated with roof filter - Future multi-trade filters not implemented (sibling fields too sparse for prod)

author: yz4git
body:
Expands the SERA Hero Asset AI Pipeline from a handful of body measurements to a persistent 96-dimensional search space driven by the real four-view Reference objective.

Key changes:
- 96 normalized parameters: skeleton 20, face 20, hair 20, arms 12, legs 12, costume 12
- deterministic budgeted coordinate + block proposals instead of exhaustive 96D brute force
- per-view silhouette regression guard
- persistent best-state JSON and bounded objective cache
- V3 wrapper keeps V2 intact for rollback
- runner emits search state/cache/report while keeping T-pose measurements diagnostic-only
- legacy style/AI feedback remains only an auditable proposal and cannot bypass the Reference objective

The initial PR state starts at generation 0. GitHub Actions performs Blender search generations; best state can be written back into the PR branch between generations for continued optimization.

author: aleksdotbar
body:
Cherry-pick of #2828 (`cc10a6290`) onto `release-2026.07.1`. The descriptor bump is this branch's own, 2.1.0 → 2.1.1; main's 4.0.1 and its changelog note describe a change that is not on this branch.

**Why.** A repository the vendor answers 403 for — suspended, deleted, or denied to the token — aborted partition generation in every pull-request child stream. The fan-out parents walk repositories in ascending `updated_on` order, so every repository updated after the refused one was silently skipped while the stream logged its record count and the sync reported success.

**What changed.** The per-repository pull-request listing's error policy — 403/404 skip that repository, everything else unchanged — now lives in one `prs_listing_error_handler` anchor and applies to the standalone `pull_requests` stream and to all four fan-out copies inside the child streams, which carried no handler at all and fell through to the CDK default of failing the stream. The eleven inline workspace repository listings get the existing `*discovery_error_handler`, matching the top-level `repositories` stream they are copies of.

**Verified.** The connector mock suite cannot run on this branch: it pins `airbyte-cdk>=6.60.9,<6.61`, and the resolved CDK refuses a manifest declaring version `7.0.4`, which every nocode connector here does. That is a pre-existing condition on this branch, not introduced by this change. What was checked instead: the resulting `connector.yaml` is byte-identical to the verified one on #2828 apart from two pre-existing comment differences unrelated to error handling, no requester in the manifest is left without an error handler, the manifest parses to its 13 streams, and `scripts/ci/connector_wiring.py` is clean. The suite runs green on #2828 against the same edits.

body:
## Summary
Fifth slice of #163, and the first slice of `app/main/**` — by far the largest remaining part of this ticket (52 page files + 73 UI component files across the student/teacher/admin trees). Covers the student dashboard page and its widget cluster:

- `app/[locale]/main/student/dashboard/page.tsx` (the onboarding CTA banner)
- `DashboardHeader`, `NextUpCard`, `AcademicArcWidget`, `UpcomingClasses`, `StudentPayments`, `WeeklyQuestsWidget`, `ClaimQuestButton`

It becomes a client component (`"use client"` + `useTranslations`) since 2 of its 7 call sites render it from inside a client-component tree, where an async Server Component version wouldn't work.

Adds `app/utils/get-intl-locale.ts` and fixes several hardcoded `toLocaleDateString("en-US"/"en-GB", ...)` calls in this cluster to use the active locale — otherwise dates would've stayed English-formatted on an otherwise-translated page.

Tier names, badge names, and weekly-quest titles/descriptions are generated by business logic (`app/lib/gamification.ts`, `gamification-utils.ts`, `quests.ts`) or seeded in the DB — not sourced from message catalogs. author: tamnd
body:
The third of four pull requests for `M0-05`.
The first was `ctxdata` in #23, the second was the two handlers in #24, and the fourth is the file handler with rotation and `log.New(config.Log)`, which is the one that will carry the checklist trailer.

Three handlers that take a handler and give one back, so a policy is written once around whatever is doing the writing.

```go
h = log.NewMultiHandler(h, other)   // write every record to both
h = log.NewFilterHandler(h, keep)   // drop the ones keep says no to
h = log.NewSamplingHandler(h, o)    // drop the ones that repeat
```

## Fan out

```go
h := log.NewMultiHandler(
	log.NewConsoleHandler(os.Stderr, log.ConsoleOptions{}),
	log.NewJSONHandler(f, log.JSONOptions{Level: slog.LevelWarn}),
)
```

Each handler decides for itself whether it wants a record, so those two write different levels to different places.

A handler that fails does not stop the next one, and the error is every failure joined together, since a record that reached one of two places is neither a success nor a total loss.
Each handler gets its own record, because a handler is allowed to add attributes to the one it is given and the next one would then see them.
`TestMultiRecordIsolation` is that case.

With no handlers the answer is `slog.DiscardHandler` rather than something to check for nil, and with one handler it is that handler.

## Filter

Level is not what this is for, since every handler here takes a `Level` of its own.
This is for the records a level cannot describe.

```go
h := log.NewFilterHandler(h, func(ctx context.Context, r slog.Record) bool {
	path, _ := ctxdata.Get(ctx, RequestPath)
	return path != "/healthz"
})
```

`keep` sees the record as it was made, without the attributes the logger carries from `With`, since those belong to the handler rather than to the record.
What it does have is the context, which is where the interesting answers are.

## Sampling

A message in a loop can fill a disk or a bill.
The sampler writes the first `Initial` records of a message in each interval, then one in `Every`, and starts counting again when the interval is over.

```go
h := log.NewSamplingHandler(h, log.SampleOptions{})   // first 100 a second, then 1 in 100
```

The count is per level and message.
A message written once for each of a thousand users is one message that repeats, and the attributes are what tell those records apart.
Sampling that kept them all would not be sampling.

Errors are never dropped, which is the default rather than a rule, since `SampleOptions.Always` is a `slog.Leveler` and a program can move it.
A failure that happens ten thousand times is still ten thousand failures, and the one that gets dropped is the one somebody needed.

Counting is a hash into a fixed table of 256 padded counters and one atomic add, not a map behind a lock on the path every record takes.
That costs 16 KiB and it means two messages can land on the same counter and share a budget, which happens to a handful of pairs out of thousands.
The clock is monotonic and starts at zero, so a counter nothing has touched is in an interval that ended long ago, and the wall clock moving does not stop the sampler for an hour.

## One fix in the console handler

A record with no attributes was written with the message padded to the alignment column, which is twenty spaces of trailing whitespace on a line with nothing to line up with.
The padding is now taken back when nothing follows it.
`TestConsoleNothingToLineUpWith` holds it.

## Cost

Apple M4, load average 6, `-benchmem`.

```
BenchmarkMulti/one-10                    340.6 ns/op   0 B/op   0 allocs/op
BenchmarkMulti/two-10                    786.4 ns/op   0 B/op   0 allocs/op
BenchmarkFilter-10                       397.2 ns/op   0 B/op   0 allocs/op
BenchmarkSampling/written-10             424.3 ns/op   0 B/op   0 allocs/op
BenchmarkSampling/dropped-10             172.7 ns/op   0 B/op   0 allocs/op
BenchmarkSampling/dropped-parallel-10     58.79 ns/op  0 B/op   0 allocs/op
```

`Multi/one` and `Multi/two` are the same record written to one JSON handler and to two, so the difference is the second write rather than the fan out.

The dropped rows are the path that runs when a program is in the state sampling is for: the record is built by `log/slog`, counted, and thrown away, and none of it allocates.
The parallel row is eight goroutines on the same handler, and it gets faster rather than slower, which is what the sharded counters are for.

## Testing

100% statement coverage, `go test -race` clean, and three more runnable examples.
`TestSamplingConcurrent` sends 800 records from 8 goroutines at a budget of 10 and checks that exactly 10 come out.

author: besselking
body:
Both High findings from the review, plus the rest of the connection lifecycle.

## The headline: the outbound queue's own deadlock

The doc comment on `_outbound` is precise about what the writer is for — answering a signal straight to the socket means "while the write is in flight we are not reading… a deadlock broken only by the tick timeout."

It holds for 4,096 frames. The channel is `BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait`, and `HandleMonitor`, `HandleLink`, `HandleUnlinkId` and `HandleExit` were all awaited **inline on the read loop**. `HandleSpawnRequest` was the one of five kept off it, with the comment explaining why.

Worse, `TickLoopAsync` queued its keepalive through the same call, so the watchdog meant to catch a wedged connection blocked in the same place — and never reached its next receive-deadline check. Nothing closed. Nothing logged.

**No hostile peer is required.** Any consumer whose TCP receive window closes does this.

### The fix

Signals produced while handling an inbound frame go through a new `TrySendSignal`, which never waits — a full queue means the peer has ignored 4,096 frames of ours, so the *connection* goes rather than the read loop. `SendAsync` still waits, because for a caller of ours that is just backpressure. Ordering is preserved: it is still one channel, still FIFO.

I chose this over offloading the handlers to `Task.Run`. Offloading would keep the connection but lose the ordering the channel's own comment relies on, and unbounded task spawning just relocates the unboundedness.

### Reproduced

`OutboundBackpressureTests` floods UNLINK_ID from a peer that never reads the acks. Against the old code:

```
BeamSharp.Tests.OutboundBackpressureTests
  .A_peer_that_never_reads_our_acks_does_not_wedge_the_read_loop [FAIL]
  Error Message:
   the connection stayed open with a peer that had stopped reading
```

## The other High: the accept loop ended for good on any error

`return` on a non-cancellation exception ends the listener for the life of the process, while the node stays registered with EPMD — a port nothing answers on, `ConnectedNodes` still listing earlier peers, every `Node.ping` timing out, and one line to a log callback that defaults to discarding.

Worth noting the review's stated trigger is wrong: a peer resetting between SYN and accept does *not* throw from `AcceptTcpClientAsync` on .NET; that socket is returned and fails on first read. The real triggers are descriptor exhaustion and listener-level errors. Fixed regardless — the blast radius is the whole node. Transient errors now retry behind a short backoff so a permanent one cannot spin.

## Also in this branch

- **Attach race** — check-then-assign on a `ConcurrentDictionary` let two inbound handshakes from one peer both pass, the loser's loops running forever against a socket nobody holds. Now `TryAdd`, evicting only a dead entry and only that exact one.
- **Handshake admission control** — `MaxConcurrentHandshakes` (default 64), refusing rather than queueing. Each attempt runs an asymmetric-crypto operation under TLS before the peer has proved anything.
- `DisposeAsync` never disposed `_stream`, leaking the `SslStream` on every TLS teardown.
- Tick timestamps read with `Volatile.Read`, written plainly — made consistent.
- `HandleExit` allocated a sentinel `ErlPid` for a removal that could never match.

## Verification

- 208 unit tests pass; new tests confirmed to fail against `main` first.
- **OTP 29 interop: 34/34 inbound, 11/11 outbound**, including the paths this touches — a crashing GenServer surfacing as an exit, and `noproc` for an unregistered name.
- **TLS suite passes**, including the plaintext-refusal check, negotiating `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`.
- Clean under `-warnaserror`.

Depends on nothing, but touches `ErlangNode.cs` alongside #10 — different regions, should merge cleanly either order.

author: tong-io
body:
Follow-up to #181. The plugin now loads a Diffusers-native SVDQuant int4 repack with the 4-step Lightning LoRA fused, so the READMEs' "2511" is wrong.

| | before | after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Download | 57.7 GB | **18 GB** |
| Peak VRAM | ~58 GB | **21 GiB** (upstream benchmark) |
| GPU | H100 | **L40S** |
| Steps | 40 | **4** |

Latency upstream measures at 12.6 s for a 1248×832 edit.

**Why 2509**: no 2511 checkpoint is packaged for the `nunchaku_lite` loader. Every nunchaku 2511 repo on the Hub is a ComfyUI single file, and those carry `weight_scale` companion tensors that Diffusers has no handling for — verified against v0.40.0's `single_file_utils.py` and `model_loading_utils.py`.

**Why L40S**: not a preference. The Diffusers Nunchaku quantizer raises on Hopper outright —

```python
if device_capability[0] == 9:
    raise ValueError("Loading Nunchaku checkpoints is not supported on Hopper NVIDIA GPUs.")
```

— so an H100 is unavailable to this checkpoint. Ada clears its Turing-or-newer floor for int4.

No code changes here; the implementation lives in the plugin repo.

author: sweepcoon
body:
## Summary

Fixes the clean Windows/Python 3.12 installation failures found during public-release validation and makes the one-click setup more reproducible for non-technical users.

## Changes

- Pins the supported wheel-backed KFA tokenizer stack to `khmercut==0.0.2`, `python-crfsuite==0.9.9`, and `tqdm==4.65.0`.
- Avoids PyPI's `khmercut` 0.1.0 source build, which failed on the clean Windows test while its legacy setup step decoded UTF-8 metadata through the Windows code page.
- Keeps `khmercut` 0.0.2's exact transitive requirements aligned so pip does not hit the `tqdm>=4.66` vs `tqdm==4.65.0` resolver conflict discovered on the first repair rerun.
- Uses the Python 3.12 Windows wheel for `sosap==0.4.3`. KFA 0.2.0's published wheel metadata still declares legacy `sosap==0.0.1`, so dependency validation allows only that exact metadata mismatch while still failing every other `pip check` error and functionally verifying KFA/sosap import plus model preload.
- Forces Python UTF-8 mode and prefers binary packages during local-timing setup.
- Verifies the expected tokenizer package versions before declaring the local timing environment healthy.
- Uses `npm ci` in the Windows setup so public installs use the reviewed lockfile dependency graph.
- Removes stale hard-coded v0.7.10 setup/launcher labels and points incomplete-install recovery back to `INSTALL-NEW-PC.bat`.
- Improves first-run installer messaging without changing caption/editor behavior.
- Updates release invariants, checklist, and changelog.

## Validation

The original Windows/Python 3.12 failure was reproduced: `khmercut` 0.1.0 attempted a source build and failed with a Windows code-page `UnicodeDecodeError`.

The first repair rerun selected the `khmercut==0.0.2` universal wheel and Python 3.12 `python-crfsuite==0.9.9` Windows wheel, then exposed the `tqdm` resolver conflict; the branch now aligns those exact constraints.

The next rerun installed the full KFA/tokenizer stack and KFA 0.2.0, then exposed KFA's stale `sosap==0.0.1` metadata. The branch accepts only that exact metadata mismatch and functionally verifies KFA/sosap import and model preload.

On the same Windows/Python 3.12 machine that reproduced the failures:

- `setup-local-timing-windows.bat` repaired the interrupted environment and now reports `KFA: READY` and `Whisper fallback: READY`.
- A subsequent timing-setup run recognized the environment as already ready without reinstalling packages.
- `setup-windows.bat` completed successfully using `npm ci`, built the shared package, verified server/web TypeScript, and re-confirmed KFA + Whisper readiness.
- `npm run check:public` passed (116 tracked files; current tree + Git history scanned).
- `npm run typecheck` passed with protected brand verification.
- `npm run build` passed; Vite transformed 1688 modules and completed the production build.
- `git status --short` was clean.

Independent diff review found only installer/dependency/documentation changes; no approved brand assets or caption/editor/timing algorithm code changed. No unresolved PR review threads remain.

GitHub-hosted Actions may remain unavailable while hosted-runner usage is exhausted; no CI-pass claim is made.

A separate truly clean `INSTALL-NEW-PC.bat` test still remains a public-release gate before announcing the release.

No caption transcription logic, Khmer text handling, timing algorithms, Review behavior, locks, correction memory, history, regeneration, project data, branding, or SRT export behavior changes.

## Summary

- prepare the Electron binary during root postinstall and before dev/start commands
- use Electron's documented China mirror by default while allowing `ELECTRON_MIRROR` overrides
- emit download heartbeats and fail with a clear timeout instead of hanging indefinitely

## Description
`Dockerfile.konflux` used an explicit whitelist `COPY` (`cmd/main.go`, `api/`, `internal/`) and never copied `pkg/`. Since #863 (SecureServing / TLS profile watcher / cert provisioning) `cmd/main.go` imports `pkg/tls`, so the konflux `strictfipsruntime` build failed:

cmd/main.go:49:2: no required module provides package github.com/opendatahub-io/odh-model-controller/pkg/tls

The ODH `Containerfile` already has `COPY pkg/ pkg/`; the downstream konflux build file had drifted. This adds the missing line.

author: xuepoo
body:
## Summary

- With `traceEvents` enabled, **every** document `pointermove` ran `resolveContext`; for canvas-targeted moves that called `pickInScene` — a full O(n) reverse tree walk — at input-event rate (120–240 Hz). Each accepted entry also rewrote trace rows and marked the panel scene dirty, so the panel repainted per mousemove even with the Events tab inactive (#707).
- The guard sits **before** `resolveContext` (the point of avoiding the pick), leading-edge on the event's own monotonic `timeStamp` — no timers, no bookkeeping, deterministic across listeners.
- Discrete semantic events (`pointerdown`/`pointerup`/`pointercancel`, `wheel`, keys) are never coalesced. Exported `POINTERMOVE_COALESCE_MS = 16`.

Fixes #707

## Validation

- New fail-first test: five synthetic moves inside one window → exactly one entry (fails pre-fix: five entries); next move after the window elapses traces again; keydown unthrottled.
- No headless performance numbers quoted anywhere (per review policy); the fix targets cost asymmetry, not measured gains.
- `just test-pkg devtools` → 352/352 ✅ · oxlint --deny-warnings ✅ · oxfmt ✅

## Summary

- add a typed `deployContract` flow for Polygon mainnet (137) and Polygon Amoy (80002)
- preserve chat context for generate, review, explicit confirmation, and deployment follow-ups
- document the mainnet and Amoy flows in the package and SDK docs app
- repair package publishing with explicit exports, a prepack build, and working Changesets commands
- add Bun tests plus CI build, test, and package-content checks

## Why packaging is included

The live `w3gpt@0.1.1` tarball contains only `README.md` and `package.json`; its referenced `dist` entrypoints are absent. The new prepack build prevents a repeat and the verified artifact contains CJS, ESM, and declaration files.

## Verification

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile`
- `bun run check`
- `bun run tsc`
- `bun run test` (4 passing)
- `bun run build` (SDK plus both Next.js apps)
- `npm pack --dry-run --json` (6 expected package files)
- clean temporary consumer imported the packed artifact through both CommonJS and ESM

## Live smoke

The local SDK reached production `/api/skill`, received the required Polygon Amoy confirmation prompt, continued on the same `chatId`, and invoked the deployment tool. The transaction was not broadcast because the production Amoy RPC returned `Monthly capacity limit exceeded` at `eth_getTransactionCount`. This is an external production RPC dependency, not an SDK routing failure. No redundant paid mainnet transaction was sent.

## Release follow-up

After merge, Changesets should open the 0.1.2 version PR. Merge that PR with a valid `NPM_TOKEN` available to Actions to publish the repaired artifact. Repository visibility is currently private and must be changed separately before claiming a public GitHub SDK deliverable.

body:
Bảng hành động trước đây chỉ bật `Visibility`: một khung hình chưa có, khung hình sau đã có đủ bốn ô. Đúng cái cảm giác "cứng" — không có gì nói cho mắt biết nó **đến từ đâu**.

## Bảng nở lên từ chính cái nút

Phóng từ 90% chiều cao lên 100%, mờ dần hiện vào, 170ms. Tâm phóng đặt ở **cạnh dưới** (`RenderTransformOrigin="0.5,1"`), nên nó nở lên ra khỏi đúng cái nút vừa biến mất, chứ không phình ra từ giữa mình về phía một cái nút không còn ở đó.

## Bốn ô vào lần lượt

Mỗi ô mờ dần hiện lên và nhích lên 12px, cách nhau 40ms.

Chính độ lệch này làm bốn hình chữ nhật đọc ra thành **một thứ đang mở ra**, thay vì bốn hình chữ nhật đang tồn tại. Đó là phần "mượt" mà bạn đang thiếu.

**Hàng dưới vào trước.** Lúc bảng mở, con trỏ đang ở đáy thẻ (vừa rê tới nút Hành động) — nên nửa gần tay bạn nhất đến đầu tiên.

## Đóng nhanh hơn mở

110ms, và chỉ `Collapsed` **sau khi** chuyển động chạy xong — một phần tử đã `Collapsed` thì không animate được nữa, ẩn trước thì coi như không có animation.

Hai đường **cố ý bỏ qua** chuyển động:
- Khi cả tấm thẻ đang ẩn đi — một bảng mờ dần trên cửa sổ đã đi rồi sẽ bị bỏ lại ở trạng thái trong suốt nhưng vẫn `Visible` cho lần mở sau
- Khi câu hỏi xoá thay chỗ bảng — hiệu ứng mờ bên dưới nó chỉ là tiếng ồn

## Trạng thái mở đọc từ field, không từ `Visibility`

Chuyển động đóng cần bảng **vẫn hiện** trong lúc nó chạy. Nên trong khoảng trăm mili-giây đó, `Visibility` vẫn trả lời "đang mở" — mà câu trả lời đó sẽ nuốt mất một lệnh mở lại, và để một bảng đang đóng tiếp tục giành con trỏ trong `OnPreviewDragOver`.

Cùng loại bẫy với `_closing` của chính tấm thẻ, đã gặp khi làm animation mở/đóng thẻ ở v0.2.1.

## Đã kiểm tra

- 72 test pass (48 Core + 24 Data)
- `SourceCheck`: 65 tệp, không vấn đề
- XAML: parse được, `x:Name` và `StaticResource` đều khớp

Ghi chú phát hành ở `docs/release-notes/v0.2.11.md`.

author: praneeth132006
body:
This is the "it says **All changes saved** but my note is not on GitHub" bug. It
was doing exactly what it looked like.

## What was happening

After five failed pushes the sync engine deleted the change from the queue
**and from IndexedDB**:

```ts
if (change.attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
  this.queue = this.queue.filter((c) => c.id !== change.id);
  await this.db.deleteQueueItem(change.id);
}
```

Nothing recorded it, nothing surfaced it, and nothing would ever retry it — the
only thing that knew the note had unsaved work was the thing that had just been
deleted. The queue then went empty, `restingStatus()` returned `idle`, and the
status bar said "All changes saved" above a note whose text had never left the
device. The note stayed marked `dirty` forever with nothing left to push it.

A test asserted this as correct behaviour, under the name *"gives up on a change
that keeps failing rather than blocking the queue forever"*. It did stop
blocking the queue — by discarding somebody's writing. That test is rewritten.

## What it does now

**Nothing is discarded.** A change that runs out of attempts is *parked*: kept
in the queue and in storage, with the reason it stopped, excluded from automatic
retries so it does not hold up everything behind it, and counted separately as
`blockedCount`.

**The status cannot claim otherwise.** `restingStatus()` returns `blocked`,
which outranks `pending` — a parked change is not waiting its turn, it has
stopped. The failure path reports `blocked` too once nothing retryable is left,
because "error" implies something will try again on its own. The status bar
reads "N changes not on GitHub — click to retry".

**Retry means retry.** That click and Sync Now both un-park everything and reset
its attempts, since being asked is precisely what a parked change is waiting
for. Previously "click to retry" would have skipped the changes that most needed
retrying.

**The damage already done is repaired.** Fixing the discard does nothing for
notes already stranded on somebody's device — which are the ones with writing in
them. `recoverStrandedEdits` re-queues every dirty note with no queue entry, and
runs on every workspace load. A note genuinely in sync is not dirty, and one
already queued is skipped, so it is safe to run always.

## Also verified

Folder creation, checked in the browser rather than assumed: `SOC 101/Phishing
analysis` created in one go produces both levels, and a note created inside is
stored at the full nested path — read out of IndexedDB, not off the tree UI,
because the stored path is what actually reaches GitHub.

## Checks

647 tests pass (7 new here, all on this bug), typecheck and lint clean across
all nine packages.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: athompson83
body:
The last of the surfaces that went on counting the whole scene array after detail scenes arrived. Each treats an aside — reachable only by clicking a hotspot, and possibly never opened — as a beat of the talk.

## Analysis

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` says the score is only the weighted mean of its checks, and that every check states what it measured. What it measured included asides:

- the running time summed stretches nobody has to watch, in a module whose own header explains that durations are estimated *because* reporting a wrong length is worse than saying nothing;
- "X of N scenes have speaker notes" marked an author down for notes on a stretch of talk that is not part of the running order;
- worst of the three, the movement grouping. A detail scene carrying a different (or null) `sectionId` between two scenes of one movement **split that movement in two**, which then fed the balance check and the structure check. `movementsOf` in the rail already handles exactly this and documents why; the analysis code did not.

Checks about a scene *in isolation* still look at every scene — a wall of text is one however it is reached, and an undescribed image is undescribed whether the audience arrives by advancing or by clicking. That distinction is now stated where the filter is, rather than left implicit.

## The narrative map

`deriveMap` gave every scene a moment. `inferRole` reads "open" and "close" from array position, so **an aside stored last was labelled the close of the argument** — and since `captivate_replace_moments` writes the map whole, those phantom beats became permanent the first time the author edited it.

## The console filmstrip

It listed asides as jump targets while the scene jumper on the same console filtered them out, with a comment explaining that listing them offers the presenter a destination with no way back into the argument. Two controls, same concern, opposite answers. Both now agree, and both number by the running order.

## Verification

`npm run verify` (typecheck, lint clean, 659 unit tests, build), the RLS suite against real Postgres, and 6 shader + 13 lifecycle Playwright tests.

Three new tests, each confirmed failing before the change:

| test | what breaks it |
| --- | --- |
| *measures the argument, not the asides hanging off it* | removing the filter from `pacingOf`/`analyse` |
| *still judges an aside's own readability* | over-filtering — scoping the rendering checks too |
| *does not turn an aside into a beat of the argument* | removing the filter from `deriveMap` |

The first asserts that a deck with an aside reports the same total seconds, the same movement list, and the same notes detail as the same deck without it — including the case where the aside carries a section id of its own.

author: aguinelo
body:
First of the design changes from the redesign recommendation, and deliberately first because it is the one that costs **no columns**.

## What was wrong

A question was a `>` in the same weight as the prose around it. On the real session, mid-scrollback, there was no way to see where one exchange ended and the next began.

```
  Quando aparecer código/configuração/docs no
  workspace, eu reviso — não sobrescrevo às cegas.
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  ❯ queremos criar um crawler de ler preço com
    https://crawlee.dev/ em python e uv ou virtualenv

  Show, antes de sair escrevendo código quero
```

The sidebar, the panel and the status bar all compete with the text for width. A rule costs one row per turn and gives back the structure that was missing. It is also the [named community complaint against the reference TUI in this category](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/52518): clear visual separation between the person's turn and the model's.

## A rule, not a colour

A question picked out by colour alone is not picked out at all on a monochrome terminal, and this is the landmark the eye scrolls to. It has an ASCII form, like every glyph in this family.

## Inset, not edge to edge

The first version drew from edge to edge. It touched both column dividers and read as a **row of a table** rather than as a seam between two turns. Insetting it to the same two-column gutter the rest of the stream uses fixed it — seen by rendering the real log, not deduced from the code. Same method that found the four defects before it.

## The gap comes before, never after

The rule calls `gapBefore`, and the turn sets `blocked` so the answer gets its own gap on the next pass — the convention the stream already had, because a blank at the end costs a row of the window it is anchored to. The first turn gets no gap above it: a stream that opens on a blank row spends one of the few rows it has on nothing.

The test asserts both of those did not regress, in Unicode and in ASCII.

## Verification

`make check` green: coverage 94.5%, gate at 90%.

body:
## Deeper moves, still well under 1 s

Cloud analysis is now **two-tier** (both free, keyless):

1. **lichess cloud-eval** — crowd-computed Stockfish analyses of known positions: **depth 30–75 in ~100–300 ms** (verified: d32 @300 ms, d53 @93 ms). Covers openings and the vast majority of real-game positions.
2. **chess-api.com** — live multi-threaded Stockfish for uncached positions: **depth ~15 in ~500 ms** (verified fallback works).
3. **Local WASM engine** — unchanged automatic fallback (~900 ms).

Lichess scores are White-relative while chess-api's are side-to-move-relative — both are now normalised correctly per side (verified with black-to-move positions).

## The "idle after 4–5 moves, refresh to fix" bug — two causes, both fixed

1. **Restarts reused the wedged worker.** The 15 s watchdog restarted by *reconnecting*, but the background page handed the fresh connection the **same possibly-wedged worker** (`ensureWorker` returns early if a worker exists). Now the background page **terminates and drops the worker** when the last port disconnects, so every restart boots a genuinely fresh engine.
2. **Missed analysis triggers were never retried.** If the board observer hiccupped (SPA quirk, animation, suspended background), nothing re-kicked analysis. The 2.5 s heartbeat now **re-analyses whenever it's the player's move, the engine is ready, and nothing is pending** — idle is structurally impossible. Game-over positions (`bestmove (none)`) are remembered so it doesn't spin.

Also: stale cloud answers for previous positions are now discarded by FEN match, so a slow reply can never paint the wrong move.

## Verified
- Live: lichess d32 @300 ms (white) / d53 @93 ms (black) · uncached → chess-api d15 @542 ms · signs correct for both sides
- Local worker harness (`npm test`): `uciok` → `readyok` → `bestmove g1f3` ✅
- XPI 5.5 MB, v4.3.0, `web-ext lint` 0/0/0

author: playmaker410
body:
Closes spoo-vault/spoovault#130

> Implements the OPAQUE PIN-verification requirements assigned to @playmaker410 in issue #130.

## Summary

- replace the browser-only PBKDF2/HMAC PIN verifier with a real two-party RFC 9807 OPAQUE exchange
- store only the authenticated private-key ciphertext and IV in IndexedDB; the OPAQUE registration record and server setup remain server-side
- pin the OPAQUE server static public key and wait for server KE3 verification before unwrapping or caching private-key material
- add a deployable Node OPAQUE verification server with durable registration storage, short-lived login state, management authorization, exact-origin CORS, and online rate limiting
- preserve passkey unlock and migrate successfully verified legacy PBKDF2/local-ZKPP records to OPAQUE
- require OPAQUE PIN enrollment during compromise-key rotation before any irreversible revocation

## Security properties

An IndexedDB-only dump contains no PIN hash, salt, KDF parameters, OPRF key, OPAQUE registration record, export key, or server setup. It therefore cannot be used as a local PIN-guessing oracle. The client also fails closed when the server is unavailable, its pinned identity differs, the PIN is incorrect, or the server rejects the final client proof.

This uses @serenity-kit/opaque 1.1.0, its RFC 9807 browser-compatible WebAssembly implementation, rather than custom protocol arithmetic. The included server is a real independent OPAQUE party; it is not simulated inside the browser.

## Deployment

The frontend requires VITE_OPAQUE_SERVER_URL and VITE_OPAQUE_SERVER_PUBLIC_KEY. The server requires a long-lived OPAQUE_SERVER_SETUP secret. Setup, storage, TLS, and multi-instance guidance is documented in docs/OPAQUE_KEYRING.md.

## Verification

- npm run build
- TypeScript no-emit check
- Node syntax checks for both server modules
- 260/260 test suites passed
- 775/775 tests passed, including full registration/login, wrong-PIN and rejected-KE3 failure, pinned-server identity, offline IndexedDB dump resistance, ciphertext binding, migration, passkey, session-lock, and key-rotation coverage

author: darccio
body:
## Summary
- `TestConcurrentAddNeverResurrectsDowngradedPayload` checked `w.payload.protocol()` right after the downgrade was confirmed applied, but nothing forces an `add()`/`flush()` call to happen *after* the downgrade lands — only those calls re-check the protocol
- If all the test's concurrent `add()` calls (in-memory, fast) finished before `refreshAgentFeatures`'s `/info` HTTP round-trip completed, `h.payload` legitimately still held the last-observed protocol, and the assertion flaked (seen in CI: expected `0.4`, got `1`) — not a production bug, just a test racing its own setup
- Fix: force one more `add()` once the downgrade is confirmed applied, so the assertion observes the writer's real settling behavior instead of racing the poll's network I/O

Investigated from a `release-v2.10.x` CI failure: https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go/actions/runs/32144929774/job/95736348552

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced the flake deterministically pre-fix by shrinking the test's goroutine/iteration counts so the add-loop reliably finishes before the downgrade's HTTP round-trip (30/30 failures)
- [x] Same reduced-scale repro passes 50/50 after the fix
- [x] `go test -race -run TestConcurrentAddNeverResurrectsDowngradedPayload -count=10 ./ddtrace/tracer` passes at full scale

author: kevinmurata-netizen
body:
## What

Clicking the **Active** / **Inactive** badge now flips it, with a tooltip saying what the change does. Applied on:

- **Settings → Deterioration Models** (the editor cards)
- **Settings → Configuration** (inspection templates)
- **Deterioration Models** (the Configured Models table)

Read-only roles get the same badge without the button affordance, rather than a control that would fail on click.

## Why the checkboxes had to go

Both editors already had an "Active" checkbox inside their save form. Leaving it alongside a clickable badge would mean **two sources of truth**: toggle the badge, then save the form, and the stale checkbox value silently overwrites the toggle.

So the checkboxes are removed and `isActive` is now optional on `updateDeteriorationModel` / `updateInspectionTemplate` — a form save leaves the flag alone, and the badge owns it.

The badge calls the server action directly rather than submitting a form, because it sits *inside* those editors' forms and a nested `<form>` is invalid HTML — the inner one gets dropped and the click submits the outer form instead.

## Verification

Deactivating a deterioration model already excluded it from simulations (`getMaterialCurves` only reads active models); this just makes it reachable in one click. Verified end to end:

```
ACTIVE     curve for Cast Iron: 65yr shape 1.2 | sim assets use serviceLife 65
deactivated ->
INACTIVE   curve for Cast Iron: ABSENT -> default | sim assets use serviceLife 75
reactivated ->
ACTIVE     curve for Cast Iron: 65yr shape 1.2 | sim assets use serviceLife 65
```

Also exercised in the browser: 8 toggles present, 0 leftover checkboxes, clicking one wrote `isActive=false` to the database and the badge re-rendered as **Inactive** with the tooltip inverted. Clicking again restored it — all 8 models verified back to active.

Typecheck, lint and production build pass.

author: eissasoubhi
body:
## Purpose

Add Manual Oracle Batch 25 using `FinesseStudioLab/modeltrace-contract` issue #74 / PR #83.

## Why this case matters

The Rust/Soroban security PR has four explicit acceptance criteria. Independent inspection finds three factually satisfied by documentation, code, focused negative auth tests and exact-head green CI, while the fourth — independent peer review with the review recorded — is observably unsatisfied before merge: the PR has no submitted reviews or conversation comments, and its own description says that row was intentionally left for someone else to add.

This is a useful counterexample to `merged/closed == done`: the PR merged and the issue closed even though an original mandatory human-review criterion was not satisfied.

## Safety

- No verifier gates weakened.
- No checked-box or merge-status proof heuristic added.
- Workflow only asserts exact requirement extraction and that the case cannot become globally PROVEN while the review evidence is absent.
- Documentation classifies a future deterministic GitHub review/lifecycle adapter as the appropriate next step.

No release or npm publication changes.

## Summary

- Remove static Open Graph, Twitter, and favicon tags that duplicated or overrode Starlight's page-specific head metadata.
- Let the custom 404 content own the `/404` route through Starlight's `disable404Route` option.
- Avoid shipping the Umami event-tracking bundle when analytics is disabled.

- Replace the bespoke `Accept` parser with the mature `negotiator` package.

- Kept `starlight-auto-sidebar`: it remains intentionally installed for future `_meta.yml` sidebar metadata. No fake metadata files were added just to silence its empty-collection warning.

body:
`Branch Coverage (workspace)` is red on every PR. This unblocks it.

## What broke

`rustc 1.100.0-nightly (c656540d6 2026-08-21)` made an inference site in **`zenoh 1.9.0`** ambiguous:

```
error[E0282]: type annotations needed
  --> zenoh-1.9.0/src/api/session.rs:1454:13
     |  Ok(session)   -- cannot infer type parameter `E`
```

A third-party crate stopped compiling and took the whole workspace instrumentation with it. Only this lane is affected — every other lane runs on the `rust-toolchain.toml` pin (1.94.1). This one needs nightly for `-Z coverage-options`.

## Why a pin and not a wait

Checked, not assumed:

| Hypothesis | Result |
|---|---|
| transient bad nightly | **no** — reproduces on two successive nightlies, `c656540d6 2026-08-21` and `c54751567 2026-08-22` |
| caused by a PR | **no** — reproduces on base `28abc694` with no changes present |
| fixed by a newer zenoh | **no** — bumped the lockfile to `zenoh 1.10.0`, within the existing `version = "1"` range, same error |

Recovery needs an upstream change that does not exist yet — either a zenoh release that annotates the site, or a rustc change restoring the inference. Meanwhile the lane was red for every PR.

`nightly-2026-08-20` is the last nightly verified to compile the workspace:

```
$ cargo +nightly-2026-08-20 check -p kirra-fleet-transport
    Finished `dev` profile
```

## Both spellings, deliberately

`RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` and the action's `toolchain:` input are pinned to the same toolchain. `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` outranks the action's own selection — that is why it is set in the first place, per the comment already there — so pinning only one would silently install one nightly and run another. The lane comment now says so.

## Unpinning is tracked, not left to notice

**#1481.** A pin with no removal trigger becomes permanent by default, and this lane exists to track the instrumentation rustc actually offers. A pin left in place indefinitely is a lane measuring a compiler nobody ships — a slower version of the problem it was added to solve.

## Scope

One lane's toolchain selection. No dependency, source, or test changes. The `Checker decision coverage (EP-07)` lane also uses nightly and is **not** touched: it is scoped to the checker crates, does not build zenoh, and is green.

The website citation line numbers moved because the added comment is 25 lines — the cited evidence itself did not move. Repointed mechanically with `check_website_citations.py --fix` and the site regenerated, which is what that gate asks for.

## Verification

- `check_workflow_pr_coverage`, `check_website_citations`, `check_quality_guardrails` — pass
- `ci.yml` parses as YAML
- The action SHA pin is unchanged, so the M-6 action-pinning gate is unaffected

author: alexisjanin
body:
Fixes #79.

## Why

`select = ["ALL"]` with an unpinned ruff gave Astral's release cadence a vote on whether our branches are green. 0.16 added `CPY001` and began formatting Python blocks inside Markdown, and #64 went red for six weeks as a result.

Worse, the red carried **no signal**: lint and tests shared one job, so the failing format step ended the job before `pytest` ran, and `fail-fast` cancelled the sibling. Note that dropping `fail-fast` alone would *not* have fixed this — both matrix jobs run the same format check and would have failed at the same step.

## What changed

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Version | Cap ruff to `>=0.16.2,<0.17` in the `dev` extra. Formatter and rule changes now arrive on a bump PR opened deliberately, not on whichever PR happens to be open. A venv on 0.15.x now fails the constraint and self-corrects on `pip install -e .[dev]`. |
| Rule surface | `select = ["ALL"]` **stays** — with the cap, it's a subscription to work at bump time rather than to surprise. |
| CI shape | Split into `lint` (once — ruff's verdict is interpreter-independent, `target-version` fixes the syntax target) and `test` (3.11/3.13 matrix, pytest only). Lint can no longer gate tests, and ruff runs once instead of twice. |
| Diagnostics | `ruff --version` echoed in every run, so a version mismatch is visible in the log's first lines instead of costing an investigation. |
| Scope | Checked scope widened from `src/` to `.` — clean today, and it starts enforcing the `scripts/*` rules `ruff.toml` already configures. Tests stay excluded. |
| Cleanup | Dropped per-file-ignores for paths that no longer exist (`example/*` has zero `.py` files; `API/app.ipynb` is gone) and the spent `PT011` entry (0 hits). |
| Policy | Recorded in `pyproject.toml` (why the cap exists) and `CONTRIBUTING.md` (how to raise it). |

Bumps stay **manual and one minor at a time** — deliberately no Dependabot: trailing a linter release is harmless, while a bot opening dependency PRs is its own maintenance surface.

## How to test

This PR is its own test — the rewritten workflow runs on it, and you should see three independent checks (`Lint`, `Test Python 3.11`, `Test Python 3.13`) rather than one job whose failure hides the others. The `Ruff version` step reports which 0.16.x the cap resolved to.

Locally, from the project venv:

```bash
pip install -U -e .[dev]
ruff --version              # expect 0.16.x
ruff format --check .       # clean
ruff check .                # clean
pytest
```

To see the masking fix directly: introduce a formatting error, and confirm the test jobs still run and report.

## Not in scope

- `ruff check tests/` reports 390 errors (tests are excluded from linting via `ruff.toml`).
- The workflow only triggers on pushes and PRs targeting `main`, so PRs into `dev` get no CI at all.

author: benzoogataga
body:
#131 made the tray a passive signal: the icon recolors and the tooltip updates, but nothing pops up, so I only learn a colleague needs me if I happen to look at the tray. This adds a real OS notification that fires when the needs-you count rises, so a review or a permission approval reaches me with the window closed.

## What changed

- **Same count as the badge, reused not duplicated.** The trigger is the count already built for the tray in #131: tasks in needs-you plus pending permission approvals (`trayCounts`). The fire decision is a small pure function, `needsYouSignal`, that reuses the board-header phrasing (`waitingSummary`).
- **Fires only on a rise.** Nothing to something, or something to more, pops a notification. A drop pops nothing (the tray badge already reflects that passively), and an unchanged re-render pops nothing, so a poll that finds the same count does not spam. A new total closes the previous notification and shows the new one, so notifications never stack.
- **Count only.** The body is the board-header phrasing, for example "2 waiting for review, 1 paused for approval". No colleague name, no message text, no task description ever reaches an OS surface, the same privacy rule as the tray tooltip.
- **Click opens the board.** Clicking the notification opens straight to the Tasks board, the same place a tray click lands when something is waiting (over the `shell:navigate` channel from #131).
- **Launch is quiet.** The startup seed does not notify, so opening the app does not pop for work that was already waiting from a prior session; only a rise during the session notifies.
- **DND is the OS's job.** A normal Notification respects Do Not Disturb and focus modes, and Stafford does not try to force through them.

## Verification

- Real Electron run driving a count sequence `[0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 2]`: `Notification.isSupported()` is true; it fired at 1 ("1 waiting for review"), 2 ("2 waiting for review"), and 3 ("2 waiting for review, 1 paused for approval"), and stayed silent on the repeated 1 and on the drop to 2. Three notifications for the three rises, each with a click handler wired to open the board, each closing the prior so they do not stack.
- Unit tests for `needsYouSignal`: fires only on a rise, is silent on a drop or an unchanged count, the content is the count-only board phrasing, and a full session sequence fires once per rise and never on a repeat or drop.
- Full suite green (732 pass), typecheck clean.

## Open question

The visible OS toast itself, and a real click on it, need a live desktop session, which the headless environment cannot capture (same limit as the tray icon in #131). The firing logic, the API support, the click-handler wiring, and the no-spam behavior are all verified above; the click-to-board routing itself was proven end to end in #131. Worth an eyeball on a real desktop to confirm the toast renders and the click lands.

author: antman1526
body:
Adds a **fourth knowledge store** alongside memory (facts about the user), skills (procedures), and documents (the user's own files). None of those was the right home for a third-party catalog: folding ~1,700 API listings into memory would poison recall, and an API listing is not a procedure.

## What's in it

Four catalogs, installable from **Settings → AI → Ecosystem → Reference Library**, verified live against the real upstream repos:

| Source | Entries | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| public-apis | **1,673** | **Agent-usable** — free APIs with auth/HTTPS/CORS |
| free-programming-books | **3,786** | Books + courses by language/subject |
| build-your-own-x | **357** | Build-from-scratch tutorials |
| developer-roadmap | **99** | roadmap.sh roadmaps |

The agent queries them with a new read-only **`reference_search`** tool, so "get me the weather" resolves to a real free API *with its auth requirements* rather than a guessed endpoint:

```
reference_search {"query": "weather", "kind": "api"}
→ weather-api [Weather] — auth: none, https: Yes
```

Deliberately **not** in `_MUTATING_TOOLS` — it's a local lookup, so observe autonomy mode allows it.

## Safety

Only the specific catalog markdown files are fetched (a few hundred KB) through the skill-pack installer's existing SSRF-guarded path — not whole repo tarballs, which for developer-roadmap alone would pull tens of MB of unused site assets. Repo/path/ref components are validated before URL construction (no traversal, no non-`.md`, no smuggled path segments in a ref).

## Two real bugs, caught by testing parsers against live data

Both are now regression-tested — assumed format would have shipped them:

1. **public-apis leaked 27 APILayer sponsor rows as if they were free APIs.** The ad block has its own `h3` heading, so the original "real entries live under h3" guard didn't hold. Now filtered by campaign markers **and** column count (real rows carry desc+auth+https+cors; ad rows have 3 cells).
2. **developer-roadmap 404'd** — its readme is lowercase — and once fetched, the parser took only the first link per line, silently dropping every "beginner" variant that shares a line with its main roadmap.

## Verification

- 18 new tests; **2055 Python + 136 JS passing**, 0 failures
- All four catalogs installed through the real API on a live instance; search, `kind` filtering, and the agent tool exercised end to end
- Settings card walked in-browser (renders counts, licenses, agent-usable badge, live search)
- compileall + runtime-paths + module-size ratchet + `import app` smoke all green

author: christianspliid-ui
body:
Christian decoupled the slice prose rewrite from the Encounter Factory retrofit on 2026-08-24 so the integrated checkpoint session does not wait for the factory to be approved and built. This is that direct pass over `src/data/encounters/vertical-slice.ts` — a **register pass only**, judged against the three plainness moves in `Docs/canon/prose.md` and calibrated against the 10 hand-edits recorded on THR-974.

## The predicate narrowed the job twice

The ticket asks for *every prose field in any template whose prose fails the standard at pickup* — a predicate, not a count — so the first task was measuring which templates actually fail, rather than rewriting all 788 authored strings on principle. Both findings are recorded in the status doc because a later pass would otherwise re-derive them:

- **Seven of the nine templates had already been through the factory line** (`content(thr-1131)`). `retrofitPending.ts` still lists exactly two — `riders_behind_caravan` and `snow_on_the_pass` — and those are precisely the two the detector sweep independently flagged.
- **`fiction` is not drift, it is the locked format.** The 61 aphoristic card lines ("What holds, holds") read as the ruling's own *"cut the aphorisms"* target until the THR-883 spec is checked: *Flavor quote · `fiction` · one short generic line, the card's only prose*. Rewriting them would have been a format change wearing a register fix's clothes.

## The baseline carried a live gating failure nobody had surfaced

`encounter.slice.riders_behind_caravan` tripped `second person x3 on mortal-drawn (>= 2)`. All three hits were **one line of quoted dialogue** — the caravan master addressing the traveler — which is character voice, not the narration-addresses-the-mortal defect the rule exists to catch.

There is strong local precedent for scoping the detector instead (THR-899 split the vagueness lexicon for exactly this shape; THR-1045 carved out a class). But the prose was also wrong on its own terms — the step narrative *opened on a bare quote*, violating plainness move 1 — so giving it a subject-first frame fixed a real defect and dropped the hits to zero as a side effect. Logged as **impediment #729**: re-read the prose before re-scoping a gate.

## Detectors over all nine templates

| | vagueness (o/s/i) | not-X-but-Y | divine | 2nd person | intensifiers | **failures** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Before** | 3 / 1 / 1 | 1 | 0 | 7 | 3 | **1** |
| **After** | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0 | **0** |

The two surviving second-person hits are single quoted lines ("The moon will find you", "You kept it"), each below the 2-hit threshold and correct character voice. The last not-X-but-Y hit was cleared by adopting Christian's own sentence: the Kin chip's *"It opens less wide than it was going to"* trips the detector, and his calibration #9 phrasing — *"It is a narrower door than it was going to be"* — is the same beat and does not.

## Deliberately not done

**`retrofitPending.ts` is unchanged.** Removing the two slice entries would claim a **Composition Contract** retrofit that did not happen. THR-1219 supersedes the "rides the THR-1043 retrofit" line for the slice *prose* only; THR-1130 still owns the rest.

**Two of my own edits came back.** `checkNudgeHand` caps carryover factor lines at 12 words and turned the suite red on two 13-word rewrites — one was a real move-1 fix (a participial opener) reworded inside the cap, the other was over-reach de-eliding a line whose terseness is the field's word budget, and was put back.

No mechanical facts changed — same steps, effects, seeds, outcome bands and constants.

## Verification

Code track (`classify:diff` → **code**; `src/data/` survives the docs filter).

```
npm test                       1058 files / 17,323 tests passed
npm run check:typecheck        OK — 3014 error(s), unchanged from baseline
npx vite build                 built in 10.97s
check:generated-freshness      OK — 34 generated artifact(s) match HEAD
check:wiki-freshness:blocking  OK — 24 page(s) checked, no stale pages
check:impediment-ids           OK — 730 rows + 97 paragraph entries, every # unique
check:process                  up to date
```

Both tree-diffing freshness gates were re-run as the last action before push, after every closeout edit (THR-896 / THR-976 general rule). No engine smoke owed — the diff touches no `src/engine/`, tick, orchestrator or agent-decision file. No browser capture owed — content pillar only, matching the ticket's own **Engine N/A · UI N/A**.

Per the ticket, no review ask goes to Christian for this — he sees it at the integrated checkpoint session, where the whole slice is level.

Fixes THR-1219

author: igwevictorkelechi-gif
body:
Lets a user open a Maplerad **USD** collection account alongside their NGN NUBAN, via a switch on the account screen.

## Why it's more than a toggle

A USD account is a real correspondent account, so Maplerad requires US-banking KYC the NGN flow never collected — a tax/ID number, employment, nationality, employer, and US-residency status — and it can require the holder to **consent to US banking terms** before it activates. So the switch reveals a short form, and the consent step is surfaced as a link rather than hidden.

## API

- **`Asset` enum gains `USD`** (schema + a lazy `ensureUsdAsset` `ALTER TYPE`, matching the `ensureTransfers` pattern since migrations aren't applied on deploy). `money.ts` maps USD → 2 decimals.
- **`maplerad/accounts.createUsdAccount`** for `POST /collections/virtual-account/usd`. The `VirtualAccount` type already anticipated USD (`status`, `require_consent`, `consent_url`).
- **`lib/usdAccount`** stores the account like the NGN one — a USD/FIAT wallet row — and surfaces the consent flow instead of hiding it. Requires an enrolled Maplerad customer; **idempotent**.
- **`POST`/`GET /api/virtual-accounts/usd`** — the POST fails clearly with **409 `not_enrolled`** when the user isn't verified, rather than letting the provider return an opaque error.
- `createUsdAccountSchema` with employment/residency enums mirroring Maplerad's.

## Clients (web + mobile)

A self-contained **`UsdAccountPanel`** behind a switch on the virtual-account screen, so the NGN flow is untouched. Off by default; flipping it on loads the USD account or shows the form (tax ID, employment status, description, employer, US residency), then displays the account number, bank, and — when consent is pending — a link to finish activation. Web uses `<select>`s; mobile uses chip selectors and a native `Switch`.

## Verification

- **311 API tests pass** (8 new): the lib's open / enrolment-guard / idempotency / consent cases, and the route's key-mapping, 409 gating, and validation.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean across **api, web and mobile**; api and web `next build` succeed with `/api/virtual-accounts/usd` and `/virtual-account` present.

## Deploy notes

- The API's `vercel.json` already runs `prisma generate` before `next build`, so the new enum value reaches the deployed client. The admin app doesn't import `@cheqpay/db`, so it's unaffected.
- Mobile users need the app rebuilt to see the switch (as with the earlier client changes).

## Scope

This **provisions and displays** the USD account. Crediting USD *deposits* (the collection webhook → a USD balance) is a separate follow-up — there's no USD balance surface yet. Worth deciding before you promote this to real users.

## Summary

- add deterministic 15-minute virtual sleeve positions, intent transitions, ordered replay and source/evidence-bound netting
- add one continuous physical-target solve with CVXPY kept in the application layer and independent domain feasibility checks
- add immutable convex cost-model inputs that evaluate into complete final-target-bound `ExpectedCostState` values
- bind exact economics, cost, risk, solver, forecast/alpha, position, decision-time and netting authority into target identities
- enforce zero-forecast no-new-exposure, exact internal-cross lineage, transaction cost once on physical delta and financing once on physical holding
- add the exact R3 evidence-purpose enum and type-bind source/evidence class through economics, risk, sleeves and targets

## Boundary and identity

Immediate parents are merged R3.A economics/SolverPolicy and merged R3.B ordered risk. R3.C authenticates their frozen values in memory and proves only the new sleeve/netting/continuous-target transformation. It does not replay evidence ancestry.

- semantic identity: changes; source/evidence purpose, economics, continuous-cost components, ordered risk, solver policy, sleeve/netting lineage and complete decision inputs are explicit
- closure identity: no durable closure is introduced; R3.E owns persisted target/report closures and create-only verification receipts
- provenance identity: explicit economics, model, risk and solver provenance remains separate from semantic meaning
- verifier/promotion identity: no verifier receipt, promotion or holdout authority is introduced
- retained evidence/migration: none
- compatibility: the unused pre-solve `expected_costs` input was deleted; no retained consumer required a bridge

No provider acquisition, broker/order operation, retained-outcome access, holdout action, multi-horizon generalisation, rounding/repair or generic evidence framework is included.

## Summary

Closes Phase 5 of the `loader-moderno-dojo` SDD change — its nine QA tasks were written as a manual procedure and are now 11 Playwright specs — and fixes **two production defects that measuring those scenarios uncovered**.

The headline is the second part. Before this PR, the landing's loading overlay did not wait for the 3D scene to load. It dismissed on a fixed 2.5 s timer regardless of the network, which made two of its own features unreachable and one failure mode silent:

- The 8 s "connection is slow" hint could never appear. The overlay left the screen 5.5 s before its threshold.
- The 20 s escape action could never appear.
- A `.glb` failure arriving more than ~2.5 s into the load was **swallowed**: the visitor got the nav bar over an empty page, with no scene, no message and no way out.

The 15 existing unit tests passed throughout, because they drive the loader with `useProgress.setState({ active: true, ... })` by hand — they injected the signal the real application never emitted.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/components/landing/Personaje.tsx` | **Fix 1.** Touch `useProgress.getState()` before the module-scope `useGLTF.preload(MESH_URL)`. +11 −1 |
| `src/components/landing/Loader.tsx` | **Fix 2.** `if (escenaFallo \|\| errors.length > 0) return;` before the completion branch. +10 −1 |
| `e2e/landing-loader.spec.ts` | **New.** 374 lines, 11 specs covering Phase 5's nine QA tasks. |
| `openspec/specs/landing-loader/spec.md` | **New.** The delta spec promoted to a main spec, with three requirements split rather than copied — see below. |
| `openspec/changes/loader-moderno-dojo/verify-report.md` | **New.** Six gates, requirements coverage, both defects, positive controls. |
| `openspec/changes/loader-moderno-dojo/archive-report.md` | **New.** Promotion decisions and what was deliberately left open. |
| `openspec/changes/loader-moderno-dojo/state.yaml` | `apply`/`verify`/`archive` advanced to `done`; `next_recommended: none`. |
| `openspec/changes/loader-moderno-dojo/tasks.md` | Phase 5 outcomes, and what stays manual with the reason. |
| `openspec/specs/automated-verification-gates/spec.md` | One follow-up closed: four open QA gaps become three. |

**Review size, declared rather than buried.** 1093 insertions, but the composition matters: **21 lines are production source**. 374 are the new test file, and ~700 are openspec prose (two reports plus the promoted spec). `forward_to_apply` in this change's `state.yaml` had already settled `pr_boundary: single-pr` and `chain_strategy: not-needed`, which is why this is not chained. The three commits are separable if you'd rather review them one at a time: `2e002ce` is the fix and its tests, `77253a3` closes the SDD cycle, `37cc787` is a record correction.

## Defect 1: a module-ordering race made `useProgress().active` permanently false

`Landing3D.tsx` imports `./Escena` (line 4) before `./Loader` (line 9). `Escena` reaches `Personaje.tsx`, whose module body calls `useGLTF.preload(MESH_URL)`. That fires `DefaultLoadingManager.itemStart` — but `Loader.tsx`'s import of `useProgress` is what creates drei's zustand store, and **creating that store is what installs `DefaultLoadingManager.onStart`**. The preload therefore emitted the first `itemStart` into a manager with no listener.

With the mesh as the only top-level item — `PersonajeReal` suspends on it before the 8 animation clips are reached — three never re-emits that `onStart` while the request is pending. So `active` stayed `false` for the entire load, `huboActividad` was never set, and the `ARRANQUE_MS` (2500 ms) cold-start guard resolved the overlay every single time.

Measured with the store instrumented: with `ninja.glb` held open, the store never changed from `{active: false, progress: 0, loaded: 0, total: 0}` in six seconds. With the preload removed, the same scenario reported `{active: true, progress: 0, item: "/models/ninja/ninja.glb", loaded: 0, total: 1}` at 415 ms.

The fix keeps the preload rather than dropping it — the preload exists to start the download early, and removing it would trade one regression for another. Touching the store first is enough, and it is measurably *faster*: `active: true` at **315 ms** with the preload, versus 415 ms without it.

An earlier hypothesis — that drei's `/* @__PURE__ */ create(...)` was lazily instantiated — was **wrong**. It was discarded by reading `node_modules/@react-three/drei/core/Progress.js` and `node_modules/three/src/loaders/FileLoader.js`, not by reasoning further.

## Defect 2: completion raced the error gate and won

A failed item ends the `LoadingManager`'s queue exactly as a successful one does, so `onLoad` clears `active` on error too. The completion effect and the error gate both fired, both deferred through `setTimeout(…, 0)`, and when completion won it set `terminado.current = true` — which the error gate checks first and returns on. The error UI was then suppressed permanently.

Measured: a 404 arriving 3500 ms into the load produced `errorUI: 0`, `overlay: 0`, `canvas: 0`. Nav bar over nothing.

The guard reads `errors` as well as `escenaFallo` because drei writes `errors` from `onError` *before* `onLoad` clears `active`, so it is already populated at that point. An immediate 404 was unaffected either way and still passes without the guard, which is the correct outcome — that path never needed it.

## Promotion is not copying

Three requirements would have become false invariants if promoted verbatim. One was actively harmful:

**`Requirement: Scope Boundary`** said the change "MUST touch only `Loader.tsx`, `useLanding.ts`, and `Landing3D.tsx`". That was a gate for one change. Read as a standing rule, **it would forbid the `Personaje.tsx` fix in this very PR** — the fix that makes the capability work. It is promoted as `Landing Loader Is the Landing's Only Loading Overlay`, keeping the durable half (the app's spinners stay separate, no route-level `loading.tsx`, `/landing-preview` inherits) and recording the file list under `History:` with that contradiction stated.

The dead-field scenario read "search `src/` for `loaded`, find zero". A search returns 12 hits for `\b(loaded|setLoaded)\b`, 9 for `loaded` alone, or 7 counting files instead of occurrences — all correct answers to different questions, none of them the requirement. Restated against the store's properties, with the exact command written beside the number.

And one requirement was **added**: `Dismissal Gated on Real Load Completion`. The delta could not describe a defect its own QA phase had not yet found. Without it the spec would omit precisely the thing most likely to regress, and would describe a decorative overlay as a working one.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` → exit 0
- [x] `npm run lint` → exit 0, **0 errors**, 49 warnings, none in these files
- [x] `npm run test:run` → **203/203** in 18 files
- [x] `npm run build` → exit 0
- [x] `npx playwright test` → **16/16** against the dev server
- [x] `CI=1 npx playwright test` → **16/16** against `npm start`

That last run is not redundant. `design.md` §Manual QA step 5 requires task 5.5 to be re-run under `npm run build && npm start`, because the dev-mode error overlay changes error-boundary reporting. `CI=1` switches `playwright.config.ts` to `npm start`, so that requirement is met by execution instead of being carried forward as manual residue.

### Positive control

Every timing spec asserts **both sides** of its threshold — absent before, present after — because a test that only checks "the hint is there" passes even when the element renders from mount. Each fix was then reverted **individually** and the suite re-run:

| Reverted | Result |
|---|---|
| `Personaje.tsx` fix | 5.1, 5.3, 5.4 and 5.5-late **fail** |
| `Loader.tsx` guard | 5.5-late **fails**; 5.5-immediate still passes |

That control caught a defective test of this PR's own making. 5.1 originally asserted only "dismissed later than 1500 ms" — which th

author: fabiogiglietto
body:
Follow-up to #74. Per-process minting fixed the two-process replay, but the
first real recluster since then still 401'd — this time from **inside a single
process**:

```
16:33:48  mint #1  exp 16:38:48   -> refresh-topics OK
16:34:30  mint #2  exp 16:39:30   -> update --recluster starts
16:42:57  Advisory token refresh failed (89s remaining); serving cached token: 401
16:44:28  WorkloadIdentityError -> run fails
          recluster: 269 assigned, 0 skipped (unchanged inputs)
```

A minted JWT lives **5 minutes**. `update --recluster` is one process that runs
about **ten** (269 papers), and when the SDK refreshes its access token it
re-reads the token file — finding an assertion that is by then both expired and
already burned. One mint per process is not enough for a process that outlives
its own token.

Note the SDK degraded gracefully first ("serving cached token") and only
hard-failed once the cached token actually ran out. The assignment pass
completed; what died was the structure-note generation that follows it
(`_generate_structure_notes` → `build_structure_note`).

## Change

Rotate the token file in the background for the length of the job — the pattern
`check_papers.yml` has used all along.

**60s rather than research-radio's 120s.** The SDK opens its advisory refresh
window at `ADVISORY_REFRESH_SECONDS = 120` remaining and hard-fails at
`MANDATORY_REFRESH_SECONDS = 30`. A 120s rotation can therefore leave a burned
token in place for most of that window — which is exactly how far this run got
before the cached token ran out. 60s guarantees a fresh assertion appears with
at least ~60s of cached-token life still in hand.

## Testing

`pytest` 131 passed. The loop was exercised locally against a fake OIDC
endpoint using the same construction as the workflow: the subshell inherits
`mint`, the `jti` rotates on every tick, and the main script exits cleanly
without the detached loop holding it open.

`mine-zettelkasten` gets the same change; `research-radio` #36 is being aligned
to 60s for the same reason.
