author: laird
body:
## Summary

`build_openai_response` never set a `"model"` field in the JSON body returned
from `/v1/chat/completions`, even though the handler already knows the
concrete backing model (`canonical_model`) it dispatched to. Per the OpenAI
chat-completions contract, `model` should report what actually served the
request.

## Downstream impact (found via athena2#1306)

Athena calls this endpoint through the `ai` npm package's
`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` provider, requesting a tier alias as `model`
(e.g. `balanced`, `deep`) that this router load-balances to a real backing
model. Because the response had no `model` field, the `ai` SDK's own
`generateText()` parses it as `undefined` and falls back to the **client's
own requested** model id — indistinguishable, from the client's side, from
the proxy genuinely reporting that value as resolved. Athena's cost
attribution pipeline was recording the tier alias as if it were the
concrete backing model, making 100% of proxied cost rows unattributable to
a real billing provider.

## Change

- `build_openai_response` now takes the resolved `model` and includes it in
  the response JSON.
- Both call sites (cache hit and live dispatch) now pass `&canonical_model`.
- Added a unit test pinning the new field.

## Testing

```
cargo test --lib openai_response_tests   # new test, passes
cargo test --lib                         # 172 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (unchanged)
cargo build                              # clean (pre-existing warnings only)
```

Note: `tests/test_embeddings.rs` and `tests/test_images.rs` fail to compile
on `main` independent of this change (pre-existing `Arc` move errors,
verified by stashing this diff and re-running) — not touched here.

Could not run `cargo fmt`/`clippy` locally (rustfmt component not installed
for the active toolchain in this environment); the diff is minimal and
matches surrounding style.

author: csharp36
body:
## What and why

`demo.mandati.ai/try` is about to be sent to a group of hotel owners, and it was not ready for strangers. This makes it ready, and in the process builds the delivery layer that self-serve signup was silently missing.

**The thing that changed the shape of the work.** `notifications.py` shipped only `ConsoleNotifier` — `notifier_from_settings` raised on anything else, and prod config still said `notifier = "console"`. So invite links and SMS verification codes were *log lines*. Signup is invite-token-only and invites were minted by an operator running `usali invite`. #83 fixed Keycloak, but nothing could ever have delivered a stranger a link or a code, which is why "Save & automate" had nowhere to point. Four of the eight commits here exist to fix that.

**1. `SmtpNotifier` (`4a66687`)** — the seam's first real adapter. Deliberately vendor-neutral: SendGrid, Mailgun, Postmark, SES and a self-hosted MTA all speak submission, so picking one is a deploy-time credential, not a code change. One connection per message — at a handful of sends a day, a pooled connection across an idle Cloud Run instance is the thing that breaks, not the thing that helps.

There is still **no SMS vendor**, so `send_sms` **raises** rather than drop a code the caller believes was delivered. That refusal is load-bearing: it forces every stranger-facing path onto email. A half-configured `notifier='smtp'` (blank host or From) fails when the notifier is *built*, so a deploy mistake surfaces at startup rather than on the first owner who asks for a link.

**2. `POST /api/signup/request` + the OTP move (`ee40f04`)** — mints an invite and emails the link. Same no-oracle posture as every other public refusal here: an address that already has an invite, or already owns a workspace, gets the identical `202`, so this cannot be used to enumerate who has signed up. A second ask mints a second invite rather than resending the first — the raw token is stored only as a SHA-256, so the original link is unrecoverable by construction, and `invites.claim` still means one invite, one tenant. **If the send fails the invite is revoked**, not left pending: the token existed only inside the message that never arrived, so a pending row for it is an unreachable credential.

The OTP now goes to the **invited email**, not the typed cell. The missing SMS vendor is the occasion, but the security reason stands alone: the cell is caller-supplied, so keying delivery on it let anyone holding a leaked invite link redirect the code to a number they control. The invited address is the one channel already proven to belong to the invitee — they got here by clicking a link sent to it. The rate-limit key moved from the cell to the invite token for the same reason: rotating one digit used to buy a fresh budget.

**3. Two synthetic samples (`f20b8e1`)** — `docs/reference/samples/*.pdf` carry **real production numbers** (`scripts/cloud/job.sh` says so; it is why the cloud seed runs `--synthetic-year`), so they can never be what a stranger downloads. `scripts/gen_preview_samples.py` mirrors only the layout geometry a real export uses — column positions, section rows, the code column, the header tokens each parser anchors on — and invents every figure.

Two details worth reviewing:
- The Opera sample deliberately leaves code `5210` **unmapped**. A sample where everything maps advertises a coverage we do not have. A test says so, so nobody "fixes" it later by adding it to `mapping/opera.yaml`.
- The AutoClerk `GRAND TOTAL` is **computed, never typed**. That adapter refuses a report whose rows do not sum to its stated total, so a figure that drifted a cent would turn the sample into "we couldn't read that file" on the very page we invited people to.

**4. The page (`d1daa8c`, `7457c2c`, `e6db80a`)** — four controls looked live and were not: two `disabled` with "coming soon", `not right?` with **no `onClick` at all**, and a `Log in` that worked but sent a first-time visitor to a Keycloak screen they have no account for. To a stranger that reads as a broken product, not an unbuilt one. All four now do something, or say who they are for.

The copy drops the acronym — USALI is what the mapping follows; to an owner it explains nothing — and describes what it does instead. It also states on the page, unprompted, that this reads **one** report from Opera or AutoClerk: signup offers SkyTouch now, but `_PREVIEW_ADAPTERS` does not, so a pack dropped here comes back `unreadable`. Better said than discovered.

`e6db80a` fixes something only visible by looking at it: the table was ordered alphabetically by major, putting **Parking above Room Revenue** on a page whose headline promises a P&L. Lines now group under statement headings with subtotals, Rooms leading its department. Ordering is a presentation decision, so it lives in the component — the API is unchanged.

No issue to close; this implements the `/try` decisions taken on 2026-08-24.

## How it was verified

- [x] `uv run pytest` passes — **1954 passed, 4 skipped** (the skips are the pre-existing face-model tests; those weights are sha256-pinned downloads, never committed)
- [x] `uv run mypy --strict src` clean — 103 source files
- [x] `uv run ruff check` clean
- [x] Frontend: `vitest` **352 passed**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `oxlint` clean

`tests/test_preview_samples.py` is the one worth a look. It runs the **committed PDFs** through the real `detect_report_signature` + preview adapter path, *and* re-runs the generator to compare payloads. The adapters' own unit tests run on word fixtures and would not notice either failure — a signature change that broke the samples would first be seen by a hotel owner.

Also verified in a browser against the live parser, not just in jsdom: the Opera sample fetched from the SPA origin → `POST /api/preview` → parsed by the registered adapter → rendered.

## Checklist

- [x] I signed the [CLA](../CLA.md) (the bot will confirm).
- [x] Commits are atomic — one concern each (we merge, we don't squash).
- [x] Tests cover the change and fail without it.
- [x] If this touches **tenancy, access control, PII, or pay disclosure**, I added a test that proves the boundary at the database (RLS-bound), not just the ORM.
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or real PII in code, tests, or fixtures.
- [x] Docs updated where behavior changed.

On the tenancy box: this adds no new tenant-scoped surface. `/api/signup/request` writes only `invite`, which is deliberately **not** OrgScoped (an invite precedes any tenant) and carries no `org_wall` policy. The existing provisioner-confinement tests still pin that `/complete` is the only path that opens the elevated session. Worth a reviewer's eye on whether a public endpoint that writes rows and sends mail wants anything beyond the rate limiter.

On the PII box: this is why the samples are generated rather than copied.

## Anything reviewers should know

**This does not work until someone gives the demo SMTP credentials, and that is deliberate.** `POST /api/signup/request` answers **502** without them. Set repo Variable `DEMO_SMTP_HOST` and create the `usali-smtp-password` secret — `docs/deploy/demo-continuous-deploy.md` has the commands and a one-line curl that distinguishes "the relay took it" from "the send failed and the invite was revoked". Deploying with `SMTP_HOST` unset is safe: the deploy keeps the console notifier and **prints a NOTE saying so**, rather than shipping a front door that quietly mints invites nobody can reach.

Trade-offs and follow-ups I would like a second opinion on:

- **A `202` is not proof of delivery.** The confirmation copy says a link is on its way *if that address can receive mail* — it cannot honestly say more, because the server deliberately does not tell the page whether the address is known. If that reads as evasive to an owner, it is worth rewording, but not worth making the endpoint leak.
- **The unsupported-vendor branch** replaced "Notify me when it's ready" with the sa

author: guillaumefont
body:
Proposes **ADR 0058 (status: Proposed)** — a successor design for ADR 0050's Decision 2 (the `BeginSplit`/build/freeze/`CutoverSplit` workflow), in two independently-shippable trains:

- **Train 1 — learner replicas in the shared `RaftCore`**: a non-voting membership class (receives `AppendEntries`/`InstallSnapshot`, excluded from quorum and elections, promoted via the existing single-server `change_membership` step). Independently justified: today a new replica joins straight as a voter and dilutes the effective quorum while catching up, on both planes.
- **Train 2 — single-entry atomic in-place split**: `BeginSplit` adds the children's placement-chosen homes as learners to the *parent's* group; ordinary Raft catch-up replaces `SeedBatch`/tail passes (no convergence predicate for a continuous writer to starve); one `SplitTablet` entry in the parent's own log is simultaneously the ordering fence and the data-plane activation — every replica materializes both children locally via kind-filtered SSTable-level clone (children still born with empty change logs); `CutoverSplit` becomes a pure recording step with no freeze, no GSI-drain veto, no final-image re-scan.

**Motivation** (all on the record in ADR 0050's as-built amendments and the lessons log): the tail-convergence predicate needed a liveness bound (`SPLIT_MAX_TAIL_PASSES`, rung 8) because a continuously-written parent never converges naturally; the GSI-drain cutover veto has no such bound (the issue #288 livelock class); the freeze window is a measured, residue-scaling write outage; and the change-log tail is structurally blind to signal-less writes, forcing the O(table) final-image re-scan. The ADR's central premise: ADR 0050's recon finding that ruled out in-place split ("zero-copy was the only split the layout permits") was scoped to the ADR 0028 shared-engine layout — Decision 1's per-tablet private engines dissolved that argument, and the workflow was never re-examined against the layout it itself introduced.

**What this PR contains** (docs only, no code):
- `docs/adr/0058-learner-replicas-in-place-split.md` — the proposal, including four rejected alternatives (among them the CockroachDB-shape metadata-only split, rejected for reopening the shared-substrate seam), an honest risk list headed by group-mint-at-apply, four explicitly open forks (G1–G4), a rung sequencing, and a testing plan keyed to the rung-8 continuous-writer lesson.
- `docs/adr/README.md` — index row.
- `docs/adr/0050-per-tablet-storage-copy-based-splits.md` — dated amendment note cross-referencing 0058 and recording the layout-scoping of the original recon finding.

The ADR also states that the interim **GSI-drain liveness fix** (Alternative 1) should ship separately and first, regardless of this proposal's fate — that fix is deliberately *not* in this PR.

**Not stacked**: this is a single reviewable logical step (one proposal document plus its mandatory index/cross-reference edits), so it ships as one flat PR per the convention's stated exception.

author: frostebite
body:
## What

`game-ci test --docker` rejected every non-Linux host outright:

> `--docker's classic batchmode test flow is currently only supported on Linux hosts/containers (got hostPlatform=win32). Windows Docker test support is tracked separately (the container-side scripts only handle builds so far).`

That guard was **correct for the code as it stood** — `dist/platforms/windows/entrypoint.ps1` had no `RUN_TESTS` branch and unconditionally ran `build.ps1`, so letting a test run through would have silently performed a *build* and reported success.

This is what fails every Windows job on [game-ci/unity-test-runner#310](https://github.com/game-ci/unity-test-runner/pull/310) (each dies in ~25s, well before Unity starts).

## Why it regressed

The original unity-test-runner action **did** support this, via its own `dist/platforms/windows/run_tests.ps1`. The capability was lost in the port to this CLI — not deliberately dropped.

## Approach

Rather than resurrect `run_tests.ps1`, `entrypoint.ps1` now reuses **`steps/test.ps1`** — the "native host" Windows test script — which is already container-safe. The only container/host difference that ever mattered is how the Unity Editor is located, and `resolve_unity_path.ps1`'s `Get-UnityEditorRoot` already returns the image-baked `$Env:UNITY_PATH` when set, before falling back to the Unity Hub default.

`Docker.getWindowsCommand` already mounts the whole `platforms/windows` tree at `c:\steps`, so the shared script is reachable at `c:\steps\steps\test.ps1` with **no new volume**.

This also keeps the strictly better implementation — package mode, `coverageEnabled` gating, array-based argv — instead of the original's string-interpolated one, and avoids a ~250-line duplicate.

## Two further bugs found while verifying end to end

**1. `--testPlatforms=standalone` was broken in Docker mode — on Linux too.**
`dist/test-standalone-scripts` was never mounted into the container, so `ubuntu/steps/test.sh`'s `cp -R "/UnityTestRunnerAction/Assets/..."` failed outright. The scripts survived the port; the mount didn't (the original action mounted the same directory as `/UnityStandaloneScripts`). Now mounted on both platforms, and only for test runs.

**2. The Windows container never propagated its exit code.**
`entrypoint.ps1` just fell off the end, so the container's status was whatever `return_license.ps1` happened to leave behind. Builds were shielded by `UnityBuildValidation` parsing the log output, but a test run has no equivalent output check — a failing suite could have reported success.

macOS stays rejected, with a clearer message: there are no Unity Editor Docker images for macOS at all, so there is nothing to run the container scripts in.

## Verification

- PowerShell scripts parse cleanly under **Windows PowerShell 5.1** — what the container actually runs (`powershell`, not `pwsh` 7). Both runtimes were also checked for the `[int]""` coercion the new exit-code casts rely on.
- `steps/test.ps1` was **executed** against a stubbed `UNITY_PATH` to confirm it resolves its sibling `resolve_unity_path.ps1` via `$PSScriptRoot`, honours `$Env:UNITY_PATH` (it attempted exactly the container's `<UNITY_PATH>\Editor\Unity.exe` shape), and surfaces `$global:TEST_RUNNER_EXIT_CODE` across the dot-source boundary `entrypoint.ps1` consumes it through.
- 5 new unit tests (Windows test dispatch resolves a `windows-il2cpp` image; standalone mount present for test runs and absent for builds, both platforms).
- Full suite: **244 pre-existing failures before and after** — no regression. (Those are unrelated: the orchestrator plugin's tests use vitest `vi.mock` under bun's runner.)

## Note on unity-test-runner#310

This unblocks the Windows half of that PR's matrix. The Linux half fails for an unrelated reason — Unity licensing (`Code 500 ... No ULF license found` / `Code 10 while verifying Licensing Client signature`), i.e. an expired or invalid `UNITY_LICENSE` secret, not a code defect. Both halves need to be resolved for that matrix to go green.

author: cmt218
body:
Closes the "iOS ignores socketTimeoutMillis" card as **invalid**. The bug does not exist.

### Measured

Against a socket that accepts and never sends a byte:

| | elapsed | exception |
|---|---|---|
| bare `HttpClient` with our exact `HttpTimeout` config | 30,550ms | `SocketTimeoutException` |
| the real `ArcanaApiClient` (auth plugin, tokens, timing plugin) | 30,619ms | `SocketTimeoutException` |

iOS is bounded at 30s, same as Android.

### Why the card was wrong

Its root cause — "Ktor's Darwin engine does not implement `HttpTimeout.socketTimeoutMillis`" — is false for Ktor 3.1.2. `TimeoutUtils.setupSocketTimeout` sets `NSMutableURLRequest.timeoutInterval` from `socketTimeoutMillis`, wired in through `DarwinRequestUtils.toNSUrlRequest`. Ktor has been pinned at 3.1.2 since 2026-03-31, so nothing moved under the card. The proposed `configureSession { timeoutIntervalForRequest = 30.0 }` would be redundant, and would have meant an expect/actual seam on the P0 networking path for nothing.

Two further errors in the card:

- **The 90s booking hazard does not exist.** It warns that `createBooking`/`cancelBooking` carry `requestTimeoutMillis = 90_000`. There is no per-request override anywhere in the codebase; `90_000` has only ever appeared as an unchecked step in a plan doc.
- **The Android engine is `ktor-client-android` (HttpURLConnection), not OkHttp.** Doesn't change the 30s result, just the attribution.

The original ~70s device reading is unexplained and left that way rather than given an invented mechanism. The obvious candidate, a stacked token-refresh retry, doesn't work: `refreshTokens` only fires on a 401 and a stalled socket never produces one. Closing it out would need a device re-measure, but no code change is justified either way.

### Changes

- **`ArcanaApiClient.kt`** — the comment asserted the false caveat and cited the card. Replaced with the measured behavior.
- **`docs/regression/inventory.md` ERR-22** — encoded it as *expected*: "iOS's Darwin engine ignores `socketTimeoutMillis` … expect roughly double Android's wait." Now states both platforms fail at ~30s, and that a 60s iOS wait means a regression rather than a platform quirk. Left as-is it would have had a driver wave through a real bug.

Both targets build, all suites green, `self_audit.sh` 0 findings.

author: heskew
body: Closes #1083. One issue only. Does not mix #1098 or #1248. No changes to `.cursor/install.sh`. #1083 is assigned to heskew. ## What was wrong `publishedEntryNames()` derived the deploy payload from `package.json`'s `files` and **silently dropped** anything it could not interpret as a plain top-level entry: ```ts .filter((f) => f !== "" && !f.includes("*") && !f.startsWith("!")); ``` For flair's current `files` — all plain names, some trailing-slashed — this is byte-identical to `npm pack`. The latent trap: add a glob or negation later, and npm still publishes it while the deployed component simply does not contain it. Fail-closed (ships less, never more), but the symptom is the same shape #1080 exists to fix — a rule that silently does less than it claims, with no signal at the moment it stops matching. ## What changed Refuse rather than drop. A `files` entry containing a glob or negation now throws a named error: ``` Cannot honour files entry "dist/**/*.js": the deploy payload filter supports plain top-level entries only. Either simplify the entry, or extend publishedEntryNames() to match npm pack semantics. ``` Did not take the `npm pack --dry-run --json` route. That would remove the divergence by construction, but it adds an npm invocation to every deploy and is more than this issue's smallest honest fix. ## Tests `test/unit/deploy-staging.test.ts` — a fixture whose `files` contains `dist/**/*.js` (and no plain `dist/` entry) fails with a message naming that entry. The emptiness refusal does not fire (`files` is non-empty); without the throw, staging would succeed with a payload missing `dist/`. ## Changelog `.changelog/unreleased/fixed-1083-deploy-files-entry-refuse.md`

author: adamjcook
body:
## Bug fix: account owners flipping after sync

Owners are stored as slot `A`/`B` and displayed through the *synced* partner names. Because both phones ran Setup independently, each recorded the names in opposite slots — the first sync's last-write-wins settings merge then silently flipped what A/B mean for every account created on the losing phone (the "owner changed seemingly randomly" report).

- Setup now has two explicit paths: **"Set up on this phone first"** (one phone only) and **"Join your partner's setup"**, which scans the partner's sync QR codes so both phones share a single name mapping from day one.
- The camera/scan UI is extracted from the Sync screen into a reusable `ScanPanel` component (Sync behaviour unchanged).
- Settings notes that partner names are shared between phones; the README documents the one-time repair for already-flipped data (re-save names + fix owners on the phone that's right, then sync).

## Loan accounts

New **Loan** account type (car loans etc.): groups under Debt, uses amount-owed wording, and gets its own dashboard card with combined balance and trend — deliberately **separate** from the credit-card payoff ring and goal, per discussion.

## Goals

- **Clear the cards by [date]**: dashboard shows "needs about £X/month" against the current card debt, a celebration at £0, and a nudge when the date passes.
- **Savings target [amount, optional date]**: dashboard shows percent progress and the monthly amount needed to hit it by the date.
- Both goals live on the synced settings record (added as optional fields — records from pre-upgrade phones merge cleanly; payload stays v1).

## Testing

- Unit: goal maths (`monthsUntil`/`monthlyToTarget` incl. passed-date, met, and exceeded cases) and loan/card separation — 32 passing.
- E2E: new **join-partner test** — phone A sets up and creates accounts owned by each partner; phone B joins via the new path and both owner labels are asserted correct on B (the flip regression), plus round-trip hash convergence. Smoke test extended with loan card and goal-line assertions — 4 passing.

## After merging

Deploys automatically if the repo's default branch is now `main`; otherwise trigger "Deploy to GitHub Pages" from the default branch (as done for v1), and both phones will offer the in-app "Update" prompt on next open.

**Repair note for your current data**: after both phones update, on whichever phone shows the *correct* picture, re-save the two names in Settings and fix the owner on any wrong account, then sync — the newest edits win everywhere.

body:
## Problem

Staff reviewing an account's users cannot jump directly to the matching Django admin page for impersonation.

The related users list can include US and EU users, so each link must target the user's source region.

## Changes

author: truenas-agent-developer
body:
Fixes #283.

`.tn-solarized-dark` drew `--tn-alt-fg1` at **3.79:1** on its own `--tn-alt-bg1` (`#93a1a1` on `#0e4853`), against the 4.5:1 body-text minimum. That fill is `tn-stepper`'s step indicator, the banner and the hovered table row, so the muted text role failed on ordinary surfaces while clearing on both page surfaces — which is all the token has ever claimed.

## Reproduced first

Measured from the shipped stylesheet, not from the ticket: `#93a1a1` on `#0e4853` is **3.7929**, and on `--tn-bg1` / `--tn-bg2` it is 5.61:1 / 4.86:1. The gap is real and it is confined to the one surface.

## The choice, and the one that was rejected

**Darkening `--tn-alt-bg1` instead was measured and rejected.** base1 clears 4.5:1 only on a surface of luminance ≤ 0.0373. This palette's `--tn-bg2` is already at 0.0308 and `--tn-bg3` at 0.0431, so `--tn-alt-bg1` would have had to darken *past the surface above it* into the narrow band just over the card — inverting the elevation the fill exists to show, and taking the banner and the hovered row with it.

**So the token moves.** `--tn-alt-fg1` is now `#a5b0b0`:

| surface | ratio |
|---|---|
| `--tn-bg1` `#002b36` | 6.75:1 |
| `--tn-bg2` `#073642` | 5.84:1 |
| `--tn-alt-bg1` `#0e4853` | 4.56:1 |

It is the smallest lift of base1 that clears 4.5:1 **by more than a rounding**, with the hue held at 180° (G = B, as base1 has them) and the saturation within an 8-bit step of base1's 6.9%. Two nearer candidates were rejected on the unrounded number, which is what the specs compare: `#a3afaf` measures **4.4956** and *formats* as "4.50", and `#a4afaf` clears by 0.006 — which any later nudge to the fill would spend.

**This leaves Solarized's own ramp, against #265's stated reasoning, and there was no alternative.** The tones above base1 are base2 (`#eee8d5`) and base3 (`#fdf6e3`); both clear on `--tn-alt-bg1`, and this theme has already spent them — base2 is `--tn-alt-fg2` and base3 is `--tn-fg1`. A muted token taken from the ramp would be another role's token under a second name, which is the distinctness the muted step exists for. #265's comment on this token is **corrected in place**, not appended to.

**Still a step below `--tn-fg2`** (`#b8c9c9`), which the ticket asks for explicitly: 1.30:1 apart on `--tn-alt-bg1`. Measured against the eight other palettes rather than judged — they ship that step at 1.11:1 (`.tn-nord`) to 3.01:1 (`.tn-blue`), so this sits inside the band, wider than two of them.

## The spec

The `.tn-solarized-dark` entry comes out of `KNOWN_GAPS` in `text-token-surface-contrast.spec.ts`, which leaves that list **empty**. The note in its place says so and says why the record stays, the same way `FG2_OUTREADS_FG1` does after #282. The file's "a recorded gap is still a gap" cases are already guarded against an empty table, so nothing else moves.

`yarn copy-themes` run; `.storybook/public/themes.css` is in the diff.

## Two claims in `theming.mdx` that #282 left false

Not asked for by this ticket, and flagged rather than folded in silently. #282 lifted `.tn-midnight`'s `--tn-fg1` and emptied `FG2_OUTREADS_FG1`, but `theming.mdx` still named `.tn-midnight` as the palette that inverts its text ramp and still listed its three fills as recorded gaps. Both were contradicting the specs the same page cites, and one of them is inside the sentence this ticket had to rewrite anyway — leaving half a sentence false was the worse option. Corrected here, in two edits, with no token change.

## Checks

Run locally, all green: `yarn lint`, `yarn test` (138 suites, 3990 tests), `yarn test:scripts` (4 suites, 42 tests), `yarn build`.

**`yarn test-sb` was not run here** — the Storybook interaction tests need a browser this machine does not have. That check runs on this PR and is the one thing about this change I could not verify locally.

## Review

`local-review.py` exit **0** — the project's own reviewer, same rubric and threshold as the required check, in a separate process. It returned one finding, a LOW: the palette-exhaustion argument named base2 and omitted base3. The argument held; its statement of why did not. Fixed in the second commit — prose only, in the `themes.css` comment and the same claim in `theming.mdx`, no token value moved — and pushed without reopening the review loop, since a comment cannot break the build and the required check reads the change either way.

Nothing was left unfixed.

author: rnoack1
body:
## Problem / Motivation

Two tests in `test/test_apps_instances_loop_offload.py` fail intermittently on Windows CI,
roughly one run in four:

```
FAILED test_mark_recovered_registry_write_off_the_loop_thread
  - AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'status'
FAILED test_cancelled_persist_waits_for_the_worker_write
  - assert not task.done()
```

The second is a consequence of the first: the same `AttributeError` kills the task before the
cancellation window opens, so `task.done()` is already true.

`SshTunnelManager._mark_recovered` reads `tunnel.status.local_port` when it refreshes the
recorded forwarder identity (`ssh_tunnel_manager.py:1838`). That read sits behind a gate:

```python
if forwarder_pid > 0:
    started = await asyncio.to_thread(platform_compat.process_start_time, forwarder_pid)
    forwarder_start = started or ""
if forwarder_pid > 0 and forwarder_start:          # <- the gate
    key = await asyncio.to_thread(_reclaim_identity_key)
    if key is not None:
        forwarder_sig = _forwarder_identity_sig(..., tunnel.status.local_port)
```

Both tests seeded the tunnel double as `SimpleNamespace(pid=4321)` with **no `status`**. On
Windows, `platform_compat.process_start_time` returns `None` unless
`_open_process_query_handle(pid)` succeeds — i.e. it is truthy **iff a process with PID 4321 is
live and queryable on that runner**. So whether these tests crashed was decided by runner state,
not by anything in the tests. Hence the intermittency, and hence the Windows bias (the Linux
branch reads `/proc/<pid>/stat`, so it is the same class of dependence, merely less likely to hit
at that particular PID).

Introduced by `388b0367b` (#5381), which added both the `tunnel.status.local_port` read and the
status-less `pid=4321` fixtures. It is in the merge-base of every open PR, so it is base-side
rather than caused by any one branch. Observed on #5577 (`1f9b7194c`, Windows shard 1) and
reported on #5579.

Note for anyone reading the CI annotation: it says `Event loop is closed`, which is a red herring
(an unrelated unraisable warning from `autonudge.py`). The real failure is only in the pytest
short summary.

## Why it matters

A base-side flake at ~25% on one shard taxes every open PR, and the cost is not just a re-run:
**the five fork AI review lanes gate on `workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`**, so a red Windows
shard makes all five skip and no AI verdict can arrive at all. A PR can therefore be structurally
un-reviewable because of a fixture defect unrelated to it.

It is also a correctness problem in the tests themselves even when they pass. The identity branch
that `388b0367b` added had no deterministic coverage in this file — it was exercised only when a
runner happened to have PID 4321 live. Deterministic result, non-deterministic coverage.

## What changed

Test-only, one file. No source change: `_SshTunnel.__init__` assigns `self.status` (a
`TunnelStatus`) unconditionally, before any I/O, so the production object cannot fail this way.
The double was simply incomplete, so hardening `_mark_recovered` would be defending against a
state that does not occur.

- `_tunnel_double(instance_id, *, pid=4321, local_port=18022)` — a shared factory for the double,
  now carrying a **real `TunnelStatus`** rather than another `SimpleNamespace`, so a rename or
  retype of `local_port` surfaces here. Its docstring records the invariant (`_SshTunnel` always
  has `.status`) so the next author does not re-omit it. Returning `Any` also lets two
  `# type: ignore[assignment]` comments go.
- `_pin_forwarder_identity(monkeypatch, *, reachable=)` — pins `process_start_time` (and, when
  reachable, `_reclaim_identity_key`) so the branch taken is chosen by the test, not by the runner.

**The judgement call, and why the pins are not uniform.** Completing the fixture alone would fix
the crash but leave the exercised path runner-dependent, so the `status` read would go back to
being covered by luck. Pinning both tests the *same* way is worse in either direction: a uniform
*open* pin adds two extra `to_thread` hops ahead of the cancellation test's blocked write,
narrowing the 50 ms window it depends on — trading one flake for another on a loaded runner. A
uniform *closed* pin leaves `tunnel.status.local_port` unread anywhere in this file, so the
fixture's `status` becomes deletable-looking dead weight and the defect can return unseen. So each
test pins the branch matching its own subject:

| Test | Pin | Why |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `..._registry_write_off_the_loop_thread` | reachable | Widest route to the hint write and the only one reading `status.local_port`, so the fixture's completeness is load-bearing on every platform and every run. |
| `test_cancelled_persist_waits_for_the_worker_write` | unreachable | Its subject is the cancellation window around the **blocked** registry write, so it wants the shortest deterministic route there — one `to_thread` hop, matching the timing profile that already passes reliably. |

Neither test's assertions changed. Nothing is skipped, xfailed, weakened, or baselined.

One thing the diagnosis turned up that is worth recording: the `.status` read is gated on **two**
conditions, not one — a truthy start time *and* `_reclaim_identity_key()` returning non-`None`
(it reads the SEL trust root and returns `None` on `OSError` or a short key). So the Windows
failure needed a live PID *and* a readable SEL key on the runner, and a deterministic open pin has
to control both.

Also checked and deliberately left alone: the sibling gate at `ssh_tunnel_manager.py:1491-1504`
has the same shape but passes a **local** `local_port` variable, not `tunnel.status.local_port`,
so it does not share this defect.

## Tests

A plain run proves nothing here — on any machine where PID 4321 is not live, both tests pass
before and after. All verification below forces the gate.

**Before the change**, with `process_start_time` pinned truthy and `_reclaim_identity_key` pinned
via a temporary session plugin (simulating a Windows runner where PID 4321 is live), the two tests
reproduce the CI symptom pair exactly:

```
2 failed, 1 passed
FAILED test_mark_recovered_registry_write_off_the_loop_thread
  - AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'status'
    at src/kiro_crew/instances/ssh_tunnel_manager.py:1838
FAILED test_cancelled_persist_waits_for_the_worker_write
  - assert not task.done()  where the Task finished with exception=AttributeError(
    "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'status'")
```

`test_mark_recovered_skips_the_write_for_an_untracked_instance` passes throughout — it returns
before the pid path.

**After the change:**

| Run | Result |
|:--|:--|
| Same forced-gate plugin (simulated live PID 4321) | 3 passed |
| `test/test_apps_instances_loop_offload.py`, plain | 14 passed |
| Same file, random order, 5 consecutive repeats | 14 passed x5 |
| `test/test_instances.py -k "mark_recovered or forwarder_identity"` | 3 passed |

**Negative control, proving the pins are not vacuous.** Temporarily stripped `status=` back out of
`_tunnel_double` and re-ran:

- the hint-write test **failed** with the original `AttributeError` — so `reachable=True` really
  does open the gate and reach `tunnel.status.local_port`, and the fixture's completeness is
  genuinely load-bearing rather than decorative;
- the cancellation test **passed** — so `reachable=False` really does keep the gate closed.

**Gates.** `mypy`: clean. `isort`: clean. `black`: this file is already in
`.github/black-baseline.txt` (line 507) and its pre-change form is equally unclean under
`--target-version py310`, so the exemption is pre-existing and main-owned; `black --diff` requests
no change to any line this PR adds. Nothing was formatted and the baseline is untouched. The one
offender `scripts/check_black_formatting.py` reports, `test/test_config_loader.py`, is unclean at
the merge-base too and is not touched here.

author: jstan13
body:
Both failures from the first real portal deployment (`CustomDeployment-20260824141239`).

## 1. `RoleDefinitionDoesNotExist` on the Key Vault role assignment

```
The specified role definition with ID '4633458b17de457ca5dd322bbab69ee3' does not exist.
```

`kvSecretsUserRoleId` was `4633458b-17de-457c-a5dd-322bbab69ee3`. That is not a
built-in role. **Key Vault Secrets User** is
`4633458b-17de-408a-b874-0445c86b69e6` — same first two groups, which is
presumably how it slipped through. Verified against the built-in roles
reference.

Consequence beyond the failed deployment: `backendAppConfig` depends on this
assignment, so the API would never have received its app settings, and the
`@Microsoft.KeyVault(...)` references for `DB-PASSWORD` and
`AZURE-CLIENT-SECRET` would not have resolved. The backend could not have
reached its database.

## 2. `Conflict` on Application Insights

The component was declared classic — no `WorkspaceResourceId`. Classic
Application Insights resources have been non-creatable since 29 Feb 2024;
the API rejects them.

Now workspace-based. That forces the Log Analytics workspace to be
unconditional, where it was previously gated on `effectiveEnableDiagnostics`
(false by default, since auto-sizing only enables diagnostics above 150 hosts —
which is exactly why this bit a default deployment).

Cost impact is nil: a workspace costs nothing to exist, App Insights telemetry
was always billed on ingestion, and the `diagnosticSettings` that stream App
Service / Key Vault logs — the actual cost driver called out in the README —
are still behind `enableDiagnostics`.

`output logAnalyticsWorkspaceId` is no longer conditional.

## Checks

- `az bicep build` clean, `infra/azuredeploy.json` regenerated.
- Grepped every `*.bicep` under `infra/` for hardcoded GUIDs; this was the only
  one. The other role definitions in the template are custom roles it creates
  itself, so they carry no lookup risk.

author: oracle989
body:
Refs #4

## Summary

Make the empty-argv acceptance PTY wait for Codex's explicit CSI-u enhanced-keyboard enablement, send the literal installed-purpose prompt, and submit it with `ESC [ 13 ; 1 u`. Replace the line-oriented fixture with a raw-terminal native stub that accepts only those exact bytes.

## Why

Final acceptance of merged candidate `d4cd8cace515cf83e173662029a027785115ca66` reached the normal trusted Codex 0.149.0 TUI, but a carriage return was displayed rather than submitted after Codex emitted `CSI > 7 u`. Exact protocol-encoded Enter submitted immediately in bounded manual reproduction. Failure authority comment 5400981763 again proves ambient-auth preservation, copied-credential deletion, APFS detach, and named-state removal.

## Change discipline

- Change tier: risky, narrowly scoped to the release acceptance PTY driver.
- The change does exactly this: waits for enhanced-keyboard readiness and sends the exact CSI-u Enter sequence required by the active TUI protocol.
- It deliberately does not do this: alter TERM, launcher argv, timeout, installer, trust config, candidate lifecycle, cleanup/evidence, login, or credential handling.
- New abstractions/dependencies/config surfaces: none; the native fixture uses the already-supported macOS compiler through `xcrun`.
- Existing repository pattern followed: checked-in Expect driver, bounded process runner, and Apple-silicon native acceptance primitive.
- TDD/test intent: the raw-mode stub first failed with the old carriage return, then passed only after exact readiness and byte sequencing were implemented.
- Maintainability: protocol readiness and submission are explicit in the small driver; PTY closure plus bounded descendant cleanup replaces protocol-ambiguous shutdown keystrokes.

## Validation

- `bin/test-acceptance-contract` — pass
- `bin/test-acceptance-primitives` — pass with raw-mode exact-byte stub
- `go test -race ./...` — pass
- Native `bin/ci` — pass on Apple silicon macOS
- `git diff --check` — pass

GitHub CI passed on exact head `925ee8180a1d2ba805b4320bd5e4903935951474`.

## Documentation

Updated deployment and development guidance with CSI-u readiness, exact Enter submission, raw-byte regression semantics, and PTY/process-runner shutdown behavior.

## Production safety

No production deploy was run. No Codex login, credential inspection, installation, migration of real state, nomination, acceptance, merge, or release was performed.

## Solution Design And Reconciliation

- Planning pull request: #30
- Plan directory removed from this implementation: `docs/plans/4-assistant-instance-isolation/`
- Reconciled head: `925ee8180a1d2ba805b4320bd5e4903935951474`
- Reconciliation verdict: `Justified drift`
- [x] Reconciliation has no unexplained drift
- [x] Durable documentation reflects the shipped behavior
- [x] Temporary plan removed
- [ ] An independent maintainer reviewed the current reconciliation and diff

Verdict: justified implementation-learned acceptance-driver drift, ready for independent maintainer review after required checks. Unexplained drift: none.

| Concern | Classification | Result / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Empty-argv native launcher smoke | Conforms | TERM, launcher argv, exact workspace trust, token requirement, and bounded timeout are unchanged. |
| TUI prompt submission | Justified drift | Candidate `d4cd8ca…` and failure comment 5400981763 exposed Codex 0.149.0's explicit CSI-u keyboard mode. |
| Byte ordering | Conforms | Driver observes `CSI > 7 u`, sends the literal prompt, then `CSI 13 ; 1 u`; raw native coverage rejects CR translation. |
| Shutdown and cleanup | Conforms | Driver closes the PTY; the existing bounded runner retains descendant cleanup authority. |
| Credentials and lifecycle | Conforms | No auth, secret, installer, manifest, evidence, cleanup, or named-instance behavior changed. |

Planned versus run: interactive empty-argv launch, exact token observation, hostile-terminal isolation, raw protocol bytes, race suite, native CI, and diff checks ran successfully. Fresh exact-candidate product acceptance remains outside this implementation PR.

| Design concern | Shipped result | Repository destination | Action | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acceptance PTY protocol | Explicit CSI-u readiness and Enter encoding | `docs/deployment.md` | Update | candidate failure 5400981763 and exact manual reproduction |
| Native regression | Raw tty accepts only prompt plus `ESC [ 13 ; 1 u` | `docs/development.md` | Update | failing-before-fix primitive in this PR |

The temporary plan remains absent; PR #30 and Git history retain design provenance. No ADR is warranted for this local protocol correction. The approved release envelope remains intact, but this implementation task stops before merge, nomination, acceptance, or release.

## Follow-up

Independent maintainer review, merge, and fresh exact-candidate acceptance/release remain required.

author: ferqx
body:
## Overview

This PR is primarily a repository-wide runtime architecture refactor. Across 73 commits, it completes the RMV1 modularization, RAV1 authority cutover, and pre-release boundary convergence across the app, Runtime Host, Kernel, Builtin runtime, storage, release tooling, tests, and documentation.

The durable approval queue, sandbox-policy convergence, and session compatibility work are the main product and reliability changes built on top of that refactored architecture.

## Architecture refactor

### Runtime modularization

- complete RMV1 modularization and move production composition into explicit bootstrap/runtime modules
- separate state execution, effects, tool pipelines, Subagent continuation, session persistence, presentation, and provider readiness
- extract app session registry, persistence, token-statistics, configuration, Git, observability, and release composition services
- organize Builtin capabilities and Subagents behind domain-specific package boundaries
- converge runtime contracts and remove cross-layer ownership leaks

### Authority and execution boundaries

- complete the RAV1 production cutover for layered Project identity and authority authenticity
- establish single-Host ownership, governed data-origin/egress facts, and isolated Store conformance
- centralize Runtime session coordination, admission, leases, command processing, and durable publication
- remove speculative, duplicated, installation-scoped, and version-numbered authority paths
- normalize Project identity across restore, symlinks, missing workspaces, and Windows path semantics
- reclaim stale single-Host leases without weakening live identity validation

### Pre-release clean cutover

- replace migration-numbered and legacy architecture names with stable domain names
- remove obsolete state/store paths, compatibility aliases, and duplicated composition roots
- add architecture and core-boundary gates to prevent old dependencies from returning
- align source layout, package exports, tests, release artifacts, active docs, and ADRs with the final architecture

## Functional changes enabled by the refactor

### Durable approvals and sandbox policy

- move approval state to a durable, replay-safe State 27 queue
- support concurrent approvals without single-slot overwrite or starvation
- restrict approval outcomes to `approve_once`, `same_command`, and reject
- make Full exclusively an interaction mode; approval grants can never elevate to Full
- release matching same-command calls atomically with Session-scoped identities and independent receipts
- preserve exact interaction/generation matching across late input, reviewers, restart, cancellation, and concurrent dispatch
- route only same-turn concurrent Explore children to Auto while preserving parent mode elsewhere
- align Planning, Building, and Full behavior with enforceable macOS, Linux, and Windows sandbox capabilities

### Session and TUI reliability

- separate approval Enter/Esc from durable whole-turn Ctrl+C cancellation
- reconcile cancellation receipts instead of discarding admission conflicts
- project approval and Subagent states from canonical durable events
- persist and clear Session command grants through the normal event/replay path
- silently read compatible historical session formats and isolate unknown records
- preserve persisted workspace and Project identity during restore
- serialize startup and session switching and reject stale asynchronous loads
- reconcile interrupted turns, tools, capabilities, approvals, and Subagents before replay

### Storage, release, and CI

- preserve snapshot/tail atomicity and isolate compatibility sidecars
- strengthen platform capability probes and execution-boundary workflows
- stabilize PTY transport/readiness and Windows startup qualification
- update active documentation, architecture maps, ADRs, and completion evidence

## Architectural and security invariants

- Kernel remains independent of app, I/O runtime, storage implementation, and TUI presentation types
- one Runtime Host owns live Session authority and durable command publication
- Project identity and capability evidence are validated at live admission boundaries
- no approval can grant Full authority

author: bernardnormier
body:
Fixes #4821.

The unobserved-task-exception harness had two defects that made it inert:

- In ten test assemblies, the `SetUpFixture` declared `namespace IceRpc.Tests` while the assembly's tests live in a sibling namespace (e.g. `IceRpc.Compressor.Tests`). NUnit applies a `[SetUpFixture]` only to its own namespace and descendants, so the harness never installed there. Each fixture's namespace now matches its assembly. The two `Features` test files move from `IceRpc.Features.Tests` to `IceRpc.Tests.Features` so the core fixture encloses them, following the `IceRpc.Tests.Transports` convention.
- `CommonSetUpFixture.OneTimeTearDown` only printed the collected exceptions, so it could never fail a run. It now ends with `Assert.Fail`, which makes `dotnet test` exit non-zero.

The harness also extends to the five test assemblies that reference `IceRpc.Tests.Common` but had no fixture: IceRpc.Slice.Tests, IceRpc.Protobuf.Tests, IceRpc.Ice.Tests, IceRpc.Slice.Generator.Tests, and IceRpc.Ice.Generator.Tests. (IceRpc.Conformance.Tests only holds abstract fixtures that run inside the covered transport assemblies.)

The remaining test assemblies — ZeroC.Slice.Codec.Tests, ZeroC.Slice.Generator.Tests, IceRpc.Ice.Codec.Tests, and IceRpc.Ice.Generator.Base.Tests — don't reference `IceRpc.Tests.Common` and don't get the harness. Their tests are purely synchronous (no task-spawning code at all), so no task can leak. If a ZeroC test assembly ever grows async tests, the harness should move down into `ZeroC.Tests.Common` rather than have ZeroC tests reference `IceRpc.Tests.Common`.

Verified with a temporary canary test that leaks a faulted task: the harness catches it in a previously-uncovered assembly and the run fails with exit code 1. Three full-suite runs plus a QUIC-enabled run of IceRpc.Quic.Tests are green — no latent unobserved task exceptions surfaced.

None — test-suite fix.

## Qué es

Tres pruebas nuevas en `tests/sin-cuenta.spec.js`, sin tocar código de la app.

La pregunta era si la burbuja de perfiles de perro se ve sin tener cuenta. Se ve, y el engranaje también, y se pueden tener varios perros. Pero comprobarlo a mano hoy no impide que se rompa mañana.

## Por qué estas tres y no una

Que la burbuja aparezca es lo fácil de ver. Lo que puede romperse **en silencio** es lo otro: que añadir el segundo perro *parezca* funcionar y no se guarde, porque sin cuenta ese guardado va por `almacen.js` (navegador) en lugar de por Supabase — dos caminos distintos para lo mismo. Es la misma familia de fallos que la ficha que se guardaba vacía: sin error, sin aviso, y te enteras días después.

1. `la burbuja y el engranaje están, sin cuenta`
2. `el segundo perro se guarda de verdad en el móvil` — recorre el asistente de 6 pasos entero y luego lee `rawku.local.perros` del navegador. **No mira la pantalla**, mira lo guardado.
3. `y los dos salen en la burbuja al volver` — que estén guardados no basta: hay que poder llegar a ellos y cambiar de uno a otro.

## Que la prueba sirve, comprobado

Quitando la escritura del perro nuevo en `almacen.js` (`escribir(CLAVE_PERROS, …)`), la pantalla se ve perfecta y la prueba 2 falla. Restaurado después.

## Lo imprescindible

- Suite web completa: **99 pasan, 2 saltados**.
- `pruebas_completas.py` del motor: en verde (perfil, generación, alergias y patologías).

author: george-dilthey
body:
## What changed

Updated `docs/sources.md` with four targeted improvements to the 50,000 per-source record limit coverage, making it discoverable and actionable for customers with Salesforce list sources that silently stop importing:

1. **Renamed the FAQ section** from "My scheduled Snowflake or CRM import appears to have stopped importing new records" to "My Salesforce, HubSpot, Snowflake, or CRM import is returning 0 new records" — removing the "scheduled" framing (the limit affects manual runs too) and leading with "Salesforce" so customers with Salesforce list sources recognize this as their scenario.
2. **Updated the opening sentence** of that FAQ to say "whether on a scheduled run or triggered manually" — the customer in this Intercom ticket was manually running the source and saw 0 records, which the old "running on schedule" framing would not have matched.
3. **Added Audiences to the "Solutions for large datasets" list** — the support rep explicitly recommended Audiences as the right long-term alternative for imports that regularly exceed 50k. The old list only mentioned bulk enrichment, not Audiences.
4. **Extended the Audiences recommendation at the end of the FAQ** from "Snowflake imports" to "Salesforce, HubSpot, Snowflake, or other CRM/database imports" — making the alternative actionable for the customer's actual use case (Salesforce list source).
5. **Updated the internal anchor reference** in the "Solutions" list to match the renamed FAQ heading.

## Why

Intercom conversation #215475573685137: A Proof.com Enterprise customer reported that their Salesforce list source was "not updating" and "shows 0 records" when manually run. The support rep (Peter Johnston) diagnosed that the source had hit Clay's 50,000 record lifetime cap on June 30th and had been silently discarding all runs since. Fix: create a new import source with dedupe enabled. Long-term alternative: use Clay Audiences.

Fin didn't answer because the existing FAQ was framed around "scheduled" imports and led with "Snowflake" — a customer describing a *manual* run of a *Salesforce list source* showing 0 records wouldn't match the old heading. These edits make the same content discoverable from the customer's vocabulary.

## Source link(s)

- Intercom conversation: https://app.intercom.com/a/inbox/w28k1kwz/inbox/conversation/215475573685137
- Verifier verdict: PASS — `apps/api/v3/tables/domain/sources/source-types.ts:19` (`DEFAULT_SOURCE_RECORD_LIMIT = 50_000`); `apps/api/v3/tables/services/find-entities.service.ts:3430-3431` (silent discard confirmed; source cannot be revived once limit is reached); Audiences exemption confirmed — Audiences use a separate `AudienceRecordLimit` flag path, not the per-source 50k cap
- Slack corroboration: #ent-findheadwaycom-clay (Jun 2026): "The 50k cap is based on total records processed by the Salesforce source over time, not the current row count in the table"; #team-enterprise-product-support (Jan 2026): explains source limit vs. table row limit distinction; #ext-pandadoc, #ent-cresta-clay, and others confirm this is expected behavior and that Audiences are the recommended alternative for large CRM imports

## Uncertainties

None. The 50,000 lifetime cap for Salesforce/CRM sources is code-confirmed, applies to all customers (no feature gate), affects both scheduled and manual runs, and Audiences are confirmed exempt from this cap.

## Related observations

- The verifier confirmed that the per-source cap for **Find People/Companies** sources is plan-dependent (1k on Starter up to 50k on Pro/Enterprise), which the existing docs already note correctly.
- Multiple Slack threads confirm this failure is silent for CRM/Salesforce sources (no UI banner), contrasting with Find People/Companies which show an explicit error. The existing docs already capture this distinction accurately.
- A product request to add source-limit warnings/notifications for CRM sources is outstanding but not shipped (#team-enterprise-product-support Jan 2026 thread). No doc change needed for an unshipped feature.

Closes DOC-2046

author: florent-uzio
body:
Alternative to the `cb-in-decryption.ts` change in #271, with the rest of that PR's example-side concurrency work left alone.

## The problem with the one-liner

#271 adds `400` to the statuses retried inside the CB_IN polling loop. Agreed on the intent — instances return `400` while several decryptions are in flight, so concurrent inbox reads (`Promise.all` over several issuances) were failing for a reason unrelated to the request.

But the terminal throw is hardcoded to `404`:

```ts
// Retries exhausted. If the decryption never materialized, surface that as a 404.
throw new CustodyError({ reason: `CB_IN decryption ${id} not found after ${n} attempts` }, 404)
```

So after #271, a genuinely bad request id polls for the full `maxRetries * intervalMs` and then surfaces as **404 "not found"** — the server's own `reason` and `statusCode` discarded. The known downside ("if you check for a decrypt result you never asked for it will take much longer to fail") is real and unavoidable, but this makes it fail *wrongly* as well as slowly. That is the same class of bug #247 point 3 describes, moved from the example into the SDK.

## What this PR does

1. **`TRANSIENT_POLL_STATUS_CODES = [400, 404]`**, documented with why each code is retried, instead of an inline array. Uses the repo's `isUndefined` helper rather than an `?? 0` coercion on the optional `statusCode`.
2. **Preserves the last transient error.** On retry exhaustion it rethrows with the original `reason` and `statusCode`, the original error as `cause`, and the attempt count in `hint` — the field `CustodyError` already has for exactly this. The synthesized `404` remains only as an unreachable fallback.
3. **Docs and tests.** Both JSDoc blocks still said "404 only"; updated. Added two tests: retry-through-400, and 400-stays-400 after exhaustion.

15 tests pass, typecheck clean.

## Notes

- The retry only wraps the **GET** status call. In `initiateAndWait` the POST sits outside the `try`, so if the concurrency `400` can also come from `initiate`, this doesn't cover it — worth confirming against a live instance.
- Related to but distinct from **#247 point 3**: that asks for a `findDecryptedAmount` returning `undefined` for *absent* ("no confidential inbox"); this handles *transient* ("try again"). Shared root cause — consumers can't distinguish absent from transient from broken, so they blanket-catch — but `getInbox` in the example keeps its `catch { return null }` and #247 point 3 stays open. Implementing it needs confirmation of what the API actually returns for "no inbox" (404? `Failed`? `Completed` with no amount?), which #247 flags as unknown.

Changeset: `.changeset/cb-in-decryption-transient-poll.md` (minor → beta.15). New file rather than extending `internal-cb-in-decryption.md`, which documents the namespace's shipped shape; this is a distinct behavioural fix.

author: zachdunn
body:
Implements §3 of #829, "Bound expensive reads and improve 429s".

## Read limiter

Authenticated reads had no rate limit of their own — the only per-workspace
limiters covered mutations, renders, poster generation, and public intake.
This adds a read-side limiter in two tiers, keyed by workspace, entirely
separate from those budgets: a read never spends a write allowance and a write
never spends a read allowance.

| Tier                          | Applies to                                                                     |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `READ_LIMITER` (2400/60s)     | A listing the caller opted out of hydrating (`?metadata=0`), `file-url`, a single object read |
| `HEAVY_READ_LIMITER` (600/60s) | `files/search`, `files/facets`, `files/by-path`, a metadata-hydrated listing   |

The tight tier is the set of shapes that fan out into D1 with per-row work.
Classification is derived from the request, never from a caller-supplied hint:
`?metadata=0` is the same opt-out the canonical listing already honors for
hydration (#837), so the parameter that removes the work also removes the
tighter bound — an unhydrated list does not pay the hydrated limit. The legacy
bearer listing is classified by its own inverted contract (`?metadata=1`
opts *in*, and any `meta.*` filter or `?name=` switches it to the D1 search
path), so both of its expensive shapes land in the tight tier and a bare prefix
list does not.

Limits live in `wrangler.jsonc` alongside every other limiter (production
`unsafe.bindings` and the previews `ratelimits` block), which is the existing
mechanism for changing them. Both fail open when the binding is absent, matching
`WRITE_LIMITER`/`RENDER_LIMITER`.

### Why these numbers are safe for current traffic

Sized well above observed legitimate use, because the point is bounding a
runaway loop rather than pacing the product:

- The signed-in web app's heaviest page (screenshots) is one `by-path` fetch
  plus facet lookups per load — a handful of tight-tier reads. 600/60s leaves
  room for many simultaneous members reloading continuously. The internal
  fan-out that tripped auth limits in #797 was removed there (by-path strips
  replaced the per-group search fan-out), so no page issues a per-item read
  burst today.
- The CLI's paged search (`uploads find`, cursor pagination from §4) tops out at
  100 results per request; 600 requests/minute is far more paging than any
  interactive or scripted use produces.
- The normal tier at 2400/60s is 40 reads/second sustained for one workspace.
- Every write, render, poster, and public-intake quota is unchanged.

## 429 semantics

Retry metadata is now emitted from one place — the API's error boundary — for
every rate-limit error, instead of a handful of routes setting a header by hand:

- `Retry-After` — the standard header (RFC 9110), in seconds.
- `X-Retry-After` — the same value, kept for compatibility. Better Auth uses
  this spelling and the shipped client reads both (`packages/uploads/src/client.ts`
  already falls back across the pair — verified, unchanged).
- `error.details.retry_after` — the same value on the body.

The value is the limiter's configured window, which is honest: waiting one full
window is always sufficient. Rate-limit errors that genuinely have no figure
(the monthly upload budget) emit no header rather than a guess.

**No `RateLimit-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset`.** A Cloudflare `RateLimit`
binding's `limit()` returns `{ success }` and nothing else, so there is no
accurate quota, remaining count, or reset instant available to report. Emitting
a fabricated one would make clients back off at the wrong time; a test asserts
the headers stay absent so a future change has to make that call deliberately.

## Tests

`pnpm test` from root: 343 files, 5155 tests passing. New coverage:

- `apps/api/src/read-limits.test.ts` — tier classification (canonical and
  legacy listings), per-workspace keying, tight-vs-normal routing, fail-open,
  write limiter untouched by reads, and the full 429 contract including the
  absence of limit/remaining/reset headers.
- `apps/api/src/routes/me.test.ts` — end-to-end through the real routes: a
  hydrated listing 429s with both headers while the same listing with
  `?metadata=0` succeeds; search, facets, and by-path 429 on the tight limiter;
  a read consumes no write budget.

`apps/api` typechecks; oxfmt clean.

## Not included

- No `packages/uploads` change, so no changeset: the client already read both
  header spellings and its behavior is unaffected.
- The MCP worker's read tools are not wired to the new limiter — it has its own
  binding set and reaches storage through a different path. Worth a follow-up if
  it should share the budget.
- OpenAPI is untouched here to avoid colliding with the §1 contract work; the
  narrative reference (`docs/api.md`) gains a "Rate limits" section.

Refs #829 §3.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added per-workspace rate limits for standard and resource-intensive read operations.
  - Added retry guidance to rate-limit responses through response headers and error details.
  - Applied read limits to listings, searches, facets, grouped views, file retrieval, and related endpoints.

- **Documentation**
  - Documented read-limit tiers, affected operations, and the 429 response format.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Standardized rate-limit responses with consistent 60-second retry information.

author: oscerd
body:
Fixes #733

## What

`getResource` walks `bundleContext.getBundles()` in install order and takes the
first bundle with a matching descriptor, loading the class from that bundle's
classloader with no scoping to the requesting context's wiring. `findClass`
caches the result per key (`addToClassMap`), so whichever bundle happened to be
scanned first stays selected for the life of the finder.

With two versions of a bundle installed side by side — a normal state during a
rolling upgrade — install order silently decides which one supplies the factory.
An operator who has installed a patched bundle has no way to tell it is being
ignored.

## How

**The selection is unchanged.** First bundle in install order still wins. What
is new is that the scan no longer breaks early, so when more than one bundle
provides the descriptor it logs at WARN which bundle was picked, that it was
picked only for being installed first, and which others also provide it:

```
Factory descriptor META-INF/services/org/apache/camel/some-factory is provided by
more than one bundle. Using the one from camel-foo/4.18.1 [42], selected only
because it is installed first; also provided by camel-foo/4.18.2 [77].
```

The list is only allocated when there actually is a clash, and `findClass`
caches per key, so this costs an already-O(bundles) scan not breaking early on
first resolution of each key.

## Why not the wiring-scoped fix

#733 floats scoping selection to the requesting context's `BundleWiring`. I have
deliberately not done that here:

- it changes the semantics of a core resolution path that has behaved this way
  for a long time, with a wide blast radius and no cheap way to prove no
  regression short of the full Pax Exam suite
- factory-finder keys are internal Camel SPI names — they never come from
  message content — so there is no urgency that would justify that risk

Making the situation visible is the cheap half, and it is what tells us whether
the ambiguity happens in practice at all. Happy to follow up with the
wiring-scoped selection as a separate change if you want it.

## Tests

`OsgiFactoryFinderTest` covers no-provider (returns null), single provider, and
several providers — the last asserting that **install order still decides**, so
the selection behaviour the rest of the resolution path depends on is pinned
against future edits to this method.

```
Tests run: 15, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
BUILD SUCCESS
```

## Note

`BundleEntry` goes from `private static class` to package-private. `getResource`
is `public` and returns it, so `private` was never actually restricting
anything; this just makes the type nameable from tests in the same package.

a tool-result carrier: the model's own tool_use turn was never concluded,
so the next turn on that session appended a second consecutive user message
on top of an exchange stuck mid-flight. The user meanwhile heard a
fabricated "Okay." claiming a completed task on a turn where nothing
actually finished.

On exhaustion the turn now closes with a synthetic assistant message
carrying the exact fallback text the user hears ("Sorry, that got
complicated — can you try again?", or its Romanian equivalent, resolved
from the same profile that picks the reply voice), and logs a warning so
the case is visible in production logs rather than silent.

Adds the repo's first tests: Node's built-in runner via tsx over
server/test/, driving runTurn against a fake Anthropic endpoint through
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and a throwaway SQLite file via DEEPBLUE_DB_PATH, so no
production seam and no real network or database is involved. The three
exhaustion tests were verified red against the pre-fix code, including one
that asserts on the actual request body the SDK sends.

author: pitvox
body:
Arregla la etiqueta ilegible que salió en el primer run real del workflow `Grafico Asado FP` (#36). Nivel A: toca un solo archivo, no toca Pages, no toca el pipeline, invisible para el sitio.

## Problema

La anotación de la última semana se dibujaba abajo-izquierda del último punto (`xytext=(-4, -22)`, `ha="right"`), que con esta serie cae justo sobre el tramo más volátil: texto tinta sobre línea azul, ilegible. Se agravó porque el máximo real histórico es de **marzo 2026**, a pocas semanas del último dato, así que las dos anotaciones competían por el mismo espacio.

## Arreglo

- La etiqueta `hoy:` va ahora a la derecha del último punto (`xytext=(9, 0)`, `ha="left"`, `va="center"`), fuera del área de datos.
- 220 días de margen en el eje x (`set_xlim`) para que quepa — lo mínimo que pide el ancho del texto; el eje sigue terminando en el tick de 2026, sin hueco visible.
- Caja blanca de respaldo (`bbox`) y `zorder=5` como red de seguridad si alguna vez la serie llega hasta el borde.
- La anotación del máximo queda igual, arriba-izquierda.

Sin cambios en datos, cifras, paleta ni en el workflow.

## Verificación

Renderizado contra un `indices.json` sintético construido para replicar la forma de la serie real (arranque fines de 2015, salto 2020–21, máximo $28.460 en marzo 2026, última semana $27.313): ambas etiquetas legibles, ninguna sobre la línea.

**No verificado en este entorno:** la descarga real de `https://carestia.cl/indices.json` — la política de red de la sesión rechaza ese host (403 en el CONNECT del proxy). El workflow no se gatilló desde acá.

body:
…them

The agent lane streamed its work for a shipped scenario and reported one word for your own file. Both ran the identical pipeline -- /analyze/upload returns nine populated agent_traces and, with a provider configured, point_b_method "openai" -- but a screen that shows its reasoning for the demo data and "complete" for your data reads as a lane that only works on the demo data. That reading cost a reviewer an afternoon, and it was a fair reading.

The backend has emitted per-agent frames for uploads since the endpoint was written. Nothing ever called it. So the upload path went through the single-request POST, and the stage list it fed had exactly one entry.

readEventStream takes an optional init because this stream is a POST: a file cannot travel in a query string. Content-Type is left unset on purpose so the browser supplies its own multipart boundary.

The progress-frame mapper moves out of the scenario lane and is shared, since both lanes emit the same frame. It being inline in one of them is part of why the other never grew one.

Verified in a browser on a real upload: nine stages stream in, Agent 8 spends 2570 ms in OpenAI, and the shipped-scenario lane still opens GET /api/agents/stream unchanged.

author: guust-franssens
body:
## What this lands

The canonical **pre-bundle work layout** that issue #291 (gaps 1 and 3) asked for - defined once,
implementing issue #234's corrected design (which itself moved twice during review, from an
initial `_work/<unit>/<run-id>/` sketch to `_runs/<NNN>-<slug>/`):

```
_runs/<NNN>-<slug>/
    run.json          <- the one authoritative description of this run
    assessment/        assess_estate.py-shaped output
    assets/             harvest_estate_assets.py-shaped downloads
    bundle/              run_estate.py-shaped conversion output
    oracle/               capture_tableau_oracle.py-shaped reference capture
    deliverables/          operator-facing outputs meant for the CUSTOMER, never for git
    scratch/                disposable, run-owned
```

Plus **`scripts/work_dirs.py`**: the single source of truth for these paths -
`sanitize_unit_key`, `allocate_run` (atomic `mkdir`-exclusive, retry on collision, never a
read-then-write race), `RunPaths`, `list_runs`. It resolves the repo root from its own
`__file__`, never `Path.cwd()`.

## Where this differs from #291's own text (with justification)

- **`_runs/`, not `_work/<unit>/<run-id>/`** - #291's body suggested `_work/...`, but #291's own
  comment thread corrected that to `_runs/` before I started, because `.gitignore`'s existing
  `**/_work/` rule means the OPPOSITE retention (its `.py` transform scripts are deliberately
  tracked). Implemented the corrected shape, not the superseded original text.
- **Numbering is global across `_runs/`, not per-unit** - matches issue #234's own worked example
  (`001-entdash`, `002-shipping` consecutively across two different units).
- **Added a `deliverables/` subdir**, not present in #234's five-subdir list. Issue #322 is a
  near-miss where an operator-facing output (`connections_manifest.py`'s `connections.json`/`.md`,
  naming 17 real customer servers) landed unprefixed and unignored at the repo root - not
  scratch, but also not safe at an arbitrary path. The canonical layout needed a place for it.

## Deliberately out of scope (said explicitly, per the brief)

This lands the **convention + helper only**. It does **not**:
- migrate `assess_estate.py` / `harvest_estate_assets.py` / `capture_tableau_oracle.py` /
  `run_estate.py` onto `work_dirs.py` - their `_assessment*/` / `_sweep*/` / `_oracle*/` /
  `_bundle*/` defaults are unchanged and still documented as-is in `AGENTS.md` /
  `docs/operator-runbook.md`.
- generate `_runs/INDEX.md` or a legacy-migration helper (issue #234's remaining acceptance
  criteria).
- reproduce `harvest_estate_assets.py`'s fail-closed `git check-ignore` output guard as a shared
  helper (issue #234 AC4) - left where it is today so this PR does not touch a file it doesn't own.

Migrating existing scripts onto the helper is real, separate follow-up work.

## Verification

- `git check-ignore -v -- _runs/001-acme/deliverables/connections.json` (no trailing slash) ->
  `.gitignore:127:/_*` - ignored by construction, same rule that covers every other scratch root.
- `sync_agent_conventions.py --check` -> all four persona character counts **unchanged**
  (27,848 / 28,054 / 28,668 / 28,848) - the new convention lives in `AGENTS.md` **outside** the
  `<!-- BEGIN:shared-conventions -->` block, and in `docs/operator-runbook.md`.
- `ruff format` / `ruff check --fix` / `pylint scripts` / `pylint .github/skills/pbip-model-refresh/scripts`
  / `pylint .github/skills/powerbi-ai-readiness/scripts` all exit 0 (10.00/10 on `scripts`).
- `pytest tests/ -q` -> **1875 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped**. The one failure is
  `test_every_script_is_documented_in_the_scripts_readme` - it correctly demands a row for the new
  `scripts/work_dirs.py` in `scripts/README.md`, which is owned by a sibling agent in this wave and
  intentionally not touched here. Flagging for routing rather than editing that file.
- Mutation-tested `tests/test_work_dirs.py` against `scripts/work_dirs.py` (see PR discussion /
  session notes for the four mutations and their outcomes) - three caught immediately, and a fourth
  (`exist_ok=True` silently swallowing a real allocation collision) exposed that my first version of
  the concurrency test used a monkeypatch that raised `FileExistsError` itself instead of delegating
  to the real `Path.mkdir`, so it could not actually distinguish `exist_ok=True` from `False`. The
  test was rewritten to pre-create the directory via the real `mkdir` and let real semantics decide
  whether the source's own call raises - it now fails against the mutation and passes against
  HEAD. Also removed one now-provably-dead `or "unit"` fallback in `sanitize_unit_key` that mutation
  testing showed no input can ever reach.

## What I could not verify

- True multi-process concurrency (two real OS processes racing `allocate_run` simultaneously) -
  only a single-process simulated race via a monkeypatched `mkdir`. The atomicity guarantee rests
  on `Path.mkdir(exist_ok=False)` raising `FileExistsError`, which is a real OS-level guarantee, but
  I did not spin up actual concurrent processes to prove it end-to-end.
- Whether `scripts/README.md`'s owner will phrase the new row consistently with neighboring entries
  - that's routed to them, not decided here.
