author: philippeferreiradesousa
body:
## Summary

- expose a correlated `queryVideoRecordingStatus()` API through the existing React Native, Android, and iOS SDK surfaces
- keep clock synchronization once per connection, but send it after the startup command burst so BLE queue delay does not become clock skew
- expose typed `mic_health` diagnostics through the existing event/listener/delegate systems, including sequence gaps, decode failures, cumulative connection counters, and last LC3/PCM receipt times
- restore the ASG battery admission check before `ota_start_ack`, controller preparation, wake-lock acquisition, and OTA download/install; known battery below 5% fails closed while unknown state remains fail-open
- reject SDK OTA-start promises when ASG reports a pre-ack failure
- document the public APIs, event semantics, clock guarantee, and OTA battery behavior

## Validation

- `MENTRA_ANDROID_CHECK_SKIP_PREBUILD=1 ./scripts/check-android-compile.sh bluetooth-sdk`
- `./gradlew :mentra-bluetooth-sdk:testDebugUnitTest --no-daemon`
- `xcodebuild -scheme MentraBluetoothSDK -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -skipPackagePluginValidation build`
- TypeScript project build with `tsc --build --pretty false`
- `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests com.mentra.asg_client.io.ota.helpers.OtaHelperBesGuardTest --no-daemon`
- `npm pack --dry-run`
- full Android app build: `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug -PreactNativeArchitectures=arm64-v8a --no-daemon`

## Hardware evidence

Tested with a USB-connected Z Fold (`RFCX71TH0CR`) paired to Mentra Live `Mentra_Live_060B` running MTK `MentraLive_20260709` and BES `26.8.8.0`.

- video recording status query returned `recording: false` with the correlated request id
- the previous startup behavior produced roughly -3104 ms skew because a timestamp waited about 2.85 seconds in the BLE queue
- after this change, the device reported -267 ms skew at receipt, with `sync_count=1` over the stable connection, confirming the intended once-per-connection behavior
- these glasses emitted no LC3/PCM packets during the mic exercise because custom audio did not start, so live sequence/decode failure injection was not possible; native builds and unit tests cover the diagnostic plumbing
- no real OTA was started; the ASG unit test verifies low battery is rejected before ack, admission, controller preparation, and wake-lock acquisition

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes OTA start timing on firmware (battery gate before ack) and defers clock sync, which can affect gallery/OTA skew; SDK additions are mostly additive but touch hot paths (mic LC3, connection ready).
> 
> **Overview**
> Closes several **Bluetooth SDK recovery gaps** and aligns glasses OTA behavior with documented contracts.
> 
> **Video recording:** Adds **`queryVideoRecordingStatus(requestId)`** on React Native, Android, and iOS. It sends ASG `get_video_recording_status` and resolves on `video_recording_status` with **`recording_status`**, including correlated `requestId` and current `recording` / `duration_ms` for resume, timeout, or reconnect flows.
> 
> **Clock sync:** **`set_system_time`** is still **once per ready connection**, but the SDK now **waits ~3s** after connect so startup BLE queueing does not skew the timestamp. Docs clarify there is **no periodic** clock correction during a long session.
> 
> **Microphone diagnostics:** New **`mic_health`** events (and `onMicHealth` / delegate hooks) when native LC3 processing sees **`sequence_gap`** or **`decode_failure`**, with per-connection counters and last LC3/PCM timestamps. Sequence checking moves from Mentra Live into **DeviceManager**; mic beat resets the sequence baseline on stream resume.
> 
> **OTA:** On glasses, **`startOtaFromPhone`** rejects **before `ota_start_ack`** when known battery is **below 5%**, sending failed **`ota_status`** with **`error_message: "battery_low"`** without touching admission, wake locks, or stale sessions. The SDK **`startOtaUpdate()`** promise **rejects with `battery_low`** for that pre-ack failure; unknown battery stays fail-open.
> 
> Public **Mintlify**, **ASG API**, and **SDK README** updates document the new APIs, `mic_health`, clock behavior, and OTA battery semantics.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1c236c9a54ef4c62b3a09f2a9665403579470fe6. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: alexander-bain
body:
Closes nothing yet — **held on cert `C-F3-CATEGORIZE-1`** (staged in `.claude/handoff/CODEX-QUEUE.md`, unclaimed).

Implements **F3** of the cross-contamination family (#2161). Queue 402, from the Fable-reviewed directive of 2026-08-24.

## The defect

`categorize_by_rules()` consumed `SPORT_PATTERNS` **first-match-wins**, so the *order of the list* was the classifier and a single ambiguous English word decided the sport. ~49 live specimens in the 49,423-market open corpus:

- "World Series of **Darts**" → `baseball:MLB:championship:2026`, filed alongside the MLB awards
- "New Zealand **Darts** Masters", "Most kills on a single map at **Masters** London" → `golf:PGA:championship:2026`
- "**Thunder** Bay Mayoral Election", "Practical **Magic** 2 · Rotten Tomatoes" → `basketball::championship:2026`

## The fix

Every matching pattern now votes, weighted by how much the **matched text** commits:

| Weight | Evidence | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ambiguous — ordinary English that happens to be a team/event name | `Masters`, `World Cup`, `Magic`, `Thunder`, `Giants` |
| 3 | ordinary | `PGA`, `WTA` |
| 5 | strong — unambiguous domain markers | `Rotten Tomatoes`, `PDC`, `Darts`, `VALORANT` |

Ties fall back to `SPORT_PATTERNS` order, so behaviour is unchanged wherever the scorer has no opinion. Plus a **non-sport veto** (`_VETO_ONLY_CATEGORIES`) returning `None` rather than a confident wrong sport — a wrong sport is persisted into the canonical key, a missing one falls through to the LLM.

`\bdarts\b` is **plural on purpose**: `darts?` matches **Jaxson Dart** (NFL QB, 5 live markets) and **Harriet Dart** (tennis). Both are pinned as controls.

## Gates

| Gate | Exit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| corpus vs **unmodified** code (red-first) | 1 | **26 failed / 22 passed** |
| corpus vs fix | 0 | **52 passed** |
| `test_futures_categorization` + `test_league_classification` + `test_event_taxonomy` + `test_league_context` + `test_futures_highlights` | 0 | **654 passed** |
| `tests/test_startup.py` | 0 | 4 passed |
| full backend suite | — | **19,255 passed, 96 skipped, 61 xfailed** (742.86s) |

RULING-CLAIMS ledger snapshot consumed by the full run (ruling 063): `digest=7dbbfd91a103 mtime=2026-08-24T18:24:57Z claims=103 deviations=0 dropped=0`.

## One specimen deliberately NOT fixed

`38277227` "Asia Masters 2026 Winner" is snooker and carries **no snooker token** — its title signal is identical to the real golf Masters. It is pinned as `C1_UNREACHABLE_BY_RULES` with a test that documents the limit, rather than dropped to reach a clean number. It needs F2's discriminators (#2163), not a title rule.

## Why it is cert-flagged

It writes `llm_sport_category`, the first term of the canonical market key. Eight production callers: `tasks/polymarket.py:716,734`, `tasks/team_linking.py:476`, `tasks/futures.py:218,607`, `tasks/kalshi.py:300`, `routes/admin_taxonomy.py:190`, `scripts/fix_misclassified_golf_markets.py:61`.

**Do not merge until `C-F3-CATEGORIZE-1` is GREEN.**

body:
Jacob: *"the text across the system is pretty hard to read at times. I need it to be a bit more straightforward and easier to read"*

## What was wrong

Three things compounding, found by auditing the CSS rather than eyeballing it:

| Problem | Extent |
|---|---|
| Text at 10px or smaller | 27 declarations, 7 of them at 8.5px |
| Letter-spacing | up to 0.42em — wide tracking destroys word shape |
| Text contrast | as faint as `rgba(120,180,215,.32)` on near-black |
| Font | Share Tech Mono — a display face — used for actual sentences |

Any one is survivable. Together they made prose genuinely hard to read.

## The rule this establishes

**Mono for things you SCAN** — labels, codes, metrics, timestamps.
**Sans for things you READ** — chat replies, feed items, task descriptions.

The sci-fi chrome is doing real work in this UI, so it stays: Orbitron headings, Share Tech Mono labels, all the glow and bracket detail. Only the prose changed face.

## Changes

- **Sizes** — nothing below 11px; each size steps up exactly once. Display sizes 14px+ untouched, they were already fine.
- **Tracking** — capped at 0.2em and only on short uppercase labels. Prose sits near 0.
- **Contrast** — faint body colours lifted from 0.32–0.55 to 0.72–0.84 opacity.
- **Inter** added for prose only.

Type scale, tracking cap and colours are now `:root` variables with a comment explaining the rule, so this doesn't regress the next time someone adds a panel.

## Verification

Rendered and inspected in-browser, not assumed:

- Computed styles confirm hierarchy is sane — title 38px › prose 13px (Inter) › labels 12/11.5px (mono)
- `document.fonts.check` confirms Inter actually loads rather than silently falling back
- No horizontal page scroll; nothing clipped
- Production build clean

One bug worth flagging: my first pass used chained `sed` substitutions, which **cascaded** — a 9.5px label went 9.5 → 11.5 → 13 → 14.5, making labels *bigger* than body text. Caught it by checking computed styles in the browser instead of trusting the diff, and redid it as a single positional pass. Noting it because the failure mode is easy to repeat.

body:
## Contexte

Le module **Production** exposait des données lacunaires : Macro sur **2023 seulement**, Manufacturing sur **2024 seulement**, Mining limité à **13 minéraux / 36 pays** (2022-2023). Cette PR enrichit et rafraîchit les sous-modules avec des **valeurs réelles publiées**, et **intègre davantage de produits**.

## Approche

Surcouche d'enrichissement **additive et idempotente** qui charge le JSON existant et fusionne les ajouts par clé naturelle — **sans jamais détruire** les 10 138 enregistrements agricoles FAOSTAT déjà en place. Écriture **atomique** (fichier temporaire + `os.replace`).

## Changements de données

| Dimension | Avant | Après | Détail |
|-----------|-------|-------|--------|
| **Macro** | 162 rec · 2023 | **514 rec · 2023-2024 · 54 pays** | **Régénéré depuis l'API World Bank WDI** (valeurs réelles) : agriculture / industrie / manufacturier / services (% PIB) + croissance PIB réel. Généré par `scripts/fetch_wdi_macro.py` → `etl/macro_wdi_data.py` (déterministe, hors-ligne). Aucune valeur hand-curée ni projection fabriquée. |
| **Mining** | 166 rec · 36 pays · 2022-2023 | **432 rec · 41 pays · +2024** | +16 minéraux (Lithium, Graphite, Tantale, Nickel, Chrome, Zinc, Étain, Titane, Zircon, Vanadium, Argent, Palladium, Plomb, Antimoine, Fluorine, Sel, Gypse) + extension 2024. Provenance USGS **par année** (2022 → MCS 2024, ≥2023 → MCS 2025), `is_estimate` sur les estimations 2024, codes commodité uniques. Uranium aligné sur la table WNA ; zinc Burkina Faso retiré (mine Perkoa arrêtée). |
| **Agriculture (prévisions)** | — | **60 rec · 2025/2030** | **OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook**, clé dédiée `agri_projections` (hors `agri_faostat`, hors résolution HS) ; exposées via `GET /production/agriculture/projections`, statistiques et overview. |
| **Manufacturing** | 190 rec · 2024 | **190 rec · 2024** (inchangé) | Laissé aux **valeurs publiées** : le contrat « valeurs publiées uniquement » interdit d'extrapoler des années non sourcées. |

## Fichiers

**Nouveaux** : `backend/scripts/fetch_wdi_macro.py`, `backend/etl/macro_wdi_data.py` (généré), `backend/etl/mining_extended.py`, `backend/etl/faostat_projections.py`, `backend/etl/macro_extended.py`, `backend/scripts/enrich_production_data.py`.

**Modifiés** : `data/json/production_africaine.json` (enrichi), `backend/production_data.py` & `backend/routes/production.py` (getter/endpoint prévisions, statistiques, overview), `backend/services/production_capacity_service.py` (mappings HS des nouveaux minéraux, HS6 spécifiques), `frontend/src/components/production/ProductionMacro.jsx` (croissance PIB séparée des graphes % PIB, couverture via `years_covered`).

## Principes respectés

- **Aucune valeur inventée / extrapolée** : macro = World Bank WDI (API), mining = USGS MCS / WNA / EIA / OPEC (sources tracées, éditions par année), prévisions = OECD-FAO (étiquetées `is_projection`).
- Enrichissement **idempotent** et **atomique**.

## Vérification

- `python3 backend/scripts/fetch_wdi_macro.py` (avec réseau) régénère les valeurs WDI ; `python3 backend/scripts/enrich_production_data.py` régénère le JSON (hors-ligne).
- Tests backend liés verts ; `black`/`isort`/`flake8` verts ; JSX validé au parse.

author: ransomts
body:
Replacing a file's content deleted its Canvas file object first, and Canvas took the module items down with it. The delete was never doing the replacing.

Fixes #77

## What the measurement showed

The upload preflight already carries `on_duplicate: overwrite`. With the `DELETE` skipped, Canvas performs a genuine replacement: the file id still rotates, but the module item keeps its own id and Canvas repoints its `content_id` at the new object, the old id keeps resolving as an alias, and no orphan is left. So the id was never what mattered — the collateral was. Full protocol and numbers in the issue.

## The fix

`org-canvas--file-clear-way-for-upload` deletes only when the entry moved folders.

**That exception is not cosmetic.** `on_duplicate=overwrite` matches on name *within a folder*, so a file with no same-named counterpart at its destination has nothing to overwrite. Skipping the delete there would leave the old object behind as an orphan still holding the module items, while `files.org` took the new id — strictly worse than today. `org-canvas--file-replace-in-place-p` reads the file's current `folder_id` from Canvas and compares; a failed lookup falls back to the old delete-and-upload path rather than guessing.

## Reporting follows the two outcomes

- An id change logs at **info** and says the old ids still resolve. It used to warn that "modules referencing them will re-sync their items" — the sentence that told users their course was temporarily broken. For the common case that is no longer true.
- A folder-move recreation records into `org-canvas--file-recreated-ids` and still **warns**, naming the files and saying a modules sync brings the items back. That case genuinely does lose them.

## Tests

12 new specs across the folder comparison (including the failed-lookup fallback), the delete decision in both directions, and the two report paths. Two existing specs moved from asserting a warning to asserting the info line, which is the behaviour change.

`eldev test` 3241 specs / 0 failed, `eldev lint` clean, coverage 99.59%.

## Caveats, carried from the experiment

One deployment, one file, one run, 2026-08-24. The file was locked, so a published file's item behaviour is inferred rather than measured. The moved-folder path is covered by tests but has not been exercised against a live Canvas.

body:
Upgrade NumPy and Pandas to fix heap buffer overflow in timedelta-to-string conversion and SQL injection in ADBC identifier handling. This update includes breaking changes that require manual migration.
⚠️ Code affected by breaking changes.
⚠️ The numpy and pandas upgrades introduce several breaking changes that affect this codebase: ## 1. Pandas Copy-on-Write (CoW) - DataFrame modifications after filtering **Where your code is affected:** - `atj_trading/backtester/__init__.py` lines 127-147: The code creates `open_trades` as a filtered view (`self.trades[self.trades['state'] == 'open']`), then iterates over it and modifies the original `self.trades` DataFrame using `.loc[x, ...]`. With CoW enabled by default in pandas 3.0, this pattern may not work as expected because `open_trades` is now a copy, not a view. **Impact:** The backtester's stop-loss and take-profit logic may fail to update trade states correctly. When iterating through `open_trades` and trying to modify `self.trades` using indices from `open_trades`, the modifications might not propagate correctly due to CoW behavior changes. **Remediation:** Refactor to work directly with `self.trades` DataFrame using boolean indexing instead of creating a filtered view first, or ensure explicit `.copy()` is used when needed and work with the original DataFrame for modifications. ## 2. Pandas Copy-on-Write - Chained assignment on filtered DataFrames **Where your code is affected:** - `projects/backtest_simulator/backtest_simulator.py` lines 76-78: After creating `open_trades` as a filtered copy with `.copy()`, the code performs multiple column assignments (`open_trades['open_time'] = ...`, `open_trades['close_time'] = ...`, `open_trades['current_price'] = ...`, `open_trades['pnl'] = ...`). While `.copy()` is used, subsequent operations on datetime columns may trigger warnings or unexpected behavior. **Impact:** The datetime string formatting operations on `open_trades` may raise `SettingWithCopyWarning` or behave unexpectedly, potentially causing the backtest simulator visualization to fail. **Remediation:** Ensure all column modifications are done using `.loc` accessor or chain operations properly to avoid ambiguity with CoW. ## 3. Pandas 3.0 - Python version requirement **Where your code is affected:** - The entire codebase (no explicit Python version constraint found in requirements.txt or configuration files) **Impact:** Pandas 3.0 requires Python 3.11+. If the environment is running Python 3.10 or earlier, the pandas upgrade will fail or cause runtime errors. **Remediation:** Verify Python version is 3.11 or higher before upgrading, or add explicit Python version constraint to project configuration. ## 4. Pandas 3.0 - Default string dtype changes **Where your code is affected:** - `atj_trading/backtester/__init__.py` lines 257-261: Uses `.astype(str)` to convert datetime columns to strings for JSON export **Impact:** With pandas 3.0's new default string dtype, the behavior of `.astype(str)` may change, potentially affecting JSON serialization format or causing type compatibility issues with downstream consumers. **Remediation:** Explicitly specify the string dtype as `.astype('object')` or use `.astype(pd.StringDtype())` to maintain consistent behavior, or test JSON export thoroughly after upgrade. ## 5. body:
Tasks 6–10 of `reroll-style-consistency`. Second and final PR of that plan; #94 was mitigation A.

## Read this before reviewing: this PR does not fix the reported bug

**Mitigation A already did**, and that is now verified rather than assumed. On 2026-08-24 "A Spot for Sunny" regenerated on `gpt-image-1` and page 5 v3 reads as the same book as the May original — soft watercolor and ink, against v2's glossy Flux render ([evidence](https://github.com/slickG0ose/storybook/issues/93#issuecomment-5402574808)). The Kontext anchor was never involved, because that book pins to `openai`.

So what this PR buys is narrower than the plan assumed when it was written: **it tightens style-lock for Fal-pinned books**, where the pin alone cannot help because Flux was always the model and drift comes from sampling rather than a model swap.

**And its central risk has never been observed.** Task 8's manual step — re-roll once with feedback, once with the box empty, and confirm the empty one is not a near-copy — has not been performed, because reaching the Kontext path needs a Fal-pinned book and a `FAL_KEY`. Until someone compares two images side by side, the variation directive is an untested hypothesis.

**Merging this is a judgment call, not a formality.** It is a reasonable call to park the branch.

## What it does

- **Style anchor** — a targeted re-roll passes the page's own current illustration as reference 0, routing Fal to `flux-pro/kontext` (1 ref) or `kontext/multi` (2+). Bulk illustrate gets no anchor on any page: bulk targets pages with no prior image by definition.
- **`resolveStyleAnchor`** returns a path only when the file is genuinely readable, and never throws. It checks `stat().isFile()`, not merely that `stat` succeeded — a directory at the anchor path stats fine and then makes `readFile` throw `EISDIR`, 500ing the re-roll through the exact path the guard exists to protect.
- **Reference precedence** — anchor at index 0, required portraits after, capped at `MAX_REFERENCE_IMAGES = 3`, warning when truncation bites.
- **Prompt split** — with feedback, keep style/palette/composition and change only what was asked; without feedback, keep style and character designs but produce a fresh composition and camera angle. Mutually exclusive, asserted in both directions: a prompt carrying both would tell the model to preserve and vary the same thing at once.
- **Client hint** — one line under "What to change on re-roll". The behaviour changed underneath the button; without a word of explanation a less-varied Redo reads as breakage rather than as the fix.

## The pricing gate is closed

Task 0 item 3 named the current Kontext price a merge blocker. Re-checked against fal.ai on 2026-08-24:

| model | price |
|---|---|
| `flux-pro/kontext` | $0.04 / image — unchanged since ADR-007 pinned it |
| `flux-pro/kontext/multi` | $0.04 / image — **never verified before**; same |
| `flux-pro/v1.1` | $0.04 / megapixel |

`kontext/multi` matching `kontext` is the useful finding: **reference count does not affect spend**, so anchor + two portraits costs what one reference costs. `COST_CENTS.illustration = 4` is correct and unchanged.

ADR-013 also records the thing that looks like a discrepancy and is not — `v1.1` bills per megapixel "rounded up", and `square_hd` is 1.048576 MP, which a strict reading would round to 2 MP and make our metering half the real cost. fal's own framing ("output is based on 1MP images") says otherwise. Both readings are written down, with a pointer to where to look if an invoice ever disagrees.

## Verification

- server **354**, client **257**, both typechecks clean, lint and build clean
- `dark-mode-parity-check` clean on the one added class
- `adr-tracking-check`: **12 items, 0 orphaned**
- The byte-identical prompt oracle added in Task 7 is **new, not extended** — nothing in the repo pinned `generateIllustration`'s assembled prompt before this branch, so a silent change to the base wording would previously have passed the whole suite

Includes a merge of `master` (#98, #99). One conflict, in `BookSpread.test.tsx`, where both sides appended a describe block and git interleaved them at a shared comment opener; resolved by rebuilding the file rather than patching the seam.

## Task 10 outputs

- **ADR-013 amended** with the three mitigation-B decisions, plus the honest note above about what this PR does and does not buy
- **#101 filed** as the permanent backlog record for the original bug, which existed only as a verbal review comment on #83
- Deferred items and #91 linked; `kontext/multi` max-reference-count question recorded as *fal documents no maximum*, so the cap of 3 is our ceiling rather than theirs

## Known, unfixed

- **#93** — the bare-Redo near-copy check and the 409 render, both still unexercised
- **#100** — the revert route accepts any URL string; this branch does not touch it

`validatePatchKeys()` heißt jetzt `validatePatch()` und prüft zusätzlich die Werte-Typen, bevor geschrieben wird — Skalar-Felder nehmen Skalare und `null`, Datumsfelder zusätzlich Timestamps und Datums-Strings, Multi-Value-Felder Arrays aus Skalaren. Zwei Tests in `MetainfoApiTest`, beide mit Kontrollwert im selben Body, der beweist, dass der Patch komplett abgelehnt wird. Gegenprobe gemacht: ohne den Fix schlagen beide mit „Failed asserting that 200 is identical to 400" fehl.

author: adrianwedd
body:
## What was invisible

SPARK's nightly memory consolidation pass — the thing that turns a day of thoughts into `state/memories-spark.jsonl` — had **no health component at all**. It was absent from `health.STALE_AFTER_S`, so `read_health()` never named it: not as `failing`, not as `stale`, not even as `missing`. `_consolidation_tick` logged a line and reported nothing either way.

The consequence is the worst kind of failure this repo's health module exists to prevent: the robot can go days without forming a single long-term memory while `overall: ok` and every dashboard reads green. It has been doing exactly that.

```
2026-08-19  failed — TimeoutExpired
2026-08-20  failed — TimeoutExpired
2026-08-21  ok — wrote 8
2026-08-22  failed — claude exit 1
2026-08-23  ok — wrote 8
2026-08-24  failed — global cooldown (828s / 1800s)
2026-08-25  failed — claude exit 1
```

Five of the last ten nights failed. Nothing anywhere said so. `state/memories-spark.jsonl` was last appended on 2026-08-23.

## What's visible now

- **`px-mind-consolidation` is a known health component**, with a **30h** staleness window. Deliberately not px-blog's `86400`: consolidation fires anywhere inside 02:00–06:00 Hobart, so two perfectly healthy runs can sit ~28h apart (02:00 one night, 05:59 the next). A daily window would report a working job as stale most afternoons, which is how an alarm teaches its reader to ignore it. 30h clears the worst case with ~2h to spare, and a night that produced no attempt at all still surfaces by the following morning.

- **`_consolidation_tick` distinguishes three outcomes**, and the distinction is load-bearing:
  - `ok` / `skipped` → `record_success`. "Skipped" (too few thoughts in 24h) is a *correct* night, not a failure — `maybe_consolidate` marks the date done for it — so recording it keeps a quiet-but-working night from ageing into stale.
  - anything else → `record_failure`. This is the case that was silent.
  - `None` (outside the window, already done today, dry run) → **records nothing**. "Not due tonight" must not refresh the record on every 60s tick; staleness already covers true silence.

- **`health.memory_formation()`** answers "when did SPARK last form a long-term memory", promoted to a top-level `memory_formation` key in `read_health()`. It keys on **`last_success_ts`, never `updated_ts`** — a failing attempt refreshes the record without distilling anything, so a pass that fails every night stays inside its staleness window *and* under the failure threshold while the store has not grown for days. That is precisely the live shape, and it is why `overdue` (>48h) is a separate axis from `status`.

- **`bin/px-motd`** renders a line in the cognitive section, right under the 24h-thought sparkline — the thoughts are the last day, this is what survived them:
  ```
  🧠 long-term memory last formed 2d ago       (red past 48h, with the last error)
  ```
  It reads the record file directly rather than importing `pxh.health`: px-motd runs as root from PAM and deliberately imports no pxh module. The duplicated 48h constant is pinned against `health.MEMORY_FORMATION_OVERDUE_S` by a test so the two cannot drift.

- **`summarize()`** returns a non-empty string for overdue memory even on an otherwise clean bill. Amnesia is not a healthy state, and `summarize()` is what reaches SPARK's own reflection context.

- **`/api/v1/health`** gains a `checks["memory"]` entry. The component is deliberately **excluded from the liveness rollup**: that endpoint gates the tunnel health check, and a newly added component reads `missing` until its first 02:00 pass — folding it in would 503 the API for a whole day over something that has nothing to do with whether the device is serving. Reported, not hidden: it still appears in `checks["daemons"]["components"]`.

## Live-failure diagnosis (read-only, not fixed here)

**Root cause of the current `claude exit 1` failures: the `consolidate` deadline is declared in two places and the tighter, ad-hoc one wins.**

`state/claude_sessions.jsonl` shows the shape unambiguously:

```
2026-08-21  duration_s 0.0    rc 1  brain_unavailable
2026-08-22  duration_s 180.1  rc 1  brain_unavailable
2026-08-23  duration_s 64.2   rc 0  success
2026-08-24  duration_s 180.1  rc 1  brain_unavailable
```

`memory.consolidate` calls `run_claude_session("consolidate", prompt, timeout=180)`. That 180 is passed straight through `_run_via_brain` into `ask_brain(timeout_s=180)`, which means `brain._DEADLINES["consolidate"] = 600` — the budget the brain module explicitly declares for this kind, and the one it would use if `timeout_s` were `None` — **can never take effect**. Successful runs measure 30–65s; the failures measure exactly 180.1s. The prompt is not small (up to 200 thoughts plus existing memories plus outcomes), so a Haiku turn on a loaded 4-core Pi crossing 180s is unremarkable.

Not fixed in this PR because the obvious one-line change is **not** obviously safe: `_consolidation_tick` blocks the px-mind loop, and letting it wait 600s would breach px-mind's own 300s health window and stall awareness for ten minutes. The fix needs a decision about whether consolidation should run off the mind loop, which is a separate change.

Two further structural bugs are visible in the same logs and also left for follow-up:

1. **The retry is guaranteed to fail.** `memory.MAX_ATTEMPTS_PER_DAY = 2`, but `claude_session._TYPE_QUOTAS["consolidate"] = 1`. Every failed night in the log is followed 60s later by `consolidation: failed — consolidate quota reached (1/1)`. The second attempt has never been able to succeed and never will.
2. **The 30-min global cooldown can eat a whole night.** Both attempts land within ~61s of each other, so if another session ran in the preceding half hour (2026-08-16, 2026-08-24) both attempts fail on cooldown and the date is lost.

Ruled out: this is not a credential, model-routing or budget-exhaustion failure — `state/brain/meter.json` records the `consolidate` request reaching the resident session, and the same path succeeded on 08-21 and 08-23 with no config change between.

## Tests

`tests/test_health_memory_formation.py` (20) and `tests/test_mind_consolidation_health.py` (8), plus two in `tests/test_api.py`. Inert by construction — conftest's autouse `_isolate_health_writes` redirects `health_dir()` into tmp, `maybe_consolidate` is stubbed, no services touched.

Covers: the component exists at all; `ok` at 28h and `stale` at 31h; `failing` at three failures; success/failure/record-nothing for each tick outcome; and the one that matters most — a component reading `degraded` with `last formed 4d ago`, the exact live shape where every dial looks survivable and the store has not grown.

Targeted runs green locally (`test_health*`, `test_mind_consolidation_health`, `test_memory`, `test_api -k "health or memory"`, `test_brain_daemon -k health`). CI is the gate.

author: indigo423
body:
Closes #593

`ExporterSamplingTable` expired a learned sampling rate after a hardcoded **60 minutes** — twice IOS-XR's `options sampler-table timeout` default of 1800 s, and unchangeable. An exporter refreshing more slowly flapped: the entry expired before the next advertisement, the rate reverted to `assumed` / `1`, and returned on the next refresh. Once per cycle, indefinitely.

## Why the constant erred the expensive way

A rate change is *pushed* — the exporter re-advertises and the new value overwrites — so this window never guards against a stale *wrong* rate. It decides one thing: how long a rate outlives an exporter that has gone quiet.

| | consequence | frequency |
|---|---|---|
| too long | serves a rate that was true recently | rare |
| too short | presents a known-wrong `1` as an answer | every cycle, forever |

**#585** made `samplingInterval` a rollup dimension, so each flap splits a rollup group in a table retained 365 days. **#590** put IPFIX on this table, where `option-refresh-rate` is operator-configured with no default riptide can reason about.

## What it does

Retention becomes a flat **24 hours** — longer than any refresh interval anyone configures, short enough that a decommissioned exporter's rate does not outlive a working day. It only ever lengthens against the old value, so nothing that resolves correctly today can start flapping.

```
parser_optionSampling_expired    rates dropped after the exporter stopped advertising
parser_selectorReport_expired    the same, for IPFIX Selector Reports
parser_optionSampling_evicted    entries displaced by table pressure rather than by silence
parser_selectorReport_evicted
```

An explicit withdrawal — an exporter re-advertising `0` because it turned sampling off — drops the entry at once and counts as neither.

## This PR replaced a much larger one, and that is the interesting part

The first version derived the window from each exporter's observed refresh cadence, at four times the measured interval. It was **wrong three times**, each fix exposing the next hole:

| attempt | failure |
|---|---|
| bootstrap shorter than the cadence | the entry always expired before the second advertisement, so the cadence was never measurable |
| retention from the latest gap | a repeat inside one cycle measured the window as the gap between duplicates |
| "no cadence yet" encoded as zero | a repeat in the **first** burst did the same; the max guard had nothing to compare against |

Two more were still open when it was abandoned: the running maximum never decayed, so lossy option delivery ratcheted monotonically to the ceiling; and `now` was read outside the atomic write, so concurrent advertisements could move the recorded arrival time backwards.

The third failure is the instructive one. It needs no unusual exporter — a sampler table with two entries emits two records per burst, moments apart, and this class deliberately does not key by `FLOW_SAMPLER_ID`, so both land on the same key. An estimator whose worst case is the bug it was written to fix, reached by an ordinary configuration, is worse than no estimator.

What the estimator bought over a flat window: dropping a *dead* exporter after four cycles instead of after a day. Not worth paying for with the bug itself.

The regression test for the second failure also **passed with its own fix reverted**, because a floor raised for a different finding masked it. Two fixes interacting. Only re-running the mutation after both landed caught it.

## Verification

- `make jar` — 1441 tests, SpotBugs 0, checkstyle clean, coverage met
- `make e2e` — 66 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped
- Docs verified in the built HTML, not the source

Every guard established by mutation rather than assumed:

| mutation | tests killed |
|---|---|
| window back to 60 minutes | 5 of 7 |
| both maps share one meter | exactly the separate-counter test |
| count `EXPLICIT` as an expiry | exactly the withdrawal test |

The suite pins an exporter sending several records per burst even though a flat window cannot fail that case. It is there because it is the case a future attempt at cleverness will break first.

## Docs

`receivers.md` states the window and its trade, documents all four counters and what each implies for provenance, and no longer claims a Selector expiry falls back to `assumed` — it falls back to the exporter-wide rate, moving provenance from `derived` to `options` with the interval possibly unchanged. Its provenance table also gains the wording #594 left stale.

## Not in scope

Keying expiry on **flow** arrival rather than a timer is the better policy and is deliberately absent. A `lookup` is not an arrival — a record carrying its own rate never consults the table — so a busy exporter stating its rate inline would look silent. Doing it properly means touching the parser path. Worth its own issue.

author: adrianwedd
body:
## P0 privacy: the `message_obi` redaction only ever covered one call site

SPARK's `message_obi` action is a private DM to a child. The redaction that was supposed to keep it private was a **local variable**.

`reflection()` computed `display_text = "[private message to Obi]"` and used it for exactly one write — the `thoughts-{persona}.jsonl` persist (`mind.py:2897`, `2926`). `expression()` is a *different* function; it re-read the raw `thought["thought"]` (`mind.py:3173`) and wrote it verbatim into the session-history entry.

Session history is not a leaf. From there the raw DM reached, in order of severity:

1. **The voice-loop prompt.** `voice_loop.build_model_prompt` injects the last 3 history entries as "Recent events" — including under **GREMLIN and VIXEN**, whose persona swap *replaces* the system prompt, so the private text arrives with none of SPARK's prose restraint around it.
2. **The reflection prompt, twice.** Directly as "Recent events", and again through `awareness_tick`'s conversation digest (`mind.py:2042-2061` reads `event == "mind"` entries into `recent_conversations`, which is in `_REFLECTION_AWARENESS_KEYS`). This one *launders itself*: the next thought could quote the DM, and that thought is public.
3. **`GET /api/v1/session`** (history projection) and **`GET /api/v1/awareness`** (full snapshot incl. `recent_conversations`).

### Verified before fixing

A sentinel DM string, run against `origin/master`'s code:

```
FAILED test_session_history_leaks   - LEAK: raw DM in session history
FAILED test_voice_prompt_leaks      - LEAK: raw DM in GREMLIN voice prompt
FAILED test_reflection_prompt_leaks - LEAK: raw DM in reflection prompt
```

All three pass with this branch.

## The fix: redaction is a property of the record

The design intent was never "one function redacts on the way to one file" — it was "this text is private". So the record carries that, not a convention each sink has to know:

- `redact_private_dm(thought)` moves the private text off `thought["thought"]` (replacing it with `PRIVATE_DM_PLACEHOLDER`) onto `PRIVATE_DM_TEXT_KEY` — an **in-process delivery field** read by exactly one consumer, `_emit_message_obi`.
- `without_private_dm_text(thought)` strips that field from every persistence path. It never reaches disk.
- `private_dm_text(thought)` is the only read, and returns `""` rather than the placeholder when the field is absent — so a record that somehow reached dispatch un-redacted sends Obi nothing, never the literal string `[private message to Obi]`.

Sinks that read `thought["thought"]` are now **structurally safe instead of safe-if-they-remember**, which is the property the old shape could not have: a sink cannot opt into a convention it has never heard of. (The spec sketched `thought["display_text"]` with every sink reading `.get("display_text") or .get("thought")`; that is the weaker shape — it still requires each sink to know. Same intent, stronger enforcement.)

Applied **idempotently at two boundaries**, the same defence-in-depth pattern as the #174 policy enforcement points:

| Boundary | Why |
|---|---|
| `reflection()` — record creation | The record is safe from the instant it exists, before any reader |
| `expression()` — dispatch | Independent of *who built* the thought: a replayed record, a future producer, or a test is still safe, and still delivered correctly |

Delivery is unchanged: Obi receives the real words.

### One subtlety kept deliberately

The anti-repetition similarity check still runs against the **raw** text. Comparing placeholder-against-placeholder scores 1.0, which would have silently suppressed every DM after the first — a "fix" that quietly deletes the feature. `test_repeated_dms_are_not_all_suppressed_as_duplicates` pins this.

Redaction still happens *before* the suppressor can flip `action` to `"wait"`, which is what the original comment at `mind.py:2892` was protecting: once the action is no longer `message_obi`, no later redaction pass can recognise the record.

## Per-sink audit

| Sink | Reads | Was it leaking? | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state/thoughts-{persona}.jsonl` | persisted record | No | Safe by the record itself, not by a call site; delivery field stripped |
| `auto_remember` → notes / `memories-*.jsonl` | persisted record | No | Ditto — and these are *retrieved back into* the reflection prompt |
| **Session history (`expression()`)** | `thought["thought"]` | **YES — the original leak** | Reads the redacted record |
| **Voice-loop prompt (incl. GREMLIN/VIXEN)** | session history | **YES** | Reads the redacted history entry |
| **Awareness digest → `recent_conversations`** | session history | **YES** | Ditto |
| **Reflection prompt ("Recent events" + digest)** | session history | **YES** | Ditto |
| **`GET /api/v1/session`** | session history | **YES** (auth-gated, still a leak) | Ditto |
| **`GET /api/v1/awareness`** | `awareness.json` digest | **YES** (auth-gated) | Ditto |
| `GET /api/v1/public/thoughts` | thoughts jsonl | No | Reads the redacted record |
| `px-post` → `feed.json` + Bluesky | thoughts jsonl | No | Reads the redacted record (its `_contains_private_content` regex stays as a second net) |
| `px-blog` | thoughts jsonl | No | Reads the redacted record |
| `bin/tool-announce` session line | `PX_ANNOUNCE_TEXT` | No — already redacted its own history line | Unchanged, but its duplicated literal is now pinned against drift by a test |
| `state/obi_chat.jsonl` | raw text | n/a — **this is the delivery path** | Unchanged, by design (auth-gated, Obi-only) |

**Surprises found while auditing** (neither was in the original diagnosis):

- The awareness digest is a *second, independent* route from session history into the reflection prompt — `recent_conversations` is on the `_REFLECTION_AWARENESS_KEYS` allowlist, so fixing only "Recent events" would not have closed it.
- `GET /api/v1/awareness` (authenticated) returns the full snapshot verbatim, so it inherited the same leak.

## Tests

`tests/test_message_obi_redaction.py` — 19 tests, sentinel-based: the string must appear in **no** sink, and the delivery path must still carry the real text. Inert (no services, no live state, no real subprocesses), and the clock is pinned to midday Hobart so the 19:00–07:00 night gate cannot turn a leak test into a vacuous pass on the robot.

```
tests/test_message_obi_redaction.py ......... 19 passed
tests/test_mind.py tests/test_mind_utils.py .. 171 passed, 1 skipped
tests/test_api.py -k "thoughts or session or awareness" .. 13 passed
tests/test_policy.py tests/test_policy_invariants.py .. 127 passed, 1 failed
```

The one failure is `test_policy_invariants.py::test_hey_spark_at_three_am_gets_an_audible_reply` — a real `bin/tool-voice` subprocess timing out at 90s under load on the robot. It **passes in isolation** and is the documented "flaky suite under load" class; this branch touches neither `tool-voice` nor `policy.py`. CI is the gate.

## Docs

`CLAUDE.md`'s two `message_obi` privacy paragraphs described the *old* one-call-site mechanism, which is a large part of why the leak stayed invisible. Both now describe the record-level invariant and say plainly: do not reintroduce a sink that reads `thought["thought"]` expecting raw text.

Implements the hard precondition in `docs/specs/2026-08-25-person-memory-minimal-design.md` — the person-memory work adds *more* conversation-derived text flowing toward prompts, so this discipline has to hold before, not after.

## FH-23 — Vista "Mis conexiones" + revocar

**Alcance:** listar cuentas conectadas del usuario, con botón para conectar nuevos proveedores y para revocar una conexión existente.

### Cambios
- `ConnectedAccountController::index()`: lista los proveedores soportados (GitHub, Discord) junto con el estado de conexión del usuario actual.
- `ConnectedAccountController::destroy()`: revoca (elimina) una conexión, verificando que pertenezca al usuario autenticado (403 si no).
- Nueva vista `resources/views/connections/index.blade.php`: una fila por proveedor, con botón "Conectar" si no está conectado, o fecha de conexión + botón "Revocar" si ya lo está.
- Confirmación de revocar implementada con el componente `x-modal` que ya trae el proyecto (mismo patrón que "Delete Account" en Profile) en vez de un `confirm()` nativo del navegador — mejor UX y consistente con el resto de la app.
- Ruta `/connections` agregada al menú de navegación (desktop y mobile).
- Nuevo logo de marca para FlowHub, reemplazando el logo por defecto de Laravel: tres nodos conectados en un ciclo, representando el flujo disparador → acción → repite. Aplicado en `application-logo.blade.php` (barra de navegación) y en el header del nuevo modal de revocar. Se agregó también como archivo standalone en `public/images/flowhub-logo.svg` para uso en el README u otros lugares.

### Verificación
- Probado en vivo: conectar GitHub/Discord, ver el estado reflejado correctamente en la vista, revocar y confirmar que vuelve a "No conectado".
- Confirmado que "Cancelar" en el modal no borra nada, y "Revocar" sí ejecuta el `DELETE` correspondiente.

author: nzrsrd
body:
Makes the model provider configuration rather than an assumption, and closes Phase 0's three probes — blocked on a live API key for the whole of Phase 1.

## What changes

`llm_base_url` selects the endpoint; the key is read from `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, then `OPENAI_API_KEY`, then `UP_LLM_API_KEY`, in that fixed order. Leaving the base URL unset means OpenAI direct, so an existing install behaves exactly as before. `openai_configured` becomes `llm_configured`, which changes one field in the `/api/health` response body.

## Phase 0 is now closed

| Probe | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Provider reachable, one minimal call | never run | `ok` |
| Which usage-metadata surface is populated | `UNVERIFIED` in ADR-001 | **both** — `usage_metadata` and `response_metadata["token_usage"]` |
| `with_structured_output(..., include_raw=True)` preserves usage | inferred from reading library source | verified; `parsing_error` is `None` |

`pytest --live` now runs the whole suite with **nothing skipped**: 494 passed. Hermetic: 489 passed / 5 skipped.

**Scope stated explicitly in ADR-001:** these were verified against OpenRouter, not OpenAI direct. A pass against one OpenAI-compatible endpoint is not a claim about another, and the rows say so in those words.

## Things measured rather than assumed

- **`validate_by_name=True` is required, and its absence was silent.** A field with a `validation_alias` accepts only that alias — and `extra="ignore"` swallows the keyword instead of raising, so `Settings(llm_api_key="sk-x")` returned `None`. Every test here builds `Settings` by keyword, so the suite would have exercised an unconfigured object while reading as configured.
- **Adding that flag changed the alias-precedence result**, so it was re-measured afterwards rather than assumed to still hold.
- **OpenRouter's model catalog lists zero embedding models; the endpoint proxies them anyway** (HTTP 200, 1536 dimensions, usage reported). Reading the catalog alone would have sent Phase 3 to OpenAI direct for no reason. Recorded in ADR-001 as a near-miss, because the catalog is not evidence about the endpoint.
- **OpenRouter reports the real per-call cost** (`8.8e-06` on a 16-token completion); OpenAI does not. Spec §9.4 now says `TrackedLLM` should prefer a measured charge over the `MODEL_PRICING` table and mark which it used — the two are not the same fact.

## Bugs fixed in passing

- Two health tests deleted only `OPENAI_API_KEY`, so `source .env && pytest` turned them red. They now clear every spelling.
- `probe_llm.py` passed the `SecretStr` wrapper to `ChatOpenAI` instead of `.get_secret_value()`, which would have sent the literal `**********` as the bearer token — a 401 that reads like a bad key rather than a bug in the probe.

## One claim corrected

A test and a config comment both used `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` as their example of an *unrelated* `.env` key — the measured argument for keeping `extra="ignore"`. That stopped being true the moment `llm_api_key` began reading it. Both now use the general case; the decision itself is unchanged.

## Verification

```
pytest                      489 passed, 5 skipped
pytest --live               494 passed, 0 skipped
ruff check                  All checks passed
ruff format --check         48 files already formatted
mypy                        Success: no issues found in 20 source files
```

No secret is committed: `.env` has never been in the history, and the only `sk-` strings are test placeholders.

body:
Second card in the Home screen build, following the vertical-slice pattern from BalanceCard.

What's in this PR

services/spendByCategory.ts → hooks/useSpendByCategory.ts → SpendByCategoryCard, gated on query status with CardSkeleton while pending
CategoryDonutChart — pure, presentational SVG ring built with react-native-svg (stacked Circle strokes via strokeDasharray/strokeDashoffset, rotated -90° so the ring starts at 12 o'clock). Takes plain { label, value, percentage, color }[], no domain knowledge of "spend"
CategoryLegendRow — one row per category, label stacked above amount/percentage rather than side-by-side, so it stays legible regardless of label length or available width
resolveColorToken(token) util — resolves the API's dotted colorToken strings (e.g. "category.housing") to the actual theme hex values, keeping the data layer decoupled from what a color means
Wired into HomeScreen below BalanceCard

Accessibility
The whole chart (including its center total) is marked decorative (importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants" + accessibilityElementsHidden) — the real accessible content is a single composed summary label on the card's wrapper ("Spend by category. Total R$ 2.440,00. Housing 37 percent. ...").

Fixes along the way

Live-simulator check caught the donut's initial size leaving too little room for the legend, crushing labels to 1–2 characters — fixed by restacking each legend row instead of tuning flex-shrink weights for one data set
Bumped the donut from 128pt to 180pt (and its center text) after the first size still clipped the center total against the ring

Testing
26 tests across CategoryDonutChart, CategoryLegendRow, SpendByCategoryCard, and resolveColorToken. tsc and eslint clean. Verified live on the iOS Simulator against the mockup.

author: r3ap3rw1lly
body:
The last piece of the Raven import — the parser and preview landed in #249, the
provenance column in #250, and this wires them to both surfaces.

## The slot counts are the point

An earlier session checked 101 journals and confirmed Elite emits **no**
architect-view slot counts. The only way in was a member reading the in-game view
and typing what they saw — which measurably doesn't scale: **of thirteen planned
systems, three ever had counts entered.** Members did three and stopped.

A Raven export has them for every body the architect has opened.

## Two steps, always

Nothing is written until the member has seen what would change. The worst outcome
available here is silently replacing a plan somebody spent an evening on, and
every failure mode is quiet — the wrong file, an old export of a system since
rebuilt. The plan would just become something else, with nothing saying which
parts were theirs.

**Losses lead** in the preview. Counts entered by hand are called out separately
from blanks being filled, because *"Import wins"* is only half the ruling and the
other half is saying so.

## Slots only, deliberately

Structures are **reported, not applied**. The plan has its own ordering, its own
primary, and rows that have become real construction projects — writing someone
else's export over that is the same silent replacement this flow exists to avoid.
The preview says what the file claims so a member can act on it themselves.

Written with `slots_source = 'import'`. Without it, the *next* import warns that
work the member never did is about to be replaced — the false alarm that teaches
people to click through real ones.

## The hub reads the file, not either client

Both surfaces upload the text; the hub parses and diffs it with the same shared
code. Parsing client-side would be a second implementation of "what this file
means", and the one that drifted would be the one deciding whether somebody's
typed counts get overwritten.

## Two guards caught me, and both were right

**`device-routes-public.spec.ts` and `companion-route-parity.spec.ts`** — inserting
the device routes split an existing `@Public()` from its route, leaving
`plans/:id/sites` unreachable to the app and double-decorating my preview. Exactly
what those specs exist for.

**My own wiring spec was wrong first** — it sliced source to end-of-file, so an
assertion about what `applyImport` does *not* touch was really about every method
after it. It failed on `#bump`, four methods away. Bounded to the method now.

## Checks

- api 1886, shared 974, companion 563, web 547 — all green
- typecheck, lint, ssot:check clean
- Mutation-tested: dropping `slots_source = 'import'` fails its guard

Members: On a plan page — website and app — you can now load a Raven Colonial
export and it will fill in the orbital and surface slot counts for every body,
instead of typing them one at a time from the in-game architect view. It shows you
exactly what would change first, including anything you entered by hand that the
file disagrees with, and nothing is written until you say so. Structures in the
file are listed but not added, so your build order stays yours.

author: wilke
body:
## What

Phase 2 of #201, serving the #353 archive design: `python/ragstack/workspace.py`, an async client over the BV-BRC Workspace JSON-RPC API + Shock for bytes, always called with the **caller's** token (passed per call, placed only in `Authorization`, never logged, scrubbed from every message the client builds).

- `ensure_collection_folder(token, subject, collection_id, *, spec_hash, tenant)` — idempotent; creates `/<subject>/home/.ragstack/collections/<id>/` + `sources/` + `versions/` and stamps `ragstack.format`, `ragstack.collection_id`, `ragstack.tenant`, `ragstack.spec_hash` on the collection folder exactly once (in the create tuple on first creation; a one-time `append` backfill if the folder pre-exists with none of the keys; a folder carrying *different* values is refused, never overwritten). Returns the `ws://` URI.
- `upload_source(token, folder, filename, stream, *, max_bytes, size=None)` — `Workspace.create` with `createUploadNodes` → streams the body to the returned Shock node in 1 MiB chunks (async iterable, async `read()`, or sync file-like), raises `WorkspaceTooLarge` at `max_bytes+1` **mid-body** (the upload never completes), never overwrites an existing object, returns the `ws://` path. With a known `size`, an oversized stream is refused before any RPC and the `PUT` carries a `Content-Length`. Any failure after the upload node was created removes the empty placeholder again (best-effort) so a retry of the same name is not blocked.
- `list_versions(token, collection_folder)` → `[(n, ws_uri)]` in numeric order (`10` after `9`); only canonical ASCII decimal names count; `WorkspaceNotFound` when `versions/` is missing.
- `stat(token, path)` → exists / type / size / user metadata (a missing path is `exists=False`, not an error).
- Typed errors: `WorkspaceError`, `WorkspaceAuthError` (HTTP 401/403, or an RPC error saying the token was missing/invalid/insufficient), `WorkspaceNotFound`, `WorkspaceTooLarge`.
- Settings `workspace_url`, `workspace_timeout` in `config.py`, `.env.example`, `docs/API.md` config table. **No Shock setting**: the reference client takes the upload URL from the create reply, so the client does too (and requires it to be http/https).

Not wired into any router — calling it from `POST /v1/collections` is the #203 follow-up. Nothing here was run against a live service, by mandate; every test runs against `httpx.MockTransport` fakes.

## Review fixes (second commit)

1. **Placeholder cleanup on any upload failure.** `_discard_placeholder` ran only for `WorkspaceTooLarge`; a missing upload node in the reply, a transport error, a stream that raises, or a Shock non-2xx left the empty object behind — and since the client never overwrites, every retry of that filename then failed. All post-create steps now sit in one `except Exception` (not `BaseException`, so no RPC is awaited during cancellation) that deletes the placeholder and re-raises. Test: Shock 500 → placeholder deleted → a second upload of the same name succeeds; same for "no upload node" and a stream that raises.
2. **`Content-Length` when the size is known.** `upload_source(size=…)`: `size > max_bytes` is refused before any RPC (no placeholder at all); otherwise the multipart head/tail are precomputed and `Content-Length = len(head) + size + len(tail)` goes out (verified: httpx 0.28.1 sends an async-iterator body fixed-length when the header is explicit — no chunked). `_bounded` still guards `max_bytes` and additionally requires the stream to match the declared size. Chunked remains the fallback when `size is None`. Tests assert the header on the sized path, the early refusal with zero requests, and the declared-size mismatch (both shorter and longer).
3. **Canonical version names.** `str.isdigit()` accepted `²` (then `int()` raised) and `٣`, and `07`/`7` both mapped to 7 with different URIs. Now `re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+")` plus `str(int(name)) == name`; non-canonical entries are skipped with a debug log. Tested.
4. Perf timing budget floored at 20 ms (`max(2 * raw_p95, 0.02)`) — an overhead / no-buffering check, not a throughput claim; docstring says so.
5. `from_meta` docstring softened about `meta[2]` (spec calls it the object path; no method depends on it). 6. `ensure_collection_folder` docstring notes the concurrent-different-`spec_hash` race is accepted on the single-writer create path.

## RPC calls used and where each shape was confirmed

Sources: GoWe's `mcp-servers/python` `client.py`, `pkg/bvbrc/client.go`, `pkg/bvbrc/workspace.go`, `pkg/staging/workspace.go`, `internal/ui/handlers.go`, `docs/BVBRC-API.md`; and the Workspace service module under `/scout/tmp/all-sandbox/build/dev_container/modules/Workspace/`: `Workspace.spec`, `scripts/ws-create.pl`, `scripts/ws-mkdir.pl`, `internal-scripts/ws-update-metadata.pl`, `lib/Bio/P3/Workspace/ScriptHelpers.pm`, `typeslist.txt`.

| Call | Shape | Confirmed in |
|---|---|---|

author: arisnachy
body:
## Why
A malformed mutable `cordis.patch.yml` can currently brick PHOENIX on cold start even though live HMR updates are transactional. The Google MCP interpolation incident reproduced this exact gap.

## What changes
- persist a `.last-known-good` generation only after a complete successful profile boot
- if a later mutable profile/home patch fails cold boot, move the candidate aside and restore the verified generation
- remove process listeners installed by the failed attempt before retrying
- retry exactly once
- if LKG also fails, restore the candidate and remain fail-loud so core defects are never hidden
- explicit `--patch` overlays remain caller-owned/fail-loud
- never print patch contents or secret values in recovery diagnostics

## Tests
Adds focused tests for LKG promotion, successful rollback, no-LKG fail-loud, failed-retry candidate restoration, and no retry when current == LKG.

author: mordam
body:
The empty-window sweep's header documented the tidy case — one 0.15s step — and that is not what the Mac this script exists because of actually pays. `pending` only empties when a window really leaves, so with N frames permanently stuck every advocate tick runs all eight poll steps and all 8xN re-queries, indefinitely. That was the ReviewAdvocate's finding on #631, and it was right. The answer is a measurement rather than a refactor. A zero-tab iTerm window cannot be staged, but it can be priced: the poll cannot tell a stuck window from a live one — both answer `count of (every window whose id is wid)` = 1, and neither ever leaves `pending` — so seeding the shipped poll with N ids of ordinary live windows, string-replacing only the collect and close passes, runs everything from the poll down byte for byte with nothing closed. Against iTerm 3.6.11 with 22 windows open: 1.44s at N=1, 1.43s at N=3, 1.63s at N=10, 1.66s at N=15, against a 5s timeout. The fixed 1.2s of `delay` is ~75% of the call; the 8xN re-queries the review flagged as the expensive half are ~15ms a window, under 1% at N=10. It would take on the order of 200 stuck frames to reach the timeout, and this Mac holds twenty-odd windows in total. No early exit, and the header now says so as a decision rather than leaving it as an omission. The only saving left is the 1.05s between the first step and the eighth, and taking it means calling a batch stuck before the eighth — guessing "stuck" from "slow", which is precisely the guess the poll was written to remove and bc-xl7n.110's bug with the sign reversed. Two safe alternatives were measured and are recorded as rejected: one bulk `id of every window` per step saves ~40ms at N=10 and trades a per-window failure mode for a whole-step one, and carrying the daemon's known-stuck ids in would save the full 1.05s but needs state in a deliberately stateless script. The one thing that changed in code is a guard. Three numbers in two files decide whether the worst case fits — the poll bound and the settle in the script, and the `timeout` `closeEmptyWindows` hands osascript in lib/iterm.js — and nothing tied them together; the old comment asked a *reader* to check the product by hand, which is an instruction followed exactly once. test/cards.mjs now asserts it. Mutating the caller's timeout alone reddens this check and nothing else in the suite, which is the gap it was added for. What I am unsure of: the 40% headroom constant. It is derived from the measured overhead (the call is ~0.4s more than the delay, plus a per-window term) and it fails on the two mutations that matter, but a different reviewer might want it tighter or looser. The measured numbers in the header will also drift with load and window count — they are dated and attributed, and nothing asserts them. **Tests:** node bin/b7e-gate: 445/446. The one red is test/chromeprofile.mjs ('a profile it could not remove is reported, not thrown') — structurally unreachable from this diff (that suite imports nothing from either file I touched; its one readFileSync targets scripts/helpers/chrome.mjs), and it passes 12/12 run alone straight afterwards, with another session's gate running concurrently at the time. Filed as bc-xl7n.136 rather than swallowed. Directly relevant suites green: test/cards.mjs 42/42, test/reap.mjs 39/39, test/swbump.mjs 37/37. The new check mutation-verified three ways — bound 8 to 30 fails, settle 0.15 to 0.5 fails, and the caller's timeout 5000 to 2000 fails with this check as the only red of 42. **Worth knowing:** The two measured numbers in the header (1.44s at N=1, 1.63s at N=10) are wall clock on one Mac with 22 windows on the desk and other sessions running; they will drift. Nothing asserts them — the check pins the 8 x 0.15s product against the caller's timeout, which is the part that can actually regress. The 40% headroom constant is a judgement call, derived in the check's own comment from the measured non-delay overhead. **Left undone:** No code change to the poll loop, deliberately — see the header's 'No early exit' paragraph. The one saving worth having if the cost ever matters (carrying the daemon's already-known stuck ids in so they skip the wait, ~1.05s) is described but not built: it needs a state channel into a script the header keeps stateless on purpose, and 1.6s inside a 30s tick does not buy that.
Files changed — 2 files · +73 −4 · against `main` ``` scripts/close-empty-windows.applescript +37 −2 test/cards.mjs +36 −2 ```
--- _Opened by a beadcause worker session on bc-xl7n.131.2 — *scripts/close-empty-windows.applescript — With N frames permanently stuck the sweep pays the full 8 x 0.15s poll plus 8*. It merges itself once the checks report; merging is what closes the bead. If this is still open, something stopped that, and the reason is on bc-xl7n.131.2 and in Adam's inbox._ bead: bc-xl7n.131.2

author: smurphy6492
body:
## What

Two output contracts on the `planner` agent, and per-pass logging in `/improve-plan`.

- **`planner` Step 4** — every phase carries a command-shaped `Verify:` that exits non-zero when the phase is not done. Phases no command can decide get `Verify: HUMAN — <what to look at>`, which is a real answer: it marks what must not run unattended.
- **`planner` Step 2** — claims about existing code carry `path:line`; claims about what is *absent* cite the search that found nothing. Unverified-but-load-bearing claims go to Open Questions with a ⚠️ instead of being asserted.
- **Output template** — gained `Files:` and `Verify:` slots per phase. This was the actual leak: Step 4 already asked "how to verify success", but the template had nowhere for the answer to land, so it evaporated.
- **`workflow-orchestration`** — carries the Verify rule too, since plan-mode plans never load the planner agent.
- **`improve-plan` Step 1b** — writes one record per judge pass: score, six dimension scores, verdict, verbatim weaknesses, `plan_source`.

## Why

Both contracts come from measured defects, not taste. Five weeks of real `plan-judge` output was recovered and themed; the two largest defect classes were a missing acceptance criterion (20% of weaknesses) and plans asserting things about the codebase that were not true.

The `improve-plan` default is also marked unsettled in this PR. It previously claimed "one revision does most of the work". Measured: first revisions gained +2.0 on average, later revisions +4.6 — the opposite. The evidence is observational and thin, which is exactly why Step 1b now logs every pass.

## What is deliberately excluded

- `CLAUDE.md`, `FUTURE-IDEAS.md` — personal framing, per the sync gate.
- `.claude/skills/improve-plan/data/` — the judge-history dataset. The *method* is public; the accumulated records name private projects, so they are not. The skill works from an empty `runs/` directory.
- `sync-config` itself — local-only by design.

## Note for future syncs

`improve-plan/SKILL.md` carries one intentional local/public divergence: the local copy hardcodes an absolute workspace root (load-bearing, since Step 1b runs from project subdirectories), and this copy uses a `<workspace-root>` placeholder. A future sync will show this file as a real diff — re-sanitize rather than copying the local path over.

## Test Plan

- [ ] `planner.md` Step 4 and the output template both carry `Verify:`
- [ ] `planner.md` Step 2 citation rule includes the absent-claim case
- [ ] `workflow-orchestration.md` states the Verify rule for plan-mode plans
- [ ] `improve-plan/SKILL.md` Step 1b contains no absolute personal path
- [ ] No reference to any private project name in the diff

author: jesse-elderlinksolutions
body:
`--cron` now emits a schedule for the platform asked about rather than crontab lines on every OS, and the README gains a full **Running it on a schedule** section.

```bash
ask-copilot --cron            # linux on Linux, launchd on macOS
ask-copilot --cron linux      # crontab lines
ask-copilot --cron systemd    # systemd user timer
ask-copilot --cron macos      # launchd agents
```

## The gotcha worth its own section

**A scheduler's `PATH` is not a shell's `PATH`.** The shebang is `#!/usr/bin/env node`, and neither cron nor launchd sources a profile — so under nvm the job dies with `env: node: No such file or directory` into a log nobody watches. That is indistinguishable from a quiet day with nothing to report, which is the exact failure this tool exists to prevent.

`--cron` now emits the **absolute** directory of the running interpreter instead of hoping the scheduler finds one. Measured on this machine: a cron-like `PATH` resolves `/usr/bin/node` v24.18.1 while the shell resolves nvm's v24.16.0 — so "it works" and "it runs what you tested" are different claims here *even where node is found*.

## Platform specifics, each of which fails quietly

- **systemd** — `Persistent=true` reruns a job missed while the machine was off, which cron simply skips. `loginctl enable-linger` is the usual reason a user timer never runs at all.
- **launchd** — `StartCalendarInterval` takes an **array** of dicts and has no weekday range, so Mon–Fri is five entries; a single dict with a range quietly runs on Mondays only. `Weekday` is 0–6 with 0 = Sunday. `bootstrap`/`bootout`, not the deprecated `load`/`unload`. Full Disk Access, or the job reads nothing and exits 0.
- **macOS cron** — still present, needs Full Disk Access granted to `/usr/sbin/cron` specifically, deprecated. Documented as the option not to take.

Also documents confirming a run by the **artifact** rather than the exit code. A scheduler exiting 0 is not evidence a brief was produced; an empty journal entry with a clean exit is the signature of the PATH problem above.

## Verification

- All four `--cron` variants exit 0 with output; an unknown platform exits 2.
- Both emitted plists **parse with `plistlib`** and assert to Mon–Fri, one time each, absolute `PATH` — with a malformed-plist **control** proving the parser rejects bad input rather than accepting anything.
- Both `OnCalendar` expressions **validated with `systemd-analyze calendar`** (next elapse Tue 06:45, Mon 18:30).
- Staged tree scanned against the four live workstation credentials with a **planted-value control**: 10 files, 0 leaks, planted value caught.

No change to `ask-gemini` or `lib/` on this branch.

body:
## Summary

Automated PR created by Pilot for task GH-5209.

Closes #5209

## Changes

GitHub Issue GH-5209: fix(alerts): circuit_breaker_trip re-fires critical every 30min off the windowed trips counter — no live trip, no state to clear, Slack channel spammed indefinitely

## Context

Since 2026-08-24 19:53Z the `circuit_breaker_trip` rule (severity critical, delivered to slack-engineering) fires exactly every cooldown period (30m) with no end in sight. Evidence:

- Last genuine `per-PR circuit breaker open` log line is 2026-08-17 (sdk PR#118 era) — a week before the alerts began.
- `pilot_platform_breaker_open` = 0; autopilot merged PRs straight through the alert window (PR#5208 auto-merged 20:19Z, 26 min after the first alert).
- The rule's condition is `ConsecutiveFailures: 1` ("any trip", `internal/alerts/types.go:409`) and the engine reads `circuit_breaker_trips` from event metadata (`internal/alerts/engine.go:1434`) — which the periodic window-stats seeding supplies as a cumulative/windowed counter (`window stats seeded` every 5m; lifetime `pilot_circuit_breaker_trips_total` = 85). Once the windowed count is nonzero — e.g. from 08-24's autopilot false-closure incidents — the condition is permanently true and cooldown just paces the spam.

## Implementation

Make the rule edge-triggered, not level-triggered: alert on trips-count INCREASE since the last evaluation (delta > 0), or on an explicit trip event, never on a standing nonzero counter. Persist the last-seen count across restarts so a reboot doesn't re-fire the whole backlog. Add a test: stats event with unchanged nonzero trips → no alert; increment → one alert.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Standing nonzero windowed/lifetime trips counter produces zero alerts.
- [ ] A fresh trip produces exactly one critical alert (plus cooldown suppression as today).
- [ ] Restart does not re-fire for pre-restart trips.

## Refs

- Daemon log 08-24 19:53→22:36 (7 identical criticals) · alert engine metadata path engine.go:1425-1434 · 08-24 incident chain that likely seeded the counter (#5167/#5175/#5183)

author: ransomts
body:
> **Stacked on the #77 fix** — it uses those symbols and depends on the reduced cost that makes forcing reasonable. Merge that one first; this diff will shrink to its own commit once it does.

Every skip in the files sync reasons from `PAYLOAD_HASH`, which describes the local file and the last successful upload. It says nothing about what Canvas actually holds, so when those disagree for a reason no hash can see, there is currently no way to ask for the upload.

That is exactly the position of the files uploaded before #70: their Canvas copies carry a stray leading CRLF, and #71's migration deliberately tolerates it rather than re-upload a whole course to shed two invisible bytes. That default is right. Being unable to override it is not.

## The commands

```
M-x org-canvas-files-force-reupload           ;; every file in files.org
M-x org-canvas-force-reupload-file-at-point   ;; just this one
```

Both confirm first. Both bind `org-canvas--file-force-upload` for one run, which takes the first branch of `org-canvas--file-sync-parsed-entry` — ahead of the unchanged-skip, the conflict check, and the legacy-hash migration, all three of which reason from the hashes being overridden.

The flag is never set globally, and its docstring says why: a sync that re-uploads everything on every run is the behaviour #71 was about.

## Why now

#77 removed what made this expensive. The upload overwrites the file where it stands, Canvas repoints the module items itself, and the old ids keep resolving. Only an entry that moved folders is still deleted and recreated — the at-point command warns when that happens, and the docstrings point at `org-canvas-sync` for the run that also repairs those items.

## Tests

9 new specs: the forced branch firing on an exactly-matching hash, the conflict check and legacy migration both being bypassed rather than merely overruled, the ordinary skip still working when unforced, both commands' confirm-and-decline paths, and the recreation warning.

`eldev test` 3249 specs / 0 failed, `eldev lint` clean, coverage 99.59%. Transient entries and manual section included.

author: sh-seol
body:
## Jira

CY-490

## 영역

- [ ] ① 도메인·코어 (엔티티, 상태 전이, 멱등성, 스케줄러, 등급 검증)
- [ ] ② 동시성 (v1 DB 락, v2 Redis Lua, k6 시나리오)
- [ ] ③ 인프라·비동기 (/entry, Entry-Token, v3 Kafka, 대기열, CB)
- [ ] ④ 데이터·검증 (더미데이터, 검증 배치, 오염셋, 통계 집계)
- [x] ⑤ 시각화·측정 (대시보드, 관리자 화면, k6, Chaos, 영상)

## 작업 내용

관제 응답의 `latency` 가 ISSUE 그룹 하나만 담고 있었다. 미터는 URI 그룹 다섯 종을 이미 쌓고 있는데 조립기가 `inGroup(UriGroup.ISSUE)` 로 걸러 나머지 넷을 버렸다.

- `LatencyMetrics` 에 `groups` 배열을 더한다. 항목은 `{ group, percentiles }` 이고 `percentiles` 는 기존과 같은 `ObservedValue<LatencyPercentiles>` 다
- `latency.success` 와 `groups[issue]` 가 헬퍼 하나(`successPercentiles`)를 나눠 쓴다
- 백분위 축약에서 `instance` 라벨이 빈 표본을 뺀다 — 기존 세 필드에도 함께 걸린다
- 표본 없는 그룹도 목록에서 빼지 않는다. 없는 이유는 값이 아니라 상태가 낸다

계측·질의 무변경이다. 시계열 증가 0, 질의 증가 0 — 조립기만 고쳤다.
시계열(`groups[].series`)은 이 PR 이 만들지 않는다. 후속 티켓 몫이다.

## 배경 / 설계 판단

**1. 카디널리티 문제가 아니다.** `UriGroup` 은 닫힌 enum 다섯 종이고 접는 자리도 `UriGroup.of(method, pattern)` 한 곳뿐이다. uri 원문이 라벨에 들어가는 경로가 없어서 그룹 수 상한 같은 방어를 새로 만들지 않았다.

**2. 무부하 그룹을 `NO_TRAFFIC` 으로 내지 않는다.** 처음에는 "표본 0 이면 NO_TRAFFIC" 을 검토했는데 두 가지가 막았다.

- `SourceStatus.NO_TRAFFIC.carriesValue() == true` 라서 `ObservedValue` 생성자가 `value == null` 을 거부한다. core 의 `SourceObservation` 과 공유하는 불변식이라 이 PR 에서 뒤집을 것이 아니다.
- 실제 Prometheus 를 쳐 보니 `app_http_latency_seconds{quantile!=""}` 가 무부하인데도 **30 시계열(5 그룹 × 2 outcome × 3 quantile)을 전부** 돌려주고 값만 0 이었다. `HttpMetrics` 가 기동 시점에 Timer 를 전부 등록하기 때문이다. 즉 백분위 셀렉터만으로는 "표본 없음" 과 "무부하" 를 구분할 신호가 없다.

그래서 값이 0 이면 기존과 같이 `PENDING` 으로 둔다. 진짜 구분이 필요해지면 `app_http_latency_seconds_count` 를 함께 읽는 별도 티켓이다.

**3. `instance` 라벨 없는 표본을 버린다.** CY-449(923a84d)가 자원 사용률에서 내린 것과 같은 판단이다. 원천이 라벨을 떨구면(federation·recording rule) 라벨 없는 표본끼리 짝이 맞아 어느 대의 것도 아닌 지연이 VALID 로 나가고, 값이 정상 범위라 예외도 로그도 안 남는다. **반대 방향 대가는 명시한다** — 그런 배포에서는 지연이 PENDING 으로 굳는다. 틀린 값을 권위 있게 내보내는 것보다 낫다고 봤다.

**4. 그룹 라벨은 `String` 이다.** 응답 전용 키 enum(`ErrorClassKey` 등)이 `@JsonValue` 를 쓰는 선례가 있지만 그 셋은 전부 `AdminMetricsResponse` 안에 산다. `UriGroup` 은 서블릿 필터 안의 계측용 enum이라 거기에 `@JsonValue` 를 달면 화면 JSON 계약의 소유권이 관측 필터로 넘어간다. 대신 enum 을 정본으로 두고 응답 라벨 전체와 대조하는 테스트를 뒀다.

**리뷰어가 물을 지점 하나** — cy-fe 가 이 저장소에 없어 `types.ts` 의 `LatencyPanel`·`LatencyGroupStat` 실제 형태를 코드로 확인하지 못했다. 필드 이름은 프론트 관제 요청안(2026-08-24)을 근거로 했다. FE 쪽 정의가 다르면 이름만 맞추면 되고 로직은 그대로다.

## 테스트

- [x] 단위 테스트 (JUnit 5 + AssertJ)
- [ ] 동시성 테스트 (해당 시 — 재고 N에 2N 스레드, CountDownLatch)
- [ ] 통합 테스트 (해당 시 — Testcontainers)
- [ ] 수동 확인만 (사유: )

신설한 계약 테스트 5개:

| 테스트 | 무엇을 잡는가 |
|---|---|
| `groups 는 UriGroup 다섯 종을 enum 순서 그대로, 미터 라벨 표기로 낸다` | 계측 enum ↔ 응답 라벨. 두 파일에 걸친 계약을 하나로 잇는다 |
| `groups 를 더해도 success·policyReject·systemFailure 는 그대로다` | 기존 계약 유지 |
| `groups 의 issue 항목과 latency.success 는 언제나 같다` | 같은 원천·같은 필터가 두 자리에서 갈리는 것 |
| `표본 없는 그룹도 목록에 남고 빈 값이 아니라 상태로 온다` | 목록에서 빠져 '그룹 없음' 과 '못 읽음' 이 같아지는 것 |
| `instance 라벨 없는 표본에서는 값을 내지 않는다` | 어느 대의 것도 아닌 지연이 VALID 로 나가는 것 |

**일부러 깨뜨려 확인했다.** 다섯 변이 전부 실패로 잡혔다.

| 변이 | 잡힌 테스트 수 |
|---|---|
| `instance` 스킵 필터 제거 | 1 |
| `tagValue()` → `name()` (대문자 라벨) | 5 |
| `groups` 에 ISSUE 만 담기(원래 버그로 회귀) | 3 |
| 표본 없는 그룹을 목록에서 제거 | 3 |
| 그룹 필터 무시하고 ISSUE 값 재사용 | 2 |

**실제 Prometheus 에 태웠다**(`prom/prometheus:v3.6.0`). 실제 응답 원문을 실제 `PromQueryClient` 로 파싱해 조립기에 통과시키는 프로브를 돌렸고(커밋하지 않음), 30 표본이 파싱되어 다섯 그룹이 enum 순서·소문자 라벨로 나왔다. 값을 비영으로 바꾼 회차에서는 그룹마다 다른 VALID 값이 나오고 `success == groups[issue]` 였다.

`./gradlew test` 는 744 개 중 19 개가 실패하는데, **전부 착수 전부터 실패하던 것**이다. 변경을 전부 되돌린 깨끗한 HEAD 에서 동일 실패를 확인했다. 원인은 `Could not resolve placeholder 'coupon.idempotency.wait-timeout'` — `api/src/main/resources` 에 `*.yml.example` 만 커밋돼 있어 신규 클론에서 Spring 컨텍스트가 뜨지 않는다. 이 PR 범위 밖이고 별도로 다뤄야 한다.

## 체크리스트

- [x] `active_count`를 **현재 보유량**(ISSUED + USED)으로 다뤘다 — 누적 발급 수가 아니다  <!-- 해당 없음: 발급 도메인 무변경 -->
- [x] 불변식을 애플리케이션 로직이 아니라 **DB 제약**으로 표현했다  <!-- 해당 없음: DB 무변경 -->
- [x] 상태 전이를 `CouponStateMachine` 밖에서 하드코딩하지 않았다 (런타임·배치 공용)  <!-- 해당 없음 -->
- [x] 로그·응답·에러 메시지·검증 리포트에 PII가 노출되지 않는다  <!-- 새 필드는 그룹 라벨과 백분위 숫자뿐 -->
- [x] 검증 배치 코드에 `now()` / `LocalDateTime.now()`를 쓰지 않았다 (주입된 `asOf` 사용)  <!-- 해당 없음. 조립기는 기존대로 TimeProvider 를 쓴다 -->
- [x] 측정 코드를 건드렸다면 기준이 여전히 **클라이언트 성공 응답 수신 시점**이다  <!-- 계측 무변경. HttpMetricsFilter 는 읽기만 했다 -->
